title: Refuse inserting cells that would push values off the worksheet (#580)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #580.

`home.insertCells` with `shift: "right"` or `"down"` moved the cells and quietly dropped any cell that landed past column XFD or row 1048576 (`shift_cols_in_rows` / `shift_rows_in_cols` keep only moved cells that are still on the sheet). In the issue's repro, a value in XFD1 or A1048576 was lost after inserting at A1, and the saved file did not have it either.

Before it edits anything, `insert_cells` now checks the cells that would be pushed off: the last `width` columns of the affected rows (shift right) or the last `height` rows of the affected columns (shift down), but only from the inserted range onward. If any of them has a value or a formula, the command fails and the workbook stays unchanged. The error text is the same "To prevent possible loss of data, Excel cannot shift nonblank cells off of the worksheet." message that `insert_lines` already uses for whole rows and columns. The table-header insert in `insert.rs` makes the same nonblank check (value or formula). Values that still fit move as before, and the entire-row/entire-column shift modes still go through `insert_lines`.

Test `inserting_cells_refuses_to_push_values_off_the_sheet` in `crates/engine/src/tests.rs` covers both directions with the issue's fixtures:
- A1=1 plus XFD1=2 (right) or A1048576=2 (down): the insertion fails with the loss-of-data error and both values stay where they were. On main the insertion succeeds, so the test fails.
- XFC1 → XFD1 and A1048575 → A1048576: a value that still fits moves to the last valid cell.

title: Chart: color pie, doughnut, treemap and sunburst points from the workbook theme (#579)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #579.

Pie, doughnut, treemap and sunburst charts color each point separately. Point 0 used the series color, which `resolve` already takes from the workbook theme. Every later point came from `series_color(&Theme::default(), j)` in `render::point_color`. So after picking another theme (for example Slate), the first slice changed and the rest kept the Craft accents. The legend swatches did the same, because they come from the same function.

Changes:
- `ChartData` gets a `palette` field (`#[serde(default)]`, so older serialized data still loads). `resolve` fills it from `wb.theme` with `default_palette`, the same source the series colors use.
- `point_color` reads point `j` from that palette. `series_color` repeats every 36 colors (6 accents x 6 tints), so `resolve` stores only one cycle (`PALETTE_CYCLE`) and `point_color` wraps with `j % len`. Long series therefore stay on the theme without a palette as long as the data. An empty palette (a `ChartData` built by hand) falls back to the default theme, as before.
- `sanitize` caps the palette like the other per-point fields.

The fix is in one place, so it covers the slices, the treemap and sunburst tiles, and the legend for all four chart kinds. Line, column and the other series-colored charts don't change.

Explicit per-series palettes (`chart.changeColors` monochrome/accentN/colors) still set only series colors. Per-point formatting is a separate limitation listed in `docs/chart-parity.md`, so this PR leaves it alone.

Test: `pie_points_follow_workbook_theme` sets the first two accents to Slate's `#4F6D8A` / `#8AA1B8`. It checks the pie wedge fills and the legend for pie, doughnut, treemap and sunburst, and it checks that a 40-point pie still uses the workbook theme after the palette wraps. Without the fix, the second point is Craft's `#E97132` and the test fails.

title: Convert TODAY and NOW to the workbook date system in 1904 workbooks (#578)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #578.

The clock (`gridcraft_calc::now_serial`) always gives a 1900-system serial, and `TODAY()` / `NOW()` returned it as-is. In a workbook that uses the 1904 date system the result was 1,462 days too high, so `YEAR(TODAY())` gave 2030 and `TODAY()` did not equal `DATE()` for the same day.

Change:
- New `gridcraft_core::date::serial_in_system(sys, serial_1900)`: returns the serial unchanged for 1900 and subtracts 1462 for 1904.
- `NOW` and `TODAY` use it with the workbook's date system. This fixes both entered cell formulas and standalone evaluation (CLI `eval`, conditional formats, data validation), because they all go through these two functions. `NOW` keeps its time fraction.
- The same clock reading was used without conversion in other places that show "today" in a workbook. They now use the same conversion:
  - conditional-format "A date occurring" (time period) rules
  - header/footer `&D` / `&T` (print, PDF export, Page Layout view)
  - Ctrl+; / Ctrl+Shift+; (insert current date / time) and the ribbon-keytip Ctrl+; path
- 1900 workbooks behave the same as before.

Tests:
- `functions::date::tests::system_1904`: with the test clock fixed at 2026-10-07 12:00, a 1904 workbook gives `NOW() = 44840.5`, `TODAY() = 44840` and `YEAR(TODAY()) = 2026`. These are the values the issue expects. Before the fix the results were 46302.5, 46302 and 2030.
- `print::tests::header_footer_date_follows_the_workbook_date_system`: the `&D` header date is the same in 1900 and 1904 workbooks. Before the fix the 1904 date was four years later.

title: Restore frozen panes when showing a custom view (#577)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #577.

`view.customViews` with `save` stores the active sheet's frozen panes in the view (`"freeze": [rows, cols]` or `null`), but `show` only applied the sheet, selection and zoom, so the saved pane state was ignored.

Now `show` also sets the active sheet's frozen panes from the saved `freeze` value: `[1,1]` freezes the first row and column again, and `null` (a view saved without frozen panes) clears the current panes. Like the sheet, selection and zoom fields, it is only applied when the view has a `freeze` key. It sets the panes the same way `view.freezePanes` / `view.unfreezePanes` do (`set_freeze` in `cmd/view.rs`).

Tests (`crates/engine/tests/custom_view_freeze.rs`):
- freeze B2, save a view, unfreeze, show the view: the panes are `(1, 1)` again (the reproduction from the issue);
- save an unfrozen view, freeze B2, show the view: the panes are cleared (the converse control from the issue).

Both fail on main.

title: Tables: names with a hyphen or other operator characters are rejected (#576)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #576.

`insert.table` and `table.rename` accepted names like `A-B`. Inside a structured reference the hyphen reads as subtraction, so `=SUM(A-B[Qty])` returned `#NAME?`. A rename to `A-B` also rewrote existing formulas, and on save the xlsx writer stored the table as `A_B`, so those formulas broke after reopening.

Both commands had their own copy of the name check (empty, space, leading digit, cell reference). They now share one `valid_table_name` that uses the same rule as the xlsx writer's `table_name` in `crates/xlsx/src/sheet_write.rs`: letters, digits, `_` and `.`, starting with a letter, `_` or `\`, and not a cell reference. Rejected names give the existing "The name that you entered is not valid." error. A rejected rename leaves the table and its formulas unchanged. `A_B`, `Sales` and the default `TableN` names still work, and names with a space are still rejected.

Test: `table_names_with_a_hyphen_are_rejected` checks that creating `A-B` fails and adds no table, that renaming `Sales` to `A-B` (or `.AB`) fails and keeps `Sales`, and that renaming to `A_B` works. It fails on main because main accepts `A-B`.

title: Reject table.resize to a range that does not overlap the table (#575)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #575.

`table.resize` only checked that the header row stays the same. Its error message also says the new range must overlap the original table, but that part was never checked. So a table over A1:B2 could be moved to a blank D1:E2: its columns became `Column1`/`Column2` and a formula like `=SUM(T[Qty])` turned into `#REF!`.

The handler now also rejects a range that does not intersect the current table range (`RangeRef::intersects`). It returns the same error message the command already uses for a changed header row. The check runs before anything is changed, so the table stays as it was.

Tests (`crates/engine/tests/table_resize_overlap.rs`):
- resizing A1:B2 to D1:E2 is rejected, and the table keeps its A1:B2 range and its `Qty` column (this test fails without the fix);
- resizing to the overlapping B1:C2 still works.

title: Keep a defined name that shares a table's name when the table is renamed (#574)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #574.

`table.rename` rewrote every bare `Expr::Name` that matched the old table name. When a workbook or sheet defined name has the same name (the table-first order the issue describes is accepted), `=Data` resolves to the defined name, because `eval.rs` looks up defined names before bare table names. The rename still changed it to `=Later`, so the result went from 100 (the defined name) to 7 (the table).

`table_rename` now checks, for each sheet, whether `wb.name(old, sheet)` finds a defined name. This is the same lookup the evaluator uses for a formula on that sheet. If it finds one, bare names on that sheet are left alone. Structured references (`Data[Qty]`) are still rewritten as before. When no defined name has the table's name, nothing changes.

Test `table_rename_keeps_a_defined_name_with_the_same_name` in `crates/engine/src/tests.rs` runs the issue's command sequence through `Session::execute`. After the rename, E1 is still `=Data` = 100 and F1 is `=SUM(Later[Qty])` = 7. On main it fails because E1 becomes `=Later`.

title: Reject out-of-range numeric filterBy columns instead of overflowing (#573)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #573.

`data.filterBy` accepts a 0-based numeric column offset. `col_param` turned it into a column with `base + o as u32`. The `as` cast truncated a `u64` silently, and the addition could overflow before the range check ran. In a debug build the overflow panicked, and the session sent back an internal error instead of the usual parameter error.

Changes:

- `col_param` now uses `u32::try_from` and `checked_add`, so a number that cannot be a column returns `None` instead of overflowing.
- `filter_by` reports a numeric `column` that does not fit as `column outside the filter range`, the same error a small out-of-range offset such as `2` or the letter `"D"` already gets. A missing or non-numeric `column` still returns `missing \`column\``.

The other `col_param` callers (sort, removeDuplicates, subtotal) also stop overflowing. A huge number there goes through the same path an unusable column already takes in each of them, so their behaviour for valid input does not change.

Test: `filter_by_huge_numeric_column_is_rejected_not_overflowed` uses the issue's setup (B1:C3 with an AutoFilter). It checks that `2`, `u32::MAX` and `u64::MAX` all return the parameter error, and that the valid offset `0` still hides exactly one row. Without the fix, `u32::MAX` overflows and the test fails.

title: Return #VALUE! for AGGREGATE without a data argument (#572)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #572.

`=AGGREGATE(9,0)` gave a plain `0`, both as a stored cell and through `gridcraft-cli eval`, even though it has no data argument. `Evaluator::subtotal` (crates/calc/src/eval.rs) handles both SUBTOTAL and AGGREGATE. Its argument guard asked for at least 2 arguments, which is enough for SUBTOTAL (function_num, ref1). AGGREGATE also takes `options`, so 2 arguments leave no reference, and the function aggregated an empty list.

The guard now asks for 3 arguments for AGGREGATE (function_num, options, ref1, as in Microsoft's documentation and our own catalog signature) and still 2 for SUBTOTAL. A short call returns `#VALUE!`, which is what `=AGGREGATE(9)` and a short `SUBTOTAL` already return. Stored cells and `eval` both go through this evaluator, so the fix covers both paths. The entry-time argument check from #409 still skips evaluator special forms, the same as for SUBTOTAL.

Test `aggregate_without_data_argument_is_an_error` (crates/calc/src/tests.rs) checks the issue's restoration list:
- `=AGGREGATE(9,0)` and `=AGGREGATE(4,0)` give `#VALUE!` (both gave 0 before this change)
- `=AGGREGATE(9,0,A1:A2)` = 3, `=AGGREGATE(9,0,A3:A4)` over an empty range = 0, `=AGGREGATE(9,0,A1:A2,A1:A2)` = 6

title: Fix SEARCH position when text contains a char with multi-char lowercase (#571)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #571.

`SEARCH` lowercases the text before running the wildcard matcher, and `lower_chars` in `criteria.rs` used `flat_map(char::to_lowercase)`. `İ` (U+0130) lowercases to two chars (`i` + U+0307), so every index after it was off by one: `SEARCH("b","İb")` returned 3, `MID("İb",SEARCH("b","İb"),1)` returned `""`, and `SEARCH("b","aİbc",4)` found the `b` before the start.

The fix lowercases one char to exactly one char (the first char of its lowercase form, so `İ` folds to `i`). This is what `fold` in `text.rs` already does for the same reason. The pattern tokenizer uses the same helper, so the pattern and the text fold the same way. Because `İ` still folds to `i`, case-insensitive matches that worked before still work: `SEARCH("i","aİbc")` is 2 and the criterion `i*` still matches `İstanbul`.

Each check from the issue's restoration list:
- `SEARCH("b","İb")` and `SEARCH("B","İb")` return 2, so `MID("İb",SEARCH("b","İb"),1)` returns `b`
- `SEARCH("b?","aİbc")` returns 3
- `SEARCH("b","aİbc",4)` returns `#VALUE!`
- the ASCII/`é` controls, start 0, and a missing `z` are unchanged

Tests: new assertions in `text.rs` `find_search` and in `criteria.rs` `wildcards`. The position assertions fail without the fix.

title: fix(engine): CSV named History keeps a valid sheet name (#570)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #570.

Opening `History.csv` (or a `.tsv`/`.txt`, any case) named the first sheet after the file stem, `History`, a name `Workbook::check_sheet_name` reserves, so Rename Sheet then rejected the sheet's own name.

`rename_first_sheet` (shared by the CSV and TSV open paths) now skips the stem when it is `History` (ASCII case-insensitive, the same comparison `check_sheet_name` uses), so the sheet keeps its default `Sheet1`. Other stems are unchanged.

Test: `csv_named_history_does_not_get_the_reserved_sheet_name` opens `History.csv`, `hIsToRy.csv` and `history.tsv` and checks the resulting name passes `check_sheet_name`; `Sales.csv` still opens as `Sales`. It fails without the fix.

title: Open files by their content, not a mismatched extension (#569)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #569.

`open_plain` already lets content win for ODS and XLSB packages, but two cases still followed the file name:

- An XLSX package named `.ods` or `.xlsb` went to the ODS/XLSB importer, because a sniffed `Format::Xlsx` fell through to the extension. It is now read as XLSX.
- CSV text named `.xlsx` went to the XLSX reader ("not a valid zip package"). When the bytes sniff as text, `.xlsx` no longer forces the XLSX reader, so the file opens as CSV.

The behaviour that the issue's restoration check asks to keep is still there. A ZIP that is not a workbook still sniffs as XLSX and fails validation. An ODS package named `.xlsx` and an XLSX package named `.csv` still open. Text named `.xlsb` still fails, as `malformed_xlsb_keeps_the_current_workbook` expects.

Test: `io::tests::content_wins_over_a_mismatched_extension` saves an XLSX package and opens the bytes as `book.xlsx/.ods/.xlsb/.csv`, then opens CSV text as `data.xlsx/.csv`. Without the fix, the `.ods`, `.xlsb` and `data.xlsx` cases fail with the errors quoted in the issue.

title: Parse an intersection whose operand became #REF! (#568)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #568.

Deleting the columns of one intersection operand prints the formula as `=A1:B2 #REF!`, but the parser dropped the space next to the `#REF!` literal, so it failed with `unexpected Error(Ref)`. That broke both re-entering the formula and reloading it from xlsx. After reload the formula did not parse, so later structural edits skipped it and the surviving `A1:B2` stopped moving.

`significant_spaces` now treats an error literal as an operand on both sides of the intersection space, the same way it treats a reference word or a closing parenthesis. `A1:B2 #REF!` and `#REF! A1:B2` now parse to the same expression as the parenthesised workaround `A1:B2 (#REF!)`, without the `Paren` node. The printer and the xlsx reader need no change: reload failed only because the text did not parse.

How each point of the issue is handled:
- Step 2 (re-entering `=A1:B2 #REF!` fails): the text now parses and prints back unchanged.
- Step 3 (after reopening, column insertion no longer moves `A1:B2`): the reloaded formula now parses, so the reference rewriting no longer skips it.
- Step 4 (`=A1:B2 (#REF!)` workaround) and `=(A1:B2) #REF!`: both parse, and the result stays `#REF!`.

Text that parsed before parses the same way. The only new input this accepts is an error literal next to an operand across a space, which was a parse error until now. Array constants are not affected, because they still need `,` or `;` between elements.

Test: `intersection_with_deleted_operand_reparses` in `crates/formula/src/tests.rs` round-trips both orders and checks that the result equals the parenthesised form. It fails on `main` with the parse error from the issue.

title: Quote sheet names when printing sheet-qualified defined names (#567)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #567.

The parser keeps a sheet-qualified defined name as one string with the bare sheet name (`'My Sheet'!Total` -> `Expr::Name("My Sheet!Total")`), and the printer wrote that string out unchanged. The result was `My Sheet!Total`, which does not parse back, so re-entering the formula or saving and reopening the workbook turned 42 into `#NAME?`.

- `printer.rs`: for a qualified name, print the sheet part through `quote_sheet`, which sheet references already use. `'My Sheet'!Total` and `'It''s'!Total` now round-trip. An unnecessary quote is still dropped (`'Data'!Total` -> `Data!Total`), as the issue's `Data` control requires.
- `adjust.rs` (`rename_sheet`): this function stored the new sheet name already quoted inside the name string, the only place that did. Now it stores the bare name, the same way the parser does, and the printer adds the quotes. Before this, after renaming to a name that needs `''` escaping (`It's`), the evaluator looked up `It''s` and returned `#NAME?`. A second rename of the same sheet also missed the already-quoted name.

Tests in `crates/formula/src/tests.rs`:
- `quoted_sheet_qualified_name_keeps_quotes`: covers a space in the sheet name, a needless quote and an escaped apostrophe.
- `rename_sheet_updates_qualified_names`: now checks that the renamed name is stored bare and that a second rename still matches it.

title: Parse two-digit years in spaced month-name dates (#566)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #566.

`Mar 4, 26` was stored as text, while `Mar 4, 2026` and `4-Mar-26` became the date. The spaced month-name branch of `parse_date` passed the year straight to `valid_ymd`, which rejects years before 1900, so a two-digit year never parsed.

That branch now expands two-digit years with the same rule the dashed and slashed forms already use (00-29 -> 20xx, 30-99 -> 19xx). It applies to both `Mar 4 26` and `4 March 26`. Four-digit years behave as before, and pre-1900 years still stay text.

Test: `month_name_short_year` in `crates/core/src/parse.rs` covers `Mar 4, 26`, `Mar 4 26`, `March 4 26` and `4 March 26`, all equal to `Mar 4, 2026`. It also checks `Mar 4, 99` = 1999, and that `Mar 4, 1776` and the invalid `Feb 30, 26` stay text.

title: Treat serials past 9999-12-31 as out of range in the 1904 date system (#565)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #565.

The upper date limit was hard-coded as the 1900-system serial of 9999-12-31 (2958465) in `datetime_from_serial`, `serial_from_ymd` (core) and `render_date` (numfmt). In the 1904 system that day is serial 2957003. So serials 2957004 to 2958465 formatted as dates in year 10000 (`1/1/10000`), and `TEXT` returned that string instead of `#VALUE!`.

Change: a new `gridcraft_core::date::max_serial(sys)` returns the last valid serial for each date system (2958465 for 1900, 2957003 for 1904). The three range checks use it. The 1900 system behaves as before.

Each point of the restoration check:
- 1904, serial 2957004: date format shows `########`, `TEXT(..., "m/d/yyyy")` returns `#VALUE!`.
- 1904, serial 2957003 and 2957003.5: still `12/31/9999`.
- 1904, serial 0: still `1/1/1904`.
- 1900, serials 2958465 / 2958466: unchanged (`12/31/9999` / `########`).
- The cell values are not touched. Only formatting changes.

Date functions that convert serials through `datetime_from_serial` (DAY, MONTH, YEAR and similar) now also return `#NUM!` for these serials in 1904 workbooks, the same as for serials past the limit in the 1900 system.

Tests:
- `core::date` tests: `serial_from_ymd(D1904, 9999, 12, 31)` = 2957003, day 32 gives `None`, and `datetime_from_serial` at 2957003.5 / 2957004.
- `numfmt` `dates_and_times`: `m/d/yyyy` at both boundaries in both date systems.
- `numfmt` `text_fn`: `TEXT` at 2957003 / 2957004 in the 1904 system.

title: Read date text in the workbook date system in arithmetic and VALUE (#564)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #564.

In a 1904-date-system workbook, `=A1+0` and `=VALUE(A1)` with A1 holding the text `1/1/1904` returned 1462 (the 1900 serial) instead of 0, while `DATEVALUE`, `DATE` and typed dates already used the workbook's date system.

Cause: numeric-text coercion (`parse_number_text`, used by `Value::to_number`) always parsed dates as D1900.

Change:
- `gridcraft_core::parse::parse_number_text_in(s, sys)` and `Value::to_number_in(sys)` take the date system. The old `parse_number_text` / `to_number` keep their signatures and behaviour (they delegate with D1900), so callers that don't deal with dates are unchanged.
- The formula operators (`+ - * / ^`, unary minus/plus, `%`) pass the workbook's date system through `binary_values` / `map_unary`.
- `VALUE` and `NUMBERVALUE` use `Ctx::date_system()`, the same source `DATEVALUE` uses. `NUMBERVALUE` had the same D1900 parse of date text.

Non-date numeric text (`1,000`, `50%`, `$3`, `10:00`) and the `#VALUE!` result for other text are unchanged, because the date system only affects date parsing.

Not changed: function arguments coerced by the shared `num()` helper in `gridcraft-functions` (e.g. `=ABS(A1)` with date text) still parse as D1900. Fixing that means passing the context through about 250 call sites, which is better done in a separate change.

Test: `date_text_coerces_in_the_workbook_date_system` in `crates/calc/src/tests.rs` runs in both date systems and checks that `=A1+0`, `=VALUE(A1)`, `=-A1` and `=NUMBERVALUE(A1)` agree with `=DATEVALUE(A1)` (1462 in D1900, 0 in D1904). Without the fix, the D1904 case gives 1462.

title: Keep history and clean state when a cell is re-entered unchanged (#563)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #563.

Typing the value a cell already holds still went through `edit`, so it built a new workbook `Arc`, pushed an "Enter Cell" undo entry, cleared the redo stack and bumped the revision. `is_dirty` compares the workbook pointer with the saved one, so a saved workbook was marked dirty. In the issue's sequence (save A1=1, enter 2, undo, enter 1) the pending redo to 2 was lost and `file.close` reported unsaved changes.

`cell.set` now builds the would-be cell on a scratch copy of the workbook (`input_to_cell` may derive a number-format style, so it can't run on the live one) and compares it with the current cell. When both are plain values (no formula) and equal in value and style, or both are empty, it returns the same `{cell, value}` reply without calling `edit`. The workbook, the undo/redo stacks, the revision and the clean state stay as they were. `shape.setText` already does this when the text is unchanged (`shape_text_edit_undo_redo_and_noop`).

What still goes through the normal path:
- formulas (re-entering a formula recalculates it, which matters for volatile functions);
- array entry (`array: true`);
- input that changes the style, e.g. `5%` typed into a General cell holding 0.05.

Locked-cell and parse errors are checked before the comparison, so they still fail the same way. Entering a different value still adds an undo entry and clears redo (`undo_redo`).

Test in `crates/engine/src/tests.rs`:
- `identical_cell_entry_keeps_history_and_redo`: enter 1, enter 2, undo, enter 1 again. It checks that the workbook `Arc` is unchanged (so `is_dirty` stays as it was), that the undo length, the redo entry and the revision are unchanged, and that redo still brings back 2. It fails on main because the redo stack is emptied.

title: Paste Special: copy the validation rule with the Validation and All options (#562)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #562.

`edit.pasteSpecial` accepted `what: "validation"` but nothing in the per-cell paste copied validation rules, so the destination stayed unrestricted. The Validation option, and All / All except borders (which include validation, as in Excel; plain `edit.paste` goes through All), now give each destination cell the rule of its source cell. A destination that had a rule but whose source has none ends up with no rule. Link paste and formats-only paste leave validation alone.

- The destination cell is removed from its old rule with the existing `remove_validation_cells` helper. `data.validation` uses the same helper, so the rule's other cells keep it.
- Relative references in the rule's formulas move with the paste, as pasted formulas do. A custom `=A1>10` on A1 pasted to C3 checks C3, measured from the first cell of the rule's range, which is how `check_validation` reads it. Constants and literal lists are kept exactly as typed.

Tests:
- `paste_special_validation_copies_the_rule`: the reporter's steps. After the paste, C3 rejects `-1` and accepts `1`, A1 keeps its rule, C3 keeps its value `7`, and a formats-only paste still leaves its destination without a rule.
- `paste_special_validation_moves_relative_references`: a pasted custom rule checks the destination cell, not the source.

title: MCP: reject invalid format_range borders as invalid params (#560)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #560.

`check_arguments` checked only the top-level `type` and `enum` of each argument, so `format_range.borders` (declared as `oneOf` a preset enum or `{preset, style?, color?}`) was never checked against its alternatives:

- `borders: 123` reached the tool and came back as a tool error (`isError: true`) instead of JSON-RPC `-32602`, which `docs/mcp.md` promises for wrong argument types.
- `borders: "bogus"` passed through to `home.borders`, which reported success with `applied: ["home.borders"]` while the cell's borders stayed unchanged.

**Fix:** a small recursive `schema_matches` in `crates/mcp/src/tools.rs` checks `type`, `enum`, `oneOf`, array `items`, and for objects `required` plus known `properties` (the schemas set `additionalProperties: false`). `check_arguments` runs it for arguments whose schema has a `oneOf` (or array items with a `oneOf`), and a mismatch returns the same `-32602` "invalid params" error as the other argument checks, before anything is applied. Other arguments are validated exactly as before.

`sort_range.keys` had the same gap (`items: {oneOf: [column string, {column, order}]}`): `keys: [123]` was a tool error and `{"order": "desc"}` or `{"column": "A", "order": "sideways"}` were not rejected up front. The same check now covers it.

**Tests** (`crates/mcp/src/tests.rs`):
- `invalid_borders_are_invalid_params`: `123`, `"bogus"`, `{"preset": "bogus"}` and `{"style": "thick"}` all return `-32602`; the issue's valid controls (`"all"` and `{"preset": "all", "style": "thick", "color": "#123456"}`) still apply.
- `invalid_sort_keys_are_invalid_params`: `[123]`, a key without `column` and an unknown `order` return `-32602`; `["A", {"column": "A", "order": "desc"}]` still sorts.

Both tests fail on main (the invalid calls return a tool result rather than a JSON-RPC error).

title: Make gridcraft-cli check compare conditional-format rule contents, not just their count (#559)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #559.

`gridcraft-cli check` compared only the number of conditional-format rules per sheet. A rule that changed during the XLSX round trip still passed. In the issue's repro, a solid data bar (`gradient: false`) comes back as a gradient bar, and check reported `condFormats` equal and exited 0.

**Change** (`apps/gridcraft-cli/src/check.rs`)
- New `cond_format_list` turns each sheet's rules into comparable text (ranges, rule, `stop_if_true`), sorted by priority. The priority number itself is left out. The writer renumbers priorities 1..n in the same order, so renumbering alone is not reported, but a change in precedence order is.
- `diff_workbooks` compares these lists. A different rule count is reported as before (`n → m`). With equal counts, the first rule that differs is reported (`old → new`), one diff per sheet as before. It uses the same `{:?}`-text approach as the `charts` comparison next to it.
- `docs/cli.md`: the `condFormats` entry now says the rules are compared in priority order, apart from the priority numbers.

The comparison uses the whole rule, as the XLSX round-trip test in `crates/xlsx` already does (`assert_eq!(b.cond_formats, a.cond_formats)`). Rules that survive the round trip still compare equal.

This PR does not fix the XLSX writer dropping the solid-bar flag. `check` now reports that loss, which is what the issue asks for.

**Test**
`diff_detects_changed_cond_format_rule` builds two one-sheet workbooks, each with one A1 data bar that matches in everything but `gradient`. The checker must report 1 `condFormats` diff. Identical copies must report 0, and so must the same rule with only its priority renumbered (1 vs 5). Without the fix, the first assertion fails (0 diffs, since only the counts were compared).

title: fix(calc): recalculate dependents of a cleared spill past 65536 cells (#558)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #558.

Incremental recalc seeded the dirty closure with only the first 65,536 cells of a changed or cleared spill range (`take(65536)` in `crates/calc/src/recalc.rs`). A formula that read a later cell, such as `=A65537` after `=SEQUENCE(65537)` was replaced by `5`, kept the old spilled value. Saving wrote that stale value, and a full recalc then disagreed with it.

This change removes the cap in both places, so every cell of the spill is a seed.

Test: `clearing_a_spill_past_65536_cells_updates_a_late_dependent` in `crates/engine/src/tests.rs` runs the reporter's repro. It fails without the fix because C2 stays at 65537.

title: Return #VALUE! when a LAMBDA call has too few argument positions (#557)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #557.

`apply_lambda` in `crates/calc/src/eval.rs` rejected calls with more argument positions than the LAMBDA has parameters. Calls with fewer positions went through, and every missing position was bound as omitted. So `=LAMBDA(a,b,a+b)(2)` and `=AddPair(2)` returned 2, and `ISOMITTED` reported the second parameter of `(1)` as omitted, the same as `(1,)`. Microsoft's LAMBDA documentation says that a wrong number of arguments returns #VALUE!.

`apply_lambda` now requires the number of argument positions to equal the number of parameters. Both entry paths, an immediate invocation `LAMBDA(...)(...)` and a defined name or LET-bound lambda called like a function, go through `apply_lambda`, so both are fixed. An explicitly empty position such as the second one in `(1,)` is still parsed as `Expr::Missing`. It counts as a position and binds as omitted, so Microsoft's ISOMITTED example keeps working.

One case is unchanged on purpose: `f()` on a one-parameter lambda. The parser gives no arguments for `()`, and that can also be read as one empty position, so the parameter is still bound as omitted (`=LAMBDA(x,ISOMITTED(x))()` stays TRUE). The issue also leaves this variant out.

Test `lambda_argument_count` in `crates/calc/src/tests.rs` covers the issue's cases:
- `LAMBDA(a,b,a+b)(2)` and the named `AddPair(2)` return #VALUE! (on main they return 2, so the test fails there). `(2,3,4)` still returns #VALUE!.
- The ISOMITTED example: `(1,)` returns "Missing", `(1)` returns #VALUE!, and `(1,2)` returns 3.
- `LAMBDA(7)()` returns 7, `AddPair(2,3)` returns 5, and `LAMBDA(x,ISOMITTED(x))()` returns TRUE.

title: SUBTOTAL 109-111 leave out nested subtotals like 1-11 (#556)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #556.

`SUBTOTAL(101..111, ...)` counted a nested `SUBTOTAL`/`AGGREGATE` cell in its range as data, so `SUBTOTAL(109,A1:A2)` with A1=2 and A2=`=SUBTOTAL(9,A1)` gave 4 instead of 2. The cause is in `crates/calc/src/eval.rs`: SUBTOTAL 101-111 are mapped to AGGREGATE option 5, and `skip_nested` was `options <= 3`, so for 101-111 it was false.

Microsoft's SUBTOTAL reference says nested subtotals in the references are always ignored, whatever the function number. The fix makes `skip_nested` true for every SUBTOTAL call. AGGREGATE keeps its own rule (it leaves out nested cells only for options 0-3), so its behaviour does not change.

Test `subtotal_109_skips_nested_subtotal` in `crates/calc/src/tests.rs`:
- the issue's repro: `SUBTOTAL(109,A1:A2)`, `SUBTOTAL(9,A1:A2)` and `SUBTOTAL(109,A1)` all give 2 (the first gave 4 before the fix);
- the issue's three-row control with row 2 hidden by hand: `SUBTOTAL(109,A1:A3)` gives 1 (the hidden row and the nested subtotal are both left out) and `SUBTOTAL(9,A1:A3)` gives 3.

The existing `subtotal_skips_hidden` and `subtotal_skips_filtered_rows` tests cover the hidden-row and filter rules, which do not change.

title: fix(xlsx): keep leading and trailing whitespace in document properties on reopen (#554)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #554.

The XLSX reader trimmed the text of the core properties (title, subject, creator, keywords, description) and of `Company` in `docProps/app.xml`. The writer emits these values exactly, and the XML parser is already configured to keep boundary text (`trim_text_start`/`trim_text_end = false`), so the trim was the only step that changed them. A title like `"  Title  "` came back as `"Title"`, a subject of just `"\n"` came back empty, and saving the reopened workbook wrote the shortened values.

Change in `crates/xlsx/src/read.rs`: read the element text as-is for all six fields (no `.trim()`).

Test: `doc_props_keep_boundary_whitespace` in `crates/xlsx/src/tests/roundtrip.rs` sets all six fields to padded values (spaces, tabs, a lone linefeed, leading/trailing linefeeds with indentation), writes and reopens the workbook, and asserts the properties are equal. It fails on `main` and passes with the fix. Unpadded values, empty values and interior whitespace are still covered by the existing `sample()` round trip.

title: Refuse XLSX export of sheet names XLSX cannot hold (#552)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #552.

A JSON workbook can hold sheet names that the insert and rename commands would refuse: blank, longer than 31 characters, containing `: \ / ? * [ ]`, or the same as another sheet's name apart from case. `write_xlsx` wrote these names as they were (or cut them to 31 characters, so two long names became the same). On reopening, `read::unique_name` repairs the names, but formulas keep the old spelling, so cross-sheet references turn into `#REF!` even though the conversion reported success.

`write_xlsx` (and so `write_xlsx_as`, which covers `.xlsm`/`.xltx`) now checks the names before writing and returns `IoError::Format` naming the sheet and the reason. The issue lists this as an acceptable result ("a clear conversion error before writing an unusable result"). The checks are the ones `read::unique_name` repairs, which are also the length, character and blank rules in `Workbook::check_sheet_name`. Duplicates are compared without ASCII case, the same way as `Workbook::sheet_index`, so the export does not refuse any workbook the app itself lets you create. Ordinary names are written unchanged.

The workaround from the issue still works: rename the sheets with `sheet.rename` (which also updates formulas), then save.

Test: `tests::sheet_names::unrepresentable_sheet_names_are_refused` covers the issue's two cases (`a/b`, and two 32-character names that share their first 31 characters), plus a case-only duplicate, a blank name and an ordinary-name control. Without the fix all four bad workbooks are written without an error.

title: Keep a solid data bar solid across an XLSX save and reopen (#550)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #550.

A data bar created with `"gradient": false` came back as a gradient bar after an XLSX save and reopen, with no warning. The 2006 `<dataBar>` element has no fill-style attribute: the writer dropped the flag and the reader hardcoded `gradient: true`.

**Writer (`sheet_write.rs`)**
- A solid bar now gets the Excel 2010 extension: the `cfRule` carries an `extLst` with an `x14:id`, and the worksheet `extLst` carries a matching `x14:cfRule` whose `x14:dataBar` has `gradient="0"`, plus the bar's min/max as x14 `cfvo`s (values as `xm:f` children, as the x14 schema requires).
- Gradient bars are written exactly as before, with no extension.
- Sparklines share the same worksheet `extLst` (the conditional-format `ext` goes first), so a sheet with both stays valid.

**Reader (`sheet_read.rs`)**
- `read_cf` records the `x14:id` of each rule. `read_ext` finds the matching `x14:cfRule` and applies its `gradient` flag to the data bar.
- The "some Excel 2010 conditional format extensions were skipped" warning stays whenever something is actually dropped: an x14 rule we can't match, or an x14 data bar with other settings GridCraft doesn't model (border, min/max length, axis, negative colours). For files that GridCraft writes itself, reopening gives no warning.

**Test**
`solid_data_bar_survives_with_sparklines_and_gradient_neighbours` (in `crates/xlsx/src/tests/roundtrip.rs`) saves a gradient bar, a solid bar with a formula maximum and a solid bar with a number maximum, plus a sparkline. It checks the x14 `cfvo` markup, that reopening gives no warnings, that the conditional formats come back equal, and that the sparkline survives. Without the fix, the solid bars come back with `gradient: true` and the test fails.

title: Fix data.filterBy inside a table installing the sheet AutoFilter instead of toggling the table button (#547)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #547.

When the sheet had no AutoFilter, `data.filterBy` turned one on by calling `toggle_filter`. With the active cell inside a table, `toggle_filter` takes its table branch: it flips the table's filter button and returns without installing an AutoFilter. `filter_by` then failed with `no filter`, and the button stayed off (the edit was already committed).

The fix moves the "install an AutoFilter over the data range" part of `toggle_filter` into a new `install_filter` helper. `filter_by` now calls that helper directly. `data.filter` (the toggle) still behaves as before, because `toggle_filter` keeps its table and turn-off branches and then calls the same helper.

The install path uses `data_range`, which already returns the table's range when the active cell is in a table. So the AutoFilter covers A1:A3 and the table's button setting is not changed, which is what the issue expects.

The regression test runs the three selections from the restoration check: A1 active, A2 active, and A1:A3 selected. For each one it checks that the AutoFilter covers A1:A3, the table button stays on, the row with `a` stays visible, the row with `b` is hidden, and the cell values do not change. Before the fix, all three cases fail with `no filter`. The no-table path and the path with an existing AutoFilter are not changed.

title: Fix histogram counts disagreeing with interval labels on bin boundaries (#546)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #546.

The histogram labels its bins as right-inclusive (`[0, 7.5]`, `(7.5, 15.0]`), but counted values with `floor((v - lo) / width)`, which puts a value equal to an interior edge into the next bin. For `0, 7.5, 15` the bars showed `1, 2` under labels that describe `2, 1`.

The renderer now builds the list of upper edges once (the same values the labels print) and picks each value's bin with `partition_point(|e| e < v)`, so a value equal to an edge goes into the bin that ends there. The label code reads its upper edge from that same list, so labels and counts can't drift apart again. The interval text is unchanged.

Kept as before: the minimum and maximum are both counted, the bin count and width are unchanged, values off a boundary land where they did (`0, 7.75, 15` stays `1, 2`), and the single-bin case for equal values (`[7.5, 7.5]` with count 3) is unchanged.

Only the chart renderer's histogram is touched; the Analysis ToolPak histogram is a separate path with explicit bins and isn't affected.

Test: `histogram_boundary_values_match_interval_labels` checks bar heights for `0, 7.5, 15` (2:1), `-15, -7.5, 0` (2:1), the off-boundary control `0, 7.75, 15` (1:2), and `0, 5, 5, 10, 15` across three bins (3:1:1). The boundary cases fail on main and pass with the fix.

title: Draw data labels on area and stacked area charts (#545)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #545.

The Data Labels flag (Add Chart Element, Format Chart pane) had no effect on Area and stacked Area charts: the area pass in `cartesian` only pushed polygons, while the column and line passes draw labels when `labels_on` is set.

The area pass now does what the line pass does: when `labels_on` is set (so the existing 200-category cutoff still applies), each point with a value gets its formatted source value, centred 5 px above the top edge of the area, in `LABEL_SIZE` and `TEXT`, bottom-aligned.

- Stacked areas show each series' own value, not the running stack total.
- The labels are drawn after all areas are filled. If each label were drawn right after its own area, the next stacked area would cover the labels of the series under it.
- The area polygons stay the same with labels on or off.

Test: `area_charts_draw_source_value_labels_only_when_enabled` runs on both Area and AreaStacked. It checks that turning labels on adds exactly one label per point (18), shows source values and no cumulative total, leaves the polygons unchanged, and draws the labels after the last area.

title: Funnel chart: hide value labels when data labels are off (#544)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #544.

The funnel renderer never read `chart.data_labels`, so the numeric value next to each bar was drawn whether data labels were on or off (the issue showed identical drawing output for both settings).

`funnel()` now takes the chart, like the waterfall, pie and treemap renderers, and draws the value text only when `chart.data_labels` is set. This matches how waterfall gates its value labels. Category names and bars are still drawn in both states. The existing height check still hides all text when the chart is too short.

The flag reaches the renderer the same way from every entry point (`insert.chart`, `chart.set` `dataLabels`, `chart.addElement` `dataLabels`, and the ribbon/pane toggles), so this one renderer change covers all of them. `docs/chart-parity.md` already documents data labels as "one on/off flag" for every chart type, so no docs change is needed.

Test: `funnel_value_labels_follow_the_data_labels_flag` in `crates/chart/src/tests.rs` renders a three-stage funnel with labels off and on. With labels on, all three formatted values appear. With labels off, none of them appear. The category names appear in both states. The test fails on main because the values are drawn with labels off.

title: Honour the gridlines flag on box-and-whisker and stock charts (#543)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #543.

`box_whisker` and `stock` in `crates/chart/src/render.rs` called `frame(..., true)`, so the value-axis gridlines were drawn whatever `chart.gridlines` said. Turning gridlines off through `chart.set`, `chart.addElement` or the Format Chart pane had no effect on these two kinds.

Both functions now take `&Chart` and pass `chart.gridlines` to `frame()`, the same way the cartesian, scatter, histogram and waterfall renderers already do. Nothing else in the drawing changes: axis labels, axis line, boxes and OHLC marks are untouched.

Test: `box_and_stock_charts_honour_the_gridlines_flag` renders BoxWhisker, Stock (four series, so the open-high-low-close path) and a ColumnClustered control with the flag on and off, and counts the full-width horizontal lines in the gridline colour. On must draw some, off must draw none. It fails on main for BoxWhisker and Stock.

title: Fix chart rasterizer panic on negative rectangle extents (#542)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #542.

`rounded_rect` clamped the corner radius to `0.0..=w.min(h) / 2.0`. When a caller passes a `Prim::Rect` with a negative width or height (or NaN), the upper bound is below the lower bound or NaN, and `f32::clamp` panics. This breaks the no-panic rule for production code.

The fix floors the upper bound at 0 (`(w.min(h) / 2.0).max(0.0)`). `f32::max` returns 0 for NaN, so both cases now give a square-cornered (degenerate) contour and the rasterizer returns the normal buffer. Valid rectangles render the same as before.

Test: `rasterize_does_not_panic_on_negative_rect_extents` rasterizes filled and stroked rects with negative width, negative height, both, and NaN extents. It panics without the fix.

title: Return #VALUE! from FIND and SEARCH when the start is past the text end (#541)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #541.

`FIND`/`SEARCH` accepted a start position of `len + 1`, so an empty search text returned that position (`FIND("", "abc", 4)` gave 4) instead of `#VALUE!`. The bound check in `find_impl` now rejects any start greater than the text length. An empty `within_text` still accepts start 1 (`FIND("", "")` stays 1), as in Excel.

Both functions share `find_impl`, so the one change fixes both. Non-empty needles are unaffected: a start past the end already ended in `#VALUE!` because nothing matched.

Test: `text.rs` checks that FIND and SEARCH with empty search text return 3 at start 3 and `#VALUE!` at start 4. The start-4 case fails without the fix.

title: Return zero from ROUNDDOWN and TRUNC at precisions beyond the number range (#540)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #540.

`round_dir` handles a negative precision by dividing by `10^-digits`. At -309 and below that factor is `inf`, so a toward-zero rounding gives `r = 0` and `0 * inf = NaN`, which surfaces as `#NUM!`. ROUNDDOWN and TRUNC share this path.

The negative-precision branch now returns `0.0` when the rounded value is zero. Every other case keeps the old arithmetic. ROUNDUP of a nonzero value at -309 still gives `#NUM!`, because the true result (10^309) cannot be stored as a number.

Test: the existing rounding test now checks ROUNDDOWN and TRUNC with 1234, -1234 and 0.5 at precisions -308, -309 and -400 (all must be 0), and checks that ROUNDUP(1234, -309) is still `#NUM!`. Without the fix, the -309 and -400 cases fail.

title: Return #NUM! from PROB for zero probabilities (#539)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #539.

`PROB` accepted a probability of exactly `0` because the range check used the closed interval `0..=1`. Microsoft's PROB documentation requires `#NUM!` when any value in `prob_range` is `<= 0` or `> 1`, so the check is now `p <= 0.0 || p > 1.0`. All other `PROB` behaviour stays the same.

Tests: added to the existing `PROB` test. They cover a zero probability inside the limits and one outside the limits, with probabilities that sum to one. Both returned a number before this change and now return `#NUM!`.

title: Reject oversized TEXTSPLIT results before building the padded grid (#538)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #538.

TEXTSPLIT pads ragged rows to the widest row, reserved and filled the whole `nrows * ncols` grid, and only then let `array_val` reject it with `#NUM!`. A text under the 32,767-character cell limit (one 8,000-column row followed by 8,000 one-cell rows) asked for about 64 million cells before being rejected.

The fix checks `nrows.saturating_mul(ncols) > MAX_CELLS` right after the dimensions are known and returns `#NUM!` before any allocation. This is the same guard the sibling array builders already use (`dynamic.rs` MAKEARRAY/SEQUENCE/EXPAND, `info.rs`). Results within the limit, padding and the default `#N/A` fill are unchanged.

Test: `split_rejects_oversized_padded_grid` feeds the 8,000 x 8,001 case and expects `#NUM!`. Without the fix the result is still `#NUM!`, but only after building the ~64M-cell grid, so the test is slow and memory-heavy rather than red.

title: Check the full PIVOTBY layout size before building column headers (#537)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #537.

PIVOTBY's early size check counted the distinct row keys plus two rows. It left out the header rows for the column fields, and each of those rows is as wide as the whole grid. With one data row and 2300 column fields and value columns, the early check saw about 14k cells. The function then built 2300 header rows of 4601 cells (10.58M cells, over `MAX_CELLS`). Only `from_rows` returned `#NUM!`, after the grid was already built.

**Change** (`crates/functions/src/dynamic.rs`)
- A new helper `pivot_dims` gives the exact height and width of the grid PIVOTBY builds: one header row per column field, the value-name row when there is one, the row-key rows, the total row when `row_total_depth` asks for it, and a width of the row-field columns plus `value_cols` cells per column key (the total column included).
- `pivotby` runs this check after it has resolved the column keys and totals, and before it builds any header or body row. It replaces the old estimate. The value-name-row condition now lives in one place, so the check and the builder cannot drift apart.
- The result does not change for any pivot inside the cap. Oversized pivots still return `#NUM!` through the normal error path, the same cap and error that `from_rows` and the other dynamic-array functions use. The check is exact, so a pivot that fits is never rejected early.

**Test** (`pivotby_size_check_counts_column_header_rows`)
- Covers the small controls from the issue: 2 fields gives 5x5, 10 fields gives 13x21, and 10 fields with both totals off gives 12x11. Each one equals `pivot_dims` for that shape.
- For the issue's 2300-field shape, the header rows alone are over `MAX_CELLS`, and PIVOTBY returns `#NUM!`.
- On main the test does not compile because `pivot_dims` does not exist. The over-cap formula returns `#NUM!` there too, but only after it has built the oversized grid. That allocation order can't be seen from a unit test without memory pressure, so the test checks the size the code computes in…

title: HSTACK checks its padded output size before building it (#536)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #536.

HSTACK's early guard only capped the sum of the input cells. The output is a rectangle of the tallest input's height times the total width, padded with `#N/A`, and it was built row by row before `from_rows` checked it against `MAX_CELLS`. Inputs of different heights could make HSTACK build an over-budget rectangle before it returned `#NUM!`.

- HSTACK now adds up the total width alongside the tallest height and returns `#NUM!` before it allocates any output rows.
- The size check moves into a small `check_output_size(h, w)` helper (saturating multiply, same rule as before). `from_rows` uses it too, so the budget rule lives in one place.
- VSTACK has no such problem: its rows are copied unpadded (input-sized), and `from_rows` checks the padded size before it allocates the output.

Small results keep their values and `#N/A` padding; the existing `stacking` test still covers the two-row column plus scalar case.

Test: `output_size_checked_before_padding` checks the helper at the budget edge (1,000,000 x 10 accepted, 1,000,001 x 10 refused, `usize::MAX` saturates). It also runs HSTACK on a 1,000,001-row column beside a 9-wide row: about 1M input cells, but a 10,000,010-cell padded result, which now returns `#NUM!`. The end-to-end assertion also held before the fix, because the old code still returned `#NUM!` after building the rectangle. Construction order is pinned by the helper being called before the row loop.

title: Return an error when a weekday fill runs past the supported dates (#535)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #535.

`fill::series` with `dateUnit: "weekday"` counts down `left` only when `datetime_from_serial` returns a weekday. Once the serial leaves the supported calendar (before serial 0 or after 9999-12-31), the conversion keeps returning `None`, `left` never reaches zero and `edit.fillSeries` never returns.

Now the loop returns `EngineError::Other("The weekday series runs past the supported date range.")` as soon as a date falls outside the calendar. The work per cell is therefore bounded by the size of the calendar (about 3 million days), however large the step is. The error is returned before any cell is written, so the sheet stays unchanged. The message is written in the same style as the other `EngineError::Other` messages in the engine.

Ordinary weekday fills (steps 5, 1, 0, -1, -5) work as before; the day, month and year units are not touched.

Test: `fill_series_weekday_out_of_range_step_errors` runs a weekday fill with step `1e12` from serial 45000. It checks that the command returns an error and that A2 stays empty. Without the fix, this test never finishes.

title: Column sort rejects a zero row key with a parameter error instead of panicking (#534)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #534.

`data.sort` with `orientation: "columns"` turned a numeric `row` key into a coordinate with `r as u32 - 1`. A row of `0` underflowed, which panics in checked builds. `Session::execute` caught the panic and returned `EngineError::Internal`. A value past `u32::MAX` was truncated before the subtraction, so `1 << 32` hit the same path.

The key is now converted with `u32::try_from(n)` and `checked_sub(1)`. When either fails, the command returns `bad("data.sort", "sort key row must be 1 or greater")`, the same `BadParams` path the command already uses for "too many sort levels" and "range too large". The check runs while the keys are collected, before anything touches the workbook, so the workbook does not change.

Valid 1-based row keys work as before: the row is still an absolute worksheet row, a key without `row` still falls back to `column`, and keys that resolve to nothing are still skipped. Row-oriented sorting is unchanged.

Test: `column_sort_rejects_row_key_zero_without_panicking` sends row `0` and row `1 << 32` and expects `BadParams` for each. Without the fix, both come back as `Internal`.

title: Refuse Total Row on a table that ends on the last worksheet row (#533)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #533.

`table.totalRow` grew the table by one row without checking for room, so a table ending on row 1,048,576 got an end row past the sheet and its "Total" label was written off the sheet.

The totals handler in `table_flag` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/insert.rs`) now returns an error when enabling the totals row would push the table's end past `MAX_ROWS - 1`. The check runs before anything is changed, so the table's range, its totals flag and its cells stay as they were. The message follows the existing `formulas.autoSum` boundary error ("There's no room below the selection for the totals."). This handler is the only place that turns on `totals_row` (the desktop checkbox calls the same command). Turning the totals row off, and turning it on anywhere else, works as before.

Tests (`crates/engine/tests/table_total_row_last_row.rs`):
- Header plus data table on `A1048575:B1048576` and a header-only table on `A1048576:B1048576`: enabling Total Row returns an error, and the range, totals flag and cells don't change.
- Ordinary control: `A1:B3` still grows to `A1:B4` with the totals row on.

title: Spelling: skip suggestions for words longer than 64 characters (#532)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #532.

`review.spelling` builds every one-character edit of an unknown word (`edits1`) before it checks any of them against the dictionary. For a word of length n that is 54n+25 strings with about 54n² bytes of text, and nothing limited n: the text-entry path keeps cell text of any length. This broke the AGENTS.md rule that input-sized allocations must be capped.

`edits1` now returns no candidates when the word is longer than `MAX_SUGGEST_LEN` (64 characters). Such a word is still reported as an issue, but with an empty `suggestions` list, so the work and memory per word stay bounded. No real dictionary word is that long, so ordinary misspellings (`helo`, `speling`, `accomodation` from the issue) keep their suggestions. The known-word, uppercase, non-ASCII, formula and user-dictionary checks in `spelling` are unchanged. `review.thesaurus` only filters the dictionary by prefix and is linear in the input, so it needs no change.

Test in `crates/engine/src/cmd/spelling.rs`:
- `edits1_is_capped_for_very_long_words`: `helo` and a 64-character word still produce 54n+25 candidates; a 65-character word and a 1,000,000-character word produce none. Fails on main (the 65-character word produces 3,535 candidates).

title: Reject row/column insert counts past the worksheet and clamp delete counts instead of overflowing (#531)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #531.

`home.insertRows`, `home.insertColumns`, `home.deleteRows` and `home.deleteColumns` read `count` through `u32_param`, which accepts any `u32`. Nothing bounded `at + count` before the unchecked additions in `insert_lines` (the "Format Same As Above" loop `at..at + count`) and `delete_lines` (the block end `at + count - 1` and the shift origin `at + count`). With overflow checks on, those panicked and `Session::execute` returned `EngineError::Internal`. In release builds they wrapped.

**Insert:** `insert_lines` now checks `at.checked_add(count)` against `MAX_ROWS` / `MAX_COLS` before doing anything else and returns `BadParams` for the command when the new lines would run past the end of the worksheet. This is the same check `sheet.moveColumns` already uses (`checked_add` + `is_none_or(|end| end > MAX_COLS)` → `bad("sheet.moveColumns", …)`). The existing "cannot shift nonblank cells off of the worksheet" guard is unchanged, and it still catches data being pushed off the sheet.

**Delete:** `delete_lines` clamps `count` to the lines left from `at` to the end of the worksheet. The block end was already clamped with `.min(MAX_ROWS - 1)`, so the existing intent was already "delete up to the end of the sheet". Clamping `count` first means the shift origin and `Edit::Delete` get the same, representable count.

`home.insertCells` / `home.deleteCells` with `shift: row|column` go through the same two functions, so they are covered too.

Tests (`crates/engine/tests/line_count_overflow.rs`), all on both axes:
- insert with `count: u32::MAX` returns `BadParams`
- insert after a line with a custom height/width and no cells (the formatting-only state from the issue, where the used-range guard has nothing to check) returns `BadParams`. Without the fix this hits the overflowing loop.
- delete with `count: u32::MAX` doesn't return `Internal`
- a normal insert/delete of 3 rows still works

title: Formula: print flat operator chains iteratively so deep trees cannot overflow the stack (#527)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #527.

A flat chain like `1+1+1+...` passes the parser's nesting guard but builds a left-nested tree with one `Binary` level per operator. `write_expr` recursed into the left child for every level, so canonical printing (`print` and `print_r1c1`, and `Formula::new` / `Formula::from_expr`, which call `print`) used stack proportional to the chain length.

The `Expr::Binary` arm now walks the left spine in a loop, collects `(op, right)` pairs, prints the leftmost operand, then appends each operator and right operand in order. The output text is unchanged; right operands and every other node kind are printed as before. A1 and R1C1 share this arm, so both are covered.

Not changed: the parser's nesting guard, and the guarded English/Spanish display in `print_input`, which keeps rejecting such trees with "formula is nested too deeply".

Test: `prints_long_flat_chain_without_deep_recursion` builds a 20000-term `+` chain and prints it with `print` and `print_r1c1` on a thread with a 256 KB stack, then checks the exact text. Without the fix the recursive printer overflows that stack.

title: Make check --json list warning messages instead of a count (#526)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #526.

`docs/cli.md` documents the `warnings` field of each file in `gridcraft-check/1` as the list of import-warning messages (`"warnings": ["..."]`), but `check --json` emitted only the number of warnings and left out the texts.

`FileReport.warnings` now keeps the `Vec<String>` that `gridcraft_engine::io::open_bytes` returns, in order, so the JSON report emits an array of strings (an empty array when there are no warnings). This matches the documented schema, so no docs change is needed. Nothing else read the count.

Test: `json_lists_warning_messages` checks that a file with one warning gets `["..."]` and a file without warnings gets `[]`.

title: Cap queued pointer events from ui.click/ui.drag control requests (#525)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #525.

`ui.click` and `ui.drag` built their whole synthetic event queue from the request's `count` / `steps` with no upper bound, so one control request could allocate an arbitrarily large queue and still reply `ok: true` (AGENTS.md asks for caps on allocations sized by control parameters).

**Change** (`crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs`)
- New `MAX_QUEUED_POINTER_EVENTS = 10_000` budget. `push_click` and `push_drag` first check that the already-queued events plus the events the request would add fit in it; if not, they return an error and leave the queue unchanged (nothing is pushed or allocated).
- All four entry points that use these helpers (`ui.click`, `ui.drag`, `ui.cell.click`, `ui.cell.drag`) return that error the same way the other control commands report failures (`err(...)`).
- `count` / `steps` are clamped to `u32::MAX` before the cast, so a huge JSON value can no longer wrap to a small one.
- Accepted requests behave as before: same event order, positions, default count (1) and default drag steps (8); the cell geometry guards and the fixed 8-step cell drag are unchanged.

**Docs**: `docs/control-protocol.md` notes the limit on the pointer rows.

**Test**: `oversized_pointer_requests_are_refused_and_leave_the_queue_alone` checks that a double click still queues 5 events, that oversized clicks and drags (including one that only overflows because of events already queued) are refused with the queue left exactly as it was, and that a normal 3-step drag still queues in full afterwards.

* **Documentation**
  * Updated the control protocol reference to describe the event limit and when pointer requests are refused.
