title: Grid: deleting several Ctrl-selected rows removes them all (#758)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #758

## Root cause
`home.deleteRows` / `home.deleteColumns` resolved their target with `lines()`, which reads only `selection.current()` (the last area). With Ctrl-selected rows the header-menu Delete therefore removed just the last one.

## What changed

title: Grid: the selection outline stays visible when extended to the last row (#687)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #687

## Root cause
The selection outline was a single `rect_stroke` of the whole current area. Extended to the last row the rectangle is ~20 million points tall; at that size f32 precision is about 2 points, and the tessellated left/right sides vanish while the fill (plain rectangles) still shows.

## Changes
- `grid.rs`: the outline is now four filled bands (`outline_bands`) cut to the pane's clip rect (plus a small margin), so no geometry is far from the viewport. Same width (2) and position as the old `StrokeKind::Middle` stroke on `outline.expand(0.5)`. Non-finite rects draw nothing.
- ROADMAP.md progress log row.

## Tests
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui --lib outline_band` (2 tests: whole-column outline keeps left/right/top sides within the viewport; out-of-view and NaN rects draw nothing)
- `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-ui-egui --lib -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt -p gridcraft-ui-egui`

## Not done / unverified
- Not verified visually in a snapshot/screenshot (only the geometry unit test); the root-cause explanation (tessellator precision at ~20M points) is inferred, not traced through epaint.
- Corner pixels may differ by sub-pixel amounts from the old stroke.
- Possible conflicts: #549 replaces the same outline line in `paint_selection` with its own `outline_sides` (already pixel-snapped); if #549 lands, the huge-range clipping must be applied to its sides too. #763 (scroll into view) touches other lines but is complementary; it does not fix this.

title: Numfmt: scientific formats with a literal after E±, a % or a comma match Excel
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #768.

The scientific branch of `render_number` glued the exponent sign to the `E`, applied `%` and scaling commas as in a plain number section, and showed a zero mantissa through the usual `#`/`?` rules. The POI workbook shows Excel does otherwise: the sign goes right before the exponent digits (after any literal that follows the `E`), `?` pads exponent digits with spaces, `%` and commas never scale a scientific section (a comma between integer digits still groups thousands), and zero shows `0` in every integer placeholder (`####.####E+#` gives `0000.E+0`, so it's all of them, not just one). That last rule also changes zero under the built-in `##0.0E+0`, which now shows `000.0E+0` like the oracle's `####.####` rows; happy to narrow it if you'd rather not touch that one without a check in Excel.

The test copies the 248 `TEXT()` rows of `NumberFormatApproxTests.xlsx` as data (the workbook isn't committed), with a reference to the file. The last row's `3.14159` trips clippy's `approx_constant`, so the table carries a scoped `allow` with a one-line reason.

Validation:
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-numfmt --test poi_number_format_approx`: fails on main (210 of 248 cases differ, the same count `gridcraft-cli check` reports in the issue), passes here
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-numfmt --lib tests::`, `cargo test -p gridcraft-calc --lib tests::text_function`
- `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-numfmt --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

title: Security: cell hyperlinks open only http, https and mailto, after a confirmation (#777)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #777 (part 1: hyperlink schemes). Part 2 (`--control` server authentication) is not touched.

## Root cause
`follow_link` sent any target containing `://` or starting with `mailto:` to the host's `open_url` (`xdg-open`/`open`/`explorer`), so a workbook could make a click open `file:`, `smb:`, UNC paths or custom URL handlers, with no prompt.

## Changes
- New `gridcraft_engine::links::classify` is the single decision point: `http`, `https`, `mailto` (case-insensitive, whitespace trimmed) are external; references stay internal; everything else (other schemes, `\\host`, `//host`, `C:\`, control characters, empty `http:`) is refused.
- New command `link.open {url? | cell?}`: references go to `edit.goTo`; allowed addresses emit `UiRequest::OpenUrl` with no dialog; refused ones return an error. The control channel, CLI and MCP reach it like any command.
- UI: a click on a link classifies it. External addresses open an "Open Hyperlink" confirmation showing the full URL (OK runs `link.open`); refused ones show a message; references work as before.
- Defence in depth: the native `open_with_system` and the web `open_url` host hooks apply the same check.

title: Security: the --control server requires an auth token and closes bad connections (#777)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #777 (part 1, the hyperlink allowlist, is #780).

## Root cause
`--control <port>` / `GRIDCRAFT_CONTROL_PORT` ran every JSON line on `127.0.0.1:<port>` with no authentication and kept reading after an unparsable line. Any local process, or a web page POSTing `text/plain` to the port, could run any command (e.g. `app.save` to any path).

## Changes
- New `gridcraft_mcp::control_auth` (shared by the app and the client in `crates/mcp`, so no code is duplicated): constant-time compare (own small fn, no unsafe), hex, handshake check, token file path and writer.
- App (`apps/gridcraft/src/control_server.rs`): on start a 256-bit token from the OS RNG (`getrandom` 0.4, already in the lockfile, no new crate) is kept in memory and written to `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/gridcraft/control-<port>.token` (else `~/.cache/gridcraft/`; Windows `%USERPROFILE%\.gridcraft\`), folder 0700, file 0600 (an older file is removed first, `create_new`). The path is printed on stderr, the token never. A user-chosen token (`GRIDCRAFT_CONTROL_TOKEN` or `--control-token`, >= 16 chars) is used instead and no file is written.
- The first line of each connection must be `{"id":..,"method":"auth","params":{"token":".."}}`. Anything else (wrong/missing token, other method, non-JSON such as an HTTP request, no line within 10 s, line > 4 KiB) gets one generic `authentication required` reply and the connection is closed. After auth an unparsable line also closes the connection.
- Client: `Remote::connect` authenticates (env token, else the port's token file); `Remote::connect_with_token` added. `gridcraft-cli send` and `mcp --connect` need no change.
- Docs: `docs/control-protocol.md` (new Authentication section), `docs/mcp.md`, CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md "Drive it" line, ROADMAP row.
- **No opt-out**, deliberately.

## Breaking change
Any client other than `gridcraft-cli`/`gridcraft_mcp::Remote` (own scripts, the Python client in #444) must send the `auth` line first, with the token from the file or from `GRIDCRA…

title: Data: Forecast Sheet Forecast Start option (#785)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #785

## What changed
- `data.forecastSheet` takes optional `forecastStart` (number or date text on the timeline). When it is a history point before the last one, the FORECAST.ETS / CONFINT / STAT formulas use only the rows before it, the forecast columns join the actuals at the previous row and run over the overlap and on into the future (periods/end as before); the chart shows actual vs forecast.
- Start equal to the last point or one step after it = current behaviour. Blank/missing = current behaviour. Start not on the timeline, before the third point (fewer than 2 values to fit), beyond the next step, or non-numeric = error, nothing built. Result JSON gains `fitted`.
- Forecast Sheet dialog gets a "Forecast start" field (looked at a snapshot). Dialog labels in this dialog are not in the i18n catalogs (like its other fields), so no catalog change.
- Docs: gaps.md §13, ROADMAP progress row.

## Tests / commands
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-engine forecast` (hindcast formulas and values on a fixed seasonal series, invalid starts, blank start unchanged), `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, fmt.

## Not done
- No xtask ci locally (CI covers it); no Excel comparison.

## Unverified assumptions (need confirmation in Excel)
- Start is the first forecast point and the model is fit to points strictly before it (per Excel's public description: data prior to the start is used); the join cell at the previous row shows the actual.
- Start = last point is treated as the default (Excel's default start), i.e. fit to all history.
- Start after the history (beyond the next step) is an error rather than a gap.
- Minimum of two values before the start is my choice.

Fixes #806

## What was redundant
`text_function` called `NumberFormat::parse(code)` on every call, and the evaluator calls it once per element, so `=TEXT(A1:A100000,"0.00")` parsed the same code 100,000 times. `chart/src/resolve.rs` did the same per resolved value, and `Fmt::new` in `chart/src/axis.rs` per label helper call. A parsed format depends on the code text only (date system and value are applied when formatting), so one parse per distinct code is enough. No timings claimed.

## What changed
- `numfmt`: `NumberFormat::parse_cached(code)`, a per-thread cache (`thread_local`, no lock, no unsafe, no dependency, wasm-safe). At most 64 codes; a full cache is emptied. Codes over 256 bytes are never stored. If the cache is unavailable (thread shutdown, re-entrant borrow) it falls back to a plain parse; no unwrap/expect.
- `text_function`, `chart/resolve.rs` and `chart/axis.rs` use it. The calc evaluator gets it through `text_function`. `NumberFormat::parse` is unchanged.

## Tests (`crates/numfmt/src/tests.rs`)
- Equality: 45 codes (numbers, dates, fractions, text sections, conditions, scientific, fill, invalid codes) x 14 values x both date systems. `text_function` equals a copy of the old uncached implementation with the cache cold and warm, and `format_value` with `parse_cached` equals `format_value` with `parse`.
- Counter (cfg(test) parse counter): 10,000 values with one code parse once; two alternating codes parse twice; capacity overflow evicts (old code reparsed, newest still cached); a long code is parsed every time.

`cargo test -p gridcraft-numfmt`, `cargo test -p gridcraft-calc -p gridcraft-functions -p gridcraft-chart`, `cargo test -p gridcraft-engine --lib display`, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-numfmt -p gridcraft-chart --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt` on numfmt and chart, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo check -p gridcraft-numfmt --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`.

## Left out
- The engine's global `Mutex<HashMap>` cache in `displ…

title: Numfmt: no panic on a fraction denominator with 65,536 zeros; format codes are capped at 255 characters (#807)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #807

## Cause
`render_fraction` zero-padded the denominator with `format!("{den_s:0>zeros$}")`. Rust format widths are limited to u16, so a denominator with 65,536 or more `0` placeholders panics ("Formatting argument out of range"). Format codes had no length limit, so such a code could come from an XLSX `numFmt formatCode`, a format command or `TEXT`, and the grid, chart axes, print and export call `format_value` directly.

## Changes
- `render.rs`: the padding is built with `"0".repeat(zeros.saturating_sub(len))`; no `$` width remains.
- `lib.rs`: new `MAX_FORMAT_CODE_CHARS = 255` (Excel's limit, counted in characters). `NumberFormat::parse` has no error path, so a longer code degrades to General (the stored code string is kept, so files still open and round-trip); `text_function` returns `#VALUE!`. Other width/repeat/allocation sites in the crate were checked: exponent and date widths are already clamped (`min(20)`), the rest scale with the token count, which the cap now bounds.
- XLSX import is unchanged: the reader stores the code string without parsing it, so a long code never drops a cell or style or aborts the open.

## Tests
- `numfmt::tests::fraction_denominator_with_65536_zeros_does_not_panic`: drives the renderer with a test-only uncapped parser (the cap otherwise keeps the code out of reach). Verified to fail on the old code with "Formatting argument out of range" at render.rs:499, and to pass with the fix.
- `numfmt::tests::format_codes_are_capped_at_255_characters`: 255 ok, 256 invalid, 255 two-byte characters ok / 256 invalid (characters, not bytes), the 65,536-zero code through `format_value` (General) and `text_function` (`#VALUE!`).
- `xlsx::tests::malformed::an_overlong_number_format_code_does_not_stop_the_open`.

## Commands run
`cargo test -p gridcraft-numfmt -p gridcraft-xlsx`, `cargo test -p gridcraft-calc -p gridcraft-chart`, `cargo test -p gridcraft-engine --lib display`, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-numfmt -p gridcraft-xlsx --all-tar…

title: Numfmt: format-code parsing is linear, and an unclosed [ is treated the same in both passes (#810)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #810

## Cause
- `tokenize` ran `position(']')` for every `[`; with no `]` that is O(n²) for n brackets.
- `analyze` searched ahead for the next non-comma token at every comma (O(k²) for k commas) and scanned all tokens for an exponent at every `/` (O(n²)).
- `split_sections` stayed "inside a bracket" after an unclosed `[`, so later `;` no longer separated sections, while `tokenize` read that `[` as a literal. `0;[Red-0` with -5 gave `[R19005-0`; `[0;0` with 5 gave `[0;5`.

## Changes (`crates/numfmt/src/parse.rs`, `crates/engine/src/display.rs`)
- Both passes compute the position of the last `]` once; a `[` at or after it is a literal at once, otherwise the bracket is consumed up to the next `]`, so every character is visited a bounded number of times.
- `split_sections` now jumps over a closed bracket verbatim (as `tokenize` reads it) instead of tracking a `bracket` flag. Decision: an unclosed `[` is a literal in both passes, because the crate has no rejection of unclosed brackets anywhere else and `tokenize` already treated it that way. One side effect: a `"` inside a closed bracket no longer toggles quoting in the splitter (the tokenizer never treated it as a quote there).
- Next-non-comma digit flags and the last exponent position are precomputed once in `analyze`; the `has_exp` at a bar is `seen_exp || last_exp > i`, which equals the old "any exponent token in the vector" at that point.
- `display::parsed` parses outside the cache lock (small, no cache redesign).
- Does not depend on, and adds no, length cap (#809 adds one separately).

## Tests (`crates/numfmt/src/tests.rs`)
- `hostile_codes_parse_in_linear_time`: 1,000,000-character codes of `[`, `0,,,`, `0///`, `0,,,0`, `[;[;` parse and render on a worker thread with a 20 s watchdog. Not a benchmark: it proves the parse does not blow up quadratically at a size where O(n²) takes minutes. Verified to FAIL on the old parser (timed out at the first case, `[` x 1,000,000); the comma and bar cases were not …

title: PDF: title and author are written as UTF-16BE when they are not ASCII (#813)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #813

## Cause
`pdf_text_string` was an alias of `pdf_string`, so the Info dictionary (/Title, /Author, /Creator, /Producer) was written as a WinAnsi literal. PDF text strings must be PDFDocEncoding or UTF-16BE with a BOM. Bytes 0x80-0x9F differ between WinAnsi and PDFDocEncoding, and everything outside WinAnsi became `?`. With Poppler `pdfinfo`, `Übersicht €5 – “Q1” 日本` showed as `Übersicht •5 Œ ﬁQ1ﬂ ??` (observed before the fix).

## What changed
- `pdf_text_string` is a real function: printable ASCII (0x20-0x7E) stays a literal `( … )` with `(`, `)` and `\` escaped; anything else is written as a UTF-16BE hex string `<FEFF…>` (surrogate pairs for characters outside the BMP).
- Info strings are cut at 1024 characters (on a character boundary) so a hostile title cannot bloat the file.
- `pdf_string` (page content text, WinAnsi) is untouched.
- ROADMAP.md progress-log row.

## Tests
- `info_strings_with_non_ascii_are_utf16be`: title `Übersicht €5 – “Q1” 日本 😀` and a Latin-1 author, parsed back from the file bytes.
- `ascii_info_strings_stay_literal_and_escaped`.
- `info_strings_are_capped`.
- With the fix replaced by `pdf_string(text)`, the first and third tests fail (checked, then restored).

## Commands that ran
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-pdf` (9 passed), `cargo test -p gridcraft-engine --lib print` (16 passed)
- `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-pdf --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt -p gridcraft-pdf -- --check`
- `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo check -p gridcraft-pdf --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`
- By hand once: a file with the title above opened in `pdfinfo` shows the title and author `Müller & Søn` correctly.

## Not done
- /CreationDate (needs a clock; skipped on purpose).
- Other review findings in crates/pdf (width overflow, dash, stroke, NaN guards) are separate work; non-Latin page text is #446.
- No full `cargo xtask ci` run (CI on this PR covers it).

Viewers other than Poppler `pdfinfo` (Acrobat, Preview, browsers) were not checked. U…

title: PDF: text width cannot overflow; dash, stroke width and NaN sizes are sanitised (#812)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #812

## Cause and change (crates/pdf/src/lib.rs)
- **B2 text width:** `text_width` summed glyph widths in a `u32`; about 8,000,000 characters of Helvetica `a` overflow it (panic in a debug build, silent wrap in release). Now a `u64` sum; result type and values for normal input unchanged. No other width or size sum in the crate accumulates input-sized counts.
- **B3 dash:** an all-zero dash array was written as `[0 0] 0 d`, which the PDF specification forbids (`n()` also rounds values below 0.0005 to 0). `dash_values` now returns an empty array (`[] 0 d`, solid) when an entry is non-finite or no entry survives rounding to a positive number.
- **B4 stroke width:** negative or NaN widths were written as is (`-3 w`). One helper `stroke_width` clamps to >= 0 (NaN and infinity become 0); used by `rect_stroke`, `stroke_line_dashed`, `polyline`, `polygon`, `circle`.
- **B5 NaN guards:** `w <= 0.0` lets NaN through (`image_rgba(w = NaN)` stored an image and wrote a singular `cm`). Helpers `extent` (positive and finite) and `finite` now guard `fill_rect`, `rect_stroke`, `stroke_line*`, `polyline`, `polygon`, `circle`, `text_rotated` and `image_rgba`; a call with a non-finite coordinate or size draws nothing, and `image_rgba` returns before storing the image. `clip_rect` is unchanged (non-finite values already give an empty clip). The `n()` clamp at +-1e7 is untouched.

Valid input produces byte-identical output; existing tests pass unchanged.

## Tests (crates/pdf/src/tests.rs)
`text_width_does_not_overflow`, `all_zero_dash_is_drawn_solid`, `negative_and_nan_stroke_widths_become_zero`, `non_finite_image_size_stores_nothing`, and `every_draw_method_survives_hostile_numbers` (every public draw method with NaN/inf/negative/huge values, output has no NaN/inf and the xref still parses). With the fix reverted, the first four fail (the overflow test with "attempt to add with overflow"); the hostile-input test passes without the fix too (it is a guard against regressions).

title: PDF: writer cleanup, q nesting limit, image dedupe, style only on change (#816)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #816

Phase 2 of the `crates/pdf` review: writer cleanup and graphics-state limits. One PR rather than two because the pieces share code (O3 and B7 both go through `Page::set_stroke`, O3 and B6 share the save stack).

## What changed, finding by finding

**Behaviour changes in the output**
- **O3 style only on change.** `Page` tracks fill, stroke colour, width, dash and join; a style operator is written only when it differs from the state in effect. The tracked state is pushed/popped with `q`/`Q` and starts empty on every page, so it always matches what a PDF reader has.
- **O4 image dedupe.** Identical pictures (width, height, RGB, alpha) are one image object (plus one soft mask), also across pages and when drawn twice on one page. Candidates are found by a `DefaultHasher` hash; a hash match is only trusted after the pixels are compared. No new dependency.
- **B6 `q` limit.** `save()` refuses the 29th nested level; the `restore()` calls that match refused saves are ignored (a counter, so the accepted levels are not popped early). Only accepted saves count; `finish()` closes what is still open.
- **B7 join leak.** Polylines and polygon strokes use round joins, rect strokes, lines and circles use miter, set explicitly and tracked like the rest. Before, one polyline switched every later stroke on the page to round joins. Nothing in the writer sets the cap style, so the cap needed nothing.
- **S3.** `/ProcSet` removed from the page resources.

**Internal, same rendering (tests pass with or without the change, so they do not prove it)**
- **O1.** `finish()` no longer stages `Vec<(u32, Vec<u8>)>` and sorts it: objects go straight into `out` (reserved for the page contents plus 1 KiB per page; images grow it by doubling), with one xref offset per id. Page content is moved out of the pages first and freed after its stream is written. Only a copy is gone: content is no longer copied twice. Not measured; I make no claim about speed or peak memory.
- **O6.** `image_rgba…

title: Numfmt: one built-in format table, fewer allocations rendering numbers and General (#817)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #817

Findings S1, S3, O3 and O4 of the `crates/numfmt` review. No behaviour change; one PR because the S3 dead arm and the `literal_text` calls sit in the lines O3 rewrites.

## What changed, finding by finding

**S1, one table of built-in formats.** The two tables were identical (checked by diffing the entries). `cargo xtask layers` forbids `gridcraft-xlsx -> gridcraft-numfmt` (FormatDep; only a dev-dependency is allowed), so the table stays in `crates/xlsx/src/tables.rs` and numfmt's copy (`builtin.rs`, `builtin_format`, `builtin_id`; used by nothing but numfmt's own tests) is removed. Nothing else in `crates/`, `apps/`, `docs/`, `xtask/` referenced them (`git grep` outside xlsx). xlsx's lookup rules are untouched and now pinned by `tables::tests::builtin_format_ids` (36 ids, 23-36 and 50 absent, `builtin_id` exact-case, ids 5-8 not written as built-ins). In numfmt's tests the three uses of the table became literal codes, and `builtins` (which tested the removed case-insensitive lookup) became `builtin_codes_render`, which keeps the three rendering assertions.

**S3, dead arm and `literal_text`.** The `Tok::At | General | Date | Comma => {}` arm in `render_number` printed nothing, which the fallback (the token's piece, empty) does too, because no code ever gives these tokens a piece. So it is removed whether or not the tokens can occur; the comment says that `At` can occur (`0@`) and `Comma`/`General`/`Date` cannot after `analyze`. New `Tok::push_literal(&mut String)`; `literal_text` calls it. `render_text`, `render_general`, `render_date` and `render_number` append through it and allocate nothing per token.

**O3, allocations per number.**
- `render_number`: `pieces`, `before` and `lits` (a `String` per token) are now one `Parts` value: one text buffer and one `Vec` of byte ranges (+ the "this literal becomes k spaces" marker for fractions). `fill_int` writes digits left to right (digit, then the separator after it) instead of building the reversed string …

title: XLS: a formula kept as its saved value keeps a text result
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #802.

A FORMULA record with a text result stores the cell with an empty value until the STRING record that follows brings the text. When the cell has the default XF, `Cells::set` drops it as blank; an attached formula gets it back in `attach`, but a formula kept as its saved value (external link, missing name, data table) doesn't, so the STRING handler found no cell and lost the text. As you suggested, `pending_string` now carries the cell's style too, and the STRING handler creates the cell when it's missing.

Validation:
- `xls_tests::text_result_of_a_formula_kept_as_its_value` (a `{=TABLE(...)}` cell with the default XF, string result, then its STRING record): fails on main (`A1` is `Empty` instead of `"103a"`), passes here
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-xlsx --lib xls_tests`, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-xlsx --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: XLSX: keep fileVersion and calcFeatures in workbook.xml on save
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #799.

The writer always rebuilt workbook.xml from scratch, so `<fileVersion>` and the `xcalcf:calcFeatures` extension were lost on save, and without both Excel ignores the cached values and recalculates on open. They're now read into the workbook's kept content (same mechanism as `<externalReferences>`) and written back in schema order: `fileVersion` as the first child of `<workbook>`, the calcFeatures `ext` inside `<extLst>` as the last, with `xmlns:xcalcf` declared on the `ext`. Only the calcFeatures ext is carried over, not the rest of the source `extLst`: other workbook extensions can point at slicer caches or timelines that GridCraft rewrites, so I kept this to what the issue needs. A workbook created in GridCraft (no source file) gets neither, as before; happy to switch if you'd rather write a default `fileVersion` there too.

Validation:
- `file_version_and_calc_features_survive_a_save` (`crates/xlsx/src/tests/passthrough_tests.rs`): fails on main (first child of the saved `<workbook>` is `workbookPr`, no `fileVersion`/`extLst`), passes here. It round-trips twice and checks order, the exact `fileVersion` attributes and the calcFeatures `ext`, and that a new workbook gets neither. Checked that it fails with extLst written before calcPr, without the `xmlns:xcalcf` declaration, with fileVersion not kept on read, and with a default fileVersion written for new workbooks.
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-xlsx --lib tests::`, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-xlsx -p gridcraft-model --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: XLSX: keep the workbook's default font on save
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #805.

The reader always mapped cell format 0 to the model's built-in default style (Calibri 11), so the file's own Normal font never reached the model and the writer emitted Calibri 11 as `fonts[0]`. The Normal style now takes its font from cell format 0 (`StyleTable::with_default`), so empty cells, typed text and the saved `fonts[0]` keep the file's size and face. The writer also puts back `<scheme val="minor"/>` on the Normal font when its face is the theme's body font, which is how Excel writes it; the model has no per-font scheme, so this is inferred from the name rather than carried through. Happy to switch to a real `scheme` field on `Font` if you prefer that. `family` is still always written as 2 (Swiss), unchanged here.

Validation:
- `tests::roundtrip::default_font_survives_a_round_trip`: fails on main (`fonts[0]` comes back as Calibri 11 instead of Arial 10), passes here; dropping the `with_default` call or the scheme condition each turns it red again
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-xlsx --lib -- tests::roundtrip tests::fixtures tests::smooth_roundtrip styles`, `cargo test -p gridcraft-engine --test command_sequence_fuzz`
- `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-model -p gridcraft-xlsx --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: XLSX: Save As into another folder keeps links on the same workbook
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #801.

The path of a linked workbook (`externalLinkPath` target) was kept as text. Excel stores it relative to the file that uses it, so after Save As into another folder it pointed next to the new copy. Following your suggested fix, `file.open` now records the folder the workbook was read from (`Workbook::source_dir`, not in JSON). When the file is saved into a different folder (`file.save`/`file.saveAs`, and `gridcraft-cli convert`), each relative target is resolved against that folder and written relative to the new one. If no relative path exists (another drive), it's written absolute as `file:///C:\…`. Saving back into the original folder writes the target unchanged. Absolute targets, URLs and paths that climb above the root aren't touched, and neither is the `xxl21:absoluteUrl` in the part. `file.saveBytes` doesn't rebase, because it has no destination folder.

Folder names that come from the file system are percent-encoded where a URI path needs it (`q2 data` becomes `q2%20data`), and non-ASCII characters are written as they are. The target's own segments keep their spelling. Happy to switch if Excel writes those differently.

Only `externalLinkPath` relationships are rebased. Relative file hyperlinks can go through the same `rebase_links` once #800 writes them as relationships. Possible overlap with #804: this adds a `source_dir` field to `Workbook`, not to `ExternalBook`. Happy to move it if #804 lands first.

Validation:
- `save_as_into_another_folder_keeps_linked_workbooks_on_the_same_file` (engine): your test. Read from `a/`, saved to `a/b/`, it writes `../Source.xlsx`. Saved back into `a/` it writes `Source.xlsx`, and read from `a/b/` then saved to `a/` it writes `b/Source.xlsx`. On main it fails with `left: "Source.xlsx", right: "../Source.xlsx"`; it passes here.
- `saving_into_another_folder_rebases_relative_links_to_workbooks` (xlsx): sibling and parent folders, `\` separators, `.`/`..`, encoded and non-ASCII names, absolute/URL/drive targets l…

title: XLS: formulas that use a skipped defined name keep their saved results
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #803.

Cell formulas were decoded before `defined_names` decided which names to keep, so a `PtgName` pointing at a name that was later skipped (e.g. one into another workbook) stayed a live formula and recalculated to `#NAME?`. The globals pass now runs the same check `defined_names` does (non-empty formula that doesn't decode) once all the link tables are read, and a cell or shared formula that uses one of those names is refused like an external reference: the cell keeps its saved result and the usual "their saved results were kept as values" warning names the reason. Names are not affected: a name that uses a skipped name (`Twice = ExtRange*2`) is still imported as before; happy to drop those too if you'd rather. Reading the name itself from SUPBOOK/CRN, the fuller fix you mention, is left for later.

Validation:
- `xls_tests::formulas_using_a_skipped_name_keep_their_saved_results` (records built in the test: external SUPBOOK, `ExtRange`, `B6 = SUM(ExtRange)` cached 60): fails on main (`B6` keeps the formula `SUM(ExtRange)`), passes here; `B7 = Local*2` still reads as a formula
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-xlsx --lib xls`, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-xlsx --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: XLSX: a hyperlink to another file is saved as an external relationship
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #800.

`Hyperlink` only kept the target text, so the writer had to guess from it, and anything without a scheme or a UNC prefix became a `location`. As you suggested, `Hyperlink` now has an `external` flag. On read it is set when the link comes from an `r:id` relationship. `insert.link` sets it the way Excel's Insert Hyperlink dialog splits its pages: `#…`, a defined name, a table name or a sheet reference (`Sheet2!A1`, `'Q#1'!B2`, or a plain `B5`) is "Place in This Document", and anything else (`Source.xlsx`, `C:\Temp\Book.xlsx`, `..\Reports\Q1.xlsx`, URLs) is "Existing File or Web Page". The writer saves external links as `TargetMode="External"` relationships, with only the part after `#` in `location`. Since sheet names can't contain `: \ / ? * [ ]`, `https://…!A1` is never taken for a sheet reference. `Book.xlsx#Sheet1!A2` counts as a file plus a place unless a sheet really has that name. Links made before the flag existed still go through the old scheme test. The flag is `serde(default)`, so older `.json` saves still load.

Path targets are written as given, e.g. `Target="C:\Temp\Book.xlsx"`, without turning them into `file:///` URIs. I'm happy to switch if you'd rather match what Excel writes for absolute paths.

Validation:
- `fixtures::hyperlink_to_another_file_stays_external` (your POI C16 case, plus file + place, a relative path, an internal location and a URL, read then written): fails on main (C16 isn't flagged external and is written as `location="WithVariousData.xlsx"`), passes here
- `tests::links_to_files_are_saved_as_external_relationships` (the three `insert.link` targets from the issue, plus file#place, a URL, a sheet reference, `#…`, a defined name, a table and a sheet called `Q#1`): fails on main (`Source.xlsx` has no relationship), passes here
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-xlsx --lib -- tests::fixtures tests::roundtrip tests::malformed`, `cargo test -p gridcraft-engine --lib link`, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-model -p gridcraft-xlsx -p gridcr…

title: Linked workbooks: references typed by file name or path go through a link, shown with the file
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #804.

**Built on #464** (it needs its `ExternalBook` and the reading of the link parts), so until #464 is merged this branch shows its three commits too; the last three commits are this PR. It sits next to #824 (#801): that one adds `Workbook::source_dir` and rebases kept link targets on Save As, and this one adds `ExternalBook::path`. They touch `passthrough.rs` and its tests in different places, and I'll rebase whichever lands second.

The model and the file keep only `[n]`, the position of the link. What changes is the way in and the way out. When a formula or a name is entered, a reference to another workbook typed by file name or path (`[Source.xlsx]Sheet1!A1`, `'C:\links\[Source.xlsx]Sheet1'!A1`, `Source.xlsx!Rate`, `'C:\links\Source.xlsx'!Rate`) is rewritten as `[n]Sheet1!A1` / `[n]!Rate`. The link is matched by path, or by file name when no folder is given. Otherwise a new link is added with the typed path. A new link has no values yet, so its sheets are marked `refreshError`, and the reference is `#REF!` as in Excel when the file is missing. `ExternalBook` now keeps the link's path, read from the `externalLinkPath` relationship (`file:///C:\links\Source.xlsx` → `C:\links\Source.xlsx`, a relative target stays relative). The formula bar, Show Formulas, the Name Manager and `document.inspect` print `[n]` back as the file (`'C:\links\[Source.xlsx]Sheet1'!A1`), and that text goes back in unchanged when you press Enter. On save, the links read from the file are still passed through as they were. Each new link gets its own `externalLink` part and rels after them, so `[1]` stays `[1]`. `<f>` only ever holds `[n]`.

In the formula language: the unquoted `[Source.xlsx]Sheet1!A1` now lexes (it was refused with `unexpected Sheet("Sheet1", None)`), and a drive's `C:` inside a quoted path is no longer read as the colon of a 3-D range. That colon is what produced the `'C:\…\[links[Source.xlsx]Sheet1]…'` text Excel showed. `[Source.xlsx]Sheet1` prints unquoted when …

title: View ribbon: lay out the Show group's checkboxes in two columns
author: bmh129
body:
The View tab's Show group stacked Ruler, Formula Bar, Gridlines and Headings in one column. The ribbon body fits only three rows, so **Headings was cut off at the bottom and couldn't be reached**. title: Linux: draw GNOME-style window buttons in the title bar on Wayland
author: bmh129
body:
On GNOME (Wayland), the compositor draws no window frames: it offers no `zxdg_decoration_manager_v1`. So winit drew its own fallback frame above GridCraft's title bar, and that frame ignores GNOME's theme, dark mode and button layout. GridCraft now asks the compositor at launch (`apps/gridcraft/src/decorations.rs`). Where the compositor draws no frames, GridCraft turns winit's frame off and uses its own title bar as the header bar, as GNOME's own apps do (`crates/ui-egui/src/window_controls.rs`), the same approach PdfCraft takes:

- Minimize, maximize/restore and close are drawn in Adwaita's style: round buttons with symbolic glyphs **drawn in code (no new assets)**. Their order and side follow `org.gnome.desktop.wm.preferences button-layout`, read through the XDG Desktop Portal. They're hidden in full screen.
- Resize zones run along the window's edges, with L-shaped corners, above the rest of the UI. A hairline outlines the window while it isn't maximized.
- **File > Options > Use system title bar** (shown only where the app draws the buttons) switches back to winit's frame immediately, without a restart. It's the UI command `view.systemTitleBar`, saved in `ui.json` as `systemTitleBar` and documented in `docs/control-protocol.md`.
- `GRIDCRAFT_TITLEBAR=app|system` overrides the detection.
- `main`'s newer option to hide the title bar (`chrome.title_bar`) is respected, except where GridCraft draws the window frame. There the title bar stays, because it carries the only close, minimize and maximize buttons and the area for dragging the window.

KDE, Sway, Hyprland, COSMIC and X11 keep the frame their desktop draws. macOS and Windows are unchanged.

**Not done:** right-clicking the title bar doesn't open GNOME's window menu, and the window has no shadow or rounded corners. The new labels are translated into all nineteen interface languages, including the eight (Greek, Italian, Dutch, Polish, Romanian, Turkish, Ukrainian, Vietnamese) added to `main` after this PR was …

title: fix(security): restrict cell hyperlink schemes and require a control-channel token
author: mendy-cohen
body:
Fixes #777.

### 1) Cell hyperlinks
`follow_link` used to hand any target containing `://` to `open` / `explorer` / `xdg-open`. Now only `http`, `https` and `mailto` links open. Any other scheme (`file:`, `smb:`, `ms-settings:`, `x-apple.systempreferences:`, ...) shows a warning notice and nothing opens. Workbook references like `Sheet2!A1` still go to the cell.

### 2) Control channel auth
- New `gridcraft_mcp::auth` module. The token is `GRIDCRAFT_CONTROL_TOKEN` if set, otherwise 32 random bytes from the OS. The app writes it to `gridcraft-control-<port>.token` in `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` or the per-user temp folder. The file is created fresh each start (never through an existing symlink) and is mode 0600 on Unix.
- The first request on a connection must be `auth` with the right token, compared in constant time. Anything else gets an error and the connection is closed, including a non-JSON first line like an HTTP request from a browser. A repeated `auth` after that is answered without reaching the UI.
- `Remote` (used by `gridcraft-cli send` and `mcp --connect`) sends the token on every connection. It looks the token up again on reconnect, so a restarted app still works.
- `docs/control-protocol.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` describe the handshake.

### Testing
- New unit tests: link schemes, token generation and matching, token file permissions, and a real-socket test showing requests reach the UI only after `auth`.
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-mcp -p gridcraft`, the new `gridcraft-ui-egui` test, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` on the touched crates, `cargo fmt` and `cargo xtask layers` all pass.
- Manual run on macOS with `gridcraft --control 7979`. A request with no token is refused, an HTTP-style request is refused, the token file is `-rw-------`, and `gridcraft-cli send 7979 ...` works.
- I didn't run `cargo xtask wasm`. `gridcraft-web` doesn't depend on `gridcraft-mcp`, and the `ui-egui` change only uses `log` and the existing `Notice`.

title: Grid: Shift+arrows in point mode extend from the pointed cell, also up and left
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #835.

`point_move` took the anchor of a Shift+arrow extension from the first cell of the reference already written in the formula. That text is normalized (top-left first), so once the range had grown up or left, its first cell was the moving end, not the anchor: from A10, Shift+Up gave A9:A10, then A8:A9, A7:A8, a two-row window sliding up instead of a growing range. The anchor is now the corner of the pointed range opposite the cell point mode is on (`point_cell`), so up/left extend like down/right already did, and Shift+Down after Shift+Up shrinks back towards the anchor as in Excel.

Validation:
- `interaction::shift_arrows_in_point_mode_extend_from_the_pointed_cell` (kittest: `=SUM(` in A11, Up, Shift+Up ×3, Shift+Down): fails on main (`=SUM(A8:A9`, expected `=SUM(A8:A10`), passes here
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui --test interaction`, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Rich text runs: per-run font colors and fonts — import, render, round-trip (#774)
author: edurbs
body:
Closes #774 (extracted from #708 item 1). Follow-up: #776 (run editing UI). Related: #833 (pre-existing row-height auto-fit gap found during verification).

## What

XLSX rich text runs — per-run font properties inside one cell's text — now survive import, render with their own fonts/colors, and are written back unchanged. Editing a cell replaces its runs with the cell-level format (milestone-1 scope; the editing UI is #776).

- **Model**: `Run`/`RunFont` (delta: only what the file set) + `Sheet.cell_runs: BTreeMap<CellRef, CellRuns>` side-table (comments pattern). `Value::Text` untouched — formulas, calc, clipboard and CSV are unchanged.
- **Import**: `<si><r><rPr>` parsed (`Si::parse`); all three color encodings (`rgb`, `theme`, `indexed`); `rFont`/`sz`/`b`/`i`/`u`/`strike`/`vertAlign` deltas; caps of 8 192 runs per cell and 2²⁰ per workbook, charged both at parse and at attachment — hostile files flatten, never fail.
- **Export**: rich `<si>` emission reusing `color_attrs`; SST dedup keyed by (text, runs); formula cached results stay plain.
- **Render**: multi-segment `LayoutJob` per run, merged over the cell font; runs win over number-format section colors; invalid or mismatched runs fall back flat everywhere (validity guard).
- **Engine**: edits clear runs (undo restores); insert/delete rows and columns, sort, remove-duplicates, cut-move and moveColumns translate entries alongside `cell_pictures`; copy/fill stay flat.

title: Fix Intel Mac crash: probe Metal shader language version support
author: mjohnson7cd
body:
## Summary

Fixes crashes on Intel Macs where all ArtCraft apps fail to launch with `Metal: error: invalid value 'metal3.2' in '-std=metal3.2'`.

The wgpu Metal backend was choosing MSL version purely from OS version, but legacy Intel GPUs have older Metal compilers that reject newer MSL versions.

## Solution

Vendors wgpu-hal 30.0.1 with the patch from gfx-rs/wgpu#10592:
- Probes the Metal compiler at adapter creation by compiling a test kernel
- Steps down from OS-selected version until compiler accepts it
- Modern Macs: tries Metal 3.2 → succeeds immediately
- Legacy Intel Macs: tries 3.2 → 3.1 → ... → 2.4/2.3 until one works

## Issues Fixed

Fixes storytold/photocraft#1859
Fixes storytold/artcraft#2126  
Fixes storytold/artcraft#2190

## Testing

- ✅ Compiles on macOS
- ✅ Passes clippy
- ⚠️ Untested on real Intel Mac hardware (awaiting community testing)

## Notes

The vendored wgpu-hal will be removed once upstream releases the fix and ArtCraft can bump to that version.

---
— sent on behalf of @mjohnson7cd by Claude Code

title: Closing the window asks to save unsaved workbooks
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #838, fixes #841, fixes #1268.

The Save Changes prompt only existed for File › Close: the window's close button (or Alt+F4, or the OS quitting the app) went straight through, so unsaved work was lost. `SheetApp::logic` now holds a close request back with `CancelClose` while any workbook is dirty and asks about each one in turn with the existing prompt (Save / Don't Save / Cancel). Once every workbook is answered the window closes; Cancel keeps everything open. A cell still being typed is committed first, as File › Close already does. `app.quit` on the control channel still quits without asking, since programmatic calls never open dialogs; happy to switch if you'd rather it went through the prompt too.

Validation:
- `file_menu::closing_the_window_asks_about_every_unsaved_workbook` and `closing_the_window_can_save_first_and_a_saved_workbook_closes_at_once`: fail on main (no `CancelClose`, the window just closes), pass here

title: Open workbooks encrypted with Excel's default password; read RC4 .xls
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Excel encrypts some workbooks (for example ones saved as read-only) with its built-in password `VelvetSweatshop` and tries that password before asking. GridCraft never tried it. A `.xlsx` like that asked for a password the user never set, and an encrypted `.xls` was refused outright.

What changed:

- Opening an encrypted workbook with no password now tries `VelvetSweatshop` first. If it works, the workbook opens without the "This workbook was password-protected" notice, since the user set no password. If it fails, you get the same password prompt (or programmatic error) as before. As before, the opened workbook has no save path, so Save never overwrites the encrypted original.
- `.xls` files with a FilePass record are now decrypted with RC4 (MS-OFFCRYPTO 2.3.6): MD5 key derivation with a new key every 1024 bytes of the Workbook stream. Record headers, BOF/FilePass and the other records the spec lists stay unencrypted, and so do the first 4 bytes of BoundSheet8 (the stream position). This also makes the existing password prompt work for `.xls` files with a real password. RC4 CryptoAPI and XOR-obfuscated `.xls` files get an "uses ... encryption, which GridCraft can't open yet" message instead of a password prompt.
- New dependency: `md-5` 0.11 (RustCrypto, on the same `digest` version that `sha1`/`sha2` already use). RC4 itself is about 20 lines in `xls/crypt.rs`.

Tests:

- Engine: `.xlsx` workbooks encrypted with the default password (Agile and Standard, built in code with the existing test encryptor) open through `file.open` with no password and without the notice. A small encrypted `.xls` built in code opens with the default password, and with a user password it asks, rejects a wrong one, then opens.
- xlsx crate: the full `.xls` sample, encrypted, reads the same as the plain one. A 500-row sheet covers records that cross 1024-byte block boundaries. A wrong password gives `WrongPassword`, and the XOR, CryptoAPI and truncated FilePass cases are covered.

title: UI: AutoComplete for cell values can be turned off, Backspace and Escape drop the proposal
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #842.

Column AutoComplete was already there (`editor::column_completion`: unique case-insensitive prefix match in the contiguous block above/below, no formulas or numbers, Enter/Tab accept with the entry's own case), but three parts of the request were missing. There was no way to turn it off, so this adds "Enable AutoComplete for cell values" under a new Editing section in File ▸ Options, saved in `ui.json`, on by default as in Excel, and reachable as the UI command `options.autoComplete {on?}` for agents. Backspace deleted the last typed character while the proposal stayed up; now, like Excel, it removes only the proposed rest. Escape cancelled the whole edit; now the first Escape drops the proposal and keeps what you typed, and a second one cancels, the same way the function list in the same editor already behaves. That Escape step is the one place I went with the issue rather than Excel (Excel cancels straight away), happy to switch.

Validation:
- `column_autocomplete_backspace_and_escape_drop_only_the_proposal`: fails on main (Backspace leaves `("b", Some("Banana"))`), passes here
- `column_autocomplete_can_be_turned_off`: fails on main (with the option off, "No" still proposes `Some("North")`), passes here
- `column_autocomplete_skips_ambiguous_prefixes_and_numbers`: pins Apricot/Apple ambiguity and numbers
- Case folding is Unicode-aware: "Ébano" and "ébano" count as one entry, and the proposed rest is cut on characters rather than bytes (typing "straß" shows "ENBAHN" after "STRAẞENBAHN"'s prefix); pinned by `column_autocomplete_folds_case_beyond_ascii`, which fails before 9c3db37
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui --test interaction column_autocomplete`, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Grid: horizontal scrollbar in the sheet tab bar
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #840.

The tab bar only had a slim position indicator squeezed into the ~90px left after the tabs: a grey thumb with no track, no click-to-page, hardcoded colours, and a range that counted frozen columns as scrollable. This turns it into a real horizontal scrollbar built the same way as the grid's vertical one (`horizontal_scrollbar` next to `vertical_scrollbar`): same theme tokens and 14px track, used range + 10 columns as the extent (kept stable while dragging), click on the track pages by one screen of the scrolling part, wheel over it scrolls sideways, and frozen columns stay out of the page. On a right-to-left sheet the thumb starts at the right end. The tab bar now splits 60/40 between tabs and scrollbar, like Excel's default; the draggable divider between them is left for a follow-up. Happy to switch the split if you prefer a different share.

Validation:
- `interaction::horizontal_scrollbar_pages_and_drags_across_a_wide_sheet` (data to column Z, column A frozen): fails on main (track is 92px wide; with that check off, clicking the track scrolls 0 instead of one page), passes here
- cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui --test interaction --test sheet_tab_rename --test right_to_left --test scroll_position
- cargo clippy -p gridcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo fmt --all -- --check
- checked the offscreen snapshot in light and dark

title: UI: Enter pastes the copied range and ends copy mode
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #845.

The grid's Enter handler always committed and moved down, even while a copied range was marked. Now, when the session clipboard holds a copy or cut, a plain Enter runs `edit.paste` into the selection and clears the clipboard, so the marching ants go away and the selection stays on the pasted range, like Excel. A cut still moves as before (paste already clears it). Only plain Enter does this; Shift/Alt/Ctrl/Cmd+Enter keep their current behaviour, happy to switch if Shift+Enter should paste too.

Validation:
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui --test clipboard enter_pastes_the_copied_cells_and_ends_copy_mode`: fails on main (D5 stays empty, Enter just moves down), passes here
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui --test clipboard --test interaction`, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Sheet tabs: All Sheets navigator with a filter field
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #839.

With many sheets the only way to reach one was scrolling the tab strip. This adds an "All sheets" button next to the previous/next arrows that opens a list of every visible sheet, with a filter field that has focus as soon as it opens: type part of a name, arrows to move, Enter or click to activate. It reuses the ribbon's existing filterable dropdown (`editable_combo`, now `pub(crate)`), so long lists scroll and keyboard behaviour matches the font/size boxes; the active sheet is the highlighted row when it opens. Hidden and very hidden sheets are left out, same as the tab strip, so Unhide stays the way to reach them. Picking a sheet goes through the same path as clicking its tab (factored into `activate_sheet`), so the in-progress edit is committed, or kept in point mode. The icon is a new code-drawn `SheetList` glyph; happy to switch to an existing icon or move the button if you'd rather have it elsewhere.

- `tabs::tests::navigator_lists_visible_sheets_by_workbook_index`: doesn't compile on main (no navigator), passes here; dropping the visibility filter makes it fail with the hidden sheets listed

title: CSV export: refuse a file over 512 MiB instead of expanding the whole used range (#528)
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #528

## Cause

`write_csv` (`crates/xlsx/src/csv.rs`) walks every position of the sheet's used range and appends to one growing `String`, with no cell, byte or reservation limit. The used range is a bounding rectangle, so two cells far apart make the file as big as the whole rectangle between them: `A1` and `XFD1048576` are 17,180,917,762 bytes (16 GiB) of commas. `file.saveBytes`, `file.exportCsv` and Save As CSV/TSV all call it before writing a file. `AGENTS.md` requires input-derived allocations for huge ranges to be capped.

## Fix

The output is capped at `MAX_CSV_BYTES` (512 MiB), and `write_csv` returns `Result<Vec<u8>, IoError>`:

- Before anything is allocated, a lower bound that needs no cell text (every row has its delimiters and a CRLF) is compared with the cap. The two-corner sheet is refused at once.
- While writing, the text produced so far is checked after each row, for sheets whose cells hold long text.
- Over the cap, the error is `IoError::TooLarge` and says what happened: `the CSV would be at least 625 MiB (40000 rows by 16384 columns), over the limit of 512 MiB; export a smaller range`. The engine reports it through `file.saveBytes`, Save As and Export; no file is written and the document is unchanged.
- Accepted exports are byte-for-byte what they were (positions and empty fields kept). `write_csv_limited` takes the cap as a parameter so tests can hit the second check cheaply.

## Verified

Two one-character cells, `A1` and `XFD40000`, saved with `gridcraft_engine::io::save_bytes(.., "x.csv")` on `main` and on this branch (the full-grid case would need 16 GiB, so I used a size that fits the 8 GiB machine):

| | result |
|---|---|
| `main` | 655,400,002 bytes (625 MiB), 42 s |
| this branch | refused instantly: `the CSV would be at least 625 MiB (40000 rows by 16384 columns), over the limit of 512 MiB; export a smaller range` |

New tests (they use the new `Result` signature and `write_csv_limited`, so they do not compile on `main`; I did…

title: Rows auto-fit oversized fonts on open and on row formatting (#833)
author: edurbs
body:
## What

Fixes the two plain-cell paths of #833 — a row whose font is taller than the row's height no longer renders top-pinned and clipped:

- **Opening a file** now grows rows without a user-set height (`customHeight`) to fit their tallest whole-cell font, as Excel auto-fits on open. New `fit_imported_rows` at the single open funnel (`open_bytes_with_password`, plain and decrypted paths), reusing the existing `auto_row_height`.
- **Whole-row / whole-column formatting** now re-fits the rows it touches — `apply_style`'s line-target branch marks `fit_rows` for the cells it already styles (cell-range formatting already did).
- **Grow-only on open**: a file's taller non-custom row is never shrunk — our line-height estimate can differ from Excel's, and shrinking files that already look right would be a visible regression. `customHeight` rows keep their height and clip, as Excel does. Hidden rows stay hidden.

## Evidence (offscreen snapshot A/B, @2x, base 47905c8 vs this branch)

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| row 5 pitch | 32 px — never grew | 58 px |
| glyph ink | 26 of 40 px, flat cut at the gridline, `p`/`g` descenders erased | full 40 px, descenders visible, gridline intact |

Both triggers measured identical before→after. Screenshots and the repro workbook are attached to #833 (`before-format.png`, `after-format.png`, `bigfont-base.xlsx`).

## Not in this PR (sequencing)

Per-run rich-text font sizes are not measured by `auto_row_height` yet — that follows #837 (noted on #833). No render change: rows that still clip (`customHeight`) clip as Excel does.

title: XLSX: keep chart sheets on open and save (#727)
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #727

## Cause

Chart sheets (a sheet that holds one chart; Move Chart › New sheet, F11) were skipped on open (`read.rs`), and the pass-through from #330 could not keep them either: `passthrough.rs` lists `chartsheet`, `drawing`, `chart`, `chartstyle` and `chartcolorstyle` as kinds GridCraft rewrites, so anything whose relationship graph reaches them is dropped. Saving a workbook lost every chart sheet with its drawing, chart, style and colour parts.

## Fix

Chart sheets are kept as they were and written back in their place:

- `KeptReader::workbook` keeps each chart sheet as workbook-level content. Its closure may pass through the drawing, chart, style, colour and user-shape kinds (`CHART_SHEET_GRAPH`); for every other root nothing changes. A new `Preserved::sheets` (`PreservedSheet`: name, visibility, position among the worksheets) records the `<sheet>` entry.
- `write_workbook` runs before the worksheets are written so the chart sheets have their relationship ids. `<sheet>` entries are interleaved at their position, with unique `sheetId`s, and everything that holds a sheet position in `workbook.xml` (`activeTab`, `localSheetId` of print areas, titles and scoped names) goes through `WorkbookKept::file_index`.
- The chart is kept as it was, so it can't follow a rename. A chart sheet is therefore left out on save (together with the parts only it reaches) when a sheet its series plot is deleted or renamed, or a worksheet took its name. This is the "drop them only when…" case from the issue.
- The "is a chartsheet and was skipped" warning is gone for kept chart sheets; if one can't be kept (Strict files, size limits, damaged parts) the open warning says so.

title: PivotTables: the PivotTable Fields pane follows the interface language
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #858.

The PivotTable Fields pane drew its labels, the field menus (Move to…, Summarize by…, Show as…, Group by…, Remove Field) and the Refresh / Calculated Field / Report Layout buttons from hardcoded English strings that never went through `Language::tr`, so changing the interface language had no effect on it. They now go through `tr` like the ribbon does, and the Spanish catalog has entries for them. "Summarize by …" and "Show as …" were built with `format!`, so they are now whole labels that a catalog can translate. Only Spanish entries are added, since that is what the issue reports; other languages still fall back to English for this pane and can be filled in the same way. Wording follows Excel's Spanish where I knew it ("Campos de tabla dinámica", "Mover a rótulos de fila", "Quitar campo"); happy to adjust any of it.

title: XLSX: XML maps survive a save, with their table columns and mapped cells
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #860 (everything but point 6, the package comparison in `check`, which I can follow up on).

The map itself was never on the pass-through list, and the bindings that point at it live in parts GridCraft rewrites, so a save dropped all of them. `xl/xmlMaps.xml` is now kept from the workbook (under its own name, since `mapId`s refer into it) and `tableSingleCells` from the sheet, the same way connections and query tables already are. On tables, `uniqueName` and `<xmlColumnPr>` are read into `TableColumn` and written back after the formulas, and `tableType="xml"` / `connectionId` into `Table`. Since the binding sits on the column, it moves with the column, goes away when the column is deleted, and new columns start unmapped. Only `tableType="xml"` is kept: a query table's definition hangs off the table part, so writing `queryTable` without it would be worse than writing a plain table (happy to switch if you'd rather keep the attribute as is).

I left out the `check` package comparison (point 6); happy to do it as a follow-up.

Validation:

title: XLSX: keep the sensitivity label, table column data formats and sheet custom properties on save
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #865.

None of the three were in the #330 pass-through or the model, so a plain open and save dropped them. The sensitivity label is a package-root part (`classificationlabels` relationship to `docMetadata/LabelInfo.xml`), so it now goes through the same path as custom document properties. Sheet `<customProperties>` and their `customPropertyN.bin` parts are kept like printer settings and controls, and written after `<colBreaks>` where the schema puts them; unlike controls they don't need the VML drawing. `dataDxfId` and `dataCellStyle` are now read into `TableColumn` (the dxf as a style, like conditional formats) and written back. The cell style name is only written when that named style is still in the workbook, so a deleted style can't leave a dangling reference (happy to switch to always writing it).

The form-control button anchor in the drawing part (the fourth row in the issue) isn't touched here: the drawing is rewritten by GridCraft, and the button's VML and ctrlProp were already kept.

This touches the same pass-through code as #863 (XML maps); whichever lands second will need a small rebase, which I'll do.

title: XLSX: write this-row structured references as [[#This Row],[Col]]
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #864.

The formula printer always spells a this-row reference with Excel's `@` shorthand, and `to_file` / `text_to_file` used it as is, so `Table[@Col]` went verbatim into cell `<f>` elements and `<calculatedColumnFormula>`. Files need the long form, which is why Excel repaired them and dropped the tables. The printer now has `struct_ref_file`, which writes `[[#This Row],[Col]]` (and `[#This Row]` for `[@]`), and `expr_to_file` uses it for structured references, the same way it already rewrites `#`, `@` and trim references into their file spelling. Reading already accepted both forms, so a round trip gives back `[@Col]` in the model. The unqualified `[@Col]` becomes `[[#This Row],[Col]]` without a table name, the form xlsxwriter writes and Excel opens; qualifying it would need the enclosing table, which `to_file` doesn't know. The reference reaches the printer as an `Expr::Name` carrying the finished text, to avoid threading a file mode through the whole printer; happy to switch to a printer option if you prefer.

Validation:
- `fmla::tests::this_row_long_form` and `tests::array_export::this_row_references_are_written_in_long_form`: fail on main (`Data[@Input]*2` written to the sheet XML, `Sales[@Units]*...` from `to_file`), pass here
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-xlsx --lib -- tests::array_export tests::roundtrip fmla::`, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-formula -p gridcraft-xlsx --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

title: Conditional formatting: reuse Format Cells controls for custom rule styles
author: kcahrens
body:
Fixes #868.

Conditional Formatting offered six preset styles, so users could not choose their own colors and formatting. This adds Custom Format… with shared Number, Font, Border and Fill controls, a combined preview, and format editing in Manage Rules.

## Behavior and design
- The four tabs share one editor with Format Cells. A conditional rule uses inheritance toggles and returns a draft; it does not format the worksheet directly.
- Optional property-presence metadata distinguishes “unchanged” from explicit off/none/automatic/General. Older JSON without it retains the existing non-default-as-set interpretation.
- One differential-style overlay serves rule priority, worksheet rendering and PDF/print. Ordinary cell rendering does not allocate presence sets.
- Creation and editing share style validation/canonicalization. Unused colors in cleared fills/borders do not create save/reopen differences, and invalid font sizes or mismatched diagonal styles are rejected.
- GUI and control-channel confirmation share the same path. Dialog-owned color drafts, captured workbook/worksheet/range, an expected rule snapshot including priority and Stop If True, and validation errors protect cancellation and avoid applying to the wrong or changed rule.
- Format edits preserve ranges, priority and Stop If True. Unchanged format-only confirmation preserves the clean/saved workbook and undo/redo stacks; stale requests still fail and combined delete/reorder requests still execute. No new dependencies or committed binary assets. UI parity documentation is updated.

## Validation
Latest verified commit `bc01aa77c84d421cab95a1c837c51c1453959a2f`: all 8 gates pass; 1,677 tests pass across the workspace.
- CodeRabbit follow-up: fixed differential XML child order (alignment before borders), added full-section serialization/round-trip coverage, and added command/UI tests for unchanged format confirmation. Documented touched functions; CodeRabbit’s completed review of 50e93a4 reported 91.46% do…

title: check: the package round trip reports relationship kinds the save lost
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #860 (point 6, the follow-up promised in #863).

`check` only validated the written package against itself, so a part GridCraft dropped on save left nothing dangling and the `package` category stayed `equal: true`, as CouchRiv saw on the XML-map file. The round trip now also collects the relationship kinds (last segment of the type, so transitional and strict compare equal) from every `.rels` part of the source and of the output, and reports each kind the source had and the output lacks, e.g. `lost relationship xmlMaps`. `calcChain` is left out: GridCraft never writes it and Excel rebuilds it, so it would flag nearly every Excel file. Only losses are reported, not gained kinds (a minimal source picking up `styles` or `sharedStrings` isn't a problem); happy to switch to a two-way comparison or to per-part counts if you'd rather.

On `main` the issue's synthetic Business Central file now reports `package: 2 difference(s)` (`lost relationship tableSingleCells`, `lost relationship xmlMaps`); #863 restores the XML maps, so with it merged only what it doesn't cover should remain.

Validation:
- `check::tests::package_reports_relationship_kinds_the_output_lost` (a source with an unknown relationship kind and a `calcChain`): fails on main (`left: []`, right: `["lost relationship madeUp"]`), passes here
