title: Refuse to save to an unknown file extension instead of writing XLSX under it
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #878.

`io::save_bytes` fell back to XLSX for any extension `FileKind::from_path` didn't know (or no extension at all), and `file.save` then treated the result as a full-fidelity save: it cleared the dirty flag and adopted `report.foo` as the document's file. `save_bytes` now returns an error naming the file and the formats it can write, the same way it already refuses `.xls`, `.xlsb` and `.ods`. Since `file.save`, `gridcraft-cli run --out`, MCP and the desktop Save As all go through it, they all get the error, and nothing is written. The desktop Save As keeps appending `.xlsx` to a name typed without an extension, so the dialog flow is unchanged; for an unknown extension it now shows the error instead. I went with refusing rather than appending `.xlsx` to the name because that's how the CLI's `convert` and the import-only formats already behave, happy to switch.

A workbook opened by content under an unknown extension (an XLSX named `budget.dat`, say) keeps saving back as XLSX with Ctrl+S: the kind found on open is used when saving to the document's own path. A text file opened that way still gets the error, rather than being overwritten with a ZIP.

Validation:
- `tests::saving_to_an_unknown_extension_is_refused` (engine): fails on main (`file.save` to `report.cvs` returns Ok and writes 4006 bytes), passes here; it also checks a bare `report`, that the document stays dirty with no file, and `file.saveBytes` with an unknown format
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-engine --lib -- save`, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-engine -p gridcraft-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `gridcraft-cli run --sample sales --out report.foo` now exits 1 with `report.foo: unknown file format. Save as .xlsx, .csv, .tsv, .json or .html.` and writes nothing; `--out report.csv` still works
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Hyperlinks: confirm before opening external links, refuse unsafe schemes
author: keysouth
body:
## Problem

`grid::follow_link` passes any hyperlink target containing `://` straight to the host's `open_url`, which runs `open` / `explorer` / `xdg-open` with no prompt. One plain click on a hyperlink cell is enough. So a workbook from an untrusted source can:

- launch a local program with a `file://` link (for example `file:///System/Applications/Calculator.app`)
- trigger app-specific URL schemes (`vscode://…`, `x-apple.systempreferences:…`, `smb://…`, and so on)
- pass a target that starts with `-` and contains `://`, which the opener may read as a command-line option

Excel asks for confirmation before opening links like these.

## Change

- **`http://`, `https://` and `mailto:` links:** a modal asks "Open this link?" and shows the full address. The link opens only when the user clicks **Open**. **Cancel** or Escape closes it, and Enter doesn't open the link.
- **Any other scheme:** refused, with a message explaining why.
- **In-workbook targets** (`Sheet2!A1`, `#B5`): navigate exactly as before.
- **`UiRequest::OpenUrl`:** goes through the same check (`grid::request_open_link`).
- **Keyboard:** the grid and global shortcuts ignore keys while the confirmation is open, the same as for `message`.

The About-window contributor links (`dialogs.rs`) are unchanged. They are hard-coded GitHub URLs, not workbook content.

## Testing

- New unit test `grid::tests::only_web_and_mail_links_may_open_outside_the_app` covers allowed schemes, refused schemes, case handling and in-workbook targets.
- Checked by hand in a release build through the control channel. Clicking an `https://` link showed the confirmation. Clicking a `file:///…/Calculator.app` link showed the "blocked" message and launched nothing.
- `cargo fmt --check` passes.
- `cargo clippy -D warnings` on Rust 1.95 still reports two existing lints that this PR doesn't touch: `collapsible_match` at `crates/xlsx/src/xls/mod.rs:257` and `overly_complex_bool_expr` at `crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs` (the `|| true` in a …

title: XLSX: keep every core document property on save (created, modified, last modified by, category, status…)
author: CouchRiv
body:
Follow-up to the corpus run in the #871 comments. GridCraft read only five fields of `docProps/core.xml` (title, subject, creator, keywords, description), so an open and save dropped everything else. On the 76 real workbooks from that run, `created` was lost on 5 of 5 files that had it, `modified` on 6 of 6, `lastModifiedBy` on 2 of 2; on 2 files the written part was an empty `<cp:coreProperties>`.

## What changed

Three changes, followed by merges of upstream `main` without rebasing or force-pushing. The save-stamping change is a separate design choice.

**1. Keep the properties** (`XLSX: keep every core document property on save`)
- `DocProps` (model) gains `last_modified_by`, `created`, `modified`, `last_printed`, `category`, `content_status`, `revision`, `version`, `identifier` and `language`, kept as the file's text (the dates are W3CDTF strings, not parsed). The struct is now `serde(default, rename_all = "camelCase")`: existing keys are single words so they don't change, JSON workbooks saved before still open, and `file.properties` reports the new fields as `lastModifiedBy`, `contentStatus`… (it serializes `DocProps`). They are read only: the command's parameters are unchanged.
- `read.rs` reads them next to the existing five, with the same `get` helper.
- `write.rs` writes them after the existing five, in the order Excel uses. `dcterms:created` and `dcterms:modified` get `xsi:type="dcterms:W3CDTF"`, which the core-properties schema requires on those two (the `xsi` namespace was already declared). Empty fields are left out as before, so a new workbook's `core.xml` is unchanged.

**2. Save records who saved and when** (`Save records the save time and the user like Excel`)
- `file.save` (and Save As) to a full-fidelity format (`.xlsx`, `.json`) sets `modified` to the current time, `created` too when it is empty (a new workbook's first save), and `lastModifiedBy` to `Prefs::user_name`, the name new comments are signed with. This is what Excel does on every save.…

title: check: a boolean cached as 1/0 without t="b" matches, and is counted apart
author: CouchRiv
body:
## What this changes

Business Central's "Open in Excel" exports write booleans as a formula with a numeric cache and no `t="b"`: `<c><f>TRUE()</f><v>1</v></c>`. GridCraft's `TRUE` is right, but the `check` oracle compared it with the cached number and reported every such cell as a mismatch (`number → bool`), so a BC export showed thousands of differences that are only how the producer saved the cache. You suggested this on #871.

`check` now treats a boolean result whose cache is the matching 1/0 number as matched, and counts those cells apart, so nothing is hidden:

- per file: `(N matched TRUE/FALSE results were saved by the producer as 1/0, without t="b")`;
- summary: `booleans saved as 1/0 by the producer: N (counted as matched)`;
- JSON: `boolAsNumber` per file and in the totals.

A real mismatch still counts: a boolean whose cache is the other value (`=1=1` cached as `0`), or a numeric result, is unchanged. `docs/cli.md` documents the new counter.

## How you verified it

- `check::tests::booleans_cached_as_numbers_match_and_are_counted_apart`: `=TRUE()` cached 1, `=FALSE()` cached 0, `=TRUE()` with `t="b"`, `=1=1` cached 0 (still a mismatch) and `=TRUE()+0` cached 1 (a number, unaffected). It doesn't build on main (no `boolAsNumber`), and passes here with the other 12 `check::tests`.
- On 76 real workbooks (BC exports, configuration packages, other workbooks): 0.6.1 reports `148831 checked: 778 matched, 148053 mismatched`; this branch reports `148831 matched, 0 mismatched` and `booleans saved as 1/0 by the producer: 148053`.
- (Linux x86_64)

This touches `apps/gridcraft-cli/src/check.rs`, like #871; the two changes are in different functions, but whichever lands second may need a rebase.

title: Conditional formats: hex colours in a custom style, and no more silently empty or never-matching rules
author: CouchRiv
body:
Three traps for a programmatic caller (MCP `execute_command`, control channel) adding a highlighted rule with `home.conditionalFormat`. The first was refused with serde messages naming internal types; the other two returned success, so the caller believed the sheet was highlighted when it wasn't.

1. **Colours.** `style` went straight into the model's `Style`, so a colour had to be written `{"Rgb": 16773836}`. `"#FFF2CC"`, which `format_range`, `colorScale` and `dataBar` all take, was refused with serde messages about internal types: `invalid type: string "#FFF2CC", expected struct Fill`, then ``unknown variant `#FFF2CC`, expected one of `Auto`, `Rgb`, `Theme` ``.
2. **Dropped keys.** A key `Style` doesn't have was dropped: `style: {"preset": "greenFill"}` (a natural reading of the `params` text `style?: {font..fill..}|preset: …`) saved the rule with an empty `<dxf></dxf>`, so it matches and shows nothing.
3. **Quoted text.** A `cellIs` value already written as a string literal, `"\"Closed\""` (how the file stores it, and openpyxl's `CellIsRule(formula=['"Closed"'])`), was quoted again: `<formula>"""Closed"""</formula>` is the text `"Closed"` with its quotes, so the rule never matches a cell holding `Closed`.

## What changed

All in `crates/engine/src/cmd/insert.rs`.
- `cf_style_json` runs on `style` before the existing merge over the default `Style`:
  - colours in `font.color`, `fill.fg`/`fill.bg` and `borders.<side>.color` may be `"#RRGGBB"`, `{theme, tint}` or `"auto"`, through the same `format::color_param` the other formatting commands use;
  - `fill` may be a colour alone, meaning a solid fill, and a fill with `fg` but no `pattern` is solid rather than invisible;
  - `fill: "none"` (or `"auto"`) is no fill, as `home.fillColor` reads it, rather than a solid fill in the automatic colour (second commit);
  - a key that isn't a `Style` field is refused, naming the known keys (and pointing `preset` to `rule.preset`), and so is a `style` that isn't an object (it u…

title: Row, column and freeze commands act on the sheet they are given (`sheet`, or a `Sheet!` prefix)
author: CouchRiv
body:
`view.freezePanes`, `home.rowHeight`, `home.columnWidth` and the other row and column commands always changed the active sheet. A `sheet` parameter was accepted and silently ignored, so a programmatic caller (MCP, control channel, CLI) laying out a sheet that isn't active got a success while the frozen panes, widths or heights landed on the active sheet, over what it had set there before. Found while building a four-sheet review workbook through MCP: the panes and column widths meant for two other sheets ended up on the first one.

Repro on `main` (fc45b7f), `gridcraft-cli mcp`, after `home.insertSheet {name: "Data"}` and `sheet.activate {sheet: "Sheet1"}`:

| call | `main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `view.freezePanes {sheet: "Data", cell: "A2"}` | `{"freeze":[1,0]}`, applied to Sheet1 | applied to Data |
| `home.columnWidth {sheet: "Data", cols: "A:A", chars: 30}` | Sheet1!A:A resized | Data!A:A resized |
| `home.rowHeight {sheet: "Data", rows: "1:1", height: 40}` | Sheet1 row 1 | Data row 1 |
| `home.columnWidth {cols: "Data!B:B", chars: 30}` | `invalid parameters for cols: not a range: Data!B:B` | Data!B:B resized |
| `view.freezePanes {cell: "Data!A2"}` | ``Data!A2 for cell names a sheet other than the one this command works on`` | Data frozen at A2 |

Saved file on `main`: `sheet1.xml` has the `<col>` and `<row ht>`, `sheet2.xml` (Data) has no pane, no `<cols>`, no row height. On the branch it's the other way round.

## What changed

- `format.rs`: `line_targets` now returns the sheet with the lines. The sheet is `sheet` (name or index, through `target_sheet` like `home.insertRows` or `data.validation`), else a `Sheet!` prefix on `rows`/`cols` (`"Data!B:B,D:F"`, same convention as `range` in `target_ranges`), else the active sheet. A prefix that contradicts `sheet` is an error; a null `sheet` counts as absent, as in `target_sheet` (second commit). `home.rowHeight`, `home.columnWidth`, `home.autofitRowHeight`, `home.autofitColumnWidth`, `home.hideRows`/`hid…

title: SORT and SORTBY order text with Excel's collation: hyphens ignored, punctuation before digits before letters, accents with their base letter
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #890.

SORT and SORTBY compared text through `sort_compare`, which ends in `compare_text`: lowercase, then code point. That puts `_` after the digits, `-` before the letters and `Ä` after `Z`. The sort key comparator in `dynamic.rs` now orders two texts with a small collation instead: hyphens and apostrophes are dropped at the first level, punctuation and symbols come before digits and digits before letters, and accented Latin letters (Latin-1 and Latin Extended-A) sort as their base letter. Ties are broken by the accents, then by putting the string without hyphens/apostrophes first; anything still equal keeps the input order, as Excel's case-insensitive sort does (`ab | AB`, `apfel | Apfel`). `compare_text` is untouched, so `<`/`>`, criteria and lookups behave as before. UNIQUE itself keeps first-occurrence order; `SORT(UNIQUE(...))` from the issue goes through the new comparator.

Other scripts (second commit, after iluebbe's check in #890):
- Diacritic marks that are not letters only break ties: Thai and Lao tone marks, Hebrew points, Arabic harakat, Indic nukta/candrabindu/anusvara, and the combining diacritics blocks. The first version counted the non-alphabetic ones as punctuation, so `ข้าว` sorted before `ขาว` (main and Excel: `ขาว, ข้าว`). The table is the general-category Mn characters of those scripts that the UCA default table (DUCET 13.0, read through Perl's Unicode::Collate) ignores at the first level. Thai vowels above/below and Indic vowel signs keep their first-level weight, so `กา, กิน` stays as on main; viramas count as letters, so `पतन, पत्र` stays as on main too.
- `ß`, `æ`, `œ`, `ĳ` are equal to `ss`, `ae`, `oe`, `ij` at every level, not an accent apart: descending SORT now keeps `ss, ß` in input order like Excel instead of reversing them. (`ĳ` follows the same rule; only `ß`/`æ`/`œ` were checked against Excel.)
- A word starting with a Thai leading vowel (เ แ โ ใ ไ) sorts before the Thai consonants. This is the rule of #1241 (#1235) for `…

title: UI: File › Account shows the version, platform and licence, with an About GridCraft button
author: marcoarnulfo
body:

This adds an **Account** page at the bottom of the File view's page list, just above Options as in Excel. title: Ribbon: the mouse wheel over the ribbon switches tabs
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #897.

The ribbon had no wheel handling, so the wheel did nothing over it. Now, once the ribbon panel has been drawn, the vertical wheel delta still left over while the pointer is on the tab row or the card switches tabs: down goes to the next tab, up to the previous one, and it stops at the first and last tab (contextual tabs count too). Running after the ribbon is drawn means any scroll area inside it that already took the wheel keeps it, and horizontal gestures are left alone, so the overflow scroll on a narrow ribbon (and its successor in #675, which merges cleanly with this) keeps priority. Deltas add up per gesture. A switch fires past half a notch and then uses up a whole notch, so a notch gives one tab and a trackpad swipe doesn't race through them. Nothing switches while a popup menu is open. The File view never draws the ribbon, so it isn't affected. A collapsed ribbon changes its selected tab without expanding. Happy to switch that if expanding fits better.

I left out the opt-out setting the issue mentions as optional, to keep this small. I'm happy to add it here or in a follow-up if you want it.

title: Keytips: Alt, F opens the File view, and its F letters still run
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #893.

`keytips.json` had no `F` entry, so after Alt the File letters only existed as the blind two-letter sequences (FA, FC, FI, FN, FO, FP, FEA, FEC). This adds `F` as a tab-kind entry for "File": Alt, F (or F10, F) opens the File view on Home, and the File button gets its `F` badge with the other tab letters. The prefix stays at `F`, so keytips keep running while the File view is open (before, they were skipped whenever it was), and the second letter does what it did before. When an F sequence finishes, the view closes and the command runs on the sheet as it used to. Esc backs out one level: the File view closes and the tab letters show again. The generator accepts `File` as a tab target, and its generated test checks that the File view opened instead of checking `ribbon_tab`.

Still open from the issue: badges on the File view's page list, and richard1912's idea of making the second letter switch page (New, Open, Info…) instead of running the command. I kept the current letters, as the issue body asks. Switching pages would change what FA/FO/FI do today, so it felt like a separate call. Happy to do it here or in a follow-up if you'd rather have Excel's page behaviour.

title: Select a cell when the button goes down, not on release
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #900.

The grid only decided a press from `drag_started()` or `clicked()`, so nothing happened while the button was down, and a press whose movement and release arrived in the same frame (past the click distance, but never recognised as a drag) selected nothing. A press on a plain cell now selects it right away (Shift extends, Ctrl/Cmd adds an area) and enters `Drag::Select` with that cell as the anchor, so dragging extends from it as before. Presses on the outline buttons, filter and list arrows, objects, freeze handles, the fill handle and the move border, and presses while editing, keep going through the existing path, so they still act on drag or release. Following a hyperlink, toggling a checkbox and double-click-to-edit stay on release, as in Excel. The selection code moved into a small `select_pressed_cell` helper shared by both paths.

Two things to know: with a drawing tool active the press still selects on release, as before. And since the cell is now selected on the way down, its fill handle is already there when the button comes up, so a click on the last few pixels of the bottom-right corner of a cell that wasn't selected before lands on the handle (no double-click-to-edit or link there). title: CELL("address") names the sheet of a reference to another sheet
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #904.

`CELL("address", ref)` always printed the bare `$C$7`, whatever sheet the reference pointed at, so `INDIRECT(CELL("address",D!C7))` read C7 of the formula's own sheet. It now prefixes the sheet name when the reference is on another sheet, quoted with the same `quote_sheet` the formula printer and ADDRESS use (`'My Sheet'!$C$7`); a reference to the formula's own sheet keeps `$C$7`. I left out Excel's `[book.xlsx]` part: the evaluator doesn't know the file name (`CELL("filename")` returns empty too), so the result matches LibreOffice's `D!$C$7`, which INDIRECT reads back. Happy to switch if you'd rather have the workbook name once it's available.

title: xlsx: inherit number format from cellStyleXfs parent (xfId) — fixes short dates showing as serials
author: setzor
body:
## Summary
- Fixes the XLSX reader ignoring `xfId` inheritance: a `cellXf` with `numFmtId="0"` and no `applyNumberFormat="1"` now inherits its number format from the `cellStyleXfs` entry its `xfId` points at (OOXML §18.8.10, matching Excel's behaviour for named styles)
- Excel commonly formats date columns through a named style (e.g. built-in "Date"/"20"), so those cells previously lost their `m/d/yyyy` format and displayed the raw date serial (e.g. `46315`) instead of a date — the exact symptom in the linked issue
- Adds a regression test (`named_cell_style_number_format_is_inherited_by_cell_xfs`) that builds an Excel-style package with a named Date style and asserts the cell displays `10/13/2026` (serial 46308) instead of the serial

## Root cause
`read_xf` in `crates/xlsx/src/styles.rs` parsed each `cellXfs` entry in isolation and dropped the `xfId` attribute. `cellStyleXfs` is now read first and threaded through as a parent list; `read_xf_with_parent` falls back to the parent's `num_fmt` only when the cell format doesn't override it (`numFmtId=0` without `applyNumberFormat`). Dates typed directly in GridCraft were unaffected because the app applies the format straight to the cell — matching the reporter's observation that only pre-existing Excel files misrendered.

## Verification
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-xlsx`: 166 passed
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-engine --lib`: 273 passed (includes the new regression test)
- `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-engine -p gridcraft-xlsx --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo fmt --check`: clean

Closes #892

title: Keyboard: Enter after a run of Tabs goes to the next row in the column the run started from
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #911, fixes #983.

`move_after_enter` treated every Enter as a plain move down, so after typing across a row with Tab, Enter landed under the last cell instead of back at the first column. The app now remembers a run of Tabs (where it started and the cell the last Tab landed on); Enter on that cell moves to the next row in the starting column, as Excel does. Any other move (arrow, click, another sheet or workbook) leaves the selection off that cell and ends the run, and multi-cell selections keep cycling inside the area as before. It applies to Enter going down only, which is what Enter does in GridCraft today. It also works when the last cell wasn't edited (Tab, Tab, Enter), as in Excel, so the existing `keyboard_navigation_does_not_replay_the_last_pointer_click` step now expects B5 instead of C5. Shift+Tab continues a run like Tab; happy to switch if you'd rather it not start one.

title: Close › Save on a new workbook closes it once the save dialog has saved it; a picture pick isn't dropped as an unsaved save (#901)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #901, fixes #385, fixes #1245.

Both crash reports have the same stack. A desktop file dialog (`rfd::FileDialog`) ran `-[NSSavePanel runModal]` inside the frame, which means inside winit's event handler. In that nested modal loop, a trackpad gesture (#901) or a drag (#385) makes AppKit run the closures winit queued meanwhile. The handler is still in use, so winit's re-entrancy panic fires inside an Objective-C block, where it can't unwind, and the app aborts (rust-windowing/winit#3992, still open on 0.30.13). This PR uses the same approach as WordCraft (#246), PhotoCraft (#1071) and VectorCraft (#1099). The app queues its request, and the frame starts an `rfd::AsyncFileDialog` parented to the window. On macOS that's a sheet, so the call returns at once. A helper thread waits for the answer and wakes the UI, and the app acts on it in `SheetApp::logic`. Every desktop dialog goes through this: Open, Save As, Export as PDF, File › Export, Insert Picture's Browse… and Save a Copy. `Services::pick_*` now return a `Receiver<Option<String>>`. The web paths are unchanged.

While a dialog is open, a second one isn't started. A save or export whose workbook is no longer the active one is dropped with a message. Close › Save on a workbook that was never saved now closes it once the dialog has saved it; a cancelled dialog keeps it open, as Cancel does. I didn't make the menu bar inert while the sheet is up, as VectorCraft did: with a sheet, nothing re-enters winit's handler. Happy to add it if you'd like it.

Validation:
- `file_menu::export_writes_the_file_once_the_save_dialog_answers`: nothing is written while the dialog is open, File stays open, and the CSV is written once the dialog answers. On main it doesn't compile, because the picker returned the path in line. title: Detect partial drawing loss in XLSX fidelity checks
author: jonathanwxh-cell

title: Web: embed a Simplified-Chinese fallback face so wasm builds render CJK
author: zxxiao2012
body:
# Web: embed a Simplified-Chinese fallback face so wasm builds render CJK

## The bug

Opening any workbook with Chinese text in the **web build** shows tofu boxes:

- `theme.rs` `load_fallback()` loads system CJK/Thai/Hebrew faces on native, but on
  `wasm32` it is a stub returning an empty `Vec` — there are no system font files in
  the browser to load.
- egui's bundled fonts (Ubuntu-Light + NotoEmoji) have no coverage beyond Latin,
  as the doc comment on `load_fallback` already notes.
- The browser offers no font path either: the JS glue exposes no
  `queryLocalFonts`/`FontFace`, and craft-fonts (as checked out by the release
  workflow, abb8331) ships only Japanese faces anyway.

Desktop builds are unaffected (system font discovery); only the web build is.

Repro: serve `apps/gridcraft-web`, open or drag in any `.xlsx` with Chinese cell
text → `□□□` where the hanzi should be. The XLSX reader is fine — `gridcraft-cli cat`
prints the same strings correctly; it is purely a rendering gap.

## The fix

`load_fallback` on `wasm32` now embeds **Noto Sans SC** (SIL OFL 1.1, file + licence
added under `crates/ui-egui/assets/fonts/noto-sans-sc/`, row added to
`ATTRIBUTION.md`) and registers it under the existing `sys-cjk-han-zh` key, which
`font_definitions_with` already appends to every role chain. The face covers
Simplified Chinese plus kana, so it serves both `HanOrder`s; Simplified Chinese has
the widest Han coverage, matching the comment on `HanOrder::Chinese`.

title: Calc: evaluate precedents first so a long reverse chain isn't #CIRC! (#555)
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Fixes #555.

## Problem
A recalc pass evaluated the dirty formulas in row-major order and followed precedents on demand, one recursion level per link (`PassHost::compute` → `cell_value` → `compute`). A chain where each formula reads the row below, entered in one edit, gets met from the wrong end. Past 2,000 links the depth cap reported `#CIRC!` even though nothing is circular. On a smaller stack (a 2 MB thread) the recursion overflowed before it reached the cap.

## Fix
`Graph::evaluation_order` (crates/calc/src/recalc.rs) orders the dirty set using Tarjan's algorithm. It runs with an explicit stack over the graph's static precedents, so each formula is evaluated after the dirty formulas it reads.
- **Finding precedents:** the dirty formulas are indexed by (sheet, column, row). Each column of a precedent range takes one range scan.
- **Circular references** form one strongly connected component and keep row-major order. The first formula still follows the loop on demand and reports `#CIRC!`, or iterates when iterative calculation is on.
- **Dynamic references** (INDIRECT, OFFSET, spill refs) still use on-demand evaluation and its depth cap.

## Tests
`tests::long_reverse_chain_entered_at_once` enters a 50,000-formula reverse chain plus its terminal value in one change. It checks:
- A1 = 50001 with no cycle reported.
- Changing the terminal gives A1 = 50010, and the same after `recalc_all`.
- A real two-cell loop at the end of the chain still gives `#CIRC!`, incrementally and after a full recalc.

Without the fix the test overflows the stack.

Checked with `gridcraft-cli run --script …` using the issue's scripts:

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| reverse-2002 | A1 `#CIRC!` | all 2,003 rows correct |
| reverse-100000 | `#CIRC!` | A1 = 100001 |
| reverse-2001, forward-2002 | correct | unchanged |
| `=B1+1` / `=A1+1` loop | `#CIRC!` | still `#CIRC!` |

Running totals over formula cells (`=SUM($B$1:Bn)`, 5,000 rows, release build) take about the same time before…

author: musicism-tai

## Summary

This PR expands Traditional Chinese (Taiwan, `zh-TW`) localization support in GridCraft and enhances the system font picker, particularly for CJK users on macOS.

title: Grid input: select on press, fill-handle double-click to adjacent data, whole-column and row references in formulas
author: echelon
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"echelon"} -->
_Requested by **Brandon**_

Before: a cell was selected only when the mouse button came back up, and a press that moved a little inside the cell could select nothing (#900). Double-clicking the fill handle used the left column only and missed data on the right or reached diagonally (#877). Clicking a heading while typing a formula inserted `B:B` but couldn't be dragged to `B:D`, whole-column and whole-row references (`A:A`, `2:2`) were neither coloured nor outlined (#873, #875), and F4 mangled them into `$A$:$A$`.

title: Arabic font fallback in cells, the formula bar and the web
author: Mouhand-Kaddo
body:
## Summary

Arabic text shows as boxes when no font in a chain has Arabic letters: in a Latin-only workbook font, in the formula bar, and on the web, where there are no system fonts. This fits Arabic into main's craft-fonts policy and the system script fallbacks.

```diff
 font setup
+ fontconfig's Arabic choice (Linux/BSD), when it has Arabic letters (first Arabic fallback)
  system script fallbacks
+   sys-arabic: Tahoma / Arial / Segoe UI, Geeza Pro, Noto Sans or Naskh Arabic
  proportional chain = UI chain
- bind installed workbook fonts (before the chain was complete)
+ bind installed workbook fonts (after it, so they keep every script fallback)
  craft-fonts faces, now including Noto Sans Arabic (required, web-allowed)
```

Font files are now read through one size-capped reader (`fonts::read_font`), so a font that grows after the scan can't be read whole.

## Issues

- Part of #229: on Linux and BSD the face `fc-match :lang=ar` picks (such as a Vazirmatn the user chose) leads the Arabic fallbacks, ahead of the system and craft-fonts Arabic faces, so it draws Arabic wherever the UI or cell font has none (the default cell fonts, and the interface when the UI font lacks Arabic). It is used only when it has Arabic letters and is skipped when `fc-match` is missing. `the_fontconfig_arabic_choice_comes_first` covers it.
  - Not fixed here: where the UI font has Arabic of its own, such as DejaVu Sans in the Flatpak (the setup in #229), the interface still draws Arabic with the UI font. egui takes each character from the first face that has it, so moving the preferred face ahead of the UI font would also hand it Latin text. title: ci: remove flatpak-pages.yml — superseded by craft-launcher
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Rationale

The `flatpak-pages` workflow published Flatpak bundles to GitHub Pages as a self-hosted Flatpak repository, allowing users to install GridCraft via:

```
flatpak remote-add --if-not-exists gridcraft <pages-url>/flatpak/gridcraft.flatpakrepo
flatpak install gridcraft ai.storyteller.gridcraft
```

**craft-launcher** (storytold/craft-launcher) now covers this use case for all Craft apps, including Flatpak delivery and updates. With the launcher as the canonical distribution channel, maintaining a per-repo GitHub Pages Flatpak remote in parallel:

- Creates two diverging installation paths for end users
- Duplicates release work (bundles must be consistent across both channels)
- Keeps GitHub Pages enabled for a channel no longer being directed at
- Adds workflow complexity and Pages storage/quota per repo

## What stays

The Flatpak bundles themselves (`.flatpak` artifacts) **continue to be built and attached to each GitHub Release** by `release.yml` — this only removes the Pages-hosted repository layer on top of them. Nothing is lost for users going through the launcher or downloading bundles directly from the Releases page.

## Scope

Only `storytold/gridcraft` still has this workflow (verified across all Craft app repos). It is a clean single-file deletion.

title: Preserve PivotTable filter listing order across XLSX saves
author: derechopiano
body:
Fixes #553.

When a row-field selection is followed by a report filter, saving and reopening the PivotTable currently changes the `pivot.fields` filter listing from Region, Channel to Channel, Region. Both selections and report values survive; the ordering does not. XLSX stores page filters and axis-field item selections separately, and GridCraft's reader had to reconstruct them in separate groups.

This keeps the standard PivotTable fields and selections unchanged, and adds optional filter-order metadata to the PivotTable definition's `extLst` for GridCraft round trips. The reader applies that order only when it matches every reconstructed filter exactly once; missing or stale metadata retains the existing standard-field fallback.

Verification:
- The new mixed row/report/column regression failed before the fix and passes for three orderings and two consecutive XLSX round trips.
- A stale-metadata test confirms that standard filters remain available in their fallback order.
- The exact #553 CLI reproduction now retains Region then Channel after save/reopen and refresh, with East = 10 and Grand Total = 10 unchanged.
- `cargo xtask ci`: all eight stages pass (fmt, Clippy, workspace tests, assets, layers, WASM, parity, keytips).

Related open PRs #719, #722 and #498 also edit the PivotTable XLSX code but cover slicers, item sorting/layout, and label/value filters respectively. They do not address this filter listing order; whichever lands later may need to reconcile nearby XML writing code. The optional extension has not been manually opened in Excel, so this PR does not claim that check.

title: Arabic bidi layout and cell reading direction in the grid and editors
author: Mouhand-Kaddo
body:

Arabic in cells and editors needs bidirectional layout that keeps the logical text for editing, copy and XLSX, and a cell's own reading direction. Main's egui 0.37 fork (`storytold/egui@6d518fc`) now has paragraph bidi layout (`LayoutJob::direction`), so this PR no longer patches egui. It uses that layout everywhere cell text is drawn and edited.

```diff

+ paragraph direction from the cell's reading order (Context / LTR / RTL), else from its first strong character
+ grid (normal, wrap, shrink, Fill, ####, rotation), in-cell editor and formula bar use it
+ General-aligned right-to-left text aligns right on a left-to-right sheet
```

title: fix(fill): respect the workbook date system in monthly AutoFill
author: anirudhqwerty
body:
AutoFill detects monthly date patterns using the workbook's date system, but previously generated each subsequent date using the 1900 system. In a 1904 workbook, filling `2026-01-31`, `2026-03-31` down to six rows produced `2026-10-01` where `2026-09-30` belongs. The command succeeded with a silently incorrect date.

Retain the workbook's date system in the detected month pattern and use it when applying calendar-month offsets. This also covers yearly patterns, which use the same path. No command or file-format API changes.

The regression exercises `edit.autoFill` in both date systems, forward and backward, checking every source and destination cell, including month-end clamping. It fails on the original code with `D1904 ... A5: 2026-09-30` (serial 44834 instead of 44833), and passes with the fix. Updated the affected parity note as requested by AGENTS.md.

Validation:
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-engine autofill_month_pattern -- --nocapture` — passed.
- `cargo xtask ci` — formatting and workspace Clippy (`-D warnings`) passed. The workspace test run was stopped at the contributor's request because the fresh desktop build consumed too much local disk and time; the remaining gate steps (assets, layers, WASM, parity, keytips) were not run.

Found during code review; no existing issue or PR for this specific AutoFill defect was found.

AI assistance: Codex prepared the fix and regression test and ran the validation listed above.

title: Merge & Center keeps the first value and asks before discarding the others
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #944.

`merge` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/format.rs` always kept `r.start` and cleared everything else, so a lone value in B2 vanished and two values lost one without a word. Thanks to @richard1912 for the comparison table in the issue: it made the expected behaviour easy to pin down. Now the first value in reading order moves into the upper-left cell, with its formula and a cell picture if there is one. The upper-left cell keeps its own format. Merge Across does the same row by row. When an area holds more than one value, the command refuses with an error unless it gets `discard: true`. That's the same shape as Data Analysis's `overwrite: true`, so programmatic calls never open a dialog. `run_or_alert` (ribbon, menu, keytips) catches that error and shows an OK/Cancel confirmation, and OK runs the merge again with `discard: true`. Undo restores everything in one step. The ribbon code from #942 is unchanged.

A few choices that are yours to make, and I'm happy to switch any of them:
- the param name `discard`;
- the wording, which I took from the issue's proposal rather than Excel's dialog text, since that text is Microsoft's;
- the move of a lone value. Microsoft's support page says only the upper-left cell's content is kept ([Merge and unmerge cells](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/merge-and-unmerge-cells-5cbd15d5-9375-4540-907f-c673a93fcedf)). I followed what the issue observed in Microsoft 365 instead.

Validation:
- `cmd::format::tests::merge_keeps_the_only_value_even_when_it_is_not_upper_left`: fails on main (A1 is `Null`, expected `"vB2"`), passes here. It also checks that undo restores B2.

title: Merge & Center unmerges a selection that contains merged cells, as Excel does
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #950. Builds on #953 (the fix for #944, same `merge()` function), so the diff includes that commit until #953 lands; the change for this issue is the last commit.

title: xlsx: persist table slicers to .xlsx
author: zaidshurbaji
body:
Follow-up to #193 — *"Saving slicers to .xlsx would be a great follow-up."*

## What
Slicers were kept on the sheet but never written to the file, so they vanished on save while their filter lingered as orphaned hidden rows. This writes them as genuine Excel **table slicers** and reads them back.

## How — write (`crates/xlsx`)
- A slicer-cache part per slicer (`xl/slicerCaches/slicerCacheN.xml`) with the `x15:tableSlicerCache` binding (table id + 1-based column).
- A per-sheet slicer part (`xl/slicers/slicerN.xml`).
- A drawing `graphicFrame` anchor (`sle:slicer`, `Requires="a14"`) with a placeholder-shape fallback — the same shape Excel writes.
- The workbook `x15:slicerCaches` and worksheet `x15:slicerList` `extLst` hooks, plus content types and relationships.
- Each slicer's selection is folded into the table column's own `<autoFilter>`, so it persists as a real table-column filter — which also clears the orphaned-hidden-rows state noted in the #193 review.

## How — read
Slicers are rebuilt from the slicer part + caches + drawing anchor, and the selection is recovered from the table column filter. The file's table id is captured before it is reassigned, so slicers re-link to their table (works for both GridCraft- and Excel-authored files).

## Validation
- New round-trip tests (`crates/xlsx/src/tests/slicer_roundtrip.rs`): a slicer with a selection and a "show all" slicer both survive save → reopen (binding, caption, position, selection), and the selection lands in the table filter.
- Cross-checked the emitted parts against an Excel-authored slicer file (content types, slicer/slicerCache rel types, the drawing `graphicFrame`, and the `extLst` wiring).
- A GridCraft-written slicer file **opens in Microsoft Excel with no repair prompt and shows the slicer**.
- Local gates pass: `fmt`, `clippy -D warnings`, xlsx + engine tests (incl. the command-sequence fuzz XLSX round-trip), assets, layers, wasm. The generated parity checklist is unchanged (no new catalog comman…

title: Grid: the in-cell editor keeps the cell's alignment, in merges too
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #948.

Thanks @richard1912 for the precise report and the pointer to `in_cell_editor`. The editor box was always laid out from the cell's (or merge's) top-left and never read `st.align`, so the text jumped to the top-left while editing. It now uses the same alignment as painting: horizontal through `TextEdit::horizontal_align` (General follows the value, so a number stays right-aligned when you F2 it; mirrored on right-to-left sheets), vertical by placing the editor within the cell (top / middle / bottom, bottom by default). When the text outgrows the cell the box grows the way it reads, as in Excel: centred text both ways, right-aligned text to the left. The General rule is now one small helper shared by painting and the editor, and the AutoComplete suffix is drawn at the text's real end instead of the widget's left edge, so it follows centred or right-aligned text.

title: i18n: Arabic (ar) interface, mirrored right to left
author: tlomts-dev
body:
Arabic (`ar`) joins the interface languages, with a mirrored right-to-left window. Modern Standard Arabic, Western digits, count-neutral wording, written from the meaning of the English labels (no vendor localisation consulted). One commit on current `main`.

## What it does

- **Catalog:** `i18n/ar.rs`, 1,428 entries, written in typing order and put into display order the first time they are used (`i18n/display.rs`, UAX #9 through `unicode-bidi`), because egui lays the runs of a line out left to right. Placeholders and keyboard shortcuts stay whole.
- **Mirrored window (`rtl.rs`):** title bar, ribbon (scrolls from the right), formula bar and Name Box, sheet tabs, status bar, task panes (on the left), Backstage, menus, context menus, dialogs and the message box. Every `egui::Grid` goes through `rtl::grid`, which avoids the NaN widget rectangles a plain Grid produces in a right-aligned layout (they panic egui's debug assertion). The sheet itself stays a document setting (Page Layout › Sheet Right-to-Left), not an interface one.
- **Fonts:** egui shapes one run per font face, so an interface face that also covers Arabic would take a whole label as one run. For Arabic the interface faces leave Arabic out and the system Arabic faces follow (Segoe UI, Tahoma, Geeza Pro, Noto Sans Arabic); switching to or from Arabic rebuilds the fonts (`theme::FontPlan`).
- **Strings that were hard-coded English** (dialog fields and bodies, menus, task panes, status bar, filter and context menus, message box, title bar) now go through the catalog, for every language.
- **Locale:** `ar` and every `ar-*` system locale, a saved choice and a switcher entry. The web build keeps English for an Arabic browser (it has no system fonts).
- **Command palette** also matches typed Arabic.

title: CSV import: From Text/CSV, sep=, apostrophes, quotes in Text to Columns and exponents match Excel
author: iluebbe
body:
## Problem

I tested CSV and text import against Excel 365 on Windows (de-DE UI). The test covered File › Open, Data › From Text/CSV (`data.fromTextCsv`), paste with Text to Columns, and NUMBERVALUE / TEXTSPLIT. It used about 60 variant files: delimiters `,` `;` TAB `|`, quoting, line ends, BOMs, en-US / de-DE / fr / de-CH / en-IN / zh-CN numbers and dates, and Windows-1252 / UTF-16 / GB18030. |---|---|---|---|---|

title: Control: Go To and Select over the control channel scroll the active cell into view
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #966.

The Go To dialog, the Name Box and the arrow keys all set `grid.ensure_visible` after moving the selection, which is what makes the grid scroll (the same flag #763 extended for the moving end). `engine.execute` in `control.rs` runs the command and stops there, so over the control channel, and through the MCP `select` tool that calls `selection.set` on it, the selection moves and the view stays where it was. Now the control channel sets the flag after `edit.goTo`, `edit.goToSpecial`, `selection.set` and `selection.move` succeed, both for `engine.execute` and for a command named as the method. I kept it to the commands that navigate rather than "any command that moves the active cell", so things like `sheet.activate` keep the sheet's saved scroll; happy to switch if you'd rather have the broader rule. `docs/control-protocol.md` mentions it.

Validation:
- `selection_scroll.rs`: two new tests drive `control::handle` in egui_kittest: `edit.goTo` to Z300 must leave Z300 on screen (and going back to A1 must bring A1 back), and `selection.set` to BZ150:CA160 must show BZ150. Both fail on main (the active cell moves, the cell is not visible) and pass here; dropping `edit.goTo` from the list makes the Go To test fail again.
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui --test selection_scroll`, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

title: Fix temporary-save collisions and silent AutoSave failures
author: nevicia2010-hub
body:
Saving a workbook currently writes through a fixed `<path>.sctmp` sibling. An unrelated file at that name is overwritten and removed; a symlink can redirect the write into another file. AutoSave also discards save errors and only recognizes a lowercase `.xlsx` suffix.

This change exclusively creates a unique sibling, syncs it before replacement, preserves existing file permissions and cleans up only its own temporary file on failure. AutoSave reuses OOXML format detection (`.xlsx/.xlsm/.xltx/.xltm`, case-insensitive), keeps dirty edits on error, disables further attempts and shows an actionable message (English/Chinese). Users explicitly re-enable it after saving.

- Existing-file and symlink regression tests fail on the original writer and pass after the fix; permission preservation and failed-save cleanup are covered.
- AutoSave regressions fail on the original block with a real egui frame, then pass for failed saves and supported filename variants.

- Native macOS UI: uppercase `.XLSM` autosaves a synthetic edit; blocking the destination shows the Chinese failure message; restoring it and manually saving retains the unsaved edit.

Checked existing work: #450 only cleans up a failed fixed-name save; #480 confines automation paths; #493 addresses running Python cells. This does not duplicate those changes. No user documents or binary fixtures are included. Native Windows/Linux runtime behavior has not been tested locally.

title: Sheet tabs: Ctrl-drag (Cmd or Option on macOS) drops a copy of the sheet
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #971.

Dragging a sheet tab always sent a plain `sheet.move`, so there was no way to drop a copy the way Excel does, although `sheet.move` already copies (it is what Duplicate and Move or Copy use). The drop now reads the modifiers: with Ctrl held (Cmd on macOS, the same modifier the fill handle uses to copy) it sends `sheet.move` with `copy: true`, and the cursor shows the copy icon while dragging. Excel for Mac uses Option for this and the issue asks for Alt, so Option copies on macOS too; off macOS I left Alt out, since Excel on Windows uses Ctrl and many Linux window managers keep Alt-drag for themselves. Happy to switch if you'd rather have Alt everywhere.

One detail: a move's `to` indexes the list without the dragged sheet and a copy's indexes it with it, so to the right the copy is sent one further, so it lands exactly where the tab would have been moved.

Validation:
- `tabs::tests::tab_dropped_with_the_copy_modifier_leaves_a_copy_where_a_move_would_land`: fails on main (the drop moves A instead of copying: `["B", "A", "C"]`), passes here; it also fails if the copy reuses the move index (`["A", "A (2)", "B", "C"]`)
- `tabs::tests::copy_drop_modifier_is_ctrl_or_cmd_or_option_on_mac`: new, pins which modifiers copy on each platform
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui --lib tabs::tests`, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `docs/ui-parity.md` updated (sheet tabs row, revision history)

title: Fonts: start the installed-font scan in the app (installed fonts were never listed or rendered)
author: richard1912
body:
## Summary
The desktop app (`apps/gridcraft/src/main.rs:353`) and the web app set up their context with `SheetApp::setup_context_for_language`, not `SheetApp::setup_context`, and only `setup_context` called `fonts::start_scan()`. So in the real app the installed-font catalog was never built:

- the Format Cells font list (`fonts::families()`) only ever showed the standard names;
- cells formatted with an installed font (Comic Sans MS, Segoe Script, Wingdingsâ€¦) never rendered in it, because nothing was ever bound (the binding in `SheetApp::logic` waits for `fonts::scan_done()`, which never became true).

This starts the scan in `setup_context_for_language` too. `start_scan` is once-only, so the later calls (language change) are no-ops, and it's a no-op on wasm.

## Validation (Windows 11)
- The scan finds 194 families on this machine in ~0.3 s on its background thread.
- Real app: Comic Sans MS (bold) and Wingdings (italic) in cells now render in those fonts; autofit sizes the column to the Comic Sans text; editing, and a whole-column autofit with Segoe Script, run fine.
- New `crates/ui-egui/tests/font_scan_starts.rs`: `setup_context_for_language` starts the scan. Fails on main (times out waiting for `scan_done`), passes here.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask wasm`.

## One thing to know
With the scan actually running, `cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui` on Windows can occasionally panic in `header_autofit` ("FontFamily â€¦ is not bound to any fonts"), passing on rerun. Cause: `fonts::BOUND` is process-wide while each kittest harness has its own `egui::Context`, so parallel tests race once the scan finds a font the tests use (Calibri is installed on Windows, not on macOS/Linux CI, which is why it never showed up). It's a test-isolation issue, not an app one (one context per app), but worth a follow-up: e.g. keying the bound set per `Context`, or having tests build their font definitions wi…

title: Use local clock time and validate financial dates in the workbook epoch
author: nevicia2010-hub
body:
NOW/TODAY and yearless date entry currently use UTC, so they can show the wrong hour, day or year for the host's timezone. This uses the local offset at the sampled instant: chrono on native platforms and the browser Date offset on WASM.

Financial calculations reuse upstream #1507's workbook-aware securities implementation. The remaining shared-helper fixes reject negative fractional date inputs before truncation, validate input bounds with `max_serial(workbook_date_system)`, and allow valid intermediate coupon dates before the 1904 epoch. For example, COUPPCD for 1904-01-02 with maturity 1905-06-30 returns -1; an invalid 1904 DISC date beyond 9999-12-31 returns #NUM!.

Synchronized with main `d8c5f5885fc5320f8f1023d5fdc9f484a185ba86` (0.12.1), preserving upstream chrono/calendar, financial, formula and window changes. The previously overlapping financial normalization is absent; current main still lacks these local-clock and boundary fixes.

- All 16 financial tests passed, including retained upstream tests, both date systems, negative/fractional input handling, pre-epoch coupon results and input upper limits.
- Isolated timezone child processes cover Rome, New York and Kolkata, including winter/summer offsets, without changing the parent environment.
- Required font validation stayed enabled. The external font input is pinned to upstream release revision `b076417b5880bd4154bd22f00695b1d28c6bea83`, with manifest SHA256 checks. No font files are committed.

title: Wildcards: one matcher for criteria, lookups, SEARCH, Find & Replace and filters, following Excel 365
author: iluebbe
body:
## Summary

GridCraft had two wildcard matchers:
- the criteria functions, lookups and SEARCH used `functions/src/criteria.rs`;
- Find & Replace, AutoFilter and Advanced Filter used a copy in `engine/src/cmd/edit.rs` (`edit::wildcard`).

The copies disagreed with each other, and each differed from Excel 365 in places. This PR makes one matcher, `gridcraft_functions::Wildcard`, and moves every caller to it. It follows the rules measured in Excel 365.

## Observed

The values `x~`, `y`, `ab`, `a~b`, `a*b`, `axb`, `İ`, `i`, `I`, `ı`, `ß`, `~`, `hello`, `HELLO`, `a?b`, `~x` and `xyz~` were run through COUNTIF, MATCH, XLOOKUP, VLOOKUP, SEARCH, AutoFilter "equals", `Range.Find` (whole and part, with and without MatchCase) and `Range.Replace` in Excel 365. "functions" is GridCraft's criteria/lookup matcher, "engine" is GridCraft's Find/AutoFilter copy, both on main before this PR.

| case | Excel 365 | GridCraft before |
|---|---|---|
| trailing `~`: `COUNTIF(…,"?~")` | 7: every one-character value; `x~` doesn't match (the trailing `~` is dropped) | functions: 1 (`x~`); engine: drops it |
| `MATCH("x~",…,0)` | `#N/A` (it looks for `x`) | `x~` |
| criterion without `*`/`?`: `COUNTIF(…,"a~b")`, `"~~"`, `"h~ello"` | counts `a~b`; 0; 0 (compared as they are) | `ab`; `~`; `hello` (read as escapes) |
| lookups and SEARCH: `MATCH("a~b",…,0)` | `ab` (`~` escapes any character) | `ab` |
| Find `a~b` (whole cell) | finds `ab` | engine: finds `a~b` (no `~` handling without `*`/`?`) |
| `COUNTIF(…,"i")`, `SEARCH("i","qİq")` | `i`, `I` only; `#VALUE!` | functions: also `İ`; 2 |
| `?` against `İ` (AutoFilter `=?`) | matches | engine: hidden (`İ` lowercases to two characters) |
| Replace `h*o` with `X` in `hello world` | `X world` | counted as replaced, cell unchanged (the pattern text was replaced literally) |
| Replace `l*`; `a?b` in `xaxbyazb`; `~*` → `+` in `a*b*c` | `heX`; `xXyX`; `a+b+c` | all three unchanged (the pattern text was searched literally) |

title: Functions: GROUPBY / PIVOTBY subtotals, sorting, headers, blanks and several functions match Excel 365 (builds on #665)
author: iluebbe
body:
**Builds on #665** (GROUPBY / PIVOTBY with a LAMBDA, PERCENTOF or CONCAT): this branch contains its commit `74e4ba4`, so please merge #665 first. After that, this PR shows only its own seven commits.

## Problem

I compared GROUPBY and PIVOTBY with Excel 365 on Windows (German UI): every cell of every spill range, for 271 formulas. The data had blanks, `""`, case variants, text numbers, `#N/A`, booleans, dates, negatives and duplicates. On main only 47 of them matched; this PR brings it to 244. I found no existing issue or PR for these differences. The labels below are English; German Excel shows them as `Gesamt` / `Gesamtergebnis`.

**1. Total depth 2 / -2 gave no subtotals.** With two or more key fields, a depth of 2 adds a subtotal for each outer group, after the group (2) or before it with the grand total first (-2). GridCraft used only the sign. A depth larger than the number of key fields is `#VALUE!` in Excel; GridCraft returned a grand total.

| formula | Excel 365 | main |
|---|---|---|
| `=GROUPBY({"a","x";"a","y";"b","x"},{1;2;3},SUM,,2)` | a x 1 / a y 2 / **a · 3** / b x 3 / **b · 3** / Grand Total · 6 | a x 1 / a y 2 / b x 3 / Total · 6 |
| `=PIVOTBY({"a";"b";"a"},{"x","p";"y","p";"x","q"},{1;2;3},SUM,,,,2)` | a subtotal column after each outer column group | no subtotal columns |
| `=GROUPBY({"a";"b"},{1;2},SUM,,2)` | `#VALUE!` | a 1 / b 2 / Total 3 |

**2. Sort orders.** PIVOTBY ignored sorting by values. With several key fields, sorting by an inner field or by value flattened the groups. A sort array used only its first number.

| formula | Excel 365 | main |
|---|---|---|
| `=PIVOTBY({"a";"b";"c"},{"x";"x";"y"},{3;1;2},SUM,,,2)` | rows b, c, a (by the total column) | a, b, c |
| `=PIVOTBY({"a";"b";"c"},{"x";"y";"z"},{3;1;2},SUM,,,,,2)` | columns y, z, x (by the total row) | x, y, z |
| `=GROUPBY({"b","x";"a","y";"b","a";"a","b"},{1;2;3;4},SUM,,0,2)` | a b 4, a y 2, b a 3, b x 1 (sorted within each group) | b a 3, a b 4, b x 1, a y 2 |

title: Calc: a contested spill area stays with its array on full recalc and reopening (#964)
author: quantmind-br
body:
Fixes #964.

When two dynamic arrays want the same cells, entering the second one gives it `#SPILL!` and the first keeps its area. A full recalculation (F9, and the one that runs when a file is opened) laid the arrays out again in reading order, so the area went to whichever anchor came first. This changes it so the result is the same as after entering the formulas.

- **Calc** (`recalc.rs`): `recalc_all` remembers what the layout it clears looked like: which formulas spilled and which ones showed `#SPILL!`. `run` writes arrays back in this order: formulas that already spill there first, formulas that were `#SPILL!` last, reading order within each group. Incremental recalculation passes an empty `Prior`, so the order there doesn't change. The `full` flag is replaced by `Prior`; it only guarded an empty `if`.
- **XLSX reader** (`sheet_read.rs`): a dynamic array (`cm`) with a multi-cell `ref` gets that area back in `spill_ranges`, so recalculating on open knows it was spilling. This is needed because the file can't cache `#SPILL!` (it holds `#VALUE!`), so on its own the calc change does nothing for reopened files.

Tests, each failing on `main`:
- `calc::tests::a_full_recalc_keeps_a_spill_with_the_formula_already_spilling_there` (F9)
- `engine::tests::a_contested_spill_area_stays_with_its_array_after_reopening` (save and reopen). It still fails with only the calc change.

Checks: `cargo xtask ci`. The command-sequence fuzz soak (`GRIDCRAFT_FUZZ_SEEDS=200 GRIDCRAFT_FUZZ_STEPS=60 GRIDCRAFT_FUZZ_KEEP_GOING=1`, release) fails the same seeds on this branch as on `main`: one, seed 138, on the `[undo]` invariant. It shrinks to a single `view.pageBreakPreview` and has nothing to do with spills. The shrunk sequence from #964 now gives `#SPILL!` in memory, after a full recalc and after an XLSX round trip. On #447, which shifts the random sequence, the soak passes with this fix.

I couldn't check what Excel does on Ctrl+Alt+F9. This follows what Excel shows when the second array…

title: Financial functions: dates follow the workbook's date system (1904 workbooks)
author: iluebbe
body:
## Summary

In a workbook that uses the 1904 date system, the securities functions read every date 1462 days off, and most of their results were wrong. These are the coupon, bond, discount, T-bill, odd-period and AMOR* functions. Their date helpers in `crates/functions/src/financial.rs` were fixed to the 1900 system. They now use the workbook's date system, like DATE and EOMONTH do.

## Observed

Excel 365, a new workbook with `Date1904 = True`:

| formula | Excel 365 | GridCraft (main) |
|---|---|---|
| `=COUPNCD(DATE(2011,3,15),DATE(2011,11,30),2)` | 39232 | 39231 |
| `=COUPPCD(DATE(2011,3,15),DATE(2011,11,30),4,0)` | 39140 | 39141 |
| `=COUPDAYBS(DATE(2011,3,15),DATE(2011,11,30),4,0)` | 15 | 14 |

To measure it, I ran 1,184 formulas in a 1900 and a 1904 workbook through Excel 365 and `gridcraft-cli check`. They cover COUPPCD, COUPNCD, COUPDAYS, COUPDAYBS, COUPDAYSNC, COUPNUM, PRICE, YIELD, DURATION, MDURATION, DISC, PRICEDISC, YIELDDISC, INTRATE, RECEIVED, ACCRINT, ACCRINTM, PRICEMAT, YIELDMAT, ODDF*/ODDL*, AMORDEGRC, AMORLINC and TBILL*, with bases 0–4, frequencies 1, 2 and 4, and six date pairs.

| | mismatches on main | with this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 1900 workbook | 169 | 169 (unchanged) |
| 1904 workbook | 543 | 209 |

Of the 209 left:
- 159 are cells that also differ in the 1900 workbook. They are existing differences, not about the date system.
- 50 are cases where Excel's own 1904 result differs from its own 1900 result for the same calendar dates, mostly 30/360 at month ends. For example, `DISC(DATE(2012,5,30),DATE(2013,2,28),97.975,100,0)` is 0.02720 in 1900 and 0.02690 in 1904. GridCraft now gives the same result in both systems.
- 4 cells matched in 1904 only by accident before (PRICE/YIELD/DURATION/MDURATION with basis 2 on 29 February). They differ in the 1900 workbook on main already, and now differ in both.

## Cause

`ymd` and `serial` in `financial.rs` called `datetime_from_serial(DateSystem::D1900, …)` and `serial_from_ymd(DateSystem::D1900, …)`…

title: XLSX export: a picture shared by several sheets is one media part (#985)
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #985

## Cause

`write_sheet` (`crates/xlsx/src/sheet_write.rs`) gave every picture of every drawing its own part: `out.images += 1`, `xl/media/image{N}.{ext}` with a copy of the bytes, and a relationship to it. Excel stores a picture that appears on several sheets (a copied sheet, a copied picture) once and lets each drawing point to it, so opening and saving such a workbook multiplied the media.

## Fix

`Out::image_part(ext, data)` (`crates/xlsx/src/write.rs`) returns the file name of an `xl/media/image*.{ext}` part that already holds exactly these bytes, and writes a new numbered part only when there is none. The drawing writer uses it, so every drawing's relationship targets the shared part. A picture is only shared when the extension and all bytes are equal, so different pictures (even of the same length) stay separate. The in-cell pictures of `richdata.rs` are separate parts and are not touched.

## Verified

The reporter's fixture (`gc_shared_image.xlsx`: one 173,298-byte PNG on four sheets), `gridcraft-cli run --in gc_shared_image.xlsx --out out.xlsx`:

| | `main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `out.xlsx` size | 704,384 bytes | 183,983 bytes (the input is 183,976) |
| `xl/media` | `image1.png` … `image4.png` | `image1.png` |
| drawing relationships | each to its own copy | all four to `image1.png` |

New `crates/xlsx/src/tests/shared_media.rs`:

- `a_picture_on_several_sheets_is_one_media_part`: picture A on three sheets (twice on one), picture B on one: two media parts instead of five (it fails on `main` with 5), every drawing relationship resolves to an existing part, the sheets that show A point to the same part, the pictures read back with the right bytes on the right sheets, and saving what was read back is stable.
- `different_pictures_with_the_same_length_stay_separate`: passes before and after (guards the equality check).

`cargo xtask ci` passes.

Two places classified number formats by looking for letters in the code text, and two renderers each kept their own colour table. Both now go through numfmt.

| `CELL("format")` of `$#,##0_);[Red]($#,##0)` | `C0-` (German Excel: `.0-`, because `$` isn't its currency) | `S0` |

title: Fix Command-click and Shift-click references during formula entry
author: pourie-he
body:
While editing a formula such as `=SUM(`, the cell-click handler returns before applying selection modifiers. After clicking C3, Command-clicking F7 replaces C3 instead of adding an argument, and Shift-clicking F7 also replaces it instead of extending the range.

This change makes Command/Ctrl-click append another argument using the edit's locale separator (`=SUM(C3,F7`) and makes Shift-click extend from a fixed anchor on the current sheet (`=SUM(C3:F7`). Plain clicks still replace the latest pointed reference. Dragging and keyboard continuation keep a separate moving endpoint, and manual typing clears the anchor. Sheet qualifiers are retained for mouse pointing.

Seven new pointer-event regressions cover the reported failures, repeated and reversed selections, previous arguments, ordinary replacement, manual separators, Spanish syntax, sheet changes and arrows after Shift-click. The existing drag test now checks the fixed anchor and moving endpoint.

Validation:

- Both reported regressions failed on the original code and pass with the fix.
- All 13 selection tests pass.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes all eight gates: formatting, clippy, workspace tests, assets, layers, wasm, parity and keytips (1,608 tests passed; one ignored).
- Offscreen UI renders were inspected for both modifier sequences. Native macOS input automation was unavailable, so this does not claim a manual test of the installed app.

The affected progress docs are updated without changing readiness estimates. Contributor credit opts @pourie-he into public GitHub profile-name synchronization, as requested.

title: Charts: box & whisker quartiles follow the chart's quartile method, as Excel draws them; one percentile implementation
author: iluebbe
body:
## Summary

GridCraft writes every box & whisker chart with `quartileMethod="exclusive"`, which is Excel's default, but draws it with inclusive quartiles. Excel draws the same chart with exclusive quartiles. The chart now stores the method, reads it from files, draws with it, and `chart.set` can change it.

The same percentile math was implemented three times: in the worksheet functions, in the conditional-formatting thresholds and in the chart. All three now share one implementation in `gridcraft_core::stats`.

## Observed

Values 1–6 in a box & whisker chart. GridCraft is main `84acf62`.

| | Excel 365 | GridCraft |
|---|---|---|
| box, file says `exclusive` | 1.75 to 5.25 | 2.25 to 4.75 |
| box, file says `inclusive` | 2.25 to 4.75 | 2.25 to 4.75 (the method isn't read, and is written back as `exclusive`) |

How I checked: I exported Excel 365's charts as PNG and converted the box edges to values, calibrated at the whisker caps, which sit at the minimum and maximum. Excel draws QUARTILE.EXC for Exclusive and QUARTILE.INC for Inclusive:

| data | Exclusive Q1 / Q3 | Inclusive Q1 / Q3 |
|---|---|---|
| 1–5 | 1.5 / 4.5 | 2 / 4 |
| 1–6 | 1.75 / 5.25 | 2.25 / 4.75 |
| 1–7 | 2 / 6 | 2.5 / 5.5 |
| 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 | – | 1.25 / 4.5 |

For colour scales and data bars, Excel computes percentile thresholds with PERCENTILE.INC. I checked this with a 3-colour scale on 1–6 whose midpoint is the 25th percentile: Excel paints the 2 as FFCCCC, 80 % of the way from red to white, which puts the midpoint at 2.25. GridCraft already did this, and still does.

title: Engine: formulas.evaluate refuses what cell entry refuses, saying why
author: quantmind-br
body:
`formulas.evaluate`, which `gridcraft-cli eval` and MCP's `evaluate_formula` go through, turned every formula that doesn't parse into `#NAME?`. That hides the cause. `=SUM(1;2)`, typed with the `;` a French or German Excel uses, looked like an unknown function (reported in https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/issues/430#issuecomment-6145127829).

The command now accepts exactly what typing the formula into a cell accepts, and refuses the rest with `cell.set`'s messages:

| Input | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `=SUM(1;2)` | `#NAME?` | error: There's a problem with this formula: expected `,` or `)`, found Semicolon |
| `=DATEDIF(1,2)` | `#VALUE!` | error: DATEDIF has too few arguments. Use DATEDIF(start_date, end_date, unit) |
| `=SUM(1,2` | `#NAME?` | `3` (missing parentheses are closed, as on entry) |
| `=SOMME(1,2)` | `#NAME?` | `#NAME?` (unknown function, as in Excel) |

The CLI prints the error to stderr and exits 1. MCP returns it with `isError: true`. The parsing from `input_to_cell` moved into `parse_typed_formula`, and `check_arg_counts` became `pub(crate)`, so `cell.set` and `formulas.evaluate` share them; `cell.set` behaves as before. The other callers of `gridcraft_calc::evaluate` (conditional formats, data validation, charts, Name Manager previews, sparklines) evaluate formulas that were checked when they were entered, so they still get a value.

`evaluate_refuses_what_entry_refuses_and_says_why` fails on `main`. Checks: `cargo xtask ci` (1600 tests), plus the CLI and MCP run by hand.

title: Fonts: scan the Flatpak host font folders and $XDG_DATA_HOME/fonts (#1069)
author: musaad-sharikh
body:
Part of #1069. Depends on #974.

This PR leaves #1069 open. It adds the folders a Flatpak sandbox mounts the host's fonts at; #974 starts the scan that reads them. A host font becomes usable in the Flatpak only with both merged, and on its own this PR has no visible effect in the app. After both, #1069 still names two causes this PR does not touch: the role candidates in `theme.rs` and an Arabic fallback face (#931).

## Problem

Inside the Flatpak sandbox `/usr/share/fonts` is the runtime's, and the fonts installed on the machine are mounted at `/run/host/fonts`, `/run/host/local-fonts` and `/run/host/user-fonts`. `system_font_dirs()` read none of them, so no font installed on the host could reach the font lists or be bound to a cell.

## Change

Everything is in `crates/ui-egui/src/fonts.rs`, in four commits.

The first (`5d7961c`) changes the folder list; the second (`c41767e`) adds tests only. On Linux and the BSDs the scan now also reads:

- `/run/host/fonts`, `/run/host/local-fonts`, `/run/host/user-fonts`
- `$XDG_DATA_HOME/fonts`, when it is an absolute path other than `~/.local/share`

A folder that does not exist is skipped. No sandbox permission is added: Flatpak exposes these folders by default.

The third (`46dea87`) makes `scan_dirs` read a folder once when it is visible at several paths. When the app is allowed the user font folder (`--filesystem=xdg-data/fonts`), Flatpak shows that one folder at `/run/host/user-fonts`, `~/.local/share/fonts` and `$XDG_DATA_HOME/fonts`. These are bind mounts with the same device and inode, but `canonicalize` returns three different paths, so the folder was read three times. A folder is now known by its device and inode on Unix, else by its canonical path. A folder whose metadata can't be read, or that reports inode 0, falls back to its path, so two different folders are never taken for one. No `unsafe` and no new dependency (`std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt`).

The fourth (`ce75993`) adds a test for the inode-0 fallback…

title: Data validation: a list typed without quotes is saved as a quoted list, and an unknown type is refused
author: CouchRiv
body:
Found while driving GridCraft 0.6.1 over MCP. `data.validation {type: "list", formula1: "Open,In progress,Closed"}` is how Excel's Source box takes a list and how an agent naturally writes it. It works inside GridCraft (`data.validate` accepts "In progress"), but the rule is saved as

```xml
<formula1>Open,In progress,Closed</formula1>
```

In a file an inline list is a quoted string literal. Excel writes `"Open,In progress,Closed"`, openpyxl documents `formula1='"Dog,Cat,Bat"'` (<https://openpyxl.readthedocs.io/en/stable/validation.html>), and GridCraft's own reader treats an unquoted list `formula1` as a formula (`read_validation` prefixes it with `=`). This shows without Excel: on `main`, save and reopen in GridCraft, and the rule's first item has become `=Open`, so "Open" is refused and "=Open" accepted.

## What changed

All in `crates/engine/src/cmd/data.rs`.
- `validation`: for a `list` rule, the source goes through `list_source`. A literal list typed without quotes is stored as the quoted string a file holds, with inner quotes doubled (`Say "hi",Bye` becomes `"Say ""hi"",Bye"`). It is stored as before when it is a formula (typed with `=`), a reference (`$A$1:$A$3`), a name, a sheet-qualified range (`Sheet2!A1:A3`), already quoted, or empty. Other rule types are unchanged.
- "Literal list" is the test `list_items` already used to choose between splitting and evaluating (quoted, or no `!` and not a bare reference or name). It moves into `is_literal_list` so both use the same rule, and GridCraft's reading of a rule doesn't change.
- `list_items` reads a quoted list as a string literal: `""` inside stands for one `"`. Without this, an item with a quote would read back as `Say ""hi""` after the change; it also reads such a list from a file correctly. Unquoted sources split as before.

title: Format: Row Height and Column Width say pixels, and take points like Excel
author: CouchRiv
body:
Found while driving GridCraft 0.6.1 over MCP. `list_commands` documents `home.rowHeight` as `height: 20 (points on screen)` and `home.columnWidth` as `width: 64 (points) | chars: 8.43`, but both values are pixels at 96 dpi, the model's unit. An agent that follows the docs, or Excel's habits, gets a 30 pt row saved as `ht="22.5"`. The range check disagrees with its own message too: `height: 500` is accepted (saved as 375 pt) while `height: 600` fails with "Row height must be between 0 and 409 points."

## Who sends what (why pixels stay the unit)

Before choosing, I checked every caller:

| caller | sends | unit |
|---|---|---|
| header drag (`ui-egui/src/grid.rs`) | `height` / `width` | pixels (toast `Height: 22.50 (30 pixels)`) |
| Row Height dialog (`ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs`) | `height` | pixels, labelled "Row height (pixels):" |
| Column Width dialog | `chars` | characters |
| Standard Width dialog | `width` (`home.defaultWidth`) | pixels, labelled "Standard column width (pixels):" |
| sample workbooks, engine and UI tests | `height` / `width` | pixels |
| XLSX | `px_to_pt` on write, `pt_to_px` on read | pixels in the model |

So the UI has no unit bug: every caller already sends pixels, and only the parameter docs and the error messages were wrong. Changing `height` to points would have broken the drags, the dialogs, the samples and the tests, so this keeps pixels and adds Excel's unit next to them.

title: MCP: read_range returns long ranges in pages, and tool results are compact JSON
author: CouchRiv
body:
Reading an export is the first thing an agent does with a workbook, and the engine is fast at it, but the MCP reply wasn't usable at size. `read_range` without `range` returned the whole used range in one reply (up to the 1,000,000-cell limit), and every tool result was pretty-printed, one cell value per line. On a synthetic 15,000 × 30 CSV (generated data), `read_range {}` was one text block of 6,582,075 characters on 480,038 lines, with nothing telling the agent how to ask for less. MCP clients cap tool output, so in practice the agent got a truncated or spilled-to-disk result.

## What changed

Two independent commits: pagination first, compact tool-result JSON second. Pagination can land without compact JSON if indented output should be retained, but must include the follow-up commit that rejects invalid maxCells values.

**1. Paging** (`MCP: read_range returns long ranges in pages`)
- `sheet.read` takes `maxCells`, a positive integer; zero, negative and non-integer values return an error, including on an empty sheet. It reads whole rows up to that many cells (at least one row, so a row wider than `maxCells` still comes back whole). When the range is longer it adds `truncated: true`, `totalRows` (rows of the whole range) and `next`, the remaining rows as a sheet-qualified range (`'My Data'!A334:AD15001`). Passing `next` back as `range` reads on from there whatever the active sheet is. Without `maxCells` the command behaves exactly as before, so the control channel and CLI are unchanged.
- The MCP `read_range` tool exposes `maxCells` and passes 5,000 when the caller gives none. The 1,000,000-cell limit still applies to what is read.
- `params` text, the tool description, `docs/mcp.md` and `docs/control-protocol.md` describe it.

**2. Compact JSON** (`MCP: tool results as compact JSON`)
- `ToolResult::json` uses `serde_json::to_string` instead of `to_string_pretty`. Agents parse the JSON either way; indented, 100 rows × 30 columns took 44,368 characters on 3,238 l…

title: Charts: multi-level category axes (year beside month) read, drawn and written back
author: Lexx143
body:
A category range two or more columns wide beside a column of values (year beside month, what Excel saves as `multiLvlStrRef`) was read as one flat list: a 36-row, 2-column range became 72 categories, so the series were squeezed into the left half of the plot with the years and months mixed on one row. Saving wrote the range back as a plain `strRef` with the flattened cache, so the two-level axis was lost for Excel too. This is the "multi-level categories" item of `docs/chart-parity.md` § Work.

**What changes**

- `gridcraft_core::category_levels`: the shape of a category range beside its values (levels are the columns when the points run down the rows, the rows when they run along the columns; the innermost level is the column or row nearest the values, up to three outer levels are kept). Shared by the chart and xlsx crates.
- `ChartData.category_levels` (serde default): the outer levels, nearest the labels first, one entry per category, non-empty where a group starts, as the cells are. `resolve` fills it from the range; a plain column is unchanged.
- Rendering: the outer levels are drawn in rows under the labels, each group's name centred under its categories with a separator at every group boundary, as Excel draws them; in bar charts they stand in columns beside the labels. Forecast slots stay in the last group.
- XLSX: `<c:cat>` is written as `multiLvlStrRef` with `multiLvlStrCache` (innermost level first, outer levels with only the cells that start a group), so the axis survives a round trip; reading already kept the reference.

Formulas stay on the canonical en-US locale, like every interface language except Spanish.

title: Compare comment contents in XLSX fidelity checks
author: jonathanwxh-cell

title: fix(grid): keep cursor stable during cell dragging (#936)
author: Zaxaerith
body:
## Problem

Dragging a cell selection could switch the requested cursor between Cell, Move and Crosshair as the pointer crossed the changing selection border and fill handle. Other grid drags could also lose their cursor over unrelated hover targets.

## Root cause

The hover cursor block ran before the grid processed drag state changes, and continued hit-testing during active drags. It could overwrite the cursor for the actual operation and miss the first drag frame.

## Changes

- Decide the grid cursor after interaction updates the drag state, including drag start and release.
- Give a recognized, held drag its own cursor: Cell for selection, Crosshair for fill, Move for cell/column/object moves, the existing axis cursors for resizing and freezing, and the existing corner cursor for object resizing. Whole-line selection keeps the default header cursor.
- Retain normal hover hit-testing when no drag is active, including presses below egui's threshold and transient state left by a click. Pen and Eraser keep their Crosshair over cells.
- Preserve hover-cell bookkeeping for cell notes independently of cursor ownership, including with Draw tools active.
- Update the affected UI parity entry without changing interaction timing or adding persistent state.

## Regression tests

`crates/ui-egui/tests/drag_cursor.rs` drives the real SheetApp through egui pointer press, movement and release events, asserting `platform_output.cursor_icon` on movement and following idle frames. It also checks selection, filled values, moved values/columns, resized dimensions, freeze counts and ink creation.

Coverage includes selection borders and fill handles, frozen panes, leaving the grid, RTL coordinates, fill, moves, both resize/freeze axes, column reordering, whole-line selection, object move/resize, Draw cursors and hover tracking, and a rapid press following a click.
