title: Insert: new rows, columns and cells take the formats of the cells above or to the left
author: CouchRiv
body:
`home.insertRows`, `home.insertColumns` and `home.insertCells` (shift down or right) leave the new cells unformatted. Only the line settings of the row above or the column to the left were copied (`LineInfo`: height or width, whole-line style). Formats set on cells, which is how Excel, openpyxl and most generators store borders, fills and number formats, were lost: a row inserted into a bordered, filled list comes out as a white strip with no borders and General numbers, and an agent has to repair it cell by cell.

Excel gives inserted cells the formats of the cells above or to the left by default ("Format Same As Above"). `Range.Insert`'s `CopyOrigin` defaults to `xlFormatFromLeftOrAbove` (<https://learn.microsoft.com/office/vba/api/excel.range.insert>), and the example on that page shows the default copies from a header row too: to take the row below instead you pass `xlFormatFromRightOrBelow`. So this keeps the simple rule, header row included.

## What changed

All in `crates/engine/src/cmd/sheet.rs`, plus regression tests and `docs/ui-parity.md`.

- New `format_same_as_before`: gives every inserted cell the style of the cell before it across the insert, i.e. the row above for rows and for cells shifted down, the column to the left for columns and for cells shifted right. Only the `StyleId`: values, formulas, comments, hyperlinks and merges stay behind.
- `insert_lines` calls it after the existing `LineInfo` copy, over the whole row or column. `insert_cells` calls it for the inserted block only (its columns for a shift down, its rows for a shift right). `shift: row|column` already goes through `insert_lines`.
- Row 1 and column A have nothing before them: inserts there store no format, the same as the existing `LineInfo` copy.
- A new cell is stored only when the copied style differs from what its row or column format already gives it, so a whole-row format (a row style plus the same style on its cells) adds no cells.

title: CSV export: check the size cap before each field, not after the row (#1023)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1023.

`write_csv_limited` compared the output with the byte cap only after a whole row was written, so one wide row of long fields could grow far past the cap before the export was refused. Quoted fields also went through `t.replace('"', "\"\"")`, which built a second, unbounded copy of the text.

Now each field is measured before it is written: its exact output size (text, plus one byte per doubled quote, plus the two enclosing quotes when it is quoted) is added to what is already written, and the export stops with the same `IoError::TooLarge` "stopped at row N" error as soon as the next field would pass the cap. Quotes are doubled while the field is copied into the output, so no temporary copy is made. The existing row-end check stays for the CRLF. The `write_csv` doc comment is updated to match.

Scope: only the export path is changed; the up-front lower-bound check, the error text and the output of accepted exports are unchanged. `cell_text` still returns each field as a `String`, so one field's own text is not bounded here; that would need an API change.

Tests (in `the_cap_counts_the_bytes_the_cells_hold_and_accepted_exports_keep_every_position`):
- a row of ten 100-quote fields (202 bytes each when written) with a 500-byte cap is refused at the third field, and `cell_text` is called only three times (ten times before this change);
- exact boundary: one such field plus CRLF is accepted at a 204-byte cap (output is exactly 204 bytes) and refused at 203.

title: Keep chart cache point positions when a reference has blank edges (#1015)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1015.

`ref_values` in `crates/xlsx/src/chart.rs` intersected every chart reference with the sheet's used range, though its comment said this was only for whole columns/rows. The num/str cache writers then numbered the shortened list from 0 while keeping the original `<c:f>`. So for `Data!$A$3:$A$6` with only A4 filled, the cache held one point at `idx="0"` and `ptCount="1"`, where it should hold `idx="1"` and `ptCount="4"`. Leading blanks moved later values to lower indices, and trailing blanks made the point count smaller. Category, X and Y ranges filled to different extents fell out of line with each other.

The change:
- Explicit ranges are now used exactly as written. Every cell has its own position, blank or not.
- Whole-column (`$A:$A`) and whole-row references still stop at the used range so the cache stays bounded. Only the far end is cut. The start stays at row 1 or column A, so indices still match the reference.
- The `MAX_CACHE` limit is unchanged.

`chartex.rs` calls the same `ref_values`, so the chartex point lists get the same fix.

Tests (`crates/xlsx/src/tests/chart_ref_offsets.rs`), both fail on main:
- `explicit_range_keeps_leading_and_trailing_blanks`: `A3:A6` with only A4 set gives `[Empty, 5, Empty, Empty]`. Main gives `[5]`.
- `whole_column_still_stops_at_used_range_and_starts_at_top`: `$A:$A` gives four points that end at the last used row and start at row 1. Main gives `[5]`.

title: xlsx: keep the first group's series kind when importing a combination chart (#1014)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1014.

`read_chart` set `Series::kind` only for series in the second and later plot groups (`gi > 0`). The series of the first group were left with no kind, so a combination chart fell back to the positional default in `effective_kind` / `write_chart` (first series a column, every other untyped series a line). A first group with two column series drew and saved its second series as a line, and a line-first combination drew its first series as a column.

Now, when a chart has more than one plot group (the case that makes it `ChartKind::Combo`), every series gets its own group's kind, the first group's included. Single-group charts are unchanged (their series still have no kind of their own), and the secondary-axis detection still runs only for the later groups, as before. Rendering and export already use a series' own kind when it is set, so both follow from the import fix.

Tests in `crates/xlsx/src/tests/chart_combo_kinds.rs`:
- `first_group_with_two_columns_stays_columns`: a clustered column group with two series plus a line group; both column series stay `ColumnClustered`, the third is a line.
- `line_first_group_stays_a_line`: a line group followed by a column group; the first series stays a line, the second a column.

Both fail on main (the first group's series have no kind).

title: Fix row keys merging distinct text rows in UNIQUE and grouping (#1012)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1012.

`row_key` in `crates/functions/src/dynamic.rs` joined the per-value keys with an unescaped `U+0001`, so a text value containing that character could shift a column boundary: the rows `["a", "b\u{1}tc"]` and `["a\u{1}tb", "c"]` produced the same key and were merged.

Each part is now written as `<byte length>:<key>`, which cannot be ambiguous whatever the text contains. `key_of` is unchanged, so case-insensitive matching and the number/text distinction stay as they were.

`row_key` is the single helper behind every affected path (UNIQUE, including exactly-once mode, GROUPBY and both PIVOTBY axes), so the one change covers all of them.

Test: `unique_keeps_rows_containing_separator_apart` uses the two rows from the issue and expects UNIQUE to keep both; it returns one row without the fix. The existing `unique` test still covers ordinary case-insensitive duplicates.

title: Calc: cap zip2/zip3 broadcast output at MAX_CELLS (#1002)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1002.

`zip2` (arithmetic and comparison operators, `TEXT`) and `zip3` (array `IF`) broadcast the row and column counts of their inputs and then allocated `rows * cols` values with no limit. Two arrays that are each within the limit, such as `SEQUENCE(5000)` and `SEQUENCE(1,5000)`, could ask for a 25-million-cell result, and `rows * cols` could overflow on 32-bit/WASM targets.

Both helpers now check `(rows as u64).saturating_mul(cols as u64) > MAX_CELLS` before allocating and return `#NUM!` when the result would be too large. This is the same check and the same error the other array builders in `eval.rs` already use, for example range reads.

Test `broadcast_output_is_limited` covers each path named in the issue: arithmetic (`SEQUENCE(5000)*SEQUENCE(1,5000)`), array `IF` and `TEXT` all return `#NUM!`, and a broadcast within the limit still gives the right result.

title: Reject unparsable fields and out-of-grid output in Text to Columns (#998)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #998.

`data.textToColumns` had two problems:

1. **Parse errors became deletions.** Each field went through `input_to_cell(...).unwrap_or(None)`, so a field that isn't a valid formula (e.g. `=1+*`) took the same path as an empty field and cleared the destination cell. The error is now propagated with `?`. The edit runs on a copy of the workbook, so the command fails and nothing is written: the sheet and undo history stay as they were.
2. **No bounds check on the output.** Destination cells were built with `CellRef::new(dest.row + i, dest.col + j)`, which could land past the last row or column. Each output cell now goes through the existing `CellRef::offset`. If any cell would fall outside the sheet, the command fails with "The result doesn't fit on the sheet below and right of the destination." The wording matches the existing check in `analysis.rs` ("The report doesn't fit on the sheet below and right of the output cell.").

The delimited path and the fixed-width path both use this loop, so both get the fix.

Test: `text_to_columns_rejects_bad_fields_and_overflow_without_changes` in `crates/mcp/src/tests.rs` checks:
- a malformed formula field over populated cells fails, and the cells keep their values
- a split from `XFD1` (past the last column) fails and writes nothing
- a split from `D1048576` (past the last row) fails and writes nothing
- an ordinary split still works

Without the fix, all three failing cases would succeed.

title: Refuse a cut-paste whose destination does not fit instead of dropping cells (#997)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #997.

`paste_special` checked only the paste anchor. For a same-document cut with `what = all` it removed the source cells first (`take_cells`), and then skipped every destination cell whose `at.offset(..)` fell off the grid. Pasting a cut block near the last row or column, or transposing it there, lost the overflowing cells.

Fix: before `edit(..)` runs, a cut move checks that the far corner of the whole footprint (`tiles × h/w`, with transpose already applied to `h`/`w`) exists. If it does not, the command returns an error and changes nothing: source, destination, clipboard and undo history all stay as they were. `edit.paste` goes through `paste_special`, so it is covered too. Copy-paste (not cut) behaviour is unchanged; its partial paste is the separate report #580.

Test `cut_paste_that_overflows_the_grid_moves_nothing`:
- cuts A1:A2 and pastes it transposed at XFD1 (second column past XFD): error, A1:A2 intact;
- pastes it at A1048576 (second row past the last row): error, A1:A2 intact;
- pastes it at XFD1 without transpose, which fits: the move succeeds, which also shows the clipboard survived the refused pastes.

Without the fix the first paste returns Ok and A1:A2 are emptied.

title: fix(ui): commit a pointed formula on the sheet it was started on (#996)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #996.

Start a formula on one sheet, click another sheet's tab (or pick it in the All Sheets navigator) to point at a reference, then press Enter. The formula was written at the same address on the sheet you pointed at, and could overwrite what was there. Ctrl+Enter did the same with `range.fill`.

**Cause.** `commit_edit` checks the input against `ed.sheet`, the sheet the edit started on. But `cell.set` and `range.fill` write to whatever sheet is active, and in point mode that is the sheet being pointed at.

**Fix.**
- `commit_edit` switches back to `ed.sheet` before it writes. `sheet.activate` restores that sheet's saved selection, so Enter writes the edited cell and Ctrl+Enter fills the original selection. This is also how Excel works: when you commit, it goes back to the sheet where you started. Because every commit path goes through `commit_edit`, this covers Enter, Tab, Ctrl+Enter, Ctrl+Shift+Enter, the formula bar's check button, and Ctrl+PageUp/PageDown.
- `activate_sheet` (the tab strip and the navigator) now stops when `commit_edit` returns false, for example when a Stop validation rejects the value. Before, it switched sheets anyway and left the open edit on a different sheet. It now does what the other callers already do (`grid.rs`, `paper_view.rs`, `backstage.rs`): `if !app.commit_edit(..) { return; }`.

**Tests.**
- `tests/commit_after_pointing.rs`: point at a second sheet, then commit with Enter and with Ctrl+Enter (a 2x2 fill). The formula lands on the origin sheet, the origin sheet is active again, and the sheet you pointed at stays empty.
- `tabs::tests::a_rejected_commit_keeps_the_sheet_and_the_edit`: a value rejected by validation keeps both the sheet and the edit. After the value is corrected, switching sheets commits it on the first sheet and then changes sheets.

All three tests fail without the fix.

title: Size the list validation dropdown to up to 8 rows (#1089)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1089.

The in-cell dropdown of a list validation (`list_picker` in `crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs`) showed only about three items, even for a five-item list. The `ScrollArea` had only `max_height(200.0)`. Inside the popup `Area`, the space it gets comes from the previous frame's size, so it never grew past egui's default 64 px minimum scrolled height.

Changes:

1. **Height fits the list, up to 8 rows (Excel parity).** The new `list_picker_height` computes rows × 18 px plus item spacing for `min(items, 8)` rows. The scroll area gets that value as both `max_height` and `min_scrolled_height`. Lists of 8 or fewer items show every item with no scrollbar. Longer lists show 8 rows and scroll.
2. **Opens above the cell near the bottom of the window.** The issue's suggestion asks for this, and Excel does it. The popup is now taller, so near the bottom edge egui's screen constraint would push it up over the cell. When the rows don't fit below the cell but fit above it, the popup now opens above the cell. Right-to-left sheets keep their mirrored anchor (`RIGHT_TOP` / `RIGHT_BOTTOM`).

Only the validation dropdown changes. The other worksheet popups (filter, header menu) are not touched.

Tests:
- `list_picker_fits_up_to_eight_rows_then_scrolls` (unit, `grid.rs`): the height for 5 and 8 items, the cap for 30 items, and one row for an empty list.
- `validation_dropdown_fits_up_to_eight_items_then_scrolls` (`tests/popup_dismissal.rs`): opens real dropdowns through the arrow button. A 5-item popup is at least 5 rows high (it was about 64 px before). A 12-item popup is at least 8 rows high and shorter than 12 rows.
- `validation_dropdown_opens_above_a_cell_near_the_bottom_of_the_window`: an 8-item dropdown on the last visible row ends above that cell instead of covering it.

title: Respect workbook structure protection in sheet rename, move, copy, hide and unhide (#1049)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1049.

`sheet.rename` and `sheet.move` (including `copy: true`) never checked `wb.protected_structure`, so a workbook with Protect Workbook on could still have its sheets renamed, reordered or copied, from the sheet tab menu, the Rename Sheet and Move or Copy dialogs, or the command API. `home.insertSheet` and `home.deleteSheet` already refuse in that case.

The issue asks for the guard on all structure-changing handlers, so `sheet.hide` and `sheet.unhide` get it too: they had the same gap, and Excel's workbook structure protection blocks hiding and unhiding sheets as well.

Each handler now starts with the same check and error message as `insert_sheet` ("The workbook is protected and cannot be changed."). The UI paths all go through these commands, so they are covered too. Cell editing is not affected.

Test: `protected_structure_blocks_rename_move_copy_hide_and_unhide_sheet` in `cmd/review.rs` protects the workbook, checks that rename, move, copy, hide and unhide (with and without a `sheet`) fail and leave the sheet names, order, count and visibility unchanged, then unprotects and checks that each one works.

title: Formula pointing: keep the sheet qualifier when moving or extending with the keyboard (#1048)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1048.

When a formula is being edited on one sheet and the user points at another sheet, mouse pointing (`select_to_pointer`, `point_header`, the click path) writes a sheet-qualified reference such as `Sheet2!B2`. Keyboard pointing (`point_move`, reached from the formula bar's Arrow / Shift+Arrow handling) wrote only `B2` or `A1:B2`, so the reference silently became local to the formula's own sheet and calculated the wrong thing.

Changes in `crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs`:

- `point_move` now qualifies the pointed text with the displayed sheet's name when it is not the sheet being edited. It uses the same `ed.sheet != wb.active_sheet` check and `gridcraft_engine::formula::quote_sheet` as the mouse paths, so names that need quotes (`'My Data'!B2`) are quoted the same way.
- When extending with Shift+Arrow, the anchor came from parsing the current pointed text as a bare `RangeRef`. A qualified range (`Sheet2!A1:B2`) failed to parse, so the anchor was lost. The sheet prefix is now stripped before parsing.
- The text building is moved into a small pure helper, `point_ref_text`, so it can be unit tested without a UI.

Same-sheet pointing is unchanged.

Test: `keyboard_pointing_keeps_the_sheet_qualifier` covers a plain move to another sheet, a sheet name that needs quotes, extending right/down and up/left with a qualified range (checking the anchor is the opposite corner), and same-sheet controls.

  * Existing sheet-qualified references remain intact as you navigate, and cell contents are not changed by the reference-selection action.
  * Left and right arrow-key behavior respects right-to-left layouts, and arrow-key input is left untouched whe…

title: fix(mcp): advertise overwriting tools as destructive (#1046)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1046.

The shared `tool()` builder in `crates/mcp/src/tools.rs` hard-coded `"destructiveHint": false`, so every mutating tool in `tools/list` (including the generic `execute_command` dispatcher) told clients it only makes additive changes.

The builder now sets `destructiveHint` from a list of the tools that can overwrite or discard existing data:

- `execute_command`: it can run any command (clear, delete sheet, remove duplicates…), so it is marked destructive, as the issue recommends.
- `write_range`, `set_cell`, `format_range`, `sort_range`: overwrite cell contents, formats or row order.
- `undo`, `redo`: undo takes back entered data; redo reapplies an overwrite.
- `open_workbook`, `new_workbook`: replace the active workbook. `save_workbook`: overwrites the file on disk.

The other mutating tools stay `destructiveHint: false`, because they only add or change view state: `select` (selection only), `insert_chart` (adds a chart), `create_table` (without a header row it shifts the data down and refuses to push cells off the sheet), `filter` (hides rows). Read-only tools keep `readOnlyHint: true` / `destructiveHint: false`. Authorization is unchanged; these are only hints.

Test: `destructive_hint_matches_capability` checks the hints of every tool in `tool_definitions()`: read-only tools are never destructive, and exactly the tools listed above are. It fails on main, where `execute_command` reports `destructiveHint: false`.

title: Read date text arguments in the workbook date system (#1038)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1038.

In a 1904-date-system workbook, date functions read date text such as `"1/1/2020"` with the 1900 system (`serial_arg` went through `num`, i.e. `to_number()`), then turned the serial back into a date with the workbook's system. The result was off by four years and a day: `YEAR("1/1/2020")` gave 2024.

**Change** (`crates/functions/src/date.rs` only):
- `serial_arg` / `day_arg` take the workbook `DateSystem` and coerce with `Value::to_number_in(sys)`, so date text is parsed in the workbook's date system, as `VALUE` already does. Every date-serial argument goes through them: YEAR, MONTH, DAY, HOUR, MINUTE, SECOND, WEEKDAY, WEEKNUM, ISOWEEKNUM, EDATE, EOMONTH, DATEDIF, DAYS, DAYS360, NETWORKDAYS(.INTL), WORKDAY(.INTL), YEARFRAC.
- The holiday list of NETWORKDAYS / WORKDAY (and the .INTL forms) uses `to_number_in(sys)` too, as the issue suggests.

Numbers, booleans and blanks coerce the same as before. In a 1900 workbook nothing changes, because `to_number()` is `to_number_in(D1900)`.

Out of scope: the financial functions (`financial.rs`: COUP*, XNPV, ACCRINT…) work in the 1900 calendar throughout, so the text they parse already matches the calendar they use. Supporting 1904 there is a separate change.

**Test:** `date_text_arguments_use_the_workbook_date_system` checks YEAR, MONTH, DAY, DAYS and NETWORKDAYS (with a text holiday) on date text in a 1904 workbook. Without the fix it fails (YEAR gives 2024, and the holiday is missed).

title: Cap CSV import fields per record at the worksheet column limit (#1037)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1037.

`parse_records` pushed a new `String` for every delimiter in a record. `read_csv` only stopped at `MAX_COLS` after the whole record had been collected. Because of this, one line of commas allocated a `Vec<String>` entry for every byte, even though everything past column 16,384 was then thrown away.

The parser now stops pushing fields once a record holds `MAX_COLS` of them. This applies on the delimiter path, the line-end path and the unterminated last row. Fields past the limit are still read, so quoting and line ends stay in sync, but they are dropped right away. Each record now holds at most `MAX_COLS` fields.

Import output does not change. Columns past `MAX_COLS` were already dropped silently by the `read_csv` callback, and they are still dropped. The issue also suggests turning oversized rows into an explicit error or warning. I left that out because it changes user-visible behaviour and is a maintainer decision. This PR only removes the allocation blow-up. Export-side row-byte accounting (#1023) is a separate change.

Test: `parser_stops_collecting_fields_at_max_cols` feeds `MAX_COLS + 50` fields followed by a short row. It also feeds an unterminated row of `MAX_COLS + 50` fields. It asserts that each record is capped at `MAX_COLS` and that the next row parses normally. Without the fix, the first record has `MAX_COLS + 50` fields.

title: Fix table without header: re-point references when the data moves down (#1030)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1030.

`insert.table` with `header: false` pushes the data down one row to make room for the generated `Column1…` header. It moved the cells and cell pictures directly but left every formula reference unchanged, so a formula outside the table (e.g. `=SUM(A1:A2)`) then pointed at the header plus only part of the data.

The no-header branch now applies the same `Edit::InsertCells { axis: Rows }` edit that **Home › Insert Cells › Shift cells down** uses (`insert_cells` in `sheet.rs`) for the one-row strip above the data:

- `shift_cell_features` moves merges, conditional formats, validations, notes, links, sparklines and cell pictures with the data. This replaces the hand-written picture shift.
- `rewrite` re-points formula references on every sheet, plus chart series and sparkline sources.

These two helpers in `sheet.rs` are now `pub(super)`, so `insert.rs` can call them. The existing guards are unchanged: the end-of-sheet check and the refusal to shift another table. The `header: true` path is not touched.

Test: `table_without_header_keeps_outside_references` adds the table over `A1:A2` with no header. It checks that the data moved, and that `=SUM(A1:A2)`, `=A2` and a reference from another sheet (`=Sheet1!A2`) now point at the moved cells and keep their values. On `main` the formulas keep their old addresses and the test fails.

title: Refuse the table Total Row when the row below the table is not empty (#1029)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1029.

`table.totalRow` checked only the sheet's last row before growing the table by one row, and `write_totals` then wrote a label or a `SUBTOTAL` formula into, or removed, every cell of that row. Any value or formula sitting directly below the table was lost.

Now, when the Total Row is being turned on, `table_flag` first looks at the table-width row below the table. If a cell there has a value or a formula, or another table overlaps that row, the command returns an error and changes nothing, the same way it already refuses when there is no room at the bottom of the sheet ("There's no room below the table for the total row."). An empty row (cells with only formatting count as empty) works as before. Turning the Total Row off is unchanged: it removes only the table's own totals row.

I went with refusing rather than inserting a row, as the issue allows either; inserting would shift unrelated content and is a bigger design choice.

Test `total_row_refuses_to_overwrite_occupied_row` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/insert.rs`: a value in the middle column below a 3-column table (a column with no totals expression), then a formula in the last column; each time the command errors, the table keeps its range and the cell keeps its content. After clearing the row, the Total Row turns on and writes "Total". The test fails without the fix.

title: Fix xlsx: combine escaped UTF-16 surrogate pairs when decoding strings (#1025)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1025.

`decode_xstring` decoded each `_xHHHH_` escape on its own through `char::from_u32`. UTF-16 surrogate units are not Unicode scalar values, so a supplementary character written as a pair of escapes (`_xD83D__xDE00_` for U+1F600) stayed as literal escape text after import.

Now, when a high surrogate escape (`D800`-`DBFF`) is followed directly by a low surrogate escape (`DC00`-`DFFF`), the two are combined into one character.

- Lone surrogates (a high one without a low one after it, or a low one alone) stay literal text, as before.
- An escape protected with `_x005F_` is still treated as literal text, so it never counts as the low half of a pair.
- Shared strings, rich text runs, inline strings, comments, `str` cells and table column names all decode through `decode_xstring`, so this one change covers each of them.
- `encode_xstring` is unchanged: it writes supplementary characters as they are, so the round trip already keeps them.

The new unit test `xstring_surrogate_pairs` checks upper- and lowercase pairs, lone high and low surrogates, a high surrogate followed by an escape that is not a low surrogate, and a protected escape. Without the fix, its first assertion fails.

title: Open notice: do not promise to keep macros that were dropped (#1024)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1024.

`show_open_warnings` turned every macro/VBA warning from `file.open` into the same notice, "GridCraft keeps them intact when you save". The XLSX reader (`crates/xlsx/src/read.rs`) also reports two cases where the VBA project is **dropped**: when the part it points to is missing, and when the part cannot be read. In those cases the notice promised to keep macros that were already gone.

Changes (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`):
- If a macro warning says the project was dropped, the notice now says so: the macros were not loaded, will not be in the saved file, and the user should keep the original file. It is still a Warning and still has the "What this means" action.
- The kept-case text no longer promises to keep macros on every save. It now says "GridCraft keeps them when you save as .xlsm". The writer only writes the VBA project into `.xlsm`/`.xltm`, and the browser Save As exports `format: "xlsx"`, so the old "keeps them intact when you save" was not true for every save route.

Not in this PR: the issue also suggests a warning or confirmation before a macro-free export. That is a new UI flow, so I left it for a maintainer to decide.

Test: `dropped_macro_warning_never_promises_to_keep_macros` (in `crates/ui-egui/tests/interaction.rs`) feeds the reader's exact missing-part and unreadable-part warnings and checks that the notice says "dropped" and never "keeps them". It also checks that the kept warning still gets the keep notice. The test fails on main.

author: harrisonoconnorhover

title: Gaps #21: add-ins, Office add-ins, VBA through an add-in, live co-editing and document chat
author: sirmmo
body:
## What this changes

GridCraft gets an add-in system and what is built on it:
- plugin functions and commands;
- Office (Office.js) add-ins;
- VBA macros run by an external add-in;
- live co-editing with document chat;
- editing inside Nextcloud.

It fills [gaps.md](docs/gaps.md) #21. The reference docs are [docs/plugins.md](docs/plugins.md) (the protocol), [docs/officejs.md](docs/officejs.md) (Office add-ins) and [docs/collab.md](docs/collab.md) (co-editing and chat). WordCraft (storytold/wordcraft#2586) and DeckCraft (storytold/deckcraft#919) get the same system, so one add-in can serve all three apps. The cross-app specs (co-editing, chat, add-in requirements, protocol 2.2) live in [sirmmo/craft-collab](https://github.com/sirmmo/craft-collab).

The add-ins are separate programs in any language. GridCraft starts them and talks JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdin/stdout, so an add-in that crashes, hangs or answers badly costs a cell an error value, never the workbook. That follows the never-crash rule: timeouts, restarts, `failed` after 3 failures, bounded input everywhere, no panics. Everything is a command: the add-ins' features are reachable from the UI, the CLI, MCP and the control channel, and programmatic calls never open dialogs.

### Step by step

The commits are grouped by feature. Each builds and passes the gates on its own:

1. **Add-ins, protocol 1** (1f36da7, 98c053b, d439ba0, 17759bb, db41d50, 1d8398f, 1eee7d5, 4fb1ed1):

   - **Ribbon groups and context-menu items.**

title: fix(edit): recalculate all changed cells after large-range clears
author: harrisonoconnorhover
body:
Fixes #1032.

Clearing `A1:A1000001` removes a value in `A1000001` but leaves formulas referring to it unchanged, because Clear reports only the first million coordinates to recalculation. A deleted formula beyond that cutoff can also leave its spilled results behind. Clear now reports all stored cells it touches instead of enumerating and truncating the selected rectangle. When clearing formats or all content removes an empty merge, it also retries blocked spill anchors, preserving behavior that previously relied on reporting empty coordinates.

Four focused regression tests cover direct and transitive dependents, undo/redo, removal of a distant formula whose spill extends outside the selection, empty merged spill blockers, and styled spill blockers. The stale dependent and stale spill cases failed before the fix; all four tests now pass. Fixtures contain only a few stored cells.

Validation on macOS arm64 with Rust 1.95.0:

- Focused regression tests and engine all-target Clippy with `-D warnings`: passed.
- Formatting, asset attribution, dependency layers, WASM, parity and keytip checks: passed.
- Full `cargo test --workspace`: 1,605 passed, zero failed, one ignored.
- `cargo xtask ci` stops at the existing `clippy::collapsible_match` error in unchanged `crates/xlsx/src/xls/mod.rs:273` on base `84acf62`; the checks above were run separately.

title: Keyboard: Show Outline Symbols (Ctrl+8 / Strg+7) and Next Corner of Selection (Ctrl+. / Strg+')
author: iluebbe
body:
**Builds on #1124** (shortcuts per interface language). This branch contains its commit `0925fca`, so please merge #1124 first; after that, this PR shows only its own commit.

## Problem

Two keyboard features Excel has in every language are missing from GridCraft. Each needs a command that doesn't exist yet.

| Feature | English Excel | German Excel (measured) | GridCraft |
|---|---|---|---|
| Show / hide the outline symbols (the band with the group brackets and level buttons) | Ctrl+8 | Strg+7 | no command; Ctrl+8 does nothing |
| Move the active cell to the next corner of the selection | Ctrl+. | Strg+' (Strg+Umschalt+#) | no command; Ctrl+. does nothing |

Behaviour in Excel 365 (German), measured with B2:C3 selected and B2 active:
- **Strg+7** turns the outline symbols off, and the second press turns them on again (`Window.DisplayOutline`).
- **Strg+Umschalt+#** moves the active cell B2 → C2 → C3 → B3 → B2, and the selection stays.
- Excel saves the outline setting per sheet as `<sheetView showOutlineSymbols="0">`.

## Fix

- **`view.outlineSymbols`** (`{on?}`, toggles without `on`, undoable like the other sheet view flags) sets the new `Sheet::show_outline_symbols`.
  - Default is shown.
  - An older saved sheet without the field reads as shown.
  - Off, the grid lays out no outline band, so there are no brackets and no level buttons; the outline itself stays.
  - XLSX reads `showOutlineSymbols` and writes it when off.
- **`selection.nextCorner`** moves the active cell clockwise to the next corner of the current area.
  - The area stays.
  - The new active cell becomes the anchor, so Shift+arrows move the opposite corner.
  - A single row or column toggles between its ends; a single cell stays.
- **Shortcuts:**
  - English: Ctrl+8 (Control+8 on a Mac) and Ctrl+. (Windows and Linux; Cmd+. is Cancel on a Mac).
  - German: Strg+7 and Strg+Umschalt+#, in `keymap/de.rs`.

title: Show copy outline and cancel stale source paste (#939)
author: derechopiano
body:
Copy mode currently hides its animated outline while the source remains selected. If that source is edited, the outline persists and Ctrl+V can paste the old snapshot. This makes the visible cells disagree with what paste will use.

This draws the copy outline beyond the solid selection border and ends copy/cut mode when a source cell or in-cell picture changes, including multi-area sources and undo/redo. Edits elsewhere intentionally keep the snapshot, as described in #939. The UI also rejects the stale text still held by the Windows clipboard after source editing.

Validation: cargo xtask ci passed all eight stages (format, Clippy, workspace tests, assets, layers, WebAssembly, parity, keytips). Manual testing in the separate Windows development build confirmed the outline is visible while selected, editing the source prevents the old value from pasting, and editing another cell preserves copy mode. The dashed border sits farther outside the selection than Excel's; exact border placement can be polished separately.

Closes #939

title: fix(core): parse unambiguous day-first dates (31/12/2026) instead of leaving them as text
author: saadkhantareen
body:
Fixes #1071

## Summary

Typed and pasted dates were only parsed month-first (the en-US order), so an unambiguous day-first date such as `31/12/2026` stayed plain text — even though the first field cannot be a month, and the workbook's number-format inference (OpenXML/ECMA-376) likewise only produces a date when the value is a valid calendar date.

Day-first is now tried as a fallback: only when the month-first interpretation fails `valid_ymd` validation. Ambiguous dates keep the existing month-first reading (e.g. `8/6/2026` still parses as August 6), and strings that are not valid calendar dates in either order (e.g. `31/4/2026`) still stay text.

## Changes

- `crates/core/src/parse.rs` — after the existing month-first attempts in `parse_date_like`, try the same layouts with the first two fields swapped, each result still checked by `valid_ymd`; covered layouts: `D/M/YYYY`, `D/M/YY`, and `D/M` with the session year.
- New unit test `unambiguous_day_first_dates` covering `31/12/2026`, `13/6/2026`, the leap day `29/2/2024`, and `25/12` (session year), plus the guard cases: impossible dates stay text and ambiguous dates keep the month-first reading.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p gridcraft-core` — 22 passed, 0 failed, including the new test.
- `cargo fmt -p gridcraft-core -- --check` — clean.

title: web: opt-in self-hosted update notice and admin-triggered update (feature self-hosted-update)
author: Dejan-Port

Adds an **opt-in, off-by-default** `self-hosted-update` feature to `apps/gridcraft-web`, for one case only: people who **host GridCraft's web build on their own server**. It is not for desktop users. title: Key tips: follow the interface language; German Excel's key tips (measured in Excel)
author: iluebbe
body:
## Problem

GridCraft's key tips (Alt sequences) are English Excel's in every interface language. German Excel uses other letters throughout:

| | English Excel | German Excel | GridCraft, German interface |
|---|---|---|---|
| Home tab | Alt, H | Alt, R (Start) | Alt, H; Alt, R opens Review |
| Bold | Alt, H, 1 | Alt, R, 1 | Alt, H, 1 |
| Top Align | Alt, H, A, T | Alt, R, K B | Alt, H, A, T |
| Merge & Center menu | Alt, H, M | Alt, R, ß | — (ß isn't recognised at all) |
| Clear Contents | Alt, H, E, C | Alt, R, L Ö, H | — (Ö isn't recognised) |
| Data tab | Alt, A | Alt, V | Alt, A |
| File › Save As | Alt, F, A | Alt, D, H | Alt, F, A |

A German user's Alt, R lands on Review instead of Home, and every deeper letter differs. Some German key tips use Ä, Ö, Ü and ß:
- Merge & Center is Alt, R, ß.
- Comma Style is Alt, R, Ö.
- Fill is Alt, R, Ü.
- Table is Alt, I, ß.
- Text Box is Alt, I, Ä.

GridCraft can't type those at all: it matches key tips by egui key name, and egui has no key for them.

I measured German Excel 365's key tips through UI Automation. Every ribbon control reports its office control id (`AlignTopExcel`) and its key tip (`Alt, R, K B`). I selected every tab, opened every drop-down menu and two second-level submenus (Format › Hide & Unhide, Conditional Formatting › Clear Rules), and read the File tab's pages. Nothing was invoked.

Microsoft's lists show own key tips for Spanish, French, Brazilian Portuguese, Czech and Russian Excel too. Only German is measured here; #1125, #1126, #1127, #1137 and #1138 ask people with those languages to measure. #1137 includes a script that reads the key tips through UI Automation.

## Fix

Key tips follow the interface language, the way `i18n` labels do:
- **`keytips.json`** gets a `de` field per entry: German Excel's sequence for the same control.
  - 328 of the 364 entries have one.
  - The 36 without one have no German counterpart and so aren't in the German table: Excel 2003 paths (E, O), English duplicates, …

title: Grid: per-frame work no longer scales with the whole sheet (#1098)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #1098. Fixes #1053 (nobody had claimed it or opened a PR for it).

## What was O(sheet) per frame
`paint` in `crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs` makes a fresh `CfCache::new()` every frame (so nothing survives from frame to frame). In `CfCache::look` (`crates/engine/src/cf.rs`), for every visible cell and every conditional-format rule that covers it:

1. the rule's statistics (`numbers_in`) were built on first use, for **every** rule kind, even ones that read none (expression, cell value, text, blanks, errors, dates). That is a pass over the rule's range clipped to the used range, with a `display().to_lowercase()` string per non-empty cell and a sort. In the issue's workbook the alternate-row rule covers the whole data area (~8,276 x 44 cells), so every frame did that scan, and trimming the range to the data area (as the reporter tried) cannot help;
2. the statistics were then `.clone()`d for **every cell lookup**: the sorted number vector and the whole text-count map (#1053).

So the per-frame cost was O(rule range) once per rule plus O(rule range) per visible cell, instead of O(visible cells).

## What changed (engine only, `crates/engine/src/cf.rs`)
- `stats_need(rule)`: statistics are gathered only for rules that read them: numbers/mean/deviation for top-N, above average, colour scales, data bars, icon sets; the text counts for duplicate/unique. Every other rule kind scans nothing. Each rule gathers only the part it reads (previously both parts, always).
- The statistics are borrowed from the cache (`&RuleStats`) instead of cloned per cell.
- Behaviour is unchanged: the same code computes the same numbers for the rules that read them.

## Tests (`cargo test -p gridcraft-engine --lib cf::`, 6 pass)
- `needed_statistics_equal_the_full_ones`: equality, old vs new: a reference copy of the previous one-pass computation vs `RuleStats::build` for each need, on several ranges (partly empty, text, errors, blank-looking text, outside the used range); numbers and counts co…

title: Charts: resolved data and rendering are cached between frames (#1139)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1139
Part of #1098

## Cause
`chartview::paint_objects` called `gridcraft_chart::resolve` and `render` for every chart intersecting the viewport on every frame. Both are O(points), so a sheet with several big charts kept the UI thread busy while scrolling, hovering or sitting idle with nothing changed.

## What changed
- New `crates/ui-egui/src/chartcache.rs`: a per-`SheetApp` cache of each chart's rendered primitives (`Arc<[Prim]>`), keyed by (document uid, sheet index, chart index) and checked against the zoom and pixels-per-point. `resolve` and `render` run only on a miss. Capped at 64 entries and 48 MiB (estimated from the primitives), least recently used out; a single chart over a quarter of the byte budget is rendered but not kept; entries of closed documents are dropped every frame; all entries are dropped when the font set changes (the two places `logic` notes that new fonts are active).
- `chartview::paint_objects` takes `&Arc<Workbook>` (its only caller already had one) and reads charts through the cache. The Recommended Charts preview (`paint_chart`) is not cached.
- No change in the engine or the chart crate.

## The invalidation key and why it is sound
The cache keeps a `Weak<Workbook>` per document and compares its pointer with the document's current `Arc<Workbook>`. This does not depend on a change counter that every mutation path would have to bump:
- The workbook is only writable through `Arc::make_mut` or by replacing the `Arc` (the model has no interior mutability: grep of `crates/core` and `crates/model` for `RefCell`, `Cell<`, `OnceCell`, `OnceLock`, `Mutex`, `Atomic*`, `UnsafeCell`, `Rc<` finds nothing; `unsafe` is forbidden).
- While a `Weak` exists, `make_mut` never writes in place: with other strong owners (undo snapshot, `saved`, the per-command `before` clone) it clones, with none it moves the value to a new allocation and cuts the `Weak` loose. Either way the document's pointer differs from the cached one. The `Weak` also keeps the…

title: Fix false circular references in VLOOKUP/HLOOKUP tables
author: LordSimal
body:
VLOOKUP and HLOOKUP over referenced tables currently materialize every table cell before searching. An unrelated result cell that refers back to the lookup can therefore create a false circular reference and contaminate calculations in cross-sheet workbooks.

The evaluator now reads the search column/row, reuses MATCH for exact/wildcard and approximate searches, and reads only the selected result cells. Array arguments keep their existing broadcasting behavior; array-literal tables use the existing function implementation. The static dependency graph still covers the table so edits recalculate its users, and genuine selected-result cycles still report #CIRC!.

Validation:
- Added synthetic regressions for both lookup directions, cross-sheet whole-column tables, incremental edits, wildcard/array lookups, blank results, index validation, and genuine cycles. No user workbook or vendor-authored fixture is committed.
- Recalculated a supplied workbook with 26,685 formula cells: no #CIRC! errors remain. Its remaining 14 error cells have identical error codes at identical addresses after LibreOffice recalculation.
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-calc`: 63 passed, 1 ignored timing test.
- All eight `xtask ci` gates passed: fmt, clippy, workspace tests, assets, layers, WASM, parity, keytips. For this Homebrew Rust toolchain, the WASM check used `-Z build-std=std,panic_abort` with `RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP=1` to build a compatible standard library from installed sources.

Updates function-parity documentation and the roadmap progress log.

Cleanup from a crate review of `crates/chart`.

They differ only on the fallback for a series whose kind is `Combo` inside a combo chart: drawing said `Line`, resolving said column for series 0 and line for the rest. title: Charts: work and memory are bounded by series x points; ranges are clipped before evaluation (#1147)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1147

**Cause.** The chart limits were per factor (255 series, 100,000 points, 16 trendlines per series) and nothing bounded their product. A column chart also drew one rectangle per series and category however narrow, `resolve` evaluated a whole range before cutting it to 100,000 points, and `render` deep-copied the chart data on every call.

**What changed (`crates/chart`)**
- A point budget per chart: series x points <= 2,000,000. Over it, every series and the category list keep their first `2,000,000 / series` points (25 series keep 80,000 each); no series is dropped, so the legend and colours stay. Applied in `resolve` (so ranges are also read only that far) and in `render` (for data that did not come from `resolve`). There is no "truncated" flag on `ChartData`: adding a field would break every struct literal elsewhere; the behaviour is documented on `MAX_TOTAL_POINTS`.
- Trendlines are limited per chart (16, in series order) instead of per series.
- Columns and bars narrower than 0.25 px (and without data labels) are merged per pixel column into one rectangle covering the same extent. Wider bars take the old path unchanged.
- `eval_list_in` cuts a plain reference (`Sheet!A1:A1000000`, `A:A`) after the rows that can still hold the first points before calc evaluates it, but never below 16,385 cells: calc reads references up to 16,384 cells at full size and trims larger ones to the used range, so a shorter clip would add trailing blanks. Anything that is not a plain reference is evaluated as before.
- `moving_average` is linear: block head/tail sums (they only add, so a huge value passing through cannot leave rounding residue the way a running add/subtract sum does).
- `fit_trendline` uses a stack array instead of a `Vec` per data point.
- `render` borrows the data when it is already clean and within budget (`Cow`); the old copying `sanitize` is used only otherwise.

**Tests** (9 new in `gridcraft-chart`)

title: XLSX: [Content_Types].xml is the first zip entry, workbook parts precede document properties, so libmagic detects the file type (#1090)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #1090

## Cause (what was checked)
GridCraft already wrote `[Content_Types].xml` first, without data descriptors or extra fields. But it wrote `docProps/core.xml` and `docProps/app.xml` *before* `xl/workbook.xml`. libmagic (as shipped here, `file` 5.48) only finds the `xl/` entry name inside a limited window at the start of the zip; I measured this with synthetic zips: a package is `application/zip` once ~5 KB of compressed data precedes the first `xl/` name. Document properties hold user text (title, description, keywords), so a workbook with a long description is detected wrongly.

Before/after with a GridCraft-saved workbook (sales sample + `file.properties` with a 40 KB description), `file --mime-type`:
- before: `application/octet-stream`
- after: `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet`

## Change
`crates/xlsx/src/write.rs`: part order is now `[Content_Types].xml`, `_rels/.rels`, `xl/_rels/workbook.xml.rels`, `xl/workbook.xml`, the other parts, `docProps/*` last (Excel's order).

## Tests
- New `tests::zip_order` in gridcraft-xlsx: first four entries, no data-descriptor flag, entry name at offset 30, `xl/` name within 2 KB even with a huge description. Fails without the change (checked by reverting), passes with it.
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-xlsx` (174 passed), `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-xlsx --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt`, `cargo check -p gridcraft-xlsx --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo xtask layers`.

## Not verified
- PHP itself (not run; PHP's bundled magic database may differ from the system libmagic). The reporter's file is not available, so I cannot confirm their file failed for this reason: a plain sample workbook was already detected correctly here before the change. If the report persists after this lands, the reporter should attach the file.

title: CSV: saving keeps the encoding and line ends the file was opened with (#1166)
author: vedran-dobos
body:
Fixes #1166. Raised in #506's discussion.

A CSV or tab-separated file saves back in the **encoding, byte order mark and line ends it was opened with**, as #427 did for the separator. Before, every text file was written as UTF-8 without a BOM with CRLF: an ANSI file's `é` became two bytes, UTF-16 ("Unicode Text") became UTF-8, a UTF-8 BOM was dropped and LF became CRLF. A workbook that wasn't read from text still gets UTF-8 and CRLF.

Windows-1252 holds only 256 characters. When the text has others (`č`, `ć`, an emoji), **nothing is written and the person is asked**: a "Save in Another Encoding?" dialog lists the encodings, with UTF-8 (which holds everything) preselected and the file's own marked "č become ?". Excel writes `?` silently; here that only happens when someone picks it. An encoding chosen there that holds every character becomes the file's, so the next Ctrl+S doesn't ask again.

## What changed
- **model** `TextFormat { encoding, line_end }`, `TextEncoding` (`utf-8`, `utf-8-bom`, `utf-16le`, `utf-16be`, `windows-1252`) and `LineEnd`, plus `Workbook::csv_format` (next to `csv_delimiter`; skipped in JSON when `None`).
- **xlsx** `decode_text_as` returns the encoding it read; `read_csv` records it with the first record's line end (a line break inside a quoted field doesn't count). `encode_text` is the reverse: for Windows-1252 it lists the characters it can't hold, or replaces them with `?` when asked. `write_csv_text` writes with a given line end. `write_csv`/`write_csv_limited` keep their signatures and output.
- **engine** `io::text_file` and `save_bytes_as` encode CSV/TSV in the file's format. Where nobody can be asked (`save_bytes`, the CLI, `file.saveBytes`), characters that don't fit are an error naming them, never `?`. `file.save` / `file.saveAs` / `file.exportCsv` take `encoding?`. Without it, when the file's encoding can't hold the text, they write nothing and answer `{saved: false, encoding, unencodable, suggested: "utf-8", command, params}`, and…

title: Data: “Convert text that looks like a date or time to a date” option (#506)
author: vedran-dobos
body:
Part of #506 (the `2.6.70` case from the comments). **Builds on #657, which builds on #583**; please review those first. Until they merge, this PR's diff includes their commits; the change here is the last commit.

A CSV field like `2.6.70` (a version, a part number) opens as the date 6 February 1970 and saves back as `2/6/1970`, and there is no way to stop it. Excel's own fourth Automatic Data Conversion option, "Convert continuous letters and numbers to a date", doesn't cover this. It only keeps runs like `SEPT2` or `12JAN2026` as text, which GridCraft never converts, which is why #583 showed it greyed out. This PR puts a working GridCraft option in its place: **Convert text that looks like a date or time to a date**, **on by default**, so nothing changes until someone unchecks it.

## What changed
- **core** `DataConversion::convert_dates` (default `true`, part of `all()`). Off, `parse_input_with` skips the date and time reader: `3/4/2026`, `2026-03-04`, `2.6.70`, `4-Mar-2026`, `Mar 4, 2026`, `Mar-26`, `1/2`, `10:30`, `25:00` and date-times stay text, as written. Numbers, fractions (`1 1/2`), currency, percentages and booleans still convert. Arithmetic on text (`=DATEVALUE("3/4/2026")`, `parse_number_text`) still reads dates, as it reads `0123` whatever the options say.
- **engine** `app.dataConversion {convertDates}`; `all` sets it with the others, so "Enable all" unchecked keeps every date as written too.
- **ui-egui** File › Options › Data: the greyed-out box becomes the new checkbox. Its tooltip says it isn't an Excel option and that it also covers Excel's letters-and-numbers case.

## Question for the maintainers

title: fix(core): bound date-time detection scans (#1004)
author: LabDennis
body:
Long ordinary text containing many spaces made date-time detection retry both parsers at every space. CSV imports and cell entry could therefore spend quadratic time deciding that a field was just text.

Closes #1004.

Only the final two token boundaries can begin a supported time (one token, optionally followed by AM/PM). The parser now checks those candidates, preserves the existing ASCII-space delimiter rule, limits date/time component collection to the supported arity, and borrows the lowercased time body instead of copying it again. Unrecognised input retains its original text.

Validation on Windows / Rust 1.95, based on upstream `84acf62`:

- All **196 tests** across core and XLSX pass, including a CSV regression with a long text field and both workbook date systems.
- A deterministic regression caps candidate count, and 480 combinations cover supported date/time forms and mixed whitespace. The candidate-count regression fails against the original scan.
- Strict core Clippy, formatting, assets, layers and the full WASM gate pass (11 crates; one existing UI dead-code warning).
- Full `xtask ci` stops at the unchanged `collapsible_match` finding in `crates/xlsx/src/xls/mod.rs:273`. Separate parity and keytip checks also report stale generated files, neither changed by this PR. No full-green workspace CI claim.

Bounded microbenchmark, five parses of a synthetic space-rich text field, same machine/profile:

| Words | Before | After |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1,000 | 39.46 ms | 0.131 ms |
| 2,000 | 145.75 ms | 0.225 ms |
| 4,000 | 556.19 ms | 0.415 ms |

This measures input parsing only, not whole-application or complete CSV-import performance. Reproduce with `cargo test -p gridcraft-core space_rich_input_timing -- --ignored --nocapture`; ordinary tests have no timing thresholds.

title: macOS: the title bar carries the document's file icon; dragging it drags the file out
author: jellologic
body:
Fixes #1169.

Native macOS document windows carry their file: the title bar shows the file's icon, dragging it out of the window drags the file (into Finder, an e-mail, a chat), and the close button wears the edited dot while there are unsaved changes. GridCraft had none of the three: it paints its own title bar, and winit 0.30 neither sets the represented filename nor offers a drag session. This adds all three on macOS; Windows, Linux, BSD and the web are untouched.

The title bar now draws the active document's file icon — the file's real Finder icon, fetched through NSWorkspace and cached as a texture — centred, immediately left of the title, Excel's arrangement. Dragging it starts a native `NSDraggingSession` with the file URL, so drop targets accept the file itself; the drag image is the file's icon. The edited dot is winit's safe `set_document_edited`. AppKit's own proxy icon was considered first (an empty title plus a represented filename shows the icon alone — verified) but AppKit draws it after the traffic lights, exactly where the Quick Access Toolbar lives, so the painted-icon route keeps the toolbar where it is.

While measuring the icon spacing I re-measured the traffic lights themselves (#170): on current macOS they are 13 pt wide on a 23 pt pitch starting 9 pt in, not the 12 / 20 / 10 the QAT offset assumed — the old numbers left a hair between the lights and AutoSave. The constants now match the measured geometry, which the existing lights test still derives.

The AppKit interop lives in the new `gridcraft-macos-window` (L0 leaf, registered in the layering table): Objective-C messaging needs `unsafe`, which the workspace forbids elsewhere — the same reasoning as `fmv-macos-events` (#69), with the `unsafe` confined to a few documented message sends. An app that keeps a native title bar (EffectCraft and SoundCraft today) would use the crate's `set_represented_filename` instead; the crate carries both strategies deliberately, and the eleven sibling apps…

title: Conditional formatting: text rules take wildcards and skip error values
author: iluebbe
body:
Fixes #1161 and #1162: two ways the text rules of conditional formatting differed from Excel.

## Problem

Measured in Excel for Microsoft 365 against GridCraft (`main` 84acf62):

- **Wildcards (#1161).** Excel saves "Text that Contains" as `NOT(ISERROR(SEARCH("a*c",A1)))`, so `*` matches any run of characters, `?` one character and `~` makes the next one literal. GridCraft searched literally: "contains `a*c`" formatted only a cell holding `a*c`, where Excel also formats abc, ABC, Abcdef, xabc, a?c and abxc. "Begins with" and "Ends with" are literal in Excel too, and stay so.
- **Error values (#1162).** GridCraft searched an error's text, so `#N/A` "contained" `a` and "began with" `#`. In Excel, an error never contains, begins or ends with anything, and always "does not contain". Excel's rule formulas fail on an error value.

## Fix

`crates/engine/src/cf.rs`:
- **Wildcards:** "Text that Contains" and "does not contain" search like `SEARCH`, case-insensitively, with the engine's existing `*`/`?`/`~` matcher (`cmd::edit::wildcard`, also used by Find and the criteria commands).
- **Errors:** an error value never matches "contains", "begins with" or "ends with", and always matches "does not contain".

`docs/gaps.md` gets §25, a list of what the measurement against Excel found (#1158–#1165).

## Testing

- `text_that_contains_takes_wildcards`: `a*c`, `a?c`, `a~*c`, "does not contain `a*c`" and "begins with `a*`" over abc, ABC, xabc, abxc, a*c, a?c and ab. Expected values are as measured in Excel; `a~*c` follows `SEARCH`'s documented escape.
- `text_rules_on_error_values`: `=NA()`, `=1/0` and `abc` under contains / begins with / ends with / does not contain, as measured in Excel.
- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers and wasm pass.
  - `parity` and `keytips --check` report their generated files out of date on this Windows checkout (`core.autocrlf`).
  - Regenerating them changes only line endings: `git diff` is empty, as on `main`.

🤖 Generated with [Clau…

title: fix: extend formula references with Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+arrows in the editor
author: paulohenriquex
body:
## What

When editing a formula (in the cell or in the formula bar), Command+Shift+arrow on macOS and Ctrl+Shift+arrow on any platform did not extend the pointed reference. They either moved the text caret or did nothing, because the editor only consumed Shift+arrow events.

Additionally, the formula bar explicitly disabled pointing altogether (`!ed.from_formula_bar`), so not even plain Shift+arrow worked there.

## Why

- The shared editor widget only matched `Modifiers::NONE` and `Modifiers::SHIFT`, so any combination with Command or Ctrl fell through to the TextEdit's default behaviour.
- The formula-bar branch of the arrow handling had a `!ed.from_formula_bar` guard that skipped pointing entirely.

## How

- Capture `modifiers.command || modifiers.ctrl` alongside `modifiers.shift` when reading arrow key state.
- Consume `COMMAND|SHIFT` and `CTRL|SHIFT` variants so the events do not slip through to the TextEdit.
- Remove the `!ed.from_formula_bar` guard so pointing works in both editors.
- Pass a `jump` flag into `grid::point_move` and use the engine's `selection::jump` when set, so Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+arrow jumps to the edge of the data region like the grid does outside editing.

## Testing

- `cargo check -p gridcraft-ui-egui` passes.
- Manually tested in the running app on macOS:
  - In-cell editor: Cmd+Shift+arrow and Ctrl+Shift+arrow now extend the reference to the edge of the data region.
  - Formula bar: Shift+arrow, Cmd+Shift+arrow and Ctrl+Shift+arrow all extend the reference (previously nothing happened).
  - Plain Shift+arrow still extends cell by cell.
  - No regression in F4 anchor cycling, Enter/Esc/Tab handling, or grid-level Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+arrow selection.

title: Prompt to save changes before closing window
author: Osaym
body:
Closes #1172

### Summary
When closing GridCraft with unsaved workbooks or active cell/text-box edits, GridCraft previously exited immediately without prompting the user to save changes. Additionally, closing the last open workbook via `Cmd+W` or choosing "Don't Save" on the close prompt cleared the screen to a new blank workbook rather than closing the window.

### Changes
1. **Window Close & Dirty Tracking** (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`):
   - Added `pub quit_confirmed: bool` and `SheetApp::close_requested(&mut self) -> bool`.
   - Active in-progress cell or text-box edits are committed before checking dirty status so changes typed right before closing are preserved.
   - If workbooks are dirty and quit has not been confirmed, cancels close and opens the `saveChanges` dialog with `closingWindow: true`.
   - Closing the last open workbook on desktop (`self.session.active().is_none()`) confirms quit and closes the window instead of respawning a blank workbook.

2. **Save Changes Dialog Actions** (`crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs`):
   - **Save** (or Enter): Commits edit, saves document, closes it, and prompts for any remaining dirty workbooks before closing the window.
   - **Don't Save**: Closes the document with `force: true`; prompts for remaining dirty documents if any, or closes the window if all are handled.
   - **Cancel** (or Escape): Closes the dialog and aborts closing, leaving the window and unsaved workbooks open.

3. **Eframe Logic** (`apps/gridcraft/src/main.rs`):
   - Wires `close_requested()` check into eframe app logic to cancel window close requests until confirmed.

4. **Tests** (`crates/ui-egui/tests/window_close.rs`):
   - Added 9 tests covering clean close, dirty prompt, in-progress cell edit commitment, Cancel, Don't Save, Save, multiple dirty workbooks, and `Cmd+W` closing behavior.

title: Draw: typed ink, Excel InkML and Draw with Trackpad (Force Touch)
author: rustycawk
body:
Brings the Draw tab closer to Excel's. Ink gets a typed model with pressure, Excel's InkML file format, editable pens and erasers, and **Draw with Trackpad** with Force Touch pressure on macOS.

### What changes for users

- **Pens:** an editable pen gallery (pen, pencil, highlighter) where each pen has a colour, a width and an optional effect (rainbow, galaxy, gold…). Pens can be added and removed.
- **Erasers:** a stroke eraser, a segment eraser that cuts at crossings, and small and medium erasers. Each eraser drag is one undo step.
- **Lasso:** a freehand loop selects ink, which can then be moved or deleted.
- **Stroke width:** width follows pressure when the input reports it, and drawing speed otherwise.
- **Fast strokes keep their shape, like Excel:**
  - a stroke takes every pointer move and keeps following the pointer past the cells (over the headers or out of the window); the grid clips what lies outside;
  - smoothing only settles jitter (at most 1.5 px) and uses a centripetal spline through the samples, so a fast zigzag keeps sharp, full-height turns instead of curling into loops;
  - on macOS, while a Draw tool is on, mouse drags aren't coalesced, and a hard press on the trackpad mid-stroke doesn't force-click.
- **Draw with Trackpad:** a floating canvas over the sheet. One finger draws, two fingers move the canvas, and any key exits.
  - On macOS, a light touch draws the thinnest line; clicking the pad down and pressing harder thickens it. It uses `NSPressureBehavior.primaryGeneric`, so there is no force click or Look Up.
  - Backends: macOS (AppKit touches), Linux (evdev) and Windows (precision-touchpad HID). The device is probed off the main thread and opened only when the mode starts.
- **Files:** XLSX ink is saved as Excel InkML behind `mc:AlternateContent`, with a DrawingML fallback for readers without InkML. Plain DrawingML polylines from #712 still open as editable ink.
- **Print and PDF:** highlighter and pencil ink print translucent, and effect …

title: Scripts with logic: Rhai with an Office Scripts-shaped object model, Code Editor and Automate tab
author: Herr-Enklo
body:
Scripts with real logic for GridCraft (gaps.md §21). Today a "script" is a recorded list of commands; this adds a scripting language with an object model, a Code Editor and Excel 365's Automate tab layout.

> **Two decisions for the maintainers.**
> 1. **Language.** gaps.md §21 leaves the language to you. This PR proposes [Rhai](https://rhai.rs): pure Rust, builds for wasm32, sandboxable. The docs describe it as a proposal.
> 2. **One new licence.** Rhai depends on `smartstring` (MPL-2.0, used unmodified). It would be the workspace's first MPL dependency. This is recorded in `docs/decisions.md`.

## Object model
- Names follow Excel's documented Office Scripts API, so existing knowledge carries over:

  ```rhai
  fn main(workbook) {
      let sheet = workbook.getActiveWorksheet();
      sheet.getRange("A1:B3").setValues([["Month", "Sales"], ["Jan", 120], ["Feb", 140]]);
      sheet.getRange("A1:B1").getFormat().getFont().setBold(true);
      run("home.fillColor", #{range: "A1:B1", color: "#FFFF00"});   // any GridCraft command
      console.log("done");
  }
  ```

- Workbook, Worksheet, Range (values, formulas, texts, number formats, offset/resize, used range, surrounding region), formats (font, fill, alignment, sizes, autofit) and NamedItem are covered.
- `run(id, params)` reaches every command.
- Every write goes through `Session::execute`, so protection, recalculation and the journal apply. One run is one undo step ("Run Script"), including a run that fails partway.

## Sandbox
- Limits on operations, time, call depth, expression depth and string/array/map size. A runaway loop or deep recursion ends with an error instead of freezing.
- Native runs use a helper thread with a large stack. The browser gets smaller limits.
- Rhai is built with `no_time`, `no_module` and `no_closure`, and `eval` is off.
- Scripts can't reach files: `file.*` commands and any `path`/`url` param are refused unless the CLI's `--allow-files` is given.
- `automate.*` is refused inside scrip…

title: Conditional formatting: show a rule's number format
author: iluebbe
body:
Fixes #1163: GridCraft didn't show a conditional format's number format.

## Problem

A rule can set a number format in three ways:
- Format › Number in Excel's rule dialog;
- `numFmt` in the rule's `dxf`;
- `"style": {"num_fmt": "0.00"}` in `home.conditionalFormat`.

GridCraft read the format and `CfCache::look` returned it. The grid's `look` and the print/PDF path's `cell_look` merged only the rule's fill, font and borders, though, so the cell kept its own format.

Example: an Excel file with the rule "greater than 2" and the number format `#,000` shows `003` in Excel and `3` in GridCraft.

## Fix

- `crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs` (`look`, which the Page Layout view also paints with) and `crates/engine/src/cmd/print.rs` (`cell_look`) take the rule's `num_fmt` when it isn't `General`. In a differential style, `General` means "not set"; `cf::layer_under` already treats it that way.
- For cells that aren't General, print's `draw_text` formatted the text with the cell's own style again (`display::cell_text`). It now formats with the look's code, through the new `display::value_text_as`. `value_text` calls `value_text_as`, so CSV/Text output is unchanged.

## Testing

- `a_rules_number_format_is_shown` (ui-egui, `grid.rs`): the rule's code replaces the cell's only where the rule matches.
- `pdf_shows_a_rules_number_format` (engine, `print.rs`): the PDF shows `3.00` for the matching cell and `1` for the other one. Before the `draw_text` change it showed `3`.
- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers and wasm pass.
  - `parity` and `keytips` report their generated files out of date on this Windows checkout (`core.autocrlf`).
  - Regenerating them changes only line endings: `git diff` is empty, as on `main`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: View: Cell grid size, a display-DPI-like scale for the grid
author: DCM4711
body:
## View › Cell grid size: a display-DPI-like scale for the grid

On macOS the grid draws noticeably smaller than on Windows on the same monitor, so people end up zooming every sheet to ~130% (Excel for Mac has the same complaint). Other spreadsheet apps let you adjust the screen DPI the grid is laid out with; this adds the equivalent.

**View › Cell grid size** (next to Interface size; 75–200% in the menu, 50–300% through `view.gridScale`) multiplies the sheet zoom on screen:

- cells, row/column headings, outline bands and cell text grow together, in Normal and Page Layout view;
- the ribbon and the rest of the window keep their size (that's Interface size's job);
- the zoom saved in the workbook is unchanged, so files look the same on other machines;
- it persists in `ui.json` as `gridScale`; malformed values read as 100, out-of-range ones are clamped.

`view.gridScale` takes `{percent: 50–300 | "default"}`; no value is an error, not a dialog. It's listed in `engine.commands` with the other UI commands. Label translated in every catalog; `docs/hardware-parity.md` updated.

- `cargo xtask ci` (fmt, clippy -D warnings, tests, assets, layers, wasm)
- New `crates/ui-egui/tests/grid_scale.rs`: 130% scales `Geo::z` by 1.3 and grows the headings, leaves egui's zoom factor and the sheet's zoom alone, persists, clamps hostile values, and reads malformed/missing `gridScale` as 100.
- Looked at it in the desktop app on macOS via the control channel: at 130% the grid matches the old 130%-zoom workaround while the status bar still says 100%.

title: Conditional formatting: icon thresholds with ">" (gte="0")
author: iluebbe
body:
Fixes #1160: icon set thresholds with ">" were evaluated as ">=".

## Problem

In Excel, each icon threshold is ">=" (the default) or ">". The file stores ">" as `gte="0"` on the threshold's `cfvo`. GridCraft ignored `gte`, so a value exactly on a ">" threshold got the next higher icon. Saving the file then dropped the `gte`.

Measured in Excel for Microsoft 365, 3 Traffic Lights over 0…10:

| Thresholds | Value | Excel | GridCraft before | GridCraft now |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number > 3, > 6 | 3 | red | yellow | red |
| | 6 | yellow | green | yellow |
| Percent > 30, > 70 | 3 | red | yellow | red |
| | 7 | yellow | green | yellow |

## Fix

- **Model:** `CfRule::IconSet` gets `greater: Vec<bool>`, one flag per threshold (same index as `thresholds`). It has a serde default, and an empty list means every threshold is ">=", so existing rules and saved state are unchanged.
- **XLSX:**
  - the reader takes `gte` from each `cfvo`;
  - the writer writes `gte="0"` where a flag is set, also when the lower bound is left out and gets prepended.
- **Evaluation** (`cf.rs`): compares with `>` where the flag is set.
- **Command:** `home.conditionalFormat` takes icon thresholds, which it had no parameter for: `{"type": "iconSet", "thresholds": [{"type": "num", "value": 3, "operator": ">"}, …]}`. List them from the lowest up, one per icon after the first; one per icon with the lower bound first, as in the file, works too.

## Testing

- `icon_thresholds_with_greater_than` (engine): the table above, plus ">=" for comparison, through the command.
- `icon_set_greater_than_thresholds_roundtrip` (xlsx): `gte="0"` is written on the right `cfvo` and read back.
- `full_roundtrip`: its icon set now carries ">" thresholds and still compares equal.
- **Excel:** a file this branch wrote with `> 3` and `> 6` opens with `IconCriteria(2..3).Operator = xlGreater`.
- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers and wasm pass.
  - `parity` and `keytips` report their generated files out of …

title: Charts: axis and data label number formats typed in the Format pane are read, drawn and saved
author: neilcawse
body:
Number formats typed in Excel's Format Axis and Format Data Labels panes were lost: on import every axis and data label followed its source cells, and saving dropped them. In a set of 11 Excel-saved fleet reports, 10 such formats (6 axis, 4 data label) appear across 5 files: a duration axis (`[h]:mm`) next to a percentage axis (`0%`) on a combo chart, `#,##0` value axes, and `0;;;` labels (positives only, so zero bars carry no label). GridCraft saved none of them, and drew the Idling Violations axes as `0`…`1.0`.

## What changed

- **Model** (`crates/model/src/features.rs`). `Chart.axis_number_formats: AxisNumberFormats { x, y, y2 }` (the X value axis of scatter and bubble charts, the value axis, the secondary value axis) and `Series.label_number_format`. Both are `Option<String>` with `#[serde(default)]`. `None` means "Linked to source", as before.
- **Read** (`crates/xlsx/src/chart.rs`). A `c:numFmt` counts only with `sourceLinked="0"`. Each value axis is matched to the chart group that uses it through the groups' `c:axId`s, not by file order: Excel can save the secondary value axis first (it does in the Idling Violations report). Scatter and bubble charts take X and Y from the group's own two value axes, X being the bottom/top one. Data labels come from the series' `c:dLbls`, otherwise from the group's. Three kinds of typed format are skipped because applying them would show something Excel doesn't: a deleted (hidden) axis's format, since GridCraft draws every axis; the value axis format of a 100% stacked line or area group, since GridCraft reads those as plain stacked and draws absolute values (a `0.0%` typed for the 0%–100% axis would read "2000000.0%"); and the format of labels that show percentages, bubble sizes or scatter X values but not the values, since it was typed for those.
- **Write.** The typed axis format is written as `c:numFmt sourceLinked="0"` on its axis, otherwise the linked `General` as before. A series with a label format gets its own `c:dLb…

title: XLSX: keep the sensitivity label, table column data formats and sheet custom properties on save
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1209.

The table writer built `<table>` with only its id, name, range and row counts, and the reader never looked at the table-level format attributes, so a plain open and save dropped them. They're now read into a `TableFormats` on `Table`, following what #867 does for a column's `dataDxfId` / `dataCellStyle`: the six dxf ids (`headerRowDxfId`, `dataDxfId`, `totalsRowDxfId`, `headerRowBorderDxfId`, `tableBorderDxfId`, `totalsRowBorderDxfId`) are kept as styles and written back through the workbook's dxf list, and the three cell styles (`headerRowCellStyle`, `dataCellStyle`, `totalsRowCellStyle`) are written when that named style is still in the workbook, same rule as the column one.

This sits on top of #867 (same table round-trip code), so until that one is merged the diff here also shows its commits. Only the last commit is new.

Thanks @richard1912 for the report and the numbers from the real workbook, and for offering to test this one on it too.

Validation:
- `fixtures::table_level_formats_survive_save`: a table with all nine attributes, dxfs listed in reverse and a conditional format taking the first dxf, so the ids change on save; each written id is checked by the format it points at. Fails without the fix (`headerRowDxfId` missing), passes here
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-xlsx --lib -- tests::fixtures tests::array_export tests::pivot_tests tests::roundtrip`
- `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-model -p gridcraft-xlsx -p gridcraft-calc -p gridcraft-engine -p gridcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
