title: engine: keep case-insensitive replace from dropping text when folding shifts byte boundaries
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
Case-insensitive Find & Replace can silently truncate a cell whose text folds to the same total byte length but with shifted character boundaries: `replace_ci` sliced the original text at byte offsets found in the lowercased copy, and a fold such as U+212A KELVIN SIGN (3→1 bytes) or U+0130 (2→3 bytes) moves those offsets off character boundaries, so `text.get(..)` returned `None` and `unwrap_or("")` dropped the tail (with an empty replacement, `input_to_cell("")` deletes the cell outright).

The fix adds `folds_in_place`, which allows the slice-based fast path only when every character folds to exactly one character of the same UTF-8 length; foldings that can move boundaries fall back to the existing lossless `text.replace`, and ordinary folds such as `É`→`é` keep the fast path. The regression test enters `Kİİ` (U+212A U+0130 U+0130) in A1, runs `edit.replace` with `what: "k"`, and asserts the cell text is unchanged — it fails on the old code (`Text("x")` vs `Text("Kİİ")`) and passes with the fix; `cargo test -p gridcraft-engine cmd::edit::tests` stays green (8/8).

Note for reviewers: open PR #980 reworks Find & Replace on character indices and would subsume this fix; if that lands first this branch can be closed. Until then this is the minimal data-loss fix that applies cleanly to current `main`.

Partially addresses #1307 (finding 5, case-insensitive replace corruption). Targeted tests green locally; `cargo xtask ci` left to the project runners.

title: Fix font dropdown list resizing and keyboard up/down navigation
author: mbaksa
body:
### Problem

When filtering the font dropdown, the list correctly shrinks as the number of matching fonts decreases. However, when characters are deleted and more fonts match the filter, the dropdown remains at its previous height instead of expanding.

For example, filtering for _Arial_ reduces the list to a few rows (one in my case), but by pressing backspace to get to _Ar_ leaves the dropdown the height of 2.5 rows, even though more results are available (4 in my case).

So, essentially, the list shrinks, but it doesn't grow back when filter is lessened.

Also, up and down keys don't behave as they should.

### Fix

The dropdown height is now recalculated from the number of filtered items, and the popup UI is given enough minimum height to grow again when the filter matches more results.

In addition, keyboard navigation in the filtered list now uses consistent filtered-item indices and automatically scrolls the selected item into view. This keeps Up/Down navigation aligned with the visible filtered list and avoids incorrect selection behavior

This actually also affects (fixes) drop-down menu for selecting cell type, and potentially other drop-down menus that might use the same _fn editable_combo_.

### Tests
#### Automatic tests
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — OK
- [x] `cargo check --workspace` — OK
- [x] `cargo test -p wordcraft-ui-egui` — OK

#### Manual test:
1. Open font dropdown list by clicking on the font name button
3. Type _arial_ → 1 row (depends on the number depends on which fonts user has installed)
3. Start pressing Backspace key so that it says only _ari_ → still only 1 row until...
4. When it only say _ar_ → 4 rows (Aptos Narrow, Arial, Candara, Garamond in my case) - before fix it displays 2.5 rows
5. Another Backpace, so it says only _a_ → 9 rows (max list height on the screen) - before fix it displays 2.5 rows

title: fix(calc): apply "Set precision as displayed" in calculation
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
Fixes #1343

With "Set precision as displayed" on, GridCraft now stores numbers the way their format shows them, and formulas calculate from those rounded values, as Excel does. Until now the flag was read and saved but never used in calculation.

- Formula results are rounded to the cell's number format before they're stored or read by other formulas (spill elements use the format of the cell they land in).
- Typed, pasted or reformatted numbers are rounded straight away; widening the format later doesn't bring digits back.
- `formulas.calculationOptions` takes `precisionAsDisplayed`. Turning it on rounds every number constant in one undo step and recalculates; turning it off restores full precision for formulas only.

Which formats round was checked in Excel with synthetic workbooks. Fixed decimals, percent, currency, thousands scaling (`0.0,,`), fractions and scientific formats round to what they show. General, dates, times and text keep the full value.

A condition doesn't pick the section that rounds; the sign does (first section for positives, second for negatives). So `[<1]0.00;0` shows 2+1/3 as `2` but stores 2.33. With a condition and a single number section, negatives keep the full value unless an `@` section follows. An empty section passes to the next one (`0.0;;0.000` stores -2.333 as -2.333). Display is unchanged.

The rounding (`NumberFormat::round_as_displayed`) reuses the renderer's digit logic, so stored values and display can't drift apart. Nothing changes when the option is off.

Not done: no Options dialog checkbox yet (command only); Excel's extra rounding of General constants shown in scientific notation; `%` inside scientific formats.

Tests cover each observed format, the issue's repro (528, 5280, 75.4286), cross-cell reads, spills, undo and reopen. All 16 files in gridcraft-corpus `excel/precision-displayed/` match Excel, including the General, date/time and `@` controls. On two real `.xls` models that use the option, every numeric mismatch…

title: XLS: formulas open as legacy formulas with Excel's implicit @ (#410)
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
Follow-up to #417, and based on its head, so it should land after it (until then this PR also shows #417's commits; the change here is the last commit). This fixes the .xls side of #410: #417 gives legacy XLSX formulas Excel's implicit `@`, and its description notes that formulas from the .xls import don't go through that classification yet.

- Every formula in a .xls file is a legacy formula. The import now runs each one that isn't a Ctrl+Shift+Enter array through `array_formula::apply_legacy`, as the XLSX reader does for formulas without `cm`. `=Data!A1:G1` in one cell shows Data!A1 instead of `#SPILL!`. Shared formulas are classified cell by cell.
- A one-cell CSE array (`{=SUM(A1:A3*2)}`) used to lose its array range on import; it now keeps it, so it still evaluates as an array.
- New `read_xls_with(bytes, FunctionInfo)`; `read_xls(bytes)` is unchanged. Saving to .xlsx needs no change: these formulas save without `cm` through #417's legacy export.
- `@` on a 2-D range now intersects on both the formula's row and column, as Excel does, instead of giving `#VALUE!`. Checked in real Excel (build 16.0): from another sheet `=@Sheet1!A1:C3` in B2 gives Sheet1!B2 and in C1 gives Sheet1!C1; outside the range's rows or columns it is `#VALUE!`; a formula inside its own range (`=@A1:C3` in B2) is a circular reference and shows 0. The test pins these.


Tests build a BIFF8 file in code (title row, shared formula, CSE arrays, `MAX(SUM(range/12),0)`, an .xlsx save that reads back unchanged) and fail with either half of the fix reverted. On two real .xls models, `#SPILL!` cells went from 18 to 0 each, with no other changes. CI passes on my fork.

Not done, same as #417: defined names and conditional-format and validation formulas aren't classified.

title: Grid: cell text keeps Excel's top and bottom insets
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
Top-aligned text nearly touched the cell's top border, and bottom-aligned text floated well above the bottom border. In Excel both sit at a small, similar inset.

Cause: egui lays out a text row as ascent + descent + line gap, with the gap under the descender. `cell_text_y` treated that row as the line box, and also drew top-aligned text 1 pt above the cell and stopped bottom-aligned text 0.5 pt short of the edge. Excel's line box keeps that space above the ascender and sits on the bottom gridline.

What changed:
- Cell text moves down by that line gap, taken from the galley's own glyph metrics (clamped), and the box stops at the bottom gridline.
- Single-line and wrapped text now share one placement rule (`cell_text_y`); the separate wrapped helper is gone.
- Measured against Excel for Microsoft 365 (Windows, 100% zoom, Calibri and Aptos Narrow, 11 and 20 pt, rows of 15 to 60 pt, wrapped and not): the top-aligned baseline is about 1.0 em below the top edge and the bottom-aligned one about 0.3 em above the bottom edge. A tall row now shows text where a standard row does, and a standard row matches Excel to the pixel.

Left as is: rotated text keeps its own placement. The in-cell editor isn't touched here; #960 handles its alignment, and it may want to use `cell_text_y` so F2 doesn't shift the text vertically.

Validation:
- New `crates/ui-egui/tests/cell_text_inset.rs`: top, middle and bottom insets in a tall row; tall row matches a standard row; wrapped text matches single-line. All three fail on main and pass here.
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui`, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`; CI passes on my fork.
- Checked offscreen snapshots before and after against Excel screenshots of the same synthetic workbook (Windows 11, 150% display scaling).
- Note: the first test checks absolute em targets, and the test harness's fallback font isn't Calibri. If CI on another OS lands outside the tolerance, it can be …

title: Keep Middle/Bottom vertical alignment for wrapped text taller than its row
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #1347

## Cause
`wrapped_cell_text_y` clamped the bottom-aligned Y to the top-aligned Y. When wrapped text was taller than its row, Middle and Bottom came out the same as Top, so the text always sat at the top of the cell.

## Fix
Removed the clamp. Taller text now overflows upward for Bottom and both ways for Middle, anchored to the cell's bottom edge or centre, and the cell's existing clip rect trims it. The old overflow test asserted the clamped behaviour, so it now checks that Top still starts inside the cell.

## Verified
- Regression test `wrapped_cell_text_y_keeps_vertical_alignment_when_text_is_taller_than_the_row`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui --lib wrapped_cell_text_y_keeps_vertical_alignment_when_text_is_taller_than_the_row`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`cell_text_y`, which handles unwrapped single-line text, still has the same clamp. Text that fits its row, rotated text, and the engine's `home.alignTop/Middle/Bottom` commands are unchanged.

title: Edit: text that would parse as a number or formula keeps its quote prefix in the editor (#1362)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1362

**Root cause:** GridCraft stores no quote-prefix flag. A cell entered as `'00123` holds the text `00123`, and `display::edit_text` (editor, formula bar, F2, Ctrl+') returned it without the apostrophe, so committing it unchanged re-parsed it as the number 123.

**What changed:** `edit_text` now prefixes a single `'` for constant text in a non-`@` cell when typing that text back would not give the same text: it would parse as a number, date, boolean or error, starts with `=` or `'`, or looks like a `+`/`-` formula. Plain text is untouched. Because the editor text re-commits to the same text, Enter unchanged keeps it as text on every path that uses `edit_text`. This follows Excel's visible behaviour of showing the apostrophe for quote-prefixed text.

**Tests / commands:** new `editing_quote_prefixed_text_keeps_it_text` (`'00123`, `'=1+1`, `'TRUE`, `''abc`: edit text equals the input and re-commit leaves the value unchanged). `cargo test -p gridcraft-engine --lib editing_`, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt -p gridcraft-engine`.

**Not done / unverified:**
- No separate quote-prefix style flag, so XLSX `quotePrefix` is not round-tripped; text that merely looks like a number (for example from an imported file) also gets the apostrophe when edited. Whether Excel shows the apostrophe in the editor needs confirmation in Excel.
- UI paths were not run interactively; they all go through `edit_text`.
- Find/Replace and `Cell::input_text` are unchanged.

title: View: Focus Cell, the tinted row and column of the active cell
author: emirbaki
body:
Fixes #1278.
Fixes #1397 .

The issue asks for a reading mode: a tint over the active cell's row and column, so the eye keeps its place. GridCraft now has Excel's name and place for that feature: Focus Cell, under View ▸ Show.

Two commands carry it, and the control channel, the CLI and MCP reach both:

- `view.focusCell` (`{on?}`) turns the tint on or off for the active sheet. A call without `on` toggles, as the ribbon click does.
- `view.focusCellColor` (`{color: "#RRGGBB" | "default"}`) sets the tint. `"default"` clears it back to the theme.

The Show group takes a split button after Headings. The body toggles, and the arrow opens the shared color palette. The button carries its name inside it and sits level with the first checkbox row. A strip under the icon shows the color in force, as Fill Color shows its own.

The tint lands over the fills and under the text, in the active cell's quadrant only. A frozen pane draws a band only where its line shows, and a hidden row or column draws no band. The headers take the same tint. The setting lives on the sheet, goes through undo, and saves in the file.

Left out for now: band shape, thickness and transparency, and applying the tint to the cell being edited. This change follows Excel's Focus Cell first.

Two limits worth naming:

- Excel has no Focus Cell in the file format, so the setting rides in `<sheetView><extLst>` under GridCraft's own namespace. Excel opens such a file and ignores the element, and GridCraft reads its own back.
- GridCraft rebuilds `<sheetView>` from the model on save, so an extension Excel wrote there is lost. That behaviour is older than this change.

The icon is drawn in code in `icons.rs`, so it needs no `ATTRIBUTION.md` row.

Validation:

- `view_focus_cell_*` in `crates/engine/src/tests.rs` (6 tests): the toggle, an explicit `on`, undo, per-sheet state, the color, and a bad hex that returns an error
- `roundtrip::focus_cell_and_its_color_roundtrip`: both halves survive a save and a read, and…

title: engine: keep every Go To Special area or fail before changing the selection
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
Go To Special collected every match but `coalesce` truncated the selection to its first 2,000 areas while the command still reported the full match count, so a follow-up delete acted on fewer cells than the count promised. The area cap is now 65,536 coalesced vertical areas; a larger result returns an explicit resource-limit error before the selection changes instead of silently dropping areas. Regression tests cover the reported 2,001-area case, the 65,536/65,537 boundary with an atomic failure check, and a contiguous run that stays one area. The full engine suite passes.

Fixes #1295

title: engine: subtotal honours header:false instead of dropping the first data row
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
The documented `header?: true` parameter was honoured by sort and removeDuplicates but ignored by Subtotal: the group scan always started at the second row, so with `header:false` the first data row dropped out of its group's SUBTOTAL and out of the grand total. Subtotal now starts at the first row the flag says, both for the group boundaries and for the grand-total range, and an explicit `header:false` keeps every row. A regression test with four headerless rows asserts East = 30 (both East rows) and Grand = 100 (all rows); without the fix it sees 20 and 90. The full engine suite passes.

Fixes #131

title: xlsx: keep every property of the default cell format when importing a file
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
Cell format 0 is the workbook's Normal cell format, but the styles reader kept only its font and discarded its number format, fill, borders, alignment and protection; cells with no `s` attribute or with `s="0"` lost those semantics, and a save rewrote XF0 without them. The default style is now the complete imported XF0, with the XF-0 → `StyleId::DEFAULT` mapping unchanged. A regression test gives XF0 a number format, a solid fill, centred alignment and unlocked protection, checks both an omitted style and `s="0"`, and asserts all of it survives a save and re-read. The full xlsx suite (174 tests) and the engine suite pass.

Fixes #1013

title: engine: rebuild cell-store bands and counts when importing a JSON workbook
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
The JSON reader deserialized the cell store's private bands and cached length as anything the file said, so a cell placed under a band its row doesn't map to vanished from lookup while iteration still saw it, and a forged count underflowed (`len -= 1`) on the next removal. JSON import now rebuilds band placement and the count from the cells themselves and drops coordinates outside the 1,048,576 × 16,384 grid with the same kind of warning the xlsx importer gives. A regression test forges a wrong band and a zero count, adds an off-grid cell, and checks lookup, the count, the warning and removal consistency. The full engine and model suites pass.

Fixes #1008

title: feat(formula): add Brazilian Portuguese (pt-BR) formula locale
author: MauriciDmarc
body:

Adds `FormulaLocale::Pt` so that, when the interface language is Português (Brasil), formulas are entered and displayed with Excel's pt-BR function names and separators (`SOMA`, `PROCV`, `SE`, `MÉDIA`, ...). Files and the engine keep canonical English names, so XLSX round-trips are unchanged.

Closes the 'Localized function names and `;` separators' gap for pt-BR (see #45).

- `crates/formula/src/input.rs`

  - Accented and unaccented spellings are both accepted (`MÉDIA`/`MEDIA`, `ÍNDICE`/`INDICE`); the accented form is used for display.
  - `;` as list separator, `,` as decimal separator, `\` as array column separator.
  - `TRUE`/`FALSE` display as `VERDADEIRO`/`FALSO`.

- `docs/function-parity.md`: localization row updated.
- `crates/formula/tests/portuguese_input.rs`: new tests.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p gridcraft-functions` (123 tests pass)

title: Keyboard: punctuation shortcuts follow the character the layout types (#1384)
author: vedran-dobos
body:
Fixes #1384.

On a Croatian or German keyboard `;` is Shift+, and `:` is Shift+., so Excel (English interface) inserts the date with Ctrl+Shift+, and the time with Ctrl+Shift+. GridCraft matched those keys by their US position and changed the font size. Punctuation keys now go by the character the layout types; digits keep their position.

## Questions for the maintainers

- When the layout types a letter egui has no `Key` for (`č`, `ö` on the US `;` key), the shortcut still falls back to the key's position, as egui-winit reports it, so Ctrl+Č / Ctrl+Ö keep inserting the date. Excel probably does nothing there. I left it, since egui doesn't tell the two cases apart. Should it change?

## What changed

- `keymap::us_key` turns a symbol or digit key press into the US key and Shift state that the English table uses:
  - digits by position, as before (Ctrl+Shift+4 is the currency format wherever `$` is);
  - punctuation by the character typed, translated to the US key that types it (`:` → Shift+;, `+` → Shift+=, `;` typed with Shift → Ctrl+;);
  - a character egui has no key for (`č`, `ö`, `<`) arrives as the position, which stands in, as before.
- `keymap::lookup` (English) and `ribbon::shortcut`, called from `grid.rs`, both read that key. Before, `lookup` matched the position and `ribbon::shortcut` the character, so the same press could mean different keys in each. On Croatian and German layouts:
  - Ctrl+Shift+, (`;`) inserts the date; it decreased the font size.
  - Ctrl+Shift+. (`:`) inserts the time; it increased the font size.
  - Ctrl++ opens Insert; it did nothing.
  - Ctrl+' copies the formula from the cell above; it did nothing.
  - Ctrl+Shift+0 (`=`) unhides columns; it opened Insert.
- US keyboards are unchanged.

## Overlap with #1124

#1124 adds German Excel’s own shortcuts for the German interface, with symbol keys by position. Its `de::lookup` runs first with the raw key and is unchanged by this PR, so the two combine. This PR changes only the English t…

title: Add Craft AI: the family's built-in local assistant (Gemma 4 catalogue, loopback runtimes, shared models folder)
author: hasan-sdaif
body:
## What this is

**Craft AI** — one assistant across the ArtCraft family, as a task pane in GridCraft. It talks to a
local model runtime on this machine and never to a cloud service:

| | |
|---|---|
| **Local and private** | Every request is `http://127.0.0.1` — Ollama (11434), LM Studio (1234) or llama.cpp's server (8080), whichever answers. No account, no key, no telemetry, and no address a cloud service could be reached at exists in the code. |
| **Light by design** | No inference engine, no weights, no GPU code enters the app. The runtime the user already has (or installs) does the running — Craft AI is a loopback conversation. |
| **Optional** | Without a runtime or a model the pane says so and touches nothing beyond loopback. Downloading is a button, never a default. |
| **Specialised** | The system prompt tells the model it is inside GridCraft and names this app's world — cells, ranges and A1 references, worksheet functions, tables and PivotTables, charts, conditional formatting, data validation, sorting and filtering, freeze panes, xlsx/csv — so answers are about this app, not generic advice. The ready-made tasks (explain a formula, build a formula, clean or transform data, chart and pivot advice, function finder) are framed for it, with the honesty clause: never invent function or menu names. |
| **One download serves every app** | The model file lands in a shared folder the whole family reads — `<data_home>/ArtCraft/Craft AI/models` — so a model downloaded here is already there in every other ArtCraft app, no second download. Ollama's own store works the same way machine-wide. |

## The three tabs

- **Assistant** — runtime and model pickers, the task, the question, the answer; the conversation is kept, copyable, and Arabic answers are drawn through the same visual-order pass as the rest of the Arabic interface. Worker thread, so the UI never blocks; a busy timer ticks while the model thinks.
- **Models** — the Gemma 4 catalogue, every figure from the mod…

title: XLSX: keep PivotTables whose source is in another workbook on save
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
A PivotTable whose source is a range or defined name in another workbook was lost on save: the table, its cache definition and records, the cache's link to the other workbook and the workbook's pivotCache entry were all dropped, leaving the report cells as plain values (with a range source the reader only warned that the reference "may not resolve"; with a name source there was no warning at all).

Repro: in Excel, build a PivotTable from a range (or a defined name) in a second workbook and save. Open it in GridCraft and save. `gridcraft-cli check` reports pivots 1 -> 0 and lost pivotTable, pivotCacheDefinition, pivotCacheRecords and externalLinkPath relationships. Excel-built examples: [`excel/pivot-external/`](https://github.com/Harrison-Booth/gridcraft-corpus/tree/main/excel/pivot-external) in my synthetic corpus (range source, defined-name source, a shared cache, plus the source workbook).

Cause: the cache's `worksheetSource` has an `r:id` to an `externalLinkPath` relationship. The reader ignored it and modelled a PivotTable whose source doesn't exist in this workbook, so on save `resolve_source` failed and the pivot was skipped. Pass-through couldn't keep the parts because it excludes pivot kinds.

Fix: such PivotTables are no longer modelled; the pass-through layer keeps them unchanged.
- The PivotTable parts stay with their sheet; the cache definition and records stay with the workbook, with the original `cacheId` and the link to the other workbook. Save As into another folder rewrites that link, as it already does for external links.
- PivotTables GridCraft writes use cache ids that don't collide with kept ones. A shared cache is written once; an unused cache is dropped, and a table whose cache wasn't kept is left out.
- `dxfId` and `numFmtId` references in the kept parts are renumbered to the rewritten styles part. Without this, Excel refuses to open the file.
- `gridcraft-cli check` counts kept PivotTables.

Limits (documented in `docs/file-format-parity.…

title: Format: Increase/Decrease Font Size step by one point below 8, stop at 72 (#1391)
author: vedran-dobos
body:
Fixes #1391.

Increase/Decrease Font Size no longer jump between 8 and 1 pt. Below 8 they step one point at a
time (8 → 7 → … → 1 and back up), from 8 to 72 they follow the Font Size list including 22 and 26,
and Increase stops at 72 instead of going on to 96 and 409.

**For the maintainers to decide:** Excel (Microsoft 365, Windows, observed) stops Decrease Font
Size at 8 pt: pressing it again does nothing, presumably so text can't shrink to an unreadable size
by accident. This PR steps on down to 1 pt instead, one point at a time, which seemed acceptable
since it's gradual and the user sees each step. If you'd rather match Excel, it's a one-line change
(drop 1–7 from `SIZES`) plus the test's expected values; happy to do either.

## What changed
- **engine** `cmd/format.rs`: `SIZES` is now 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, then Excel's Font Size list 8,
  9, 10, 11, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 28, 36, 48, 72. `step_font` moves to the next entry in
  that direction and leaves the size unchanged past either end (it fell back to 1 and 409). A size
  off the list steps to its neighbour (10.5 → 11 or 10, 7.5 → 8 or 7); a size typed above 72 steps
  down to 72 and stays there going up.

## Tests
New `crates/engine/tests/font_size_steps.rs` (all three fail on `main`):
- `decrease_steps_down_to_one_by_one_point_and_increase_climbs_back`: from 11 down to 1 and back up

title: Selection: a merged active cell is selected whole on open and on a sheet's first visit (#1348)
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #1348

## What was wrong

A click on a cell goes through `selection.set`, which grows the area until merged cells are whole, so clicking a merged cell already selects all of it. Two selections never went through that:

- **The selection a workbook opens with.** `DocState::new` builds it from the sheet's saved active cell with `Selection::at`, a bare cell.
- **A sheet's first visit.** `wb_switch_sheet` starts an unvisited sheet at the default selection, a bare A1.

With A1 merged across `A1:AG1` (the timesheet in the report), opening the file therefore outlined A1 alone, while the name box and formula bar showed the merged cell. Reproduced with `gridcraft-cli`: a saved workbook with `A1:AG1` merged reopens with selection `A1`, while `selection.set {"cell":"A1"}` returns `A1:AG1`.

## The fix

Both places now run `Selection::expand_merges` on the selection they start with, so a merged active cell is selected whole, with the active cell at its top-left, the same as a click. A remembered selection is unchanged (it was already expanded when it was made).

User-visible change: opening a workbook (or visiting a sheet for the first time) whose active cell is part of a merged cell now outlines the whole merged area instead of its first cell.

@oliverstreetcreative, if you still see the single-cell outline after *clicking* the merged cell (not just after opening), I'd appreciate a note: on `main` a click already selects the whole area here.

## Tests

- New `opening_and_switching_sheets_select_a_merged_active_cell_whole`: writes a workbook with `A1:AG1` merged on Sheet1 and `A1:C2` on Sheet2, opens it with `file.open` and checks the selection is `A1:AG1` (active A1), then `A1:C2` on Sheet2's first visit, and that a remembered `B3` comes back as it was. Fails on `main` (`A1`), passes with the fix.

title: io: save through a unique temporary file and keep the workbook's permissions
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
`write_file` saved every workbook through the same predictable sibling path
(`<name>.sctmp`) with a plain `fs::write`, so a save could follow a pre-planted symlink and overwrite
another file, two concurrent saves of the same workbook could truncate or delete each other's temporary
file, and the rename recreated the workbook with the umask defaults instead of the permissions it had.
Each save now writes to a private sibling path (process id, clock and a sequence number make it
unique), opened with `create_new`, copies the existing workbook's permissions onto it, syncs it and
renames it into place; a failure cleans up only that save's own temporary file. Regression tests cover
a planted sibling symlink, a 0640 workbook keeping its mode through a save, and a failed save leaving
another save's temporary file untouched. The full engine suite (289 tests) passes. Fixes #999

Targeted tests green locally; `cargo xtask ci` left to the project runners.

title: M12: formula separators follow the regional format
author: quantmind-br
body:
**Stacked on #443 and #447.** Only the last commit (`7e34e45`) is new here; the rest of the diff is those two PRs, merged together. This stays a draft until they land, and then I'll rebase it onto `main`.

With #443, the formula separators come from the interface language: French formulas always use `;` and `,`, and English formulas always use `,` and `.`. Excel doesn't work that way. It takes function names from the interface language but takes the argument and decimal separators from the Windows regional settings:

- English Excel with a Croatian region accepts `=SUM(1;2)` and `=1,5*1,5` (measured on #447).
- A French tester on #191 reports `;` and `,` in his French Excel 2013, and `,` and `.` in his French Excel 2024. The 2024 machine rejected `=FILTRE(...;...)` as a syntax error.
- Stack Overflow [57120417](https://stackoverflow.com/q/57120417) measured the same `INDEX` formula in all four combinations of French and English Excel with French and US regional settings. The table below is copied from there.

This PR splits the two:

- **Argument and decimal separators come from the Regional format** (`app.region`, File › Options from #447), whatever the interface language.
- **Array separators come from the language** (each `Dialect` keeps its preferred column and row separators). If the language's column separator is the region's decimal, the column separator becomes `\`. That reproduces every measured combination:

| Interface | Region | `INDEX({1,2;3,4.1},2,2)` is typed as |
| --- | --- | --- |
| French | France | `=INDEX({1.2;3.4,1};2;2)` |
| French | United States | `=INDEX({1\2;3\4.1},2,2)` |
| English | France | `=INDEX({1\2;3\4,1};2;2)` |
| English | United States | `=INDEX({1,2;3,4.1},2,2)` |

Code changes:

- `Separators::of(region)` becomes `Separators::new(locale, region)`.
- `Region` drops `array_column` and `array_row`, and keeps `list`.
- The editor, formula bar, cell display, Insert Function and argument hints all pass the workbook's region.

## Open `.xml` files as a table (like Excel's "As an XML table"), and read `.xls` formatting and pictures

Up to date with `main` (0.12.1). Three pieces, in order:

1. **`.xml` opens as a table** instead of CSV text (below).
2. **`.xls` import** shows its overview in the info bar only (no "OK" box), and reads cell formatting and pictures.
3. **Review follow-ups** (CodeRabbit, and a comparison with desktop Excel by @Harrison-Booth).

### 1. `.xml` as a table

Opening an `.xml` file read it as CSV text: the whole document landed in `A1`. An NF-e (Brazilian tax invoice) was unusable. `FileKind::from_path` did not know `.xml`, so it fell through to the CSV branch.

title: UI: Improve Command Palette keyboard navigation and layout
author: mbaksa
body:
### Problem

The Command Palette (Search Commands) has several usability issues:

- When navigating with the Up/Down arrow keys, the selected command can move outside the visible portion of the list.
- Keyboard navigation can become unresponsive because the search field repeatedly requests focus, which also causes the search field to flicker.
- The dialog changes its size and position as the number of filtered results decreases, making it difficult to visually track the search field.
- The search field and command list do not fully use the available dialog width.

### Fix

- Automatically scroll the command list to keep the selected item visible during keyboard navigation.
- Request focus for the search field only when the dialog is first opened. This required adding a `focus_initialized` field to the `Dialog` struct.
- Keep the dialog height stable while filtering by disabling vertical auto-shrinking, ensuring that the search field stays in the same position.
- Adjust the search field and list items to use the available width, eliminating unnecessary empty space on the right.

### New keyboard navigation features

- **Page Up / Page Down:** Move through the command list by approximately one visible page, with the step calculated from the list height and row spacing.
- **Ctrl+Home / Ctrl+End:** Jump to the first or last command.
- **Home / End:** Continue to move the text cursor within the search field.

### Tests

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — OK
- [x] `cargo check --workspace` — OK
- [x] `cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui` — OK

title: XLSX: locale-specific built-in number formats read as Excel shows them, so their dates aren't serial numbers
author: tisca26
body:
## What this changes

Dates stored with a locale-specific built-in number format now show as dates instead of serial numbers, and keep their date format when the workbook is saved.

**Cause.** A `numFmtId` from 27–36 or 50–81 has no format code in the file: ECMA-376 §18.8.30 defines these ids only for the East Asian and Thai locales. Workbooks from other locales use them too. A workbook saved with the es-MX region stored its dates as 58. `crates/xlsx/src/tables.rs` only knew the en-US ids (0–22, 37–49), so `styles.rs` read the rest as General. The dates showed as `46307` where Excel shows `12/10/26`, and saving wrote them back as General.

**Fix.** `LOCALE_FORMATS` maps each locale-specific id to the en-US built-in that Excel shows it as, and `builtin_format` consults it. `builtin_id` is unchanged, so saving writes the en-US id (58 → 14), which Excel shows the same way. The `.xls` reader and pivot caches use the same lookup, so they get the fix too.

## Observed, not looked up

The mapping comes from black-box observation of Excel for Mac (es-MX region). I used a synthetic workbook with one cell per built-in id 0–81, all holding 46307.5625, and read each cell's `number format`, `number format local` and displayed text through AppleScript. The workbook was never saved.

| ids | Excel shows them as |
|---|---|
| 27–31, 36, 50–58, 71, 72 | `m/d/yy`, the short date (14) |
| 32–35, 77 | `h:mm:ss` (21) |
| 59–62, 63–66, 67–68, 69–70 | 1–4, 5–8, 9–10, 12–13 |
| 73, 74, 75, 76, 78, 79, 80, 81 | 15, 16, 17, 20, 22, 45, 46, 47 |
| 23–26 | General (unchanged) |

## Tests

- `tables::tests::locale_builtin_ids_read_as_excel_shows_them`: the mapping, ids that stay General (23–26, 82+), save as 14, and every en-US built-in untouched.
- `tests::fixtures::locale_date_format_reads_as_a_date_and_saves_as_one`: a synthetic workbook with a date in id 58 reads as `m/d/yyyy`, then is written and read again with the same format.

title: fix(engine): Advanced Filter copyTo clears only the real output footprint and refuses overflow (#1031)
author: Vhierly
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1031 — `data.advancedFilter` with `copyTo` destroyed workbook data in two ways:

1. **Over-clear:** the destination rectangle cleared before writing used `list.height()` (the whole input list) instead of the actual output height, so every cell in that tall rectangle was deleted — including unrelated data *below* the copied result.
2. **Silent truncation:** destinations were built with `filter_map(|..| ..?)` over `CellRef::offset` (returns `Option`), so any output cell past the sheet edge was dropped with no error, and `offset_clamped` on the reported range hid it. The command returned success with a partial result.

## Fix

`crates/engine/src/cmd/whatif.rs` (56 insertions, 2 deletions):

- Compute `out_range` from the **real output** (`rows_out.len()` rows × `list.width()` cols) using checked `CellRef::offset`, and `?`-return `bad(CMD, "the extract range doesn't fit on the sheet")` when the output leaves the sheet. This happens **before** any mutation, so refusal is atomic.
- Use `out_range` for the clear loop instead of `extract`; cells below the real output now survive.
- The pre-existing overlap guard (`extract.intersects(&list)`) is left exactly as it was, so no existing rejection behaviour changes.

## Tests

Two new regression tests:

- `advanced_filter_copy_preserves_cells_below_the_output` — sentinels below a 2-row output survive.
- `advanced_filter_copy_refuses_overflow_atomically` — edge overflow refused with the workbook untouched; the exact-fit destination one row/one column in from the edge succeeds.

title: Accuracy: system date/time codes, colour-only sections and Excel's fractions
author: MacJedi42
body:
## What

Three classes of number formats where GridCraft's display differs from Excel's, found with the [Spreadsheet Accuracy Suite](https://github.com/MacJedi42/Spreadsheet-Accuracy-Suite)'s number-format golden (Excel's own `TEXT()` answers) and confirmed on Windows Excel 16.0 (build 20430).

### System date and time codes

`[$-F400]` / `[$-x-systime]` (system long time) and `[$-F800]` / `[$-x-sysdate]` (system long date) rendered as an empty string or with the written pattern. Excel draws the system pattern (en-US: `h:mm:ss AM/PM` and `dddd, mmmm d, yyyy`) and ignores whatever follows the tag. `[$-F800]dddd, mmmm dd, yyyy` shows "Thursday, March 1, 1900", not "March 01". A colour or condition on the section is kept.

### A section with only a colour or condition

`[Blue]` there is a whole number-format code, not a colour name in the prose. In Excel's custom format codes, a tag in square brackets like `[Blue]`, `[Red]` or `[Color10]` sets the text colour for that section. Normally it sits in front of a pattern, as in `[Blue]#,##0.00`, which shows the number with two decimals in blue.

The case fixed here is a format code that is only the colour tag, with no pattern after it:

| Format code | Value | Excel shows | 0.7.0 showed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `[Blue]` | 1234.5678 | `1234.5678` (in blue) | nothing |
| `[Blue]` | -3 | `-3` | `-` |
| `0.00;[Red]` | -1234.5678 | `1234.5678` (in red) | nothing |
| `[>100];0.0` | 1234.5678 | `1234.5678` | nothing |

With no digits or text to draw, Excel falls back to showing the number as General. GridCraft was treating the section as empty and drew nothing, or a lone minus sign.

In `0.00;[Red]`, the `;` separates sections: positives use `0.00`, and negatives use the second section, which is only `[Red]`. So negatives appear in red, as General, without the minus sign, because a second section never adds one. `[>100]` is a condition tag, and a section with only a condition follows the same rule.

title: Recalc: an anchor's new formula no longer reads its old spill area
author: nihilist-narwhal
body:
## What happened

When a dynamic array's anchor gets a new formula that reads the cells its old array spilled into, the new formula keeps the old values:

- A1 `=SEQUENCE(3)`, then A1 `=SUM(A2:A3)+1`: A2:A3 are empty now, but A1 shows 6 (2 + 3 + 1) instead of 1.
- A1 `=SEQUENCE(3)`, then A1 `=SEQUENCE(1,A2+1)`: it reads A2 as 2 and spills over A1:C1 instead of showing 1.
- A1 `=SEQUENCE(3)`, then A1 `=SEQUENCE(MAX(1,A3-1))`: it reads A3 as 3 and spills 1, 2 over A1:A2 instead of showing 1.

Recalculating from scratch (Calculate Now) gives the right values.

## Why

The new formula is evaluated while the old array is still laid out, because spills are only cleared and laid out again at write-back. So it reads the old spilled values. Write-back then sends the dependents of the changed spill area to another round, but it leaves the anchor itself out so that an array never reads its own array. Once the old array was gone, nothing evaluated the anchor again.

## Fix

At write-back, the anchor goes to the next round with the other dependents of its spill area when its old array is gone or only partly covered by the new one. It is still left out when the new array covers the old one, because there reading the area would mean reading its own array.

## Tests

- `calc`: `an_anchor_given_a_formula_that_reads_its_old_spill_area_sees_it_empty` covers the three cases above (the anchor stops spilling, spills somewhere else, or spills over part of the old area). It fails without the fix.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes on Linux (fmt, clippy -D warnings, test, assets, layers, wasm, parity, keytips).
- A command-sequence fuzz soak (`GRIDCRAFT_FUZZ_SEED` 0–399, 200 steps each) gives the same results as on main. The 21 seeds that fail on main fail with the same first invariant, and no seed fails that didn't before.
- The code merges cleanly with #1061 and #1428, and the calc tests pass with all three applied. This PR and #1428 both add a ROADMAP progress-log row, so whichever lands second n…

title: Recalc: formulas reading an array that loses a spill conflict see #SPILL!
author: nihilist-narwhal
body:
## What happened

With B1 `=SEQUENCE(3)` and A2 `=SEQUENCE(1,3)`, both arrays want B2. After a full recalculation (opening a file, Calculate Now), B1 spills and A2 is `#SPILL!`. The formulas that read A2's array keep its values anyway: `=A2*10` shows 10, `=SUM(A2#)` shows 6, and `=C2` and `=SUM(C2:C3)` show 3, although C2 is empty. If the same formulas are entered one at a time, they give `#SPILL!`, `#REF!`, 0 and 0.

The same thing happens on an ordinary edit that recalculates both arrays. With B1 `=SEQUENCE(X1)` and A2 `=SEQUENCE(1,X1)`, changing X1 from 1 to 3 makes A2 `#SPILL!`, but `=A2*10` keeps 10.

## Why

While the pass runs, an array is only checked against things that can't move in that pass: cells, merges, tables, and the spills of arrays that are not being recalculated. A full recalculation lays every spill out again from scratch. So two arrays of the same pass both look free, and the formulas evaluated after them read both. At write-back the arrays are laid out in row-major order, and the second one finds B2 taken and becomes `#SPILL!`. The readers of a changed spill area are evaluated again in another round. But an array that is blocked at write-back has no new area, and its anchor did not count as changed, so its readers kept what they had read.

## Fix

When an array is blocked at write-back, the formulas that read its anchor, or any cell of the area it would have spilled into, go to the next round, where they read `#SPILL!` and empty cells. Only arrays that were not already blocked during the pass reach this point, because an array blocked during the pass is already `#SPILL!` for every formula evaluated after it.

## Tests

- `calc`: `formulas_reading_an_array_that_loses_a_spill_conflict_read_spill_errors` covers the anchor, `A2#` and the cells of the area A2 would have spilled into. It fails without the fix.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes on Linux (fmt, clippy -D warnings, test, assets, layers, wasm, parity, keytips).

title: Stop BINOM.INV/CRITBINOM hanging when trials exceed 2^53
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/functions/src/stat.rs:1244` (no existing issue): BINOM.INV / CRITBINOM never return (infinite loop) when trials is above 2^53, freezing recalculation.

## Cause
`binom_inv`, which backs both BINOM.INV and CRITBINOM, finds k by bisection on f64. It loops `while hi - lo > 1.0` and computes `mid = ((lo + hi) / 2.0).floor()`. When the number of trials is above 2^53, neighbouring f64 values are more than 1 apart, so `mid` rounds back to `lo` or `hi`. The gap never shrinks and the loop never ends. A formula such as `=BINOM.INV(1E17,0.5,0.5)` or `=CRITBINOM(1E300,1,0.5)` therefore hangs recalculation.

## Fix
The bisection loop now stops as soon as `mid` is no longer strictly between `lo` and `hi`, and returns the current upper bound `hi`. For trial counts up to 2^53 the loop behaves as before, so ordinary results are unchanged.

## Verified
- Regression test `binom_inv_huge_trials_returns`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p gridcraft-functions --lib binom_inv_huge_trials_returns`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Trials above 2^53 are still accepted, not rejected with #NUM!. For these inputs the result is the bracket's upper bound when bisection can no longer make progress, so it is only as precise as f64 allows at that magnitude. `binom_cdf` is unchanged.

title: Refuse table names that clash with defined names or R1C1 references
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/insert.rs:477` (no existing issue): table.rename accepts a name already used by a defined name (and R1C1-style names), which insert.table and Define Name refuse.

## Cause
`table.rename` only checked the name's characters and whether another table already had that name. It never checked the workbook's defined names, which `insert.table` does. Also, `valid_table_name` had no R1C1 check (Define Name has one), so names like `R2C3`, `c` and `r` were accepted by both `table.rename` and `insert.table`.

`table.rename` now refuses a name used by any defined name, ignoring case, with the same 'already exists' error that `insert.table` gives. `valid_table_name` now also rejects R1C1-shaped names using the existing `is_r1c1` helper from `formulas.rs`, which is now `pub(crate)`.

title: Fix fraction numerators saturating at u64::MAX for large values
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/numfmt/src/render.rs:470` (no existing issue): Number format: a fraction with no whole-number part shows 18446744073709551615 as the numerator for large values.

## Cause
In a fraction format with no whole-number part (`?/10`, `?/1000000000`, `?/?`), the whole value goes into the numerator, and the code computed it with a float-to-u64 cast. Rust saturates that cast, so once value × denominator passed about 1.8e19 the cell showed 18446744073709551615 as the numerator, with no error marker.

## Fix
`render_fraction` now keeps the numerator as an f64. Values of 1e15 or more skip the continued-fraction search and become `n/1`. Numerators of 1e15 or more are printed with the same 15-significant-digit `fixed` routine the whole-number part uses, so `?/1000000000` with 2e10 shows `20000000000000000000/1000000000`.

## Verified
- Regression test `fraction_numerator_beyond_u64`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p gridcraft-numfmt --lib fraction_numerator_beyond_u64`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`approximate` keeps its own `x >= 1e15` early return. `render_fraction` no longer reaches that branch, so I left it alone. Formats with a whole-number part render as before.

title: Reject non-regular files in read_file and bound the read itself
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #1018

## Cause
read_file compared std::fs::metadata(path).len() against 2 GB, then called an unbounded std::fs::read(path) as a separate step. Nothing checked that the path was a regular file. Special files such as FIFOs were accepted: they report a size of 0 but can supply any amount of data, or block forever when no writer is attached. A file that grew after the size check could also exceed the limit.

## Fix
read_file now checks the path's metadata and rejects non-regular files with a "<path>: not a regular file" error before opening them, so an idle FIFO cannot block the open. After opening, it checks the handle's own metadata again for is_file and size, in case the path was replaced in between. It then reads through a new read_bounded helper capped at MAX_FILE_BYTES + 1 bytes. If more than MAX_FILE_BYTES arrive, it returns the existing "files larger than 2 GB aren't supported" error. The metadata check and the bounded read therefore report oversize input with the same message. A unit test covers read_bounded at the exact limit, one byte over, and on an endless reader.

## Verified
- Regression tests `read_file_rejects_fifo`, `read_file_rejects_fifo_without_writer_promptly`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p gridcraft-engine --test read_file_bounds`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The wasm32 read_file stub and the 2 GB limit value are unchanged. read_file_returns_ordinary_file_unchanged is a success-path test that also passes without the fix.

title: Accuracy: Excel's powers, subnormals, unary plus, ROUND digits and PMT at tiny rates
author: MacJedi42
body:
Five calculation edge cases where GridCraft's answer differed from Excel's. Each was measured in Windows Excel (16.0, build 20430) with synthetic workbooks, black-box: only the values Excel shows and saves.

## Problem

| Formula | Excel | GridCraft before |
|---|---|---|
| `=(-8)^(1/3)` | -1.9999999999999998 | #NUM! |
| `=(-8)^0.5` | #NUM! | #NUM! |
| `=2^-1074` (a subnormal) | 0 | 4.94E-324 |
| `=+TRUE` | TRUE | 1 |
| `=ROUND(1.23456,2.9999999999999996)` | 1.235 (digits read as 3) | 1.23 (digits truncated to 2) |
| `=PMT(1E-9,360,100000)` | -277.7778279166697 | wrong after the 7th digit |

- **Powers.** `^` and `POWER` used `powf`, whose last bits differ from Excel's for integer exponents, and a negative base with a fractional exponent was always `#NUM!`. Excel gives the odd root when `1/y` is an odd integer.
- **Subnormals.** Excel holds any number smaller than 2.2250738585072014E-308 in size as 0, whether typed, read from a file or computed.
- **Unary plus** turned a logical into a number; in Excel it changes nothing.
- **ROUND digits** (and every function using the shared digits argument) were truncated straight away; Excel rounds them to 15 significant digits first.
- **PMT** formed `1+rate` before raising it to `nper`, so a tiny rate lost most of its digits.

### Why the subnormal case? Isn't Excel objectively worse than an IEEE 754 subnormal (gradual underflow)?

Well... yes, it technically is numerically,  2^-1074 is exactly representable as a double, so 4.94E-324 is the true answer and 0 is wrong however:

- The difference spreads into other results, and that's what users notice. No one reads `4.94E-324` in a cell, but formulas that depend on it come out differently:

  | Formula                              | Excel     | GridCraft without the change |
  |--------------------------------------|-----------|------------------------------|
  | `=1/2^-1074`                         | `#DIV/0!` | `#NUM!` (overflow)           |
  | `=IF(2^-1074=0,"zero","not zero…

title: XLSX: don't add a pageSetup the workbook didn't have (A4 sheets turned into Letter)
author: sky-helper
body:
## Problem
Saving wrote `<pageSetup orientation="portrait"/>` for every worksheet, including sheets whose file had no `<pageSetup>` and sheets created in GridCraft. Without `paperSize` that element means Letter: ECMA-376 gives `paperSize` the default 1. A sheet without `<pageSetup>` names no paper and is printed on the application's default paper (seen in LibreOffice), A4 in most locales. So opening and saving a workbook without pageSetup moved its sheets from that paper to Letter, changing page breaks and page counts.

Two more paths ended on Letter too:
- a `paperSize` outside the 14 sizes GridCraft names was dropped on read;
- the Page Setup commands kept other spellings of a paper as given (`11x17`, `A-4`), which the writer, knowing only the XLSX names, saved as Letter.

## Fix
- `PrintSettings::page_setup` (`#[serde(default)]`): the sheet has page setup of its own. The XLSX reader sets it when the sheet has `<pageSetup>`; choosing a paper (`pageLayout.size`, `pageLayout.pageSetup {paper}`) sets it through the new `PrintSettings::set_paper`.
- `PrintSettings::paper_code`: a `paperSize` number without a name, written back as it was; choosing a paper clears it. Layout still uses Letter for it, as before.
- The writer emits `<pageSetup>` only when `page_setup` is set or a value differs from the default (paper other than Letter, landscape, scale ≠ 100, Fit To, kept printer settings `r:id`). Orientation, scale and Fit To need no flag: their defaults mean the same whether written or not. The paper does, because "no `<pageSetup>`" leaves the paper to the application while "no `paperSize`" means Letter, so an explicit Letter choice is remembered.
- Both paper commands keep the name XLSX saves (`11x17` → Tabloid, `A-4` → A4, `us letter` → Letter). `pageLayout.size` now refuses a paper it can't lay out, as `pageLayout.pageSetup` already did.

title: Rows: keep heights saved in the file when opening
author: sky-helper
body:
Opening and saving an XLSX workbook no longer changes the row heights it saved, and editing a row that merged cells cross no longer collapses it.

Since #855 (for #833), opening a file fitted every row that has cells to our estimate of its content and kept the saved height only when the estimate came out smaller. The estimate is approximate, so a plain open-and-save rewrote heights the file had saved. Most visibly, a row of wrapped text merged across several columns, saved at 42.75pt, was measured against its first column alone and grew to the 409.5pt cap.

## Changes (XLSX only)
- Opening fits only rows saved without a height (`engine/src/io.rs`). A row the file saved a height for keeps it exactly. #833 still holds for rows saved without a height: they grow to their tallest font. This replaces #855's grow-only clamp.
- Merged cells don't size their row (`engine/src/cmd/mod.rs`): their text spans several columns or rows, which the per-cell line count doesn't measure. This matches Excel as Microsoft documents it in the support article "You cannot use the AutoFit feature for rows or columns that contain merged cells in Excel" (KB 212010; the page has since been retired, so no link), and our own AutoFit Column Width, which already skips merged cells.
- Because merged text isn't measured, an edit never shrinks a row that a merged area crosses: the row may grow (for a taller unmerged cell) but keeps at least the height it has, so the merged paragraph it was sized for isn't cut off. AutoFit Row Height, the explicit command, still sizes such a row by its other cells alone and may shrink it.
- The XLSX reader keeps every saved `ht` (`xlsx/src/sheet_read.rs`), including one equal to the sheet default. Rows are streamed before `sheetFormatPr` is applied, so the old "a height equal to the default is noise" check compared with the built-in 15pt instead of the file's default: on a 14.25pt sheet a 15pt row was dropped and reopened at 14.25pt (and at 16.5pt on a 16.5pt sheet).

title: Calc: open without recalculating (file.open recalculate:false; honour manual calc mode)
author: sky-helper
body:
## Summary
`file.open` can open a workbook with the results stored in it instead of calculating every formula again, and a workbook saved in manual calculation mode now opens that way by default.
- `recalculate: false` keeps the stored results: a `TODAY()` keeps the date it was saved with, and array results (legacy and dynamic) show as stored. `recalculate: true` always calculates.
- Without the flag, formulas are calculated again as before, unless the workbook was saved in manual calculation mode and doesn't ask to be calculated on load. A workbook asks when its `.xlsx` has `<calcPr fullCalcOnLoad="1">`, its `.xls` has an `Uncalced` record, or GridCraft couldn't keep some of its cached array results (see How).
- The result carries `recalculated: bool`; a non-boolean `recalculate` is refused before the file is read. A path that is already open is switched to as it is: the result has `alreadyOpen`, plus `recalculateIgnored: true` when `recalculate` was given.
- A formula stored without a cached result is blank until it is calculated.
- `view.newWindow` doesn't calculate its copy, so a second window shows the same results.

## Why
Some workbooks have to read exactly as they were saved (approval forms, signed reports). GridCraft recalculated every formula on open, so volatile functions showed the day the file was viewed and any difference between calculation engines showed up as changed numbers; the workbook's manual calculation mode wasn't taken into account on open either.

## Behaviour change
- A manual-calculation `.xlsx` (or `.xls`) that doesn't ask for a full calculation on load now opens with its stored results by default; with `fullCalcOnLoad` (`.xls`: `Uncalced`) it is calculated as before. Automatic-mode workbooks are unchanged.
- This applies to every entry point that opens through `file.open` without `recalculate`: the desktop and web UI (File › Open, recent files, files opened from the OS), the CLI (`run --in`, `convert`, `eval --in`, `cat`, `info`, `mcp -…

title: Web: let the embedding page drive the control channel over postMessage
author: sky-helper
body:
Web: let the embedding page drive the control channel over postMessage

## Summary

The web build can already be embedded in a same-origin `<iframe>` with `?host=parent`: the parent
sends a workbook (`gridcraft:open`) and receives what GridCraft saves (`gridcraft:save`,
`gridcraft:dirty`). It could not *drive* the app: the control channel (`engine.execute`,
`document.inspect`, `cell.get`, `ui.*`, every command id) only existed as the desktop app's
localhost TCP port.

This PR carries the same methods over `postMessage`:

- Parent → GridCraft: `{type: "gridcraft:control", id, method, params?}`
- GridCraft → parent: `{type: "gridcraft:reply", id, ok: true, result}` / `{…, ok: false, error}`
- `gridcraft:ready` lists `"control"` in `capabilities`.

The workbooks the parent sends and its requests wait in one queue and run in the order they
arrived, after the app's per-frame logic: `gridcraft:open X` followed by `cell.set` edits X, and
every request is answered in that same frame. The message ⇄ request conversion and the queue live
in `apps/gridcraft-web/src/protocol.rs` (plain JSON, unit-tested natively); `host.rs` only moves
messages in and out of JavaScript.

## Threat model

- **Who is heard:** only messages whose `event.source` is `window.parent` **and** whose
  `event.origin` equals GridCraft's own `location.origin` (the same two checks `gridcraft:open`
  already had).
- **Where answers go:** replies, saves and dirty reports are posted with `targetOrigin` set to
  GridCraft's own origin. The only `"*"` post is the fixed-text `gridcraft:failed` sent when the
  page's URL has no origin; it carries no user data.
- **What it grants:** nothing new. A same-origin parent can already reach into the frame
  (`iframe.contentWindow`) and run arbitrary code there. Cross-origin pages are never heard.
  Message data is parsed as JSON, never evaluated.
- **Resource limits:** a control message holds at most 16 MiB of JSON text, checked in UTF-16
  code units before it is copied in…

title: Fonts: let the host register extra fonts at runtime (CJK on the web build)
author: sky-helper
body:
Fonts: let the host register extra fonts at runtime (CJK on the web build)

## Summary

The web build has no system fonts and bundles none (fonts live in craft-fonts, never in this
repo), so Chinese, Japanese and Korean text renders as tofu there. This lets whoever hosts
GridCraft hand it fonts while it runs:

- `theme::add_font(name, bytes, index) -> Result<FontAdded { added, covers }, String>` registers a
  TrueType/OpenType face process-wide. Every font set built afterwards appends it to the end of
  every family, after the system fallback faces and any font added before it, so it only catches
  glyphs those lack (where two added fonts overlap, the first one added wins).
- The same checks, in the same order, on every path: the name (non-empty, at most 200
  characters), a name already added (ignored and reported with `added: false`), the size (at most
  64 MiB), how many there are (at most 32 fonts, 256 MiB in all), then the face itself with the
  parser and call epaint uses (egui panics on a face it can't read).
  `theme::check_new_font(name, len)` runs everything but the last check before any bytes are
  copied or decoded.
- `SheetApp` notices an added font and rebuilds its fonts at the next frame;
  `SheetApp::reload_fonts()` is public.
- UI command `app.font.add {name, base64, index?} → {name, added, covers: {hangul, han, kana}}`,
  listed in `engine.commands`, so the desktop control channel and a connected MCP server reach it.
- Web host bridge: `gridcraft:font {name, bytes, index?}` (an `ArrayBuffer` or `Uint8Array`),
  answered with `gridcraft:fontResult {name, ok, added, covers | error}`; `gridcraft:ready` carries
  `capabilities: ["font"]`. A parent sends `gridcraft:ready` → `gridcraft:font` → `gridcraft:open`.

## Memory

An added font is kept exactly once, for the life of the app: its bytes become a `&'static [u8]`
(`Box::leak`, `FontData::from_static`), which epaint shares each time it rebuilds its fonts. Owned

title: Let GROUPBY and PIVOTBY take a LAMBDA as their function
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #903

## Cause
The evaluator turned a LAMBDA argument into a plain value before calling GROUPBY/PIVOTBY, and a lambda as a plain value is #CALC!. On top of that, the functions could only pick from a fixed list of built-in aggregates (numbers or text names), so they had no way to call a lambda.

## Fix
When the function argument of GROUPBY (argument 3) or PIVOTBY (argument 4) is a LAMBDA, the evaluator now passes it to the function context instead of turning it into a value. GROUPBY/PIVOTBY then call it once per group (and per total) with that group's values as a column; a result that is not a single value gives #CALC!, and a lambda that does not take exactly one parameter gives #VALUE!.

## Verified
- Regression test `groupby_and_pivotby_take_a_lambda`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p gridcraft-calc --lib groupby_and_pivotby_take_a_lambda`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Built-in aggregate names, numbers and bare function names still work as before. Any other value given as the function still returns #VALUE!.

title: fix(solver): commit solutions and reports atomically
author: euisuh
body:
Requesting a Solver report can currently return an error after changing solution cells and the saved model: for example, an Answer report on a structurally protected workbook, or an unsupported Limits report.

Prepare all report data before mutation, then commit the optional solution, saved model and report sheets in one existing edit transaction. Refused reports preserve the workbook, dirty state, selection, revision, Undo/Redo and journal. Successful solves and reports share one Undo step. Preserve locked-cell/legacy-array checks and row autofit after inserted report sheets shift the model sheet.

Closes #1050

Validation:

title: Conditional formatting: text rules never match an error value (#1162)
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #1162.

In Excel the "Text that Contains", "Begins With" and "Ends With" rules are `SEARCH`/`LEFT`/`RIGHT` formulas, which fail on an error value, so an error cell is never formatted by them, and it always matches "Does Not Contain". GridCraft matched on the error's display text instead (`v.display()` in `CfCache::look`), so `#N/A` "contained" `a` and "began with" `#`, and `#DIV/0!` "ended with" `!`; "does not contain `a`" left `#N/A` unformatted.

The change in `crates/engine/src/cf.rs` skips error values in the three positive text rules and matches them in `notContainsText`. Nothing else in the evaluation changes; `beginsWith`/`endsWith` stay literal and the wildcard question of #1161 is left alone (it has its own fix approach on the issue).

Regression test `cf::tests::text_rules_skip_error_values` puts `=NA()`, `=1/0` and text in four columns and checks the four rules against the table in the issue. `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -p gridcraft-engine` pass.

Developed with AI assistance (Claude Code); reviewed and tested locally.

title: Control channel: ui.dialog.confirm sends what OK sends (#1459)
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #1459.

Clicking OK in a dialog and confirming it with `ui.dialog.confirm` over the control channel should run the same command with the same parameters. OK goes through `build_params(&d)`, which reshapes the field values for several dialogs (`cfQuick` wraps them in `rule`, Text to Columns turns the check boxes into `delimiters`, Remove Duplicates and Subtotal split `columnsText` into `columns`, Data Validation drops the fields its type/operator don't use, Zoom, Series and Define Name have their own adjustments). `ui.dialog.confirm` sent `Json::Object(d.values.clone())` instead, so a Highlight Cells rule confirmed from the control channel added nothing (`home.conditionalFormat` saw no `rule` and asked for the dialog again) and a Text to Columns confirm ignored the ticked delimiter.

Changes:
- `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs`: `build_params` is `pub(crate)`, with a one-line doc.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs`: `ui.dialog.confirm` builds the parameters with it.
- `docs/control-protocol.md`: says `confirm` runs the dialog's command with the same parameters as its OK button.
- `crates/ui-egui/tests/dialog_confirm.rs`: two tests drive dialogs over the control channel (`ui.dialog`, `ui.dialog.set`, `ui.dialog.confirm`) and check the model: Greater Than… adds a `CellIs` rule with the typed value; Text to Columns with Semicolon ticked splits `a;b` into two cells. Both fail on `main` and pass with the change.

`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui --test dialog_confirm` pass.

Developed with AI assistance (Claude Code); reviewed and tested locally.

title: XLSX: preserve carriage returns in saved text
author: derechopiano
body:
Saving a workbook could silently turn carriage returns in cell text into line feeds: the XLSX writer emitted raw CR characters, which XML parsers normalize on reopen. This changes cell values and can leave cached formula results inconsistent with the saved text.

Encode CR as `_x000D_` in ST_Xstring values, matching the representation GridCraft already reads. Escape CR as `` in other XML text nodes. Ordinary LF and literal `_x000D_` text retain their existing behavior.

The regression test uses a synthetic workbook with CRLF, lone CR, LF, a literal escape marker, a cached formula string, and a comment. It failed on the original code and passes with the fix. The existing XLSX reader test already covers decoding `_x000D_`.

Related carriage-return issues in [WordCraft #423](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/issues/423) and [PhotoCraft #3074](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/issues/3074) were already fixed in merged [WordCraft PR #479](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/pull/479) and [PhotoCraft PR #3138](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/pull/3138), respectively. Those concern paragraph and caret behavior; this PR addresses GridCraft's XLSX serialization.

Validation: `cargo test -p gridcraft-xlsx --lib` (174 passed); `cargo xtask ci` (all eight stages passed). No Excel application smoke test was run.

Fixes #1488.

title: Recalc: defined names as static precedents, per-pass name cache, TEXT fast path
author: RedBearAK
body:
**Summary**

- Formulas that use a defined name become ordinary static dependencies instead of being recalculated on every edit; names are followed through names to a bounded depth and nesting, past which a formula stays dynamic.
- A recalc pass parses each name's formula once instead of once per cell that uses it, and `TEXT()` over a range converts the format code once (an integer through `"0"` is its decimal digits).
- Changing a defined name recalculates the formulas that read it, directly or through another name, including the hidden names that commands rewrite without a structural edit and the Watch Window list, after an undo or redo too.
- Tests at the depth and nesting bounds (both sides, on a 1 MiB thread), for recursive and mutually recursive names, for the readers of rewritten hidden names, and a sweep of the `TEXT` fast path against the renderer.

A real workbook written by a generating library (one 1M-cell sheet, 49K live formulas calling workbook-level LAMBDA names such as `=fn_decode(Z2, rng_return)` over a 1,900-row named lookup range, no cached values because the library writes none) took **447 s to open** and **about 10 s per unrelated edit** on a 2-core machine, and scrolling ran at under 1 fps. Excel opens and edits the same file without trouble. Profiling the open (stack samples) found three independent causes, all in how formulas that use defined names are handled.

Rebased onto current main; the conditional-format statistics change this PR used to carry landed separately in #1098 and is no longer part of it.

`precedents()` treated any defined name as dynamic (`Expr::Name(_) => dynamic = true`), and dynamic nodes join the dirty set on every recalc, and a second time on open when spills exist. So a column of LAMBDA calls was recomputed on every edit anywhere in the workbook. title: Calc: CELL understands the German info types
author: Hamza0101
body:
Addresses the second half of #1489, reported by @KNUFFIXX.

## The bug

Excel translates `CELL`'s **function name** but not its first argument, which is a plain string in the file. A German Excel saves `ZELLE("Dateiname";A1)` as `CELL("Dateiname",A1)`, and `cell_info` matched only the English names, so every German info type came out `#VALUE!`.

The reported corpus run puts that at **83 of 400 real workbooks (21%)**, 6,931 calls.

## The change

The twelve names are accepted as aliases of their English counterparts — `adresse`, `zeile`, `spalte`, `inhalt`, `typ`, `breite`, `dateiname`, `schutz`, `farbe`, `klammern`, `präfix`, with `format` needing no entry since it is spelled the same in German.

The argument is now lower-cased by **Unicode** rather than ASCII. Without that, `PRÄFIX` stays `prÄfix` and misses the table — the reporter measured that specific trap, and `cell_accepts_the_german_info_types` pins it so it cannot come back.

An unknown type is still `#VALUE!`, which the same test asserts: this understands more names, it does not make `CELL` permissive.

## What this does **not** fix

The issue's first half, `CELL("filename")` always returning `""`, is not addressed here, so the formula the report leads with —

```
=MID(CELL("Dateiname",A1),FIND("]",CELL("Dateiname",A1))+1,31)
```

— still fails. It fails one step later, in `FIND` on an empty string rather than in `CELL`, which is worth knowing when reading a `check` run.

I looked at both ways to carry the path and would rather a maintainer chose:

- **A `Host` method.** Only two implementors (`PassHost`, `FnHost`), and a defaulted method breaks neither. But the value has to reach `PassHost::new`, which means `recalc_all` and `evaluate_expr` grow a parameter, and those are called from `pivot_calc`, `cmd/whatif` and `cmd/formulas`.

title: Next/Previous Sheet never land on a hidden sheet
author: nihilist-narwhal
body:
## What happened

Next Sheet and Previous Sheet (the arrows by the sheet tabs, Ctrl+PageDown / Ctrl+PageUp, Option+Right / Option+Left on a Mac) could activate a hidden sheet. In a workbook with `Data` and a hidden `Meta`, Next Sheet from `Data` showed `Meta`, though its tab stays hidden; the same happened with Previous Sheet and a hidden first sheet. Excel stays on the current sheet.

Other ways the active sheet changes could also leave a hidden sheet active: deleting the active sheet when a hidden sheet followed it, moving or copying a hidden sheet (with `sheet.move`), and opening a file whose saved active tab is hidden. Hiding the active sheet jumped to the first visible sheet of the workbook rather than its neighbour.

## Why

`step_sheet` looked for the next visible sheet, but clamped the search at the ends of the workbook and then switched to wherever it stopped, visible or not. Deleting the active sheet activated whatever sheet moved into its place, `sheet.move` always activated the moved sheet or the copy, and an opened workbook kept the `activeTab` it was saved with.

## Fix

- Next / Previous Sheet go to the nearest visible sheet that way, skipping hidden and very hidden sheets, and stay put when there is none (no wrapping, as in Excel). The search lives in two new `Workbook` helpers, `next_visible_sheet` and `visible_sheet_from`.
- Hiding or deleting the active sheet activates the next visible sheet, or the previous one when none follows.
- Moving or copying a hidden sheet leaves the active sheet alone.
- A workbook whose active sheet is hidden opens on the nearest visible sheet (`DocState::new`). The XLSX writer already wrote a visible active tab.
- `sheet.activate` still activates a hidden sheet, so scripts and `gridcraft-cli --sheet` can work on one. Its params doc and `docs/decisions.md` record this.
- The tab-bar arrows get accessible names ("Previous sheet", "Next sheet").
- ROADMAP progress log and `docs/ui-parity.md` updated.

title: Read securities function dates in the workbook's date system
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #1457

## Cause
The financial date helpers `ymd` and `serial` in `crates/functions/src/financial.rs` always used the 1900 date system, and the worksheet functions never passed `c.date_system()` to them. In a 1904 workbook, every date argument was therefore read 1,462 days off, which shifted coupon dates, day counts and year fractions (e.g. COUPNCD gave 30 May instead of 31 May).

## Fix
`ymd`, `serial` and all the helpers built on them now take a `DateSystem` parameter: `days360`, `day_count`, `year_frac`, `year_basis`, `shift_months`, `coupons`, the COUP*, discount, T-bill, maturity, bond and odd-period helpers. Every securities function and AMORLINC/AMORDEGRC pass `c.date_system()`. The local `is_leap` copy is replaced by `gridcraft_core::date::is_leap`, and the year-fraction fallback at the end of the calendar uses `max_serial(sys)`.

## Verified
- Regression test `securities_read_dates_in_the_1904_system`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p gridcraft-functions --lib securities_read_dates_in_the_1904_system`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The financial 30/360 and actual/actual rules are unchanged and stay separate from DAYS360/YEARFRAC, so a 1904 workbook gives the same result as a 1900 workbook for the same calendar dates. This does not copy the cases where Excel's own 1904 result differs from its 1900 result. Date text in date arguments (#1038) and the Analysis ToolPak host's fixed 1900 system are not changed.

title: Calc: a dynamic array of one value still anchors a spill range
author: Hamza0101
body:
Fixes #1491, reported by @KNUFFIXX.

## The bug

`C1#` gave `#REF!` whenever the dynamic-array formula in C1 happened to return a **single** value — a `FILTER` matching one row, a `SORT` or `UNIQUE` over one item. In Excel the formula is still the anchor of a 1 × 1 range, so `ROWS(C1#)` is 1 and `SUM(C1#)` is the value.

Reproduced from the reported fixture before changing anything:

| | before | after | Excel |
|---|---|---|---|
| `=ROWS(C1#)` | `#REF!` | **1** | 1 |
| `=SUM(C1#)` | `#REF!` | **5** | 5 |
| `=ROWS(C3#)` | `#REF!` | **1** | 1 |
| `=COUNT(C5#)` | `0` | **1** | 1 |
| `=ROWS(C9#)` (two rows, control) | 2 | 2 | 2 |

So any formula counting or summing a filtered list broke the moment the list had exactly one entry — which depends on the data on the day the file is opened, which is what makes it unpleasant.

## The cause

A recalc pass recorded the spill only for an array larger than one cell:

```rust
if a.rows > 1 || a.cols > 1 {
    self.spills.insert(k, a.clone());
}
```

A 1 × 1 result therefore left no range for `PassHost::spill_range` to answer with, and `eval` turned the missing range into `#REF!`. It is now recorded unconditionally.

## Why not the rule the report suggested

The issue proposed treating every formula that carries `cm` as an anchor. That turned out not to be expressible: **nothing in the model says "dynamic array" positively.** `sheet_read.rs` uses `cm` only to decide whether to set `Formula::array`, so a dynamic array is distinguished from a legacy CSE formula by the *absence* of that field — and an ordinary `t="normal"` formula looks identical to a dynamic one.

The arm itself is the better test, and needs no new state: a formula whose result is a scalar never reaches it, because it never produces a `Value::Array`. `=1+1` does not become an anchor, which the test pins explicitly. It also agrees with Excel 365, where `=A1:A1` is a 1 × 1 anchor in its own right.

title: fix(ui): dark theme no longer thickens cell text (#1217)
author: neonworker
body:
Fixes the heavy, blurry cell text in the dark theme reported in #1217.

### Cause

egui keeps one coverage-to-alpha curve for all text (`Visuals::text_options.color_transfer_function`). `theme::apply` builds the dark theme from `Visuals::dark()`, which picks `TwoCoverageMinusCoverageSq`, a curve that thickens glyphs so white-on-dark text holds up. Cells stay dark ink on white paper in both themes, so the same curve made cell text in the dark theme heavy and smeared.

### Fix

Both themes use `FontColorTransferFunction::LIGHT_MODE_DEFAULT`. Cell text now renders identically in dark and light. Trade-off: in the dark theme, ribbon and menu text is slightly lighter than before. The grid is the main content, so it gets the curve that suits it.

### Measured

Four rows of cell text, rendered offscreen at 1x with `examples/snapshot` (same pixels, same region):

| | Ink | Edge contrast |
|---|---|---|
| Before, dark | 2,703 | 0.862 |
| After, dark | 2,184 | 0.946 |
| After, light | 2,184 | 0.946 |

Before this change, the dark theme put down 24% more ink for the same text. After it, dark and light are pixel-identical. I also checked by eye on Windows 11 (2560x1440, 100% scaling) in a web build of this branch.

Cell text, 3x nearest-neighbour:

![Cell text before and after, 3x](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neonworker/gridcraft/pr-assets/1217-dark-theme-text/cell-text-3x.png)

Whole window, dark theme, 1x:

![Window in the dark theme before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neonworker/gridcraft/pr-assets/1217-dark-theme-text/window-dark-before-after.png)

### Not in this PR

- I tried turning off `subpixel_binning`. Edge contrast didn't improve (0.940 vs 0.946), and letter spacing became visibly uneven, so I left it on.
- The remaining softness at 100% zoom comes from `DISPLAY_SCALE = 0.8` (#1185, #1197, #1266) and is out of scope here.
