title: Reject formula number literals too large for f64 as parse errors
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/formula/src/lexer.rs:258` (no existing issue): Formula number literal too large for f64 (e.g. =1E+400) is accepted and silently rewritten as 0.

## Cause
The formula lexer parsed number literals with `str::parse::<f64>()`, which returns infinity for out-of-range text such as `1E+400`, and it never checked that the result was finite. The infinity went into the AST, and the printer wrote it as `0`, so `Formula::new` stored `=1E+400*A1` as `0*A1`.

## Fix
The lexer now returns a `LexError` ("number too large") when a parsed number literal is not finite. Such formulas are now parse errors, and `Formula::new` keeps the user's original text, as it does for any other unparseable formula.

## Verified
- Regression test `number_literal_too_large_for_f64_is_a_parse_error`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p gridcraft-formula --lib number_literal_too_large_for_f64_is_a_parse_error`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The printer's `number_to_text` handling of non-finite values is unchanged. Only the lexer can produce an infinite literal.

title: File: keep the password in new windows, drop it with a warning on JSON (#770)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #770 (the File > Info dialog comes next, as a separate PR). Encrypted workbooks are now saved with their password, and `file.encryptWithPassword` sets or removes the password to open.

In Excel, a workbook opened with a password stays encrypted when you save it (Save As .xlsx too), and File > Info > Protect Workbook > Encrypt with Password sets the password, or removes it when you clear the field. Before this PR GridCraft opened these files but wrote them back without the password ("GridCraft saves it without the password"). Now the password is kept on the document and Save encrypts with it. Setting or removing the password counts as an unsaved change. View > New Window windows keep it too. CSV/HTML exports stay plain, and the password never goes into the journal. Save As `.json` can't hold a password: the document then becomes that unencrypted file, drops its password and the info bar says so. Happy to switch to refusing JSON as the document's file while a password is set, if you prefer. The file is written the way Excel writes it, following the public [MS-OFFCRYPTO] spec: Agile encryption with AES-256 and SHA-512, 100,000 spins, fresh random salts and key on every save, the data-integrity HMAC and the `\x06DataSpaces` storage. It goes into a compound file through a new [MS-CFB] writer (DIFAT for files over ~7 MB, sibling red-black tree), and `testing::compound_file` now calls this writer instead of keeping its own copy. All constants come from the spec. The one new dependency is `getrandom` 0.4 (MIT/Apache-2.0, pure Rust, already in Cargo.lock through tempfile), with `wasm_js` on wasm32. The Info-page dialog isn't part of this PR, so in the app the command is only reachable over the control channel, the CLI and MCP. I can send the dialog next as a separate PR. title: M12: formula dialects (one data table per formula language)
author: quantmind-br
body:
Part of #430. First of the smaller PRs that replace #443 (one language per PR after this one).

## What changes

A formula language becomes data. `crates/formula/src/input/<language>.rs` holds its function names, booleans, error literals, structured-reference specifiers and separators, and the lexer, parser and display printer read every language through that one `Dialect` table. | | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |

title: functions: NETWORKDAYS.INTL accepts the all-weekend string "1111111"
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
`weekend_mask` rejects the all-weekend string outright for **both** functions (`crates/functions/src/date.rs:289`, the `|| b.iter().all(|c| *c == b'1')` clause). Microsoft's documentation has the two differ: NETWORKDAYS.INTL — *"Only the characters 1 and 0 are permitted in the string. Using 1111111 will always return 0"*; WORKDAY.INTL — *"Also, 1111111 is an invalid string."* So `=NETWORKDAYS.INTL(DATE(2006,1,1), DATE(2006,2,1), "1111111")` returns `#VALUE!` where Excel returns `0`.

The crate already implements exactly that split — `workday_core`'s `per_week == 0` guard (`date.rs:397`) errors when no workday exists — and that guard is **unreachable dead code today**, because no mask `weekend_mask` could produce has zero workdays while the extra clause stood. The dead guard is strong evidence the maintainers intended this behaviour and the clause is the bug.

**Fix:** drop the extra clause. `count_workdays` naturally counts zero for NETWORKDAYS.INTL, and WORKDAY.INTL errors through the guard it already has. (Caveat, honestly: LibreOffice/ONLYOFFICE docs call the string invalid for both; Microsoft's wording plus the dead in-repo guard carry the day here.)

**Regression test:** the `working_days` assertions — on main the NETWORKDAYS.INTL `"1111111"` assertion fails (`is_err` where Excel returns 0); with the clause dropped it asserts `0` and WORKDAY.INTL is asserted to error. Full `gridcraft-functions` lib suite green (123 passed).

title: engine: pageLayout.printTitles only touches the axes it is given
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
`print_titles` reads both `rows` and `cols` into `Option`s and assigns both unconditionally (`crates/engine/src/cmd/view.rs:234`), so `pageLayout.printTitles {"rows":"2:2"}` sets `title_cols = None` and `{"cols":"A:A"}` sets `title_rows = None`: the repeated columns (or rows) disappear from every printed page, with no message and no way to set or clear just one axis. Reachable from any programmatic caller — control channel, MCP `execute_command`, or the CLI.

The sibling command already reads these the right way: `pageLayout.pageSetup` distinguishes "key absent" (leave alone) from "key present but empty/null" (clear) via `Option<Option<..>>` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/print.rs:1612`). The two commands disagree about the same two settings today.

**Fix:** read both axes the way `pageSetup` does — an absent key leaves that axis alone, an empty/null value clears it, and anything else that isn't a range is an error rather than a silent wipe.

**Regression test:** `print_titles_keeps_the_axis_it_is_not_given` — on main the rows-only call clears the columns (`left: (Some((1, 1)), None)`); with the fix each axis is touched only when named, an explicit empty value still clears that axis on purpose, and a bad range errors. Full `gridcraft-engine` lib suite green (287 passed).

title: xlsx: keep a table's filter criteria when the sheet AutoFilter coincides with it
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
The engine's live filter state is always `sheet.autofilter` — `apply_filter` (`data.rs:585`), `filter_values`, `clear_filter`, `reapply` and `cmd/slicer.rs` all read and write it, and the auto-filter dropdown of a table header installs one over the table's own range (`ui-egui/src/grid.rs:2749` runs `data.filter {"range": <the table's range>}`) — while `Table::filter` is **only ever filled by the XLSX reader**. Writing then suppressed the sheet `<autoFilter>` whenever any table merely *intersected* it (`sheet_write.rs:342`) and wrote the table part from `Table::filter`, which is empty: a filtered table saved with its rows still `hidden="1"` and **no filter criteria anywhere**. On reopen there is no filter to clear, the dropdown shows no selection, `data.clearFilter` restores nothing, and Excel shows an inactive filter over mysteriously hidden rows. A slicer's selection is discarded by the same path (a slicer is front-end over the same filter state).

**Fix:** where the sheet filter's range *coincides* with a table's (contains, header row, filter button) and the table has no criteria of its own, fold the sheet criteria into the table part — the stored `colId` offsets are relative to the range's first column and both ranges start at the same column, so they carry over verbatim. A sheet filter that only *partially* overlaps a table still has no valid home (an `<autoFilter>` beside the table's own would be invalid XML) and keeps being suppressed; the suppression test is narrowed from `intersects` to that case so partial filters are written as before.

**Regression test:** `a_table_filter_criteria_survive_a_round_trip` — on main the table part carries no criteria after a save (the `expect("…kept on save")` fires); with the fold the criteria round trip, the hidden row stays hidden, and the sheet keeps no duplicate autoFilter. Full `gridcraft-xlsx` lib suite green (174 passed).

title: engine: a cut takes the source's notes, hyperlinks and merged areas with it
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
A cut removes the source's cells and pictures (`crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs:950`) and then re-creates the block's merged areas at the destination (`:1158`) and copies the source's notes to it (`:1128`) — but removes none of those from the source. Cut a merged, noted block and one merged block becomes two (an empty one left at the old place) and the note is on both the old and the new cell; Excel moves both and leaves the source clean.

A second gap in the same path: paste never transferred hyperlinks at all (only `edit.clear` touched `Sheet::hyperlinks`), so clearing the source on cut would have lost them.

**Fix:** the cut clears the source range's `comments`, `hyperlinks` and `merges` exactly the way `edit.clear` already does; the destination is written from the clipboard snapshot taken before the cut, so nothing that should reach it is lost. Paste now carries hyperlinks in `What::All`, and a `What::Hyperlinks` variant makes `edit.pasteSpecial {"what":"hyperlinks"}` work like `"comments"`.

**Regression test:** `a_cut_moves_the_sources_notes_hyperlinks_and_merges` — on main the old merge stays behind (`[A1:B1, D1:E1]`) and the note is on both cells; with the fix the merge, note and link all move and the source is clean. Full `gridcraft-engine` lib suite green (287 passed).

title: engine: sort and remove duplicates move the rows' notes and hyperlinks
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
`do_sort` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/data.rs:296`) moves cells, formulas, cell pictures, row heights and floating-object anchors through the sort permutation, and `remove_duplicates` (`:765`) moves cells and pictures through the compaction — but neither touches `Sheet::comments` or `Sheet::hyperlinks`, which are keyed by `CellRef`. So a note that described one record stays behind and annotates whatever landed on that row ("late payment" now on a paid invoice), and a note on a row removed by Remove Duplicates annotates blank cells. `Sheet::comments`/`hyperlinks` are exactly the range-scoped side data that row/column inserts already remap (`sheet.rs:155`, `:968`) and that `edit.clear` already clears, so the omission looks unintended rather than deliberate.

**Fix:** both maps travel through the same permutation the cells use. The sort collects the entries before re-inserting (a swap cannot resurrect an entry from a destination that is also a source: the body is cleared first, then the permuted entries inserted); Remove Duplicates compacts the kept rows' entries to `start + i` and drops the entries on removed rows.

**Regression test:** `sort_and_remove_duplicates_move_the_rows_notes_and_links` — with unambiguous sort keys, on main the note and link stay on their old cells (assertions fail); with the fix they travel with their record, and a note on a removed row is dropped with the row. Full `gridcraft-engine` lib suite green (287 passed).

title: #1447: PivotTables in XLSX open in Excel and keep date groups, report filters and layout
author: HyakoV3
body:
Part of #1447 (items 1, 3, 4, 5 and 6 of its list; the issue stays open for 2 and 7).

All in `crates/xlsx/src/pivot.rs`:
1. **Unopenable file:** booleans and errors in the source count as strings in the cache `<sharedItems>` flags, as Excel writes them. Before, `containsString="0"` next to them made Excel refuse the file (even with repair).
3. **Report filter:** `pageField@item` is read through the pivot field's `<items>` (`x` = shared item), so `Qty = 3` is no longer read as another item.
4. **Date groups with a blank date:** `containsSemiMixedTypes="0"` is only written when there is no blank.
5. **Day groups:** a date-grouped field is written without `sortType` (Excel sorted its labels as text) and a date group without `sortType` reads back as ascending.
6. **Two value fields, no column field:** `firstHeaderRow="0"` plus `<x14:pivotTableDefinition hideValuesRow="1"/>`, so Excel 365 adds no `Values` row (no more `#SPILL!` below the report). One value field is unchanged.

**Not in this PR:** 2 (source headers with leading/trailing spaces: engine + xlsx header handling) and 7 (PivotChart link needs the file name threaded to the writer). Happy to do them next; they touch other files.

Tests: cache flags for the six column kinds of the issue's table, date-group flags with and without a blank, hideValuesRow, and the report-filter read. The three write-side tests fail on `main`. The existing round-trip fixture's Years group now uses `PivotSort::Asc` (the default) since a date group without `sortType` reads as ascending. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

Open PRs #722, #474, #498, #719 and #684 touch the same files, so a rebase may be needed.

title: UI: Delete dismisses the AutoComplete proposal, and deleting text never brings it back (#1521)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1521.

When a column already holds `SomeText` and you type `Some` in the next row, AutoComplete proposes `SomeText`. The report says neither Delete nor Backspace gets rid of it. There were two causes:

1. **Delete was ignored.** #842 made Backspace drop the proposal, but Delete was never handled. With the caret at the end, the text box treats Delete as a no-op, so the proposal stayed and Enter still committed `SomeText`. Backspace and Delete now go through one `dismiss_completion` helper, so both drop the proposal the same way Escape does.
2. **Deleting text brought the proposal back.** After the first Backspace dropped the proposal, the next Backspace (`Some` to `Som`) changed the text, the editor looked for a completion again, and `SomeText` came straight back. So you could not delete your way out of it. Now the editor only proposes a completion after typing, not after the entry gets shorter. Excel does the same: AutoComplete never comes back while you delete.

The change is in `crates/ui-egui/src/formula_bar.rs`, which handles both the in-cell editor and the formula bar. Typing still proposes completions as before, and Escape and Tab still work the same way.

Tests (in `formula_bar.rs`):
- `backspace_and_delete_dismiss_completion` sends real Backspace and Delete key events through an `egui::Context` and checks that each one drops the proposal, while other keys leave it in place.
- `only_typing_proposes_completion` checks that a shorter entry (`Some` to `Som`) does not count as typing, while a longer one or one of the same length does.

title: Focus the Find what field when Find and Replace opens (#1518)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1518.

In Excel, Ctrl+F opens Find and Replace with the cursor already in "Find what", so you can type the search term and press Enter right away. GridCraft opened the dialog with nothing focused, so you had to click the field first.

The Find and Replace dialog now asks for focus on "Find what" the first time it is drawn. A `focused` flag in the dialog's values makes this happen once per opening, so clicking "Replace with" afterwards still moves the cursor there (the Go To and Insert Function dialogs request focus every frame, which would lock the cursor in place here because this dialog has two text fields). The change is in the dialog itself, so every way of opening it gets it: Ctrl+F, Ctrl+H, Shift+F5, Cmd+Shift+H on Mac, the ribbon's Find & Select menu and the keytips.

Test: `crates/ui-egui/tests/find_dialog_focus.rs` presses Ctrl+F (and Ctrl+H, which opens the Replace tab) through real egui key events, types "abc", and checks that "Find what" holds it. Without the fix, the text never reaches the field.

title: Remember the AutoSave switch between launches (#1496)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1496.

AutoSave lived only in `GridState::autosave`, which every launch creates with the switch off, and `ui.json` did not store it. So turning AutoSave on (ribbon toggle or File > Options > Save) was forgotten as soon as GridCraft was closed.

- `UiState` gets an `autosave` field (default off; `#[serde(default)]` means an older `ui.json` keeps AutoSave off, as before).
- `SheetApp::ui_to_save` copies the live switch into the preferences, and `save_prefs` writes that to `ui.json` on exit.
- `load_prefs` calls `SheetApp::restore_autosave` after reading `ui.json`, so the switch comes back on the next launch.

The live flag stays in `GridState`, so the ribbon toggle, the Options checkbox and the autosave timer are unchanged.

Test: `autosave_switch_is_saved_in_ui_json_and_restored` in `crates/ui-egui/tests/interaction.rs`, next to the AutoComplete preference test. It turns AutoSave on, round-trips the preferences through JSON into a new app, and checks the switch is on again; it also checks an old `ui.json` without the field keeps AutoSave off.

title: Open the Insert Chart dialog from Recommended Charts instead of inserting a chart (#1399)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1399.

**Cause.** #301 (f58b123) made the Recommended Charts ribbon button open the Insert Chart dialog with `open_dialog("recommendedCharts")`. The keytip-badge change (95b3641) later switched the button back to running the `insert.recommendedCharts` command directly, and that command inserts the first recommendation. For two numeric columns that is a scatter plot. The `NR` keytip and command search also go through `run_or_alert`, so they ran the command directly too.

**Fix.**
- `run_or_alert`, the shared entry point for menus, the ribbon, keytips and command search, now opens the `recommendedCharts` dialog when `insert.recommendedCharts` comes with no chart `type`. This works the same way as the existing `file.exportPdf` case just above it (menu-style calls ask the user; programmatic `run` calls keep the old behaviour). The engine command, the MCP and CLI callers are unchanged.
- The ribbon button goes through `act(...)` again, like the other Insert buttons. Selecting the new chart still works, because the dialog's OK button runs `insert.chart`, and `run` already selects the chart that command creates.

**Test.** `recommended_charts_command_without_a_type_opens_the_dialog` sets up a data selection, calls `run_or_alert("insert.recommendedCharts", {})`, and checks that the dialog is open and no chart has been inserted. Without the fix, a scatter chart is inserted and no dialog opens. The existing `recommended_charts_dialog_inserts_the_chosen_chart` test still covers choosing a chart in the dialog.

title: Keep nan/inf time and fraction look-alikes as text
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/core/src/parse.rs:~170 (parse_time, parts parsed with f64::parse)` (no existing issue): Typing or importing text like "1:nan" or "nan:30" turns it into a #NUM! error instead of leaving it as text.

## Cause
`parse_time` and `parse_fraction` parsed their parts with `str::parse::<f64>()`, which accepts `nan`, `inf`, signs and exponents. For `nan` every range check is false, so the text was accepted as a time. `time_fraction` then gave NaN, which `Value::number` turns into `#NUM!`.

## Fix
Added a `plain_number` helper that accepts only ASCII digits, plus an optional `.digits` fraction for the seconds part. `parse_time` and `parse_fraction` use it, so inputs like `1:nan`, `nan:30`, `1:30:NaN`, `1 nan/2`, `1e1:00` and `+5:00` fall through to text. Hours and minutes, and the parts of a fraction, must now be whole digits.

## Verified
- Regression test `non_digit_time_and_fraction_parts_stay_text`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p gridcraft-core --lib non_digit_time_and_fraction_parts_stay_text`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Date parsing and plain number parsing are unchanged. Valid times such as `h:mm:ss.000` and `h AM` still parse. Decimal hours or minutes (for example `1.5:00`), decimal fraction parts (for example `1 1.5/2`) and a trailing dot in the seconds (for example `1:00:30.`) now stay text instead of being accepted, which matches the rule that time and fraction parts are plain digits.

title: PDF: Greek and Cyrillic text in an embedded system font, desktop and CLI (builds on #1487's patch)
author: Dejan-Port
body:
PDF export and printing write Cyrillic (and Greek) text as `?`, because `crates/pdf` only uses the unembedded base-14 fonts with WinAnsiEncoding. This is gap #5 in `docs/gaps.md`.

## Credit: the core of this PR is @plousbooks' patch from #1487

**The design and most of the diff are not mine.** They come from the patch @plousbooks attached to #1487 (`greek-printing.patch`, against e6b6b34, which is still `main`). The first commit applies that patch **unchanged** and keeps @plousbooks as its git author:

- `crates/pdf/src/truetype.rs`: a small, bounds-checked TrueType reader with no dependencies (units per em, metrics, cmap format 4/12, advance widths). It rejects CFF and `.ttc` files, and fonts whose `fsType` forbids embedding.
- `crates/pdf/src/lib.rs`: a run that WinAnsiEncoding can't carry is set in an embedded CIDFontType2 font (Identity-H, `/CIDToGIDMap /Identity`, a `/W` array and a ToUnicode CMap) when an app has registered a fallback font with `set_unicode_font_loader`. Latin-only text is unchanged. Without a loader, the output is the same `?` as before.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs` `pdf_unicode_fonts()` and the registration in `apps/gridcraft/src/main.rs`.
- The tests that build a tiny TrueType font in code, so no font fixture is committed.

That mechanism already handles any script: it looks up each code point in the font's cmap. What it didn't do yet is choose fonts for Cyrillic, and the CLI didn't use it at all. That's what this PR adds.

## What this PR adds on top (second and third commits)

1. **Fonts are chosen for Cyrillic too.** `pdf_unicode_fonts()` only accepted a font that had `Ω` and `ω`. A font now qualifies if it has Greek **or** Cyrillic (`pdf_font_covers_greek_or_cyrillic`). For Cyrillic it checks `Ж` (U+0416) and `џ` (U+045F):
   - `Ж` has no Latin look-alike in the source (`А` does).
   - `џ` is the last letter of U+0400–U+045F. A font with only the 33 Russian letters doesn't qualify, so Serbian, Macedonian, Ukrainian and Belarusian te…

title: Sort and de-duplicate data.textToColumns fixed-width breaks
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/data.rs:826` (no existing issue): data.textToColumns with unsorted fixedWidths duplicates text and leaves empty columns.

## Cause
The fixed-width branch of `text_to_columns` used the `fixedWidths` break positions in the order given, with no sorting or de-duplication. Unsorted breaks such as `[6, 3]` made an out-of-order window (6..3) that yielded an empty cell and an overlapping window (3..10) that duplicated text. A duplicate break or a 0 also produced an empty column.

## Fix
The break positions are now filtered to those strictly between 0 and the text length, then sorted and de-duplicated before the column windows are built. `[6, 3]` on `abcdefghij` now gives `abc | def | ghij`.

## Verified
- Regression test `t2c_fixed_widths_are_positions_in_any_order_without_duplicates`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p gridcraft-engine --lib t2c_fixed`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Delimited splitting (`split_delimited`) and the handling of the destination range and cell writes are unchanged.

title: calc: bounded references up to 1,048,576 cells keep their full shape
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
Fixes #1010.

A reference over 16,384 cells was cut to the sheet's used range when read into an array. Next to a full-size operand the two no longer lined up. `SUMPRODUCT(D3:AZ400*B3:B400,(A3:A400=1)*(D1:AZ1=2))` gave #VALUE!, `D3:AZ400*B3:B400` filled with #N/A, and ROWS, COUNTBLANK and `--(r="")` lost the blanks past the data. Excel keeps the reference's size.

Bounded references now keep their full shape up to one column's worth of cells (1,048,576). References that run to the edge of the sheet (`A:A`, `A2:A1048576`, several whole rows) and larger blocks still stop at the used range, so whole-column formulas stay fast. The audit's other cases (blanks in those larger ranges) would need a sparse, blank-aware evaluator, which this doesn't add.

Real-world effect: on one 86k-formula workbook, this with #1359 and #1341 takes the cells that differ from Excel from 26,095 to 2. Trade-off: that workbook recalculates about 2x slower, because the formulas now do the full work Excel does.

Tests: new calc tests for the SUMPRODUCT, array multiplication and ROWS/COUNTBLANK cases above.

title: numfmt: number and date output follow the locale (German)
author: AndreasHink
body:
# PR: numbers and dates are written in the locale's conventions (German)

## What this does

Excel paints a formatted number or date with the machine's conventions: `1.234,56` and
`15. Oktober 2026` in German, `1,234.56` and `October 15, 2026` in English. GridCraft painted
everything en-US, so a German user saw wrong separators and English month and weekday names in the
grid, the clipboard, printed output, chart labels and `TEXT()`.

This PR makes number and date **output** follow a locale:

- `gridcraft_core::Locale` (`en`/`de`), built from a BCP 47-ish tag (`de`, `de-DE`, `de_AT`) — the
  decimal and thousands separators and the long and three-letter month and weekday names live there.
- `crates/numfmt` takes the locale through `format_value`, `text_function`, the General display
  format and the render path. **English output is unchanged, byte for byte** — it is still the
  default and the existing tests keep their meaning.
- `Workbook::locale` carries it for the session, next to `date_system`, but is *not* part of the
  file: opening a workbook never changes how numbers are painted.
- New command **`app.locale.set`** (`{"locale": "en"|"de"}`): sets it programmatically, recalculates
  so cached `TEXT()` results are rewritten, does not dirty the workbook (same idiom as `store_view`).
- Picking **German in View ▸ Interface language** (or a saved `ui.json`) switches numbers and dates
  to German; every other interface language keeps en-US.

## Deliberately not in this PR

Format codes, function names, the `,` argument separator and typed input stay en-US — localized
formulas and German format *entry* are a separate, larger piece of work (see PR #163 and issue #45),

locale while reading it back does not.

title: XLSX: keep dynamic-array cell metadata (cm) on save
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
GridCraft was dropping the "this is a dynamic-array formula" mark when it saved a file. Excel then reads those formulas the old way and can change the answer.

Example: `SUMPRODUCT(IFERROR(B1:B3/C1:C3,0))` is 1.25. After a GridCraft save, Excel reads it with an implicit `@` and shows 0. Nothing in the file warns about it.

The mark is the `cm` attribute on the cell, which points into `xl/metadata.xml`. Now:
- A formula read with `cm` keeps it (`Formula::dynamic`), and the writer saves it and the metadata part, even when the formula returns one value.
- It survives moves, row and column inserts and deletes, sheet and name renames, and LAMBDA fixes.
- Retyping a formula drops it, and the writer decides from the formula's shape as before.
- Documents without the mark are saved exactly as before.

Real-world effect: across 40 real-world workbooks with dynamic-array metadata, 11 lost the metadata part on save and others dropped the mark on up to 11,733 cells each. Now none do.

Related: #417 makes legacy formulas open with Excel's `@`. This keeps the dynamic mark on save, the other direction, and the two merge cleanly.

Tests: round trips in the xlsx and engine tests for moves, inserts, renames and retyping, plus the `SUMPRODUCT(IFERROR(...))` case.

title: XLSX: fix Excel refusing files with cell pictures, and keep #SPILL! and #CALC! on save
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
Two problems in how GridCraft writes Excel's "rich value" data.

1. Excel refused to open files that contain pictures in cells (added in #105). Two small details in the metadata were wrong: the `XLRICHVALUE` type was missing `coerce="1"`, and the extension URIs had to be lower case. Both are fixed, and Excel 16.0 opens these files again.

2. A `#SPILL!` or `#CALC!` value was saved as `#VALUE!` and reopened as `#VALUE!`. This hits a pasted value or a cached formula result. Excel saves these as a cached `#VALUE!` plus a value-metadata (`vm`) link to an `_error` rich value that carries the real error type. GridCraft now writes and reads them that way, sharing the rich-value table with cell pictures, and also reads Excel packages that have no `richValueRel` part. Typed `#SPILL!` and `#CALC!` stay text, as Excel keeps them.

Tests: round trips for both errors, for cell pictures, and for packages without `richValueRel`. Excel opens a saved file with cell pictures without repair.

title: Calc: a whole-row reference stops at the used range like a whole column
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
A whole row such as `5:5` is exactly 16,384 cells, one short of the size above which references are trimmed to the used range. So it was read at full width, while `1:2` and `A:A` were trimmed. As the lookup value of a lookup inside an array formula (`{=IFERROR(XLOOKUP(5:5,6:6,7:7),...)}`), that meant 16,384 lookups over 16,384 cells per formula, about 3 s per cell in a release build.

Whole rows now stop at the used range like whole columns. A real-world workbook with 114 such cells took 420 s to open and now opens in 21 s, with the same calculation results (360 mismatches against Excel's cached values before and after).

Based on #1568, which edits the same lines. Merge that one first.

Related: #891 (slow opens).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code). Reviewed by @Harrison-Booth before posting.

title: Fix: list and render installed fonts again (TH Sarabun New)
author: NakaSato
body:
## Problem

Installed fonts never showed up anywhere, so Thai fonts such as **TH Sarabun New** couldn't be picked, and a cell set to one never drew in it.

- The desktop app calls `SheetApp::setup_context_for_language` directly (to apply the saved interface language). Since 12bfdb0 (i18n: Chinese, Korean and Russian interface languages), only `setup_context` started the background font scan (added in f654615, #4), and nothing calls it any more. The scan never ran, so:
  - the Format Cells → Font list stopped at the 17 standard names (ends at Verdana)
  - the code that loads a workbook's installed fonts waits for the scan to finish, so it never ran: cells in TH Sarabun New drew in the fallback face
- The Home ribbon font box only ever listed the fixed 17 names, even when the scan worked.

## Fix

- **`lib.rs`:** start the font scan in `setup_context_for_language` (runs once per process; does nothing on wasm). This covers the desktop, web and language-switch paths.
- **`ribbon.rs`:** the ribbon font box lists `fonts::families()` (standard names first, then every installed family A–Z), like the dialog.
- **`fonts.rs`:** `families()` builds the list once (the ribbon asks every frame) and skips hidden macOS system faces (`.ThonburiUI`, …).
- **`theme.rs`:** the Sukhumvit Set Thai fallback path is `Supplemental/`.

Turning the scan on exposed two bugs that never showed while it was off:

- **Dropped input when workbook fonts load.** The frame that switched to a new font set skipped painting, so a click in that frame was lost (made `borders::diagram_menu…` flaky, 1 of 2 runs). Now the frame keeps the families that are already active and switches the next frame (`fonts_pending`), with no skipped paint.
- **The combo's Enter picked the wrong row when filtered.** `sel` mixed an index into the full list with a position in the filtered list. With only 17 names, "arial" matched a single row; with installed fonts it matches Arial, Arial Black, Arial Hebrew, Arial Narrow…, and Ent…

author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1561.

The note's text field is multiline, so Enter (or Shift+Enter) typed the new line, and then `ok_cancel` saw the same key press and pressed OK. title: Copy, paste and duplicate the selected chart, picture or shape
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1563.

With a chart selected, the grid's Cmd/Ctrl+C handler still copied the cells of the cell selection and Cmd/Ctrl+V pasted the clipboard text into them, so no copy of the chart ever appeared, and there was no command to duplicate a floating object. This adds `object.duplicate {kind, id, dx?, dy?}`, which clones a chart, picture or shape on the active sheet with a fresh id and the same series and formatting (same ranges, so the copy is independent but plots the same data), offset 12 pt right and down, as one undoable step. It builds on the delete-the-selected-object work in #213.

In the grid, Copy with an object selected remembers the object and ends the cells' copy mode. Paste duplicates it, each paste a step further, with the copy selected, as long as the system clipboard still holds what it held at the copy, so text copied in another app afterwards still pastes into the cells. A few details:
- Where the clipboard can't be read on request (web), the first paste's text is taken as the copy's.
- With no text on the clipboard, egui-winit sends neither a Paste event nor the key press for Cmd/Ctrl+V, so the key's release pastes the object when no Paste event came before it.
- If the copied object has been deleted or undone in the meantime, Paste falls back to the text.
- The ribbon and menu Paste go through the same path, and Cmd/Ctrl+D duplicates the selected object instead of filling down, as in Excel.
- Moving the cell cursor from the keyboard or starting to type deselects the object, so Copy and Cmd/Ctrl+D act on cells again.

Left out, happy to add or switch: pasting on a different sheet still pastes cells (the series would keep pointing at the original sheet, which felt like its own decision); Cut, the ribbon Copy button and the context menus still act on the cells. If #470 lands first I'm glad to rebase onto its `ObjRef` selection.

title: Web: live control channel through a WebSocket relay, and file.reload
author: gudjon
body:
## Why

GridCraft for the web had no control channel, so seeing a model change meant reopening the file. With this PR, a page opened with `?control=` updates live: from a file that another program rewrites, or from scripts, `gridcraft-cli send` and MCP, the same way they drive the desktop app's `--control` port.

```sh
cd apps/gridcraft-web && trunk serve --release        # http://127.0.0.1:8771
gridcraft-cli relay --watch /path/to/model.xlsx      # control on 7979, browser link on 7980
# open http://127.0.0.1:8771/?control=7980
```

## What

- **`file.reload` (engine command).** Replaces an open workbook with the file's current contents in place. The window, uid, active sheet, selection and scroll stay. Opens the file when it isn't open. Keeps unsaved changes unless `force: true`, so a reload never discards work. Works on desktop too (`app.open` on a path that is already open only switches to it).
- **`gridcraft-cli relay`.** A page can't listen on a port, so it dials out to the relay over a WebSocket (handwritten RFC 6455 on the workspace's `sha1`, no new crates). The relay serves the unchanged JSON-lines protocol on 7979 and does the file work the browser can't: paths on `app.open`/`file.open`/`file.reload`, `app.save {path}`, `ui.screenshot {path}`. `--watch FILE` (repeatable) reloads the file on every change and every reconnect. Only localhost pages may connect (`--origin` allows others), and the newest page wins. Inputs are capped: lines 64 MB, messages 256 MB, files 128 MB, handshake 16 KB.
- **`gridcraft-web ?control=7980`** (or `?control=ws://host:port`). Requests run through `control::handle`, like the desktop port. The page reconnects every 2 s when the relay restarts. A request that gets no frame in 10 s (a screenshot in a hidden tab) fails with a clear error.
- **Docs:** `docs/control-protocol.md` ("In the browser"), `docs/cli.md`, README.

## Testing

- `cargo xtask ci`: all 8 steps pass.
- New tests: 3 engine tests (`file.reload` in place, unsaved cha…

title: Calc: CELL("filename") names the workbook's file
author: Hamza0101
body:
The other half of #1489. The German info types are #1502; this is `CELL("filename")` itself, which returned an empty string for every workbook, saved or not.

## The bug

```
=CELL("filename",A1)                                          ->  ""
=MID(CELL("filename",A1),FIND("]",CELL("filename",A1))+1,31)  ->  #VALUE!
=ISNUMBER(FIND("]",CELL("filename",A1)))                      ->  FALSE
```

That middle formula is the classic way to put a sheet's name in a cell, and @KNUFFIXX measured it in 83 of 400 real German workbooks. With no `]` in the string, `FIND` fails and the cell shows `#VALUE!`.

Excel returns `<folder>\[<file>]<sheet>`, and empty only for a workbook that has never been saved.

## Why it was empty

The workbook model had no file to report. `source_dir` exists, but it is there for a different job: it names the folder that relative links to other workbooks are relative to. It must *not* be updated on a Save As into another folder, because the links held in memory are still written for the old one — only the saved copy is rebased. So it could not be reused here, and overwriting it would have broken linked workbooks on the second save.

`Workbook::source_path` is therefore its own field, with that distinction written down where someone will meet it. It is set in two places:

- **open** — from the path, made absolute, so the folder is the one the user sees. A workbook that arrived as bytes knows its name but never a folder, so it reports `[name]Sheet` with none, which still splits on the `]`. An import reports the file it came from, as Excel does, even though Save must still ask where to put the `.xlsx`.
- **save** — when a full-fidelity save makes a file the document's own. Set before the `saved` snapshot, or the workbook would read as dirty the moment it was saved, and only when it actually changes, so an ordinary Save does not clone the workbook for nothing.

`CELL("filename")` then builds the string with `Path::join`, so the separator is the platform's. …

title: Calc: IF runs in its own frame, so a recursive LAMBDA can go about 15% deeper
author: luigiPinna
body:
For #917, a follow-up to #1809. Two commits in `crates/calc`: `a382e66d` gives IF its own frame, and `b72d2a1a` raises the two recursion limits into the stack that frees.

Since #1809, a recursion stops at 140 LAMBDA calls (`MAX_LAMBDA_CALLS`) or 400 evaluation levels (`MAX_DEPTH`), at the same point on every build, with an 896 KiB stack check behind them as a guard. The limits only stay build-independent while every form reaches one of them before the guard. The tightest case is the `LET(e,me(me,n-1),e+1)` form on Windows release: through `gridcraft-cli eval` on `main` it reaches the guard at `n` = 151 and stops at 131. Raising the limits on `main` alone would leave that form to the guard.

**IF in its own frame (`a382e66d`).** Every step of a recursive LAMBDA goes through its base case, and that is almost always IF. IF was the first arm of `Evaluator::call`, so each step paid for `call`'s frame, which holds the locals of every special form it handles (992 bytes on macOS arm64 release). IF now runs in `if_`, which inlines into `eval`. Its array case is in `if_array`, and the other functions stay in `call_named`; both are `#[inline(never)]` so they don't fold back into the recursive path. Behaviour doesn't change.

**Limits (`b72d2a1a`).** `MAX_DEPTH` goes from 400 to 460, so the countdown `F(F,151)` runs, and `MAX_LAMBDA_CALLS` from 140 to 160, 8 calls above the 152 that countdown has in progress, the gap #1809 left at 131 and 140. The recursion tests run the new boundaries on a 1 MiB and a 64 MiB thread.

Deepest `n` that returns the right answer, through `gridcraft-cli eval` on `main` at `17b9f6ff` (rustc 1.99.1 on the runners, 1.99.0 on macOS):

| form | `main` | this PR | guard alone, Windows release: `main` → this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `IF(n<=0,0,1+me(me,n-1))` | 131 | 151 | 176 → 212 |
| `IF(n<=0,0,LET(e,me(me,n-1),e+1))` | 131 | 151 | 151 → 176 |
| `IF(n=0,0,me(me,n-1))` | 139 | 159 | 207 → 260 |
| through `MAP` | 69 | 79 | 98 → 107 |

title: cf: share the per-rule statistics instead of copying them per lookup
author: rdexel
body:
## The problem

`CfCache::look` is called once per cell while the grid paints. The per-rule statistics — `sorted: Vec<f64>` of every number in the rule's range, and `counts: HashMap<String, usize>` of every distinct display value — are computed once and cached correctly, then **cloned out of the cache on every lookup**:

```rust
let st = self.stats.entry(idx).or_insert_with(|| { /* … */ }).clone();
```

So each lookup costs the size of the rule's range rather than a constant, and the cache is defeated by its own return value.

## What it cost

Found while opening a trial-balance workbook: 2 sheets, ~80k cells, 947 rows — three `cellIs` rules over `J11:BD413` (~22.5k cells), plus 19 more rules on the second sheet. Measured with the offscreen `snapshot` harness on an M5, release build:

| | load | steady-state frame |
|---|---|---|
| `--sample sales` | 5.6 ms | 0.4 ms |
| the workbook, before | 201 ms | **~170 ms** |
| the workbook, after | 201 ms | **~9.8 ms** |

~170 ms a frame is about 6 FPS — the grid visibly lagged on any scroll or repaint. `sample(1)` put 12,441 of 12,528 samples on `grid::show` → `paint_quadrant` → `grid::look` → `cf::CfCache::look`, dominated by `String::clone`, hashbrown table construction and `memmove`/`malloc`/`free`. Instrumenting the rule showed the cloned statistics held 18,894 numbers and 8,215 distinct strings, copied per painted cell per rule per frame.

## The fix

Hold the statistics behind an `Arc` so the existing `.clone()` is a pointer clone. Deref coercion covers every use (`st.sorted`, `st.counts`, `&st` into `threshold`), so the change is three lines.

**No behaviour change:** the `snapshot` render of the workbook is byte-identical before and after (`sha256 9f3017833b2510d7a88b3798…`).

## Tests

- `cf_lookup_does_not_cost_the_size_of_the_rule_range` — 500 lookups against a rule over 1k cells vs 20k cells; the cost must not grow with the range. Before the fix: 11.2 ms vs 171.0 ms (15x), fails. After: equal, passes. `#[ignore]`…

title: Fix MEDIAN overflow for large finite middle values
author: MMexicann
body:
Fixes #1579.

`MEDIAN(1E308,1E308)` returned `#NUM!` even though its median is the finite value `1E308`. Negative middle values have the same failure, and `AGGREGATE(12,…)` shares it.

## Root cause and correction

The even-length median branch added the two sorted middle values before dividing by two. That intermediate addition can overflow; the existing numeric validation then reports `#NUM!`. Use [`f64::midpoint`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.f64.html#method.midpoint) for this one expression. It avoids intermediate overflow without unconditionally halving tiny operands. Rust stabilised the method in 1.85, below the workspace's 1.90 minimum. Sorting, collection, coercion, error propagation, and the odd-length path are unchanged. No new dependency, allocation, unsafe code or native-only API is introduced.

The existing formula/command paths expose the corrected behavior to the UI, CLI and MCP. Workbook serialization and history are untouched. Only the relevant function-parity note and revision history are updated.

## Regression coverage

- Functions: positive/negative overflowing pairs, unequal pairs, finite f64 extremes, opposite signs, unsorted four-value input, scalar and range MEDIAN, and the shared AGGREGATE helper.
- Controls: ordinary and odd-sized inputs, a single value, minimum normal/subnormal values with exact assertions, direct text/logical coercion, ignored range text/logicals/blanks, empty data and propagated errors. Subnormal tests preserve the existing GridCraft behavior; they do not claim Excel supports subnormal results.
- Calculation: MEDIAN and AGGREGATE formulas over a range with downstream formulas; edits recalculate from positive results through zero to negative results.

Before the production change, the new overflow regression and the calculation regression both failed with `Error(Num)`; the controls passed.

title: AutoFilter: Enter in the filter menu applies the filter and closes it
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1516.

The AutoFilter menu only applied on a click on Apply. Enter in the search box made the text field drop its focus, and with focus on nothing the grid picked the keyboard back up, so the next keys moved the active cell under the still-open menu. After clicking a value, Enter went straight to the grid and moved the cell down. In Excel, Enter in this menu is OK: it applies the filter and closes it. Now `filter_menu` takes Enter first, before the search box or a focused checkbox (which would toggle) can see it, and applies the filter like Apply does. A Tab-focused button (Sort, Clear Filter, Apply) still treats Enter as its own click. The grid's keyboard handler also ignores keys while the filter menu is open, the same way the ribbon key tips already do, so nothing typed in the menu reaches the sheet.

With nothing checked (a search that matches nothing, or Select All cleared), Enter does nothing and the menu stays open, since applying would hide every row; Excel disables OK in that state. I left a click on Apply as it is, because `popup_dismissal` asserts that it hides every row. Happy to disable Apply in that state too if you'd prefer the Excel behaviour.

#1509 reworks the value list of the same menu. The two changes don't overlap, but they sit close together in `filter_menu`, so whichever lands second may need a small rebase. Happy to do it.

Validation:
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui --test filter_menu_enter`: the two Enter tests fail on main (Enter leaves every row visible: `[false, false, false]`), and pass here. The empty-selection test fails if Enter applies regardless (`[true, true, true]`). Without the grid-keyboard check, Enter after clicking a value moves the active cell to A2.

title: Web: keep preferences such as dark mode between visits
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1562.

`load_prefs`/`save_prefs` only exist in the desktop app, and `apps/gridcraft-web` never read or wrote `UiState` or the engine prefs, so a reload brought back light mode and the defaults. This follows the same approach as storytold/wordcraft#2205 (thanks @benandez): a small `prefs` module in the web app keeps what the desktop writes to `ui.json` and `prefs.json` in `localStorage` (`gridcraft.ui`, `gridcraft.prefs`), restores it at startup (a saved language replaces the browser's, as on desktop it replaces the system's), and writes it back from `logic` as soon as something changes, because a reload or a closed tab runs no exit code. Missing, oversized or unreadable values keep the defaults; storage errors are only logged. Under `?host=parent` the author the framing page passes is for that visit only, so it is never stored over the user's own name (the other preferences still are).

It uses `web_sys::Storage` directly rather than eframe's `persistence` feature, which would pull `ron` into the lockfile; PdfCraft uses `cc.storage`, happy to switch if you prefer that.

title: Read CELL("format") and AutoFill dates from the parsed number format
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #1451

## Cause
`cell_format_code` in eval.rs searched the lower-cased format text for letters, so the `e`/`d` of a colour tag such as `[Red]` or a quoted literal made a code scientific or a date. Decimals counted only `0`s, dates and times were always D1/D9, and `CELL("color")`/`CELL("parentheses")` always returned 0. AutoFill's `Pattern::detect` used the same case-sensitive text test (`contains('d') || contains('y') || …`) to decide whether a number is a date.

## Fix
numfmt gets `NumberFormat::cell_info()`, which works out the CELL code, colour flag and parentheses flag from the parsed sections. It uses a new `Section::paren` flag, set for an unquoted, unescaped `(`. `CELL` uses it for all three info types, and the old text heuristics are removed. AutoFill now uses `NumberFormat::kind()`: Date steps by a day, Time by an hour, and the Date kind also drives the month-step check.

## Verified
- Regression tests `single_number_fill_reads_the_parsed_format`, `cell_format_color_and_parentheses_follow_the_parsed_code`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p gridcraft-engine --lib -- single_number_fill_reads_the_parsed_format cell_format_color_and_parentheses_follow_the_parsed_code`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The issue doesn't give Excel's value for `dddd, mmmm d, yyyy`. It follows the issue's rules literally (first two parts are d, m, so D2), and no test covers it. Every other info type of CELL is unchanged.

title: fix(calc): bound SUBTOTAL and AGGREGATE input work
author: harrisonoconnorhover
body:
Fixes #1033.

`SUBTOTAL` and `AGGREGATE` materialize their inputs into one vector, but did not enforce the evaluator's existing size limit. Two far-apart occupied cells can make a trimmed reference span millions of blank cells. The functions now apply the existing 16-million-cell limit cumulatively across data references, union areas, arrays and scalars. Each reference is charged after trimming and before scanning; arrays are charged before copying. Hidden rows, nested totals and ignored errors still count toward the work limit. Oversized input returns `#NUM!`.

Five new regression tests cover safe early rejection, cumulative inputs, exact-fit boundaries, skipped cells and AGGREGATE's `k` argument. The oversized-range tests failed on main at their first attempted cell read and pass with the fix, without allocating an oversized fixture or attempting to reproduce an out-of-memory crash. The private limit parameter lets cumulative cases run with four-cell fixtures; production always uses `MAX_CELLS`.

Validation on macOS arm64 with Rust 1.95.0:

- Calculator suite: 64 passed, zero failed, one existing test ignored.
- Full workspace tests: 1,613 passed, zero failed, one existing test ignored.
- Calculator all-target Clippy with warnings denied, formatting, assets, dependency layers, WASM, parity and keytips checks passed.

title: XLSX: keep header and footer pictures on save
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #1257.

Excel stores header and footer pictures (`&G` in the header text) in a VML drawing of their own, which the sheet names with `<legacyDrawingHF>`, plus the images that drawing points at. The XLSX pass-through (#333) only looked for `<legacyDrawing>`, so on save the `&G` codes stayed in the header text but the element, the VML part and the images were dropped, and the letterhead was gone the next time the file was opened in Excel. This keeps that drawing and its images byte for byte with the rest of the sheet's kept content, and writes `<legacyDrawingHF>` back in schema order right after `<legacyDrawing>`. A sheet with a note and a header picture keeps both drawings separate, and the notes drawing GridCraft writes now takes VML shape blocks after the ones the kept header drawings use, so the two can't end up with the same `o:idmap` block and shape ids.

What's left of #1257: GridCraft still doesn't show header/footer pictures in print preview or Page Layout, and can't insert new ones. That's a bigger piece (rendering plus an Insert Picture flow in the header editor), so this PR only stops them from being lost on save. Opening such a file adds a "not shown; kept for saving" note like the one for embedded objects, happy to drop it if it's too noisy.

Validation:
- `passthrough_tests::header_and_footer_pictures_survive_a_save` (header logo + footer picture + a note, saved twice): fails on main (`no <legacyDrawingHF>` in the saved sheet), passes here
- `passthrough_tests::notes_take_shape_blocks_the_header_pictures_dont_use`: on the first fix alone the notes reused block 1 (`notes reuse shape block 1`), passes here

title: Formula parser: 8,192-character limit at entry only; file text bounded by its operators and 256 KiB
author: nihilist-narwhal
body:
## What this changes

#1330 put Excel's 8,192-character limit in `parse_syntax`, which both typed formulas and formula text read from files go through. A formula's file form is longer than what was typed: `LET(x,1,x+1)` is saved as `_xlfn.LET(_xlpm.x,1,_xlpm.x+1)`, `A1#` as `_xlfn.ANCHORARRAY(A1)` and `@A1` as `_xlfn.SINGLE(A1)`. So a LET formula of 4,049 typed characters (eight `SUM`s of 250 uses of `x`) is saved as 16,061 characters. It is accepted when typed but, after a save and reopen, keeps only its file text and cached value instead of calculating. Excel files with formulas near the limit are affected the same way.

- **Entry.** Entering a formula longer than 8,192 characters is still refused, as in Excel. `check_entered_length` is called by cell entry, by the command API (`cell.set`, `range.setValues`, fill, replace), by localized formula input and by `formulas.defineName`.
- **File text.** Formula text that `parse` reads from files, or gets from its other callers, is held to 256 KiB (`MAX_FORMULA_BYTES`). The limit is checked before tokenizing, because tokens take about 160 bytes per character: a formula of 20 million `%`, about 19 KB in a compressed file, would otherwise take 3 GB to refuse. The longest file form of a formula that can be entered is about 112 KiB, since each `@` is saved as `_xlfn.SINGLE(…)`, 14 bytes.
- **Operator count.** Formula text is also refused when its operators alone would not fit in 8,192 typed characters. The parser counts each operator it applies at the fewest characters it takes when typed:

  | Operator | Counts as |
  |---|---|
  | `%` | 1 |
  | a binary operator and its operand, or calling a result | 2 |
  | a trim range | 3 |

  This keeps the left-deep trees of long operator chains about as deep as a typed formula's at most. Parentheses, calls and prefix operators are held to the nesting limit and are not counted. The file prefixes add no operators, so no formula that can be typed is refused when read back.

title: Update check in About (opt-in) and `cargo xtask update` for source installs
author: GuxtavoLiu
body:
Two complementary pieces, so a GridCraft built from a checkout can learn that it is behind and get current. Nothing downloads or installs itself; the app tells, the xtask does the work on request.

## In the app: Help ▸ About ▸ Check for Updates

- **`help.checkForUpdates`** (UI-only command, also "Check for Updates…" in the macOS Help menu) asks GitHub's public API, off the UI thread, for the latest release. Newer than this build's version: "GridCraft X is available" with the release page. Otherwise, when the build knows its commit, one more request compares it with `main`: "This build is N commits behind main" with the compare page, and the hint that a source install updates with `cargo xtask update`. Else "up to date".
- **`ui.updates`** reads the state (`{checking, version, commit, result?, error?}`); **`options.checkForUpdatesOnStartup {on?: bool}`** is the About window's checkbox. It is **off by default**: no build talks to the network unless the user turns it on (README promises no telemetry). Something new is announced in the notice bar under the ribbon; "up to date" and errors show only in About.
- **`crates/ui-egui/src/updates.rs`** has no network code: version comparison, GitHub JSON parsing (size-capped, field by field, GitHub's `{"message"}` errors surfaced), and the check's state machine, all pure and unit-tested. The host provides a `Services.fetch` (GET on a worker, answer on a channel); web and headless runs pass none and the command says checks are unavailable there.
- **`apps/gridcraft`** implements `fetch` with `ureq` 3 (rustls + webpki roots, no system TLS library): https only, GitHub's `User-Agent`, 15 s timeout, body cap; an HTTP error status still delivers its JSON body so GitHub's own message is shown.
- **`crates/ui-egui/build.rs`** bakes the checkout's commit in as `GRIDCRAFT_BUILD_COMMIT` (packaging may set the variable; a tarball without git simply has no commit). About shows "Build abc1234".

author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Scroll down a Table and its header names, with their filter buttons, take the place of the column letters.

As in Excel, this happens when the active cell is inside a Table whose header row has scrolled out of view: the letters over the Table's columns become the header names, and each filter button opens that column's usual filter menu. Once you scroll past the Table's last row the letters come back. That last part is my reading of Excel, so happy to switch if it behaves differently. The names are left-aligned and cut off at the button, with no ellipsis. I'm happy to switch to centred or to "…" if you'd rather. Plain Data › Filter ranges keep their letters as in Excel. title: XLSX: a note keeps its box's place and size through open and save (#1608)
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #1608

## Cause

The reader took only `<x:Visible/>` from a note's VML shape (`read_note_visibility`), and `vml_xml` wrote every note with a fixed geometry: `<x:Anchor>col+1, 15, row, 2, col+3, 15, row+4, 16</x:Anchor>` and `width:108pt;height:59.25pt`. A plain open and save therefore replaced every box Excel had stored; the issue's 224 × 89 pt box over B1 came back as 104 × 78 pt at C2.

## Fix

- `Comment` gets an optional `note_box: NoteBox`: the anchor's two corners (column, pixel offset, row, pixel offset), stored **relative to the note's cell**, plus the shape's width and height in points. Because the corners are relative, the box follows the note wherever the engine moves it (row/column insert and delete, sort, paste), with no extra bookkeeping.
- `read_note_shapes` (was `read_note_visibility`) reads the anchor and the style size for notes and threaded comments' legacy shapes. An anchor that isn't eight unsigned numbers inside the sheet is ignored.
- `vml_xml` writes the stored box back, with its corners clamped to the sheet, or the default box for notes made in GridCraft. A box from a file that equals the default box is kept as `None`, so models that compared equal before a save still do (`full_roundtrip`).
- `docs/file-format-parity.md`: the XLSX row and the revision history.

## Tests

New `crates/xlsx/src/tests/note_box.rs`, using the issue's anchor (`1, 10, 0, 2, 5, 32, 5, 8`, 224.25 × 89.25 pt, note on B2):

- the box is read relative to its cell;
- an unedited note's anchor, width and height are written back unchanged, also after a second GridCraft round trip;
- a note moved to C3 takes its box along (`2, 10, 1, 2, 6, 32, 6, 8`);
- a box that would start above row 1 after a move is clamped to the sheet;
- a new note still gets the default box;
- damaged anchors (too few values, non-numeric, negative, out of range) are ignored.

Four of the six fail on `main`. The last two pass there too and are there to guard behaviour.

title: XLSX: keep custom column widths that round to the default width
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1607.

`read_cols` treated a column whose width rounds to the default pixel width as noise and skipped it, even when the `<col>` carries `customWidth="1"`. The chars to px conversion maps several stored widths onto the default 64 px (9.08, which is what openpyxl writes for Excel's 8.43, and 9.14 or 9.2), so those columns came back as plain default columns and the save wrote no `<col>` for them. The line just above already keeps a custom width equal to the default on purpose, and that matches Excel: a custom-width column is pinned, Standard Width doesn't move it. So the extra skip now only drops entries with nothing set at all; non-custom widths equal to the default are still read as the default, as before.

The 8.5 case in the matrix maps to 59 px with the 7 px digit, so I couldn't reproduce that one on main from the stored value alone. #1349 changes `col_width_to_px` in the same function but not this line, so the two should merge cleanly.

author: marcoarnulfo
body:

title: Match tildes in COUNTIF criteria and trailing ~ in patterns the way Excel does
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
Fixes part of #1455. COUNTIF and the other criteria functions ran every text criterion through the wildcard matcher, even when it held no `*` or `?`. So `COUNTIF(A5,"a~b")` with A5 = `a~b` gave 0, and with A4 = `ab` gave 1. `COUNTIF(A2:A18,"~~")` counted the cell `~`, and `COUNTIF(A2:A18,"h~ello")` counted `hello` and `HELLO`. Excel 365 gives 1, 0, 0 and 0. A trailing `~` was also kept as a literal: `COUNTIF(A2:A18,"?~")` counted only `x~`, where Excel counts every one-character value, and `MATCH("x~",A2:A18,0)` found `x~`, where Excel looks for `x` and gives `#N/A`.

The code change is in `crates/functions/src/criteria.rs` and `crates/functions/src/database.rs`; tests are added in those two files and in `lookup.rs`, `math.rs` and `text.rs`. It follows rules 1 and 2 measured in the issue:
- **A text criterion is a wildcard pattern only when it holds `*` or `?`.** `Criterion` decides this once, when it parses the criterion (a new `Operand::Pattern`). Any other text compares as plain text with `compare_text`, tildes included. Non-text cells still never match `=` and always match `<>`, and the `<`/`>` comparisons are unchanged. The `*IF(S)` functions get this through `Criterion`.
- **D-functions.** A plain-text D-function criteria cell is a "begins with" match, built by adding `*` to the text, which made it a pattern and kept `~` as an escape. When that text holds no `*` or `?`, its tildes are now escaped first, so `a~b` matches the values that begin with `a~b` (not `ab`), and `a~` those that begin with `a~`. Criteria with an operator (`=a~b`) get the plain-text comparison from `Criterion`. The issue lists the D-functions under rule 2 but doesn't measure them; the DCOUNTA test applies rule 2 to the begins-with form.

title: Reject unsupported flip param in arrange.rotate
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/extra.rs:664 (command doc at extra.rs:114)` (no existing issue): arrange.rotate ignores its documented `flip` parameter and swaps the shape's width and height instead.

## Cause
Found by our own testing; there is no issue. `arrange.rotate` is documented as accepting `flip?: horizontal|vertical`, but the handler never read it. It always swapped the shape's width and height, so a flip call reported success and made a 90° turn. The shape model has no flip state, so a flip cannot be applied.

## Fix
`rotate` now returns a `BadParams` error when `flip` is present and non-null, before any edit, so there is no undo step and the workbook is unchanged. The command doc now says that `flip` is rejected and that the command swaps width/height for a 90° turn.

## Verified
- Regression test `rotate_rejects_flip_param_instead_of_swapping_size`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p gridcraft-engine --lib rotate_rejects_flip`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
I did not add flip state to the shape model, so flipping is still not implemented. A call without `flip` still swaps width and height as before. I did not check whether another open pull request changes this function.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Keyboard: Ctrl+Shift+A after a function name inserts its argument names
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Ctrl+Shift+A (Control+Shift+A on a Mac) after a function name now inserts its argument names, as in Excel.

In Excel, with the caret right after a function name in a formula, Ctrl+Shift+A inserts the argument names and the parentheses: `=SUMIF(` (or `=SUMIF`) becomes `=SUMIF(range,criteria,sum_range)`. This PR does the same in the cell editor and the formula bar, using the names the argument hint already shows. Optional arguments lose their brackets, the `(` is added when missing, and the caret ends after the `)`. Anywhere else (inside the arguments, in a text literal, after a name that is not a function) the shortcut does nothing, and it no longer falls through to the text box's select-all. One Undo in the editor takes back just the inserted names, even when the function name was typed a moment before. Ctrl+A after a function name (Function Arguments dialog) stays out: it is a separate feature.

#1523 moves the argument names into per-language tables; this PR reads them through `formula_locale::signature`, so it picks those up without changes once #1523 lands.

title: Memory: undo steps share picture and macro bytes instead of copying them
author: arcanii
body:
## What it does

Each undo step keeps the workbook as it was before the edit. Sheets and their 64-row bands of cells are shared between steps (copy-on-write), but two byte blobs were not:

- **a floating picture's bytes** (`Image.data`), copied with its sheet at every edit on that sheet;
- **the VBA project** (`Workbook.vba_project`), copied with the workbook at every edit.

So one 20 MB picture cost another 20 MB for every cell typed on its sheet, up to the 100 steps of the history (2 GB). Both are now `Arc<Vec<u8>>`, as cell pictures (`Arc<CellPicture>`) already are, so the steps share one payload.

## How

- `Image.data` and `Workbook.vba_project` are `Arc<Vec<u8>>`.
- `gridcraft_model::b64::shared` (new) and `b64::opt` (now for `Option<Arc<Vec<u8>>>`) keep their JSON exactly as before: base64 text. XLSX reading and writing are unchanged.
- The rest is call sites: `.into()` where a `Vec` becomes the field, `.to_vec()` where the XLSX writer copied the bytes into a part before.

**How it was measured:**
- macOS 27.0.1 on an Apple M3 Max, release builds of `main` (`bb685e3`) and of this branch.
- Physical footprint (Activity Monitor's "Memory") through `proc_pid_rusage`: the kernel's lifetime peak for `gridcraft-cli run --script`.
- A synthetic 2600 × 2600 noise PNG of 19 MB, inserted with `insert.picture`, then N `cell.set` on the same sheet:

| Cell edits after the picture | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 21 MB | 21 MB |
| 10 | 215 MB | 21 MB |
| 50 | 992 MB | 22 MB |

## Not in this pull request

- **Undo after commands over whole ranges.** A sort or a format over every row copies every band, so every cell. On a 2-million-cell sheet that is about 110–140 MB a step (20 sorts peaked at 3 GB). That is #1227, and #1263 caps the history by an estimate of the cells it keeps. That estimate counts cells only, so it wouldn't have caught the pictures; the two fit together.
- **Other fields of a touched sheet are still copied at every edit:** the spill map, comments, …

title: Memory: interface fonts are read once and shared with egui, not copied into it
author: arcanii
body:
## What it does

egui copies the bytes of an owned font into its text engine and keeps the original `FontData` too: epaint's `blob_from_font_data` does `data.clone().font`, and a `Cow::Owned` clone copies the `Vec`. So every interface and script fallback font GridCraft loads was in memory twice. On a Mac the fallbacks alone are 89 MB of files: Hiragino Sans GB, Hiragino Sans, Apple SD Gothic Neo, Thonburi, Arial Hebrew and Apple Symbols.

Bytes egui borrows for `'static` it shares instead. `try_load` now keeps each file it reads for the rest of the run and hands egui those bytes with `FontData::from_static`.

- **These faces are loaded by every font rebuild** for as long as the app runs (at startup, then whenever the interface language or the workbook's fonts change), so keeping them costs nothing. Rebuilds also no longer read them from disk again.
- **Only a file that parses is kept.** A missing or broken file is looked for again next time, as before.
- **Unchanged:** which faces load and in what order. Workbook fonts (`fonts::bind_faces`) load as before.

**How it was measured:**
- macOS 27.0.1 on an Apple M3 Max, release builds of the `snapshot` example from `main` (`bb685e3`) and from this branch.
- Both builds held the process for 4 s after the picture so the settled footprint could be read. That hold was in the measuring builds only, not here.
- Physical footprint (Activity Monitor's "Memory") through `proc_pid_rusage`, Metal backend. Each run twice; the runs agreed within 5 MB.

| | Settled | Peak (with the render's own cost) |
|---|---|---|
| Empty workbook | 258 → 158 MB | 706 → 606 MB |
| `--sample sales` | 261 → 160 MB | 709 → 608 MB |
| A cell in Chinese, emoji, Thai, Devanagari and Arabic | 258 → 158 MB | 706 → 606 MB |

The three rendered PNGs are byte-for-byte the same before and after.

For scale, the same empty workbook with no script fallback faces at all settles at 87 MB. Loading those faces only once a character of their script appears would save…

title: Memory: floating pictures' textures are bounded, sized to what is drawn, and dropped with their workbook
author: arcanii
body:
## What it does

Floating pictures (Insert › Pictures) were drawn from `TEXTURES` in `chartview.rs`, one process-wide map of textures that:

- **decoded every picture at full size, with no limits,** and briefly in two or three copies (`to_rgba8`, then `ColorImage`);
- **never let go,** not even when the picture's workbook was closed;
- **told pictures apart by id and byte length alone.** Picture ids are per workbook, so a second open workbook could show the first one's picture: a new test shows it on `main`;
- **tried a picture it couldn't decode again every frame.**

A new `crates/ui-egui/src/floating_pictures.rs`, built the way `cell_pictures.rs` is, replaces it.

## How

- **A cache per egui context,** keyed by workbook (`DocState::uid`), picture id and size.
- **Bounded at 128 MB,** dropping the least recently drawn first. A picture drawn in the last frame is never dropped, so no picture turns into a placeholder, whatever the budget.
- **A workbook's textures go when it closes.** This is checked every frame in `SheetApp::logic`, so it works even when no sheet is painted.
- **Decoded with limits:** the header is read first (16,384 px a side, 64 megapixels at most), then the picture is decoded with `image::Limits`.
- **Decoded at about the size it is drawn:** the next step of a power of two or three quarters of one (…, 1024, 1536, 2048), up to 4,096 px or the GPU's `max_texture_side`. It is decoded again only when drawn larger than that, so zooming in re-decodes at most every half or third larger.
- **A picture that can't be decoded is remembered,** not retried every frame.

**How it was measured:**
- macOS 27.0.1 on an Apple M3 Max, release builds from `main` (`bb685e3`) and from this branch.
- A throwaway example, not in this pull request, using the `snapshot` example's harness. It opens an `.xlsx` with 12 or 24 copies of a 2600 × 2600 picture (each drawn 640 points square) beside a blank workbook. It scrolls to each picture in turn, rendering at each, holds, th…

title: Files: notice a file another program rewrote, and ask which version to keep
author: goesByhc
body:
## Summary

A workbook whose file another program rewrites (a Git checkout, another editor, a script) is noticed within a second, and GridCraft asks which version to keep:

```
File Changed on Disk
model.xlsx was changed on disk by another program (a Git checkout, another editor) since GridCraft read it.
Use the version on disk, or keep the version in GridCraft.
[Use Disk Version]  [Keep Current Version]
Closing this prompt keeps the version in GridCraft.
```

With unsaved changes it adds a line in the theme's danger colour: "The workbook has unsaved changes: the disk version discards them."

Today nothing is noticed: another program's version is silently overwritten by the next Save, and there is no way to see it.

## Changes

- **Detection (engine).** `DocState` keeps a `FileStamp` (the file's mtime and length), recorded when the file is opened and after GridCraft's own save, so a save is never reported as an external change. `file.externalChanges` compares the stamps of the open workbooks: `{changed, documents: [{index, uid, title, path, dirty}]}`. The browser has no file system, so it never reports one.
- **The frame loop (UI).** `SheetApp::check_external_changes` runs at most once a second, only while a workbook has a file, and keeps the frame loop alive so the question is asked without input. It stands down while a cell is being edited, while another dialog is open and in the Backstage view.
- **The two answers.** `file.reload` replaces the workbook in place — window, uid, active sheet, selection and scroll stay, and the undo history starts over, since the base it referred to is gone. It refuses a workbook with unsaved changes unless `force: true`, which the prompt passes. `file.ignoreExternalChange` keeps the version in GridCraft and accepts the file's stamp as it is now, so the change is not asked about again until the file changes once more. Closing the prompt (✕, Escape, `ui.dialog.cancel`) is that second answer.
- **AutoSave** waits while the prompt is op…

title: Memory: undo steps share the parts of a sheet an edit leaves alone
author: arcanii
body:
## What it does

Every edit keeps the workbook as it was for Undo. The cells were already shared between undo steps, 64-row band by band. The sheet's other large parts were not: a typed cell copied all of them into its step, up to the 100 steps of the history. The same went for the workbook's names and styles.

They are shared now, until an edit changes them:
- **On the sheet:** row and column sizes, spilled values, notes and comments, hyperlinks, conditional formats and validations.
- **On the workbook:** names and styles.

**Measured:**
- macOS 27.0.1 on an Apple M3 Max, release builds of `main` (`f1894c6`) and of this branch, `gridcraft-cli`.
- The kernel's peak physical footprint, from `proc_pid_rusage`.
- One synthetic workbook per part, built with the CLI and saved as `.xlsx`, then opened and given 50 `cell.set` edits on the same sheet.

| Part | Open → 50 edits, `main` | This branch | Each typed cell kept, `main` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spilled values (`=SEQUENCE(100000)`) | 17 → 343 MB | 17 → 18 MB | 6.5 MB |
| Custom row heights, 50,000 rows | 7 → 140 MB | 7 → 8 MB | 2.7 MB |
| Distinct styles, 5,000 | 22 → 138 MB | 22 → 24 MB | 2.3 MB |
| Notes, 10,000 | 58 → 170 MB | 58 → 58 MB | 2.2 MB |
| Hyperlinks, 10,000 | 20 → 101 MB | 20 → 22 MB | 1.6 MB |
| Conditional-format rules, 2,000 | 6 → 39 MB | 6 → 7 MB | 0.7 MB |
| Defined names, 5,000 | 5 → 36 MB | 5 → 6 MB | 0.6 MB |
| Validations, 2,000 | 5 → 27 MB | 5 → 6 MB | 0.4 MB |

The size at open varies by a few MB from run to run.

## How

title: fix(ui): move selection glide on the drag frame
author: sabyr-cpu
body:
## Summary

```diff
 on selection range change
-  restart glide clock at now
-  draw the outline where it already was
+  count the time already elapsed this frame
+  ease the outline toward the cells under the cursor
```

A drag that reached a new cell every frame restarted the 0.12s glide at progress zero, so the border sat still until the pointer paused. The frame that changes the range now counts, and the border keeps easing onto those cells.

## Evidence

- **Before:** `a_drag_moves_the_outline_on_every_new_cell` — each new cell left the outline unmoved (`drawn.max.x` did not increase).
  **After:** that test passes, and `a_pointer_drag_glides_the_outline_with_the_cursor` shows the border in flight after a drag to F7, then settled on `A1:F7`.
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui --lib selection_glide` — 11 passed.
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui --test selection_glide` — 8 passed.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

The glide duration and easing curve are unchanged. Reverting the clock line restores the old pause.

**Blast Radius:** selection outline

Keyboard glides, scroll-with-the-sheet, screenshots, and View › Animations off still take the existing paths. Only the frame a selection changes uses the elapsed time.

title: fix(xlsx): bound repeated column expansion
author: harrisonoconnorhover
body:
Fixes #1022.

Repeated wide `<col>` declarations can make a compact worksheet repeatedly rewrite the same 16,384 column entries. Import now allows at most 1,000,000 expanded column assignments per worksheet, shared across all `<cols>` blocks. Each nondefault span is charged after clipping to the grid and before insertion. The existing `IoError::TooLarge` path rejects the import when the limit is exceeded, instead of silently dropping a partially read sheet.

Three regression tests cover repeated spans in one or multiple blocks, exact-limit acceptance and one-assignment overflow, clipping/default/invalid records, and last-wins widths, hidden flags and styles. Two budget tests failed on main because the reader accepted excess work; ordinary overlaps passed. These are bounded fixtures (at most 16,384 stored columns), not a claim that a hang was reproduced.

Validation on macOS arm64 with Rust 1.95.0:

- All 177 XLSX tests passed, zero failed.
- Formatting, assets, dependency layers, WASM, parity and keytips checks passed.
- Full workspace tests passed: 1,614 passed, zero failed, 1 existing ignored test.
- `cargo xtask ci` stops at the unchanged `clippy::collapsible_match` in `crates/xlsx/src/xls/mod.rs:273` on base `f1894c6`. A diagnostic all-target XLSX Clippy run reports that warning plus existing `clippy::nonminimal_bool` at `tests/passthrough_tests.rs:480`, with no warnings in the changed code. title: fix(ets): avoid repeated scans while interpolating gaps
author: harrisonoconnorhover
body:
Fixes #1042.

FORECAST.ETS interpolation restarted a forward search for every missing point, repeatedly inspecting the same gap. It now keeps one forward-only iterator over known points and retains the next point until the output reaches it. Lookahead inspects each slot once, uses constant extra storage, and keeps the existing interpolation arithmetic, nearest-value endpoint behavior and missing-point limits.

Three new tests cover asymmetric/multiple gaps and endpoints, deterministic lookahead work, and series preparation at the 30% missing-point boundary (including zero-fill and refusal above the limit). A test-only thread-local counter measures the actual search predicate, with no instrumentation in non-test builds:

| Completed slots | Old lookahead visits | New lookahead visits |
|---|---:|---:|
| 2,000 | 180,300 | 2,000 |
| 4,000 | 720,600 | 4,000 |

The work-bound regression failed on the old algorithm while the other eight ETS checks passed. These are operation counts from bounded synthetic fixtures, not wall-clock latency or UI responsiveness measurements. Model fitting and seasonality detection are unchanged.

Validation on macOS arm64 with Rust 1.95.0:

- All 126 function-library tests passed.
- Function-library all-target Clippy with warnings denied, formatting and diff checks passed.
- Assets, dependency layers, parity and keytips checks passed.
- WASM and full workspace tests passed (1,614 passed, 1 ignored, 0 failed).
