title: Fill handle: right-drag opens the fill menu (Copy Cells, Fill Series, Fill Formatting Only, Fill Without Formatting, Series…)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Dragging the fill handle with the right mouse button now opens Excel's fill menu on release instead of filling.

In Excel, a right-drag of the fill handle shows the same dashed outline as a normal drag, but fills nothing when you let go. Instead it opens a menu where you release the button: Copy Cells, Fill Series, Fill Formatting Only, Fill Without Formatting, then the date, trend and Flash Fill items, then Series…. This PR adds the first four and Series…:
- Copy Cells repeats the source.
- Fill Series extends it. Unlike a plain drag, a lone number counts up.
- Fill Formatting Only copies only the formats.
- Fill Without Formatting extends the series but leaves the target cells' formats alone.
- Series… selects the source plus the dragged cells and opens the Series dialog for them. The dialog now opens set to Rows after a sideways drag; before, it always said Columns, so OK did nothing on a row.

Esc during the drag, or with the menu open, fills nothing. Once the drag has left the source, Esc also keeps the copied range; while the pointer is still on the source, Esc clears it, as it does for a left drag today. A plain right-click on the handle still opens the cell context menu, and the left-button drag is unchanged.

On the engine side, `edit.autoFill` gets an `extend` mode for Fill Series. The `values` mode, which was already meant to be Fill Without Formatting, now extends the series the way Excel does instead of copying. No UI path sent `values`; a script passing `mode: "values"` to `edit.autoFill` on a series source (1, 2) now gets 3, 4 instead of 1, 2. Happy to rename `extend` if you prefer something else.

title: XLSX import: plain formulas keep legacy implicit intersection (explicit @)
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
A plain formula like `=IF(ISBLANK(B:B),0,IF(B4="Thierry",C4,0))` was evaluated as a dynamic array: the whole-column reference lifted into an array that cannot spill, so the cell returned `#SPILL!` and the error propagated through every dependent formula. Under legacy Excel rules the reference intersects at the formula's row — the formula tests `B4` and the cell shows `7`.

The fix is at import time, matching how Excel distinguishes the two eras: when a plain (shared or normal) `<f>` formula is read from a file, a multi-cell reference sitting in a scalar position gains an explicit `@`. Whole-column and whole-row references included, the brief's `G4` evaluates to `7` after a plain open.

Nothing else changes semantics: aggregates and anything that consumes ranges as ranges, `SUM(IF(…))`, `FILTER`/`MAP`, lambdas, defined names, `TYPE`/`ROWS` and friends never get the `@`, formulas written by the app are untouched, and modern `t="array"` formulas keep spilling — the rewrite only fires on the legacy file shape where Excel itself applies implicit intersection.

Tests: 35 rewrite cases (scalars get `@`, aggregates don't, mixed forms, whole-column/row), a legacy-shaped file round-trips its formulas, and an open-with-blocking-cell end-to-end check reads `G4 == 7`. The xlsx (177), calc (59) and engine suites pass.

Fixes #1636

title: Merged cell with Wrap Text: auto-fit skips it, so the text draws and the row keeps its default height
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
A merged cell with Wrap Text drew nothing, and a save wrote `<row r="1" ht="165">` — the text wrapped at column A's 18-character width instead of the merged width, 11 lines × 15 pt.

One root cause covers both symptoms: `auto_row_height` computed the wrap for merged cells at the anchor column's width alone, like Excel it should skip merged cells entirely (column autofit already does). With the bogus 138–165 pt height gone, the save writes `<row r="1">` with no `ht` — Excel keeps its default height for merged rows — and the text draws, because the old height was pushing bottom-aligned text out of the clip; no paint change was needed.

Test: the issue's shape (A1:E1 merged, wrap on, a long sentence, no stored height) — the row gets no custom height and the wrapped line ends at the merge edge; the red test showed `size: Some(184.0)` on main. Verified open→save on the release binaries against an Excel-shaped file.

Fixes #1605

title: Names: refuse names that begin like an R1C1 reference, as Excel does
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1663.

`is_r1c1` only refused a name that is an R1C1 reference as a whole, and didn't look at the numbers. This follows the rule @iluebbe measured in Excel 365: a name can't begin with `R` and a row number (1 to 1,048,576), or with `C` or `RC` and a column number (1 to 16,384), where the number is the whole run of digits; a `.` may follow the number, so `R1.x`, `C1.x` and `RC1.x` are fine (`R1C1.x` is not). `R`, `C` and `RC` alone are still refused, and `R0C0` / `R1048577C1` are now accepted. Create from Selection already prefixes `_` to a label `valid_name` refuses, so `R1 Total` now gives Excel's `_R1_Total`. The existing test listed `R1C1X` as a valid name; the measurements say Excel refuses it, so I moved it to the refused list.

Names already in a file (e.g. `R1_Total` written by Create from Selection in 0.7.0) are still read and saved as they are. Name Manager › Edit doesn't re-check a name it keeps, so you can still change what such a name refers to, or rename it to a valid one. Happy to switch if you'd rather refuse those edits too.

The function keeps its `fn is_r1c1(&str) -> bool` signature, so #1434 (table names) picks up the same rule once both land; the two touch neighbouring lines, so whichever goes second needs a one-line rebase.

Not covered here: non-ASCII digits (`R١x`, `R²x`, which Excel refuses) and the Z/S letters of the German UI. They need a rule for which characters count as digits or letters that I can only measure partly, so I left them out.

title: macOS: bold interface text draws Cyrillic е open, not like ө
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1184.

On macOS the bold interface role loads Helvetica Neue Bold (`HelveticaNeue.ttc`, face 1), and epaint applies the font's own TrueType hints by default. Those hints close the aperture of Cyrillic е at 26 px, so 13 pt bold text on a Retina screen draws `значений_пример.xlsx` as `значөний_примөр.xlsx`. Core Text never runs TrueType hints, which is why every other Mac app gets it right. This turns hinting off (`FontTweak::hinting = Some(false)`) for that one face on macOS. Thanks to @dfgodvan for the exact diagnosis.

I kept it as narrow as the bug: only the macOS bold UI face. The regular UI face (SF), the cell faces and the fallback faces keep egui's default, and so do Windows and Linux, where hinted text is what people expect. I rendered 12/13/14 pt bold before and after: the е opens at 13 pt and Latin text looks the same, with unchanged advance widths. If you'd rather unhint every system face on macOS, the way Core Text does, it's the same line without the role check. Happy to switch.

The change is in `font_definitions_with`, next to where the face is registered, not in `try_load`, so it doesn't overlap #1630, which rewrites `try_load`.

Validation:
- `theme::tests::macos_bold_interface_face_is_drawn_unhinted`: fails on main (`left: None, right: Some(false)`), passes here
- Offscreen render (egui_kittest, wgpu, 2 px per point) of the bold UI family at 12/13/14 pt: `значөний` on main, `значений` here; Latin and the regular face unchanged
- `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

title: Keep overflow text visible when its source cell scrolls out of view
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #1613

## Cause
`paint_quadrant` only laid out text for cells inside the visible column range. When a text cell scrolled off one side, nothing drew its overflow into the visible empty cells next to it, so the whole text disappeared.

## Fix
For each visible row, the text pass now also handles the nearest non-empty cell up to 20 columns left and right of the visible range. That cell must be in the same frozen or scrolled pane, visible, and not merged. Its overflow is painted clipped to the quadrant. Merges are now looked up across the same widened range, so overflow coming in from off-screen still stops at merged cells.

## Verified
- Regression tests `overflow_text_stays_visible_when_source_cell_scrolls_out_left`, `right_aligned_overflow_stays_visible_when_source_cell_is_right_of_view`, `scrolled_overflow_does_not_draw_over_frozen_columns`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui --test text_overflow_scroll`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Backgrounds, borders, sparklines and filter buttons are still painted only for visible cells. The 20-column overflow limit, which already applied to visible cells, is unchanged.

title: Numfmt: Japanese 和暦 date formats (era tokens, gannen 元年, day-accurate era boundaries)
author: midasdf
body:
## What this adds

Excel-compatible **和暦 (Japanese calendar) date formats** in `crates/numfmt`, so a Japanese workbook's cell formats render as Excel renders them: `[$-411]ggge"年"m"月"d"日"` → `令和8年10月17日`.

Today the crate is en-US only and every `[...]` locale tag is parsed and dropped, so 和暦 format codes fall back to literal text (`ggg` printed as `ggg`, `e` as the 4-digit year).

- `[$-411]`, `[$-ja]`, `[$-ja-JP]` (case-insensitive) make a section's `g`/`e` Japanese era tokens; every other tag and every untagged format keeps **this crate's** behaviour exactly as before (`g` stays literal, `e` stays the 4-digit year, `[$-409]` etc. unchanged).

  This is deliberately *not* Excel parity for the untagged case: on an en-US Excel 16.0, an untagged `ggg` (and `[$-409]ggge`) renders as empty text and `ge.m.d` as `2026.10.17`, while this crate keeps printing the literal letters. Changing that is out of scope here; the note records the difference rather than claiming it matches.
- Era tokens: `g` → `M`/`T`/`S`/`H`/`R`, `gg` → `明`/`大`/`昭`/`平`/`令`, `ggg` → `明治`/`大正`/`昭和`/`平成`/`令和`, `e` → era year, `ee` → era year zero-padded to two digits.
- 元年: `[$-ja-JP-x-gannen]` renders era year 1 as `元` for both `e` and `ee`. The legacy `[$-x-gannen411]` is accepted **leniently** — Excel 16.0 (en-US) rejects that tag as a number format and `TEXT()` gives `#VALUE!` — so reading it is an extension, not a fidelity claim.
- Day-accurate era boundaries: 明治 1868-01-25, 大正 1912-07-30, 昭和 1926-12-25, 平成 1989-01-08, 令和 2019-05-01; both the 1900 and 1904 date systems are honoured. A date before 明治 has no era, so the era tokens render nothing and the section's literals survive.
- `TEXT()` goes through the same path.

Behaviour reference (documentation only, no code copied): [Microsoft Q&A「日本の年号変更と元年」](https://learn.microsoft.com/ja-jp/answers/questions/5029923/question-5029923) (the `[$-411]` / `[$-ja-JP]` tag and the 元年 section) and the era-token table and boundaries at [ReoGrid: Japanese Era Dat…

title: XLSX: keep Japanese phonetic runs (ふりがな) on open and save
author: midasdf
body:
## What this fixes

Excel's Japanese furigana lives in `xl/sharedStrings.xml` as `<rPh sb="…" eb="…"><t>…</t></rPh>` runs (plus a `<phoneticPr>`), where `sb`/`eb` are zero-based offsets into the base text. GridCraft dropped both — `xml::rich_text()` read `<t>` and `<r>` only, `Ctx.sst` kept text alone, and the writer emitted `<si><t>…</t></si>` — so a plain **open + save silently deleted a Japanese workbook's furigana**.

An open + save now keeps the readings:

- `PhoneticRun { start, end, text }`, `PhoneticProps { font_id, kind, alignment }` and `PhoneticString { text, runs, props }` in `crates/model`, with a serde-defaulted `Workbook::phonetics` field (additive: old JSON still loads, existing `Workbook` literals use `..Default::default()`).
- `xml::phonetic_data()` reads the runs and `<phoneticPr>`, validating every offset against the base text and dropping damaged runs (`sb >= eb`, wholly past the end, no `<t>`, empty reading) instead of repairing them; the reader warns with the count. `xml::si_body()` writes the runs back — and is **byte-identical to `t_el()`** for a string without phonetic data.
- The table is keyed by base text because that is the only handle a cell keeps on its shared string (the format's `uniqueCount` holds each text once); the lookup on save is one `HashMap`, so no O(n²).
- Scope: `<si>` shared strings. Comment `<text>` and inline `<is>` strings keep today's behaviour.

Behaviour reference (documentation only): ISO/IEC 29500-1 §18.4.6 `rPh` / §18.4.7 `phoneticPr`, and the Microsoft Learn [`PhoneticRun`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/office/developer/office-2010/cc820083(v=office.14)) page.

## Tests

`cargo test -p gridcraft-xlsx -p gridcraft-model` → **182 + 15 passed, 0 failed**; `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-xlsx -p gridcraft-model --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean.

```

title: Charts: series that refer to defined names (`[0]!Name`) plot their data, and are saved qualified
author: bldred
body:
Fixes #1686.

Excel writes a workbook-scoped defined name in a chart reference as `[0]!Name`. `chart.rs` kept that text verbatim, the lexer read `[0]` as a structured reference, and the series evaluated to `#NAME?`, so a chart over dynamic (OFFSET) names opened blank with one `#NAME?` category. This handles the notation at the XLSX boundary, the way `fmla.rs` already handles other file-only syntax; the formula parser is unchanged.

- **Read** (`xlsx/src/chart.rs`, `chart_ref_from_file`): `[0]!Name` becomes `Name` in `c:f` for `cat`, `val`, `xVal`, `yVal`, `bubbleSize` and `tx`, in chartex `cx:f`, and in the `_xlchart.*` names chartex parts point at. It only drops `[0]!` at the start of a reference or after an operator, and only before a name, so external books (`[1]Sheet1!$A$1`, `[2]!Rates`), quoted sheet names, string literals and structured references keep their current behaviour.
- **Write** (`chart_ref_to_file`): a name in a chart reference is always written qualified, because Excel draws a chart with a bare name blank (see below). A workbook-scoped name is written `[0]!Name`, as Excel writes it; a sheet-scoped one (including one that shadows a workbook name on the chart's sheet) `Sheet!Name`, with the sheet quoted when needed; an already qualified name keeps its sheet; an undefined name gets `[0]!`, as the file it came from had. A reference to a sheet that doesn't exist is written as it was. A series name that is a defined name (qualified or not) is written as a `strRef`; before, `is_ref` sent it down the literal path and it was saved as text.
- **Resolve** (`chart/src/resolve.rs`, `series_name`): a series name that is a defined name (`Name`, or `Sheet1!Name` looked up on that sheet, as the evaluator does) is evaluated rather than shown as its text, matching what the writer treats as a reference.

title: Charts: box & whisker charts honor their quartile method
author: webdevtodayjason
body:
Box & whisker charts always drew inclusive quartiles but wrote `quartileMethod="exclusive"` to XLSX, so the same chart showed a different box in GridCraft and Excel (values 1 to 6: 2.25 to 4.75 here, 1.75 to 5.25 in Excel). Saving an inclusive chart from Excel also turned it exclusive.

Each series now keeps its quartile method (`QuartileMethod`, default exclusive like Excel). The renderer uses it for the box, whiskers and outliers, `cx:statistics@quartileMethod` is read and written per series (missing or unknown reads as exclusive), and `chart.set {"quartiles": "exclusive" | "inclusive"}` sets it for every series in the chart and rejects anything else. With fewer than three values, exclusive Q1 and Q3 clamp to the minimum and maximum so the box stays drawable, as the issue suggests; Excel's own small-sample behavior wasn't measured. Worksheet QUARTILE functions are unchanged.

Fixes #1453

## How it was tested

- `box_whisker_default_quartiles_are_exclusive` fails on main (2.25 instead of 1.75) and passes with the change. `quartile_methods_and_short_samples` checks both methods for 0 to 7 values, matching QUARTILE.EXC and QUARTILE.INC wherever those are defined.
- `box_whisker_draws_each_series_quartile_method` renders one exclusive and one inclusive series in the same chart.
- `box_whisker_reads_quartile_method_and_defaults` covers a missing `cx:statistics`, an empty one, an unknown value, and both methods. `box_whisker_quartile_methods_survive_xlsx` round-trips a chart with mixed methods and checks `chart.set` validation.
- `cargo xtask ci`: all 8 steps pass (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm, parity, keytips).

title: XLSX: new workbooks get <fileVersion appName="gridcraft"/> (fixes #1699)
author: aviiciii
body:
Fixes #1699.

## What changes
- A workbook created in GridCraft had no `<fileVersion>` in `xl/workbook.xml`. It now gets `<fileVersion appName="gridcraft"/>` as the first child of `<workbook>`, and keeps it on later saves.
- A workbook read from an Excel file still keeps its `<fileVersion>` as it was, **`appName="xl"` included**. Rewriting it would bring back #799.

## Why Excel files keep `appName="xl"`
I tested this in Excel for Mac 16.114 with synthetic workbooks. Each had `B1 = A1*2` with a stale cached value, the calcFeatures extension and `calcPr calcId="191029"`. Only the `<fileVersion>` element differed:

| `<fileVersion>` | B1 shown on open |
|---|---|
| `appName="xl"` | 99 (cached value kept) |
| `appName="gridcraft"` | 2 (recalculated) |
| `appName="Calc"` | 2 |
| no `appName` attribute | 2 |
| no `<fileVersion>` | 2 |

With `appName="xl"` and a cached value of 12345, B1 opened as 12345 and a forced full recalculation gave 2. So Excel trusts the cache only when `appName` is `"xl"`. With any other value it recalculates everything on open, and lookups into closed workbooks come back as `#CALC!` (#799).

The application that last saved the file is already recorded in `docProps/app.xml` as `<Application>GridCraft</Application>`. GridCraft rebuilds that part on every save, and #799 showed it has no effect on Excel's recalculation.

A new workbook with `<fileVersion appName="gridcraft"/>` and no calcFeatures opens in Excel without a repair prompt and is recalculated, the same as before.

## Tests
- `file_version_and_calc_features_survive_a_save` now checks that a new workbook carries `<fileVersion appName="gridcraft"/>` first in `<workbook>`, keeps it on a second save, and has no `extLst`.
- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm all pass.

title: Fonts: find the cell, serif, mono, Thai and Hebrew faces in Fedora's package folders (#1694)
author: tydude001

Part of #1694 (problem 1, except CJK).

On Fedora the cell font roles in `crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs` find no face. Fedora keeps each family in its own
package folder (`google-carlito-fonts/`, `liberation-sans-fonts/`…), and the roles only list the Debian/Ubuntu/Arch
folders. Every cell then falls back to egui's built-in proportional font, which has one weight and no italic, so bold

title: Reject table.resize when the new range overlaps another table
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/extra.rs:818-855 (table_resize, overlap check at ~832)` (no existing issue): table.resize lets a table grow over another table, leaving two overlapping tables.

## Cause
`table_resize` only checked that the header row stayed in place and that the new range intersected the table's own old range. It never compared the new range with the other tables on the sheet, so a resize could leave two overlapping tables.

## Fix
`table_resize` now returns "A table can't overlap another table." when the new range intersects any other table on the sheet. This is the same check `insert.table` uses. The table being resized is skipped, so resizing over its own old range still works.

## Verified
- Regression tests `resize_over_another_table_is_rejected`, `resize_next_to_another_table_still_works`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p gridcraft-engine --test table_resize_overlap`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The existing header-row and self-overlap checks and error message are unchanged. Resizing next to another table without intersecting it still succeeds.

title: Fill Justify: Excel text reflow and keytips (fixes #1673)
author: sam-f-gh
body:
## Summary

Implements Microsoft Excel's **Fill Justify** (`edit.fillJustify`) command matching `Home > Editing > Fill > Justify` behavior (fixes #1673).

### Features & Parity
- **Reflow & Consolidation:** Ingests text across the selected range, word-wraps it to fit the combined column width (`points_to_chars`), and writes reflowed lines into the leftmost column. Empty cells in the selection are cleared.
- **Atomic Word Wrapping:** Words wrap strictly at whitespace boundaries. Long unbroken words exceeding column capacity remain whole on their line without slicing or hyphenation, allowing clean re-justification across wider ranges.
- **Safety Guards:**
  - Rejects selections containing formulas (`"Cannot justify cells containing formulas"`).
  - Bounds check against sheet height (`MAX_ROWS`).
  - Guards against extending below selection unless `allow_overflow: true` (default).
  - Guards against overwriting non-empty cells below selection unless `overwrite: true`.
- **Formatting Preservation:** Reflowed cells preserve the style of the first populated cell.
- **Keytips & Shortcuts:**
  - Modern ribbon sequence: `Alt` -> `H` -> `F` -> `I` -> `J` (`edit.fillJustify`).
  - Legacy Excel 2003 sequence: `Alt` -> `E` -> `I` -> `J` (`edit.fillJustify`).
  - Added to Home > Editing > Fill dropdown menu in Ribbon.

### Verification
- `cargo xtask ci` passes all 8 quality gates (`fmt`, `clippy`, `test`, `assets`, `layers`, `wasm`, `parity`, `keytips`).
- Parity checklist regenerated: 275 / 291 commands implemented (94.5%).
- Added unit tests in `crates/engine/src/fill.rs` covering reflow, multi-column consolidation, formula rejection, overflow/overwrite guards, and atomic word preservation.

title: Rows: a big font isn't counted twice when the sheet's default height already fits it
author: tisca26
body:
## What this changes

Rows of big text open at the height Excel gives them when the sheet's default row height already fits that text. They used to open about 1.45 times taller.

**Cause.** `auto_row_height` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/mod.rs`) estimates one line of a font bigger than 11pt as `max(round(size × 1.8), default × size / 11)`, where `default` is the sheet's default row height. That scaling assumes the default fits 11pt text. Excel for Mac saved a workbook of 16pt Montserrat text with `defaultRowHeight="21"` (28px) and no `ht` on its rows, so the default already fit the font. On open, `fit_imported_rows` (#855, for #833) fitted every row to 28 × 16 / 11 = 40.7px, where Excel shows them at 28px. The cells kept their alignment, but in rows that tall the Middle-aligned columns sat visibly higher than the Bottom-aligned ones, so the sheet looked misaligned.

**Fix.** The estimate scales `DEFAULT_ROW_HEIGHT`, the height of an 11pt row, instead of the sheet's default. On that sheet, a 16pt row opens at 29.1px. On a sheet with the 15pt default, the result is the same as before, so #833 still holds.

## Tests

- `tests::open_fits_big_font_rows_from_the_font_not_the_sheet_default`: a synthetic workbook with a 28px default row height and a 16pt cell in a row without a height opens with that row between 28 and 30px. With the change reverted, it fails with 40.73px.
- #833's open-time tests (`open_grows_default_height_rows_to_their_font` and the four after it) pass unchanged.

On macOS 27.0.1 (Apple silicon), Rust 1.99.0, on `f1894c6`:

- `cargo test -p gridcraft-engine`: 287 passed
- `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean

By hand: the original workbook (private data, not attached) opens in `cargo run -p gridcraft` with rows the height Excel for Mac shows, and its columns line up.

title: Shift print titles and page breaks on row/column insert and delete
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/sheet.rs:115 (shift_sheet_features; the print-area shift is at ~line 212)` (no existing issue): Inserting or deleting rows/columns does not move print titles or manual page breaks.

## Cause
`shift_sheet_features` remapped `print.print_area` when rows or columns were inserted or deleted, but never touched `print.title_rows`, `print.title_cols`, `print.row_breaks` or `print.col_breaks`. After an insert or delete above them, the repeated titles and manual page breaks stayed at their old indices and pointed at the wrong lines.

## Fix
`shift_sheet_features` now shifts the title span and the manual breaks for the edited axis. On insert, lines at or after the edit point move down. A title span pushed entirely off the sheet is dropped, and one that only reaches the edge is cut there. On delete, lines move up. A title span that is wholly deleted is cleared, and a partly deleted one shrinks. A break inside a deleted block falls onto the line that takes its place, and breaks pushed off the sheet are dropped.

## Verified
- Regression tests `inserting_lines_moves_print_titles`, `inserting_lines_moves_page_breaks`, `deleting_lines_moves_or_drops_print_titles`, `deleting_lines_moves_page_breaks`, `titles_pushed_off_the_sheet_are_dropped_or_cut`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p gridcraft-engine --test print_titles_breaks_shift`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The separate cell-shift path (`shift_cell_features`) is unchanged. Print-area handling is unchanged.

author: richard1912
body:
## Summary

`home.borders`, `data.validation` and `home.conditionalFormat` now read style, operator and validation type names from one table per enum in the model. ## Cause

The names of `BorderStyle`, `CfOperator` and `ValidationKind` were spelled out again in each command, dialog and the XLSX reader and writer, and the copies disagreed:

title: PivotTable: delete report when cleared, refuse partial clearing (fixes #1719)
author: sam-f-gh
body:
### Description
In Microsoft Excel, PivotTables have well-defined deletion and clearing semantics:
1. Selecting the **entire PivotTable range** and pressing `Delete` (`edit.clearContents` or `edit.clearAll`) completely deletes the PivotTable object from the worksheet, clearing its layout, styles, and unregistering the table so the PivotTable Fields pane no longer opens. Full undo/redo is supported.
2. Selecting a **partial range** (e.g., subset of cells or row/column labels) and pressing `Delete` or clearing is blocked with:
   > *"Cannot change part of a PivotTable report."*
3. Deleting or inserting rows/columns/cells that cut through a PivotTable report is similarly refused.

Previously in GridCraft, pressing `Delete` on a PivotTable range only cleared cell values while leaving the underlying `PivotTable` in `sheet.pivots` and its table styling intact. Partial deletions also erased cell text, corrupting the visual state of the report.

### Changes
* **`crates/engine/src/cmd/pivot.rs`**: Extracted `delete_pivot_in_sheet` to clean up pivot output cells, unlink any linked PivotCharts, remove the pivot from `sh.pivots`, and schedule row height refitting.
* **`crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs`**: In `clear()`, check PivotTable boundaries:
  - If the selection completely encloses the PivotTable and `what` is `"contents"" or `"all"", the PivotTable is deleted.
  - If the selection only partially intersects a PivotTable, the operation is blocked with *"Cannot change part of a PivotTable report."*.
* **`crates/engine/src/cmd/sheet.rs`**: Guarded `delete_lines`, `delete_cells`, and `insert_cells` against invalid partial PivotTable intersections. Deleting rows/columns that completely enclose the PivotTable deletes it cleanly.
* **Tests**: Added test cases in `crates/engine/src/cmd/pivot.rs` covering full deletion, undo/redo, partial clear refusal, and structural line/cell deletion boundaries.

Fixes #1719

title: Remember desktop window size and position between sessions
author: TheRenegadeDev
body:
Fixes #1431.

title: Move PivotTables with their cells on row/column insert and delete
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/sheet.rs:115 (shift_sheet_features; it never touches sh.pivots)` (no existing issue): Inserting or deleting rows/columns does not move a PivotTable's anchor or range, so it no longer matches its cells.

## Cause
Inserting or deleting rows or columns moved a PivotTable's output cells but not its `anchor` or `last_range`, so the PivotTable no longer matched its cells. The formula rewrite step also skipped the pivot `source`, so a source range left stale by a row or column shift on its sheet made a later refresh read the wrong cells or fail.

## Fix
`shift_sheet_features` now moves each pivot's `anchor` and `last_range` along with its cells. An anchor whose line is deleted moves to the line that takes its place, and a report that is deleted entirely has no last area until the next refresh. `rewrite` now adjusts every pivot's `source` reference on all sheets, but only when the edit actually moves it, so table and defined-name sources keep their text.

## Verified
- Regression tests `inserting_or_deleting_lines_moves_the_pivot_with_its_cells`, `inserting_rows_on_the_source_sheet_moves_another_sheets_pivot_source`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p gridcraft-engine --lib cmd::pivot::tests::inserting_`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Insert/Delete Cells (`shift_cell_features`) and `sheet.moveColumns` still do not move a pivot's anchor or report area; they do get the source rewrite. Deleting all the rows or columns that hold a report does not delete the PivotTable.

title: Conditional formatting: data bars keep Automatic and Lowest/Highest Value bounds apart (#1159)
author: TheRenegadeDev
body:
Fixes #1159.

## Summary

Excel writes both Automatic and Lowest/Highest Value data bars as `min`/`max` in the main section. Only the x14 rule tells them apart. GridCraft now keeps them apart all the way through:

```diff
 CfValueKind (model)
   Min, Max, Number, Percent, Percentile, Formula
+  AutoMin, AutoMax            # data bars only

 threshold() (engine/cf.rs)
+  AutoMin → min(lowest, 0)
+  AutoMax → highest
 DataBar arm
-  lo = if lo > 0 { 0 } else { lo }   # every minimum pulled to 0
+  (removed: Lowest Value / Number / Percent minimums are honoured)

 read (xlsx/sheet_read.rs)
-  autoMin/autoMax → Min/Max; x14 rule gives only `gradient`
+  autoMin/autoMax → AutoMin/AutoMax; linked x14 rule also gives the bounds

 write (xlsx/sheet_write.rs)
   main section: Min|AutoMin → min, Max|AutoMax → max   # never autoMin here
-  x14 rule only for solid bars
+  x14 rule for solid bars OR Automatic bounds, with autoMin/autoMax

 home.conditionalFormat dataBar
-  default min/max: Min/Max
+  default min/max: AutoMin/AutoMax (Excel's Data Bars gallery); accepts {"type":"autoMin"|"autoMax"}

The issue's repro (`range.setValues` 10…20, then `home.conditionalFormat` `{"type":"dataBar"}`):

title: Analysis ToolPak: moving-average standard errors use a running sum (#1043)
author: TheRenegadeDev
body:
Fixes #1043

## Problem
With **Standard errors** on, `forecast_grid` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/analysis.rs`) re-added every squared residual in each window (`for j in s0..=i`). That's O(n × window) work, so a long series with a wide interval could freeze the app.

## Fix
Keep a running sum of squared residuals over the window: add the term that enters it and subtract the one that leaves it. Missing forecasts (the leading points, or any `None`) reset the sum and the run length, so every window that touches one is still `#N/A`, as before. The sum is clamped at 0 before `sqrt` so rounding in the subtraction can't produce a NaN.

## Tests
- New regression test `forecast_standard_errors_match_the_full_window_rescan`. It compares the new output with the old rescan code on an 11-point series with a gap in the middle, for windows 1–5 (tolerance 1e-12), and checks that the `#N/A`s around the gap are unchanged.
- `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo xtask assets`, `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask wasm` all pass.

## Note on `cargo xtask ci`
The clippy step (`-D warnings`) fails on two existing warnings in `crates/xlsx`, which this PR doesn't touch:
- `crates/xlsx/src/xls/mod.rs:273`: `if` can be collapsed into the outer `match`
- `crates/xlsx/src/tests/passthrough_tests.rs:480`: boolean expression can be simplified

Those two are the only warnings `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` reports; there are none in `crates/engine`.

title: Keep chart source range in step with inserted and deleted lines

title: XLSX theme: keep the major/minor East Asian (ea) and complex-script (cs) typefaces through open + save
author: midasdf
body:
## What this fixes

A workbook theme's `<a:fontScheme>` holds three typefaces per font — `<a:latin>`, `<a:ea>` (East Asian) and `<a:cs>` (complex script). Excel's Japanese themes set the `ea` one (游ゴシック, ＭＳ Ｐゴシック, …), and Japanese text in the workbook then uses that face. GridCraft's `Theme` had only `major_font`/`minor_font`, the reader read `majorFont/latin` and `minorFont/latin` only, and the writer emitted `<a:ea typeface=""/>` and `<a:cs typeface=""/>` **unconditionally** — so a plain open + save silently replaced a Japanese workbook's theme fonts with empty ones, with nowhere in the model to keep them. This is the same class of loss the repo tracks in the "style and sheet details that change on a plain open + save" work.

- `crates/model/src/style.rs`: `Theme` gains `major_font_ea`, `minor_font_ea`, `major_font_cs`, `minor_font_cs`, each `#[serde(default)]` and documented as `<a:ea>`/`<a:cs>`. `Theme::default()` still sets them empty (empty = the file did not set one), so GridCraft's own default theme is unchanged.
- `crates/xlsx/src/theme.rs`: a small `typeface(fs, font, kind)` helper (absent **or** empty → `None`), the reader fills all six typefaces, and the writer emits the stored values `esc_attr`-escaped. With the new fields empty the emitted `<a:fontScheme>` is **byte-identical to today's output**, so nothing changes for a workbook that has no `ea`/`cs` typefaces.
- No rendering change: the UI's font resolution does not consume `ea` yet, and wiring the East Asian theme face into cell rendering (so Japanese text uses the workbook's intended face) is a deliberate follow-up, not smuggled in here.

title: Keep large XLSX imports responsive and reduce eager recalculation
author: leewangwoo
body:
Opening a large XLSX currently copies inbox bytes through base64/JSON, eagerly recalculates all formulas, and blocks the interface while importing. This change reduces import allocations and keeps ordinary XLSX/XLSM opening responsive through cooperative preparation and atomic publication.

Changes:
- Pass inbox bytes directly to the engine, collect imported row indexes once per stored row, and retain large-sheet formula expressions lazily.

title: Ctrl+Alt+letter that types a character no longer triggers the Ctrl shortcut (#1530)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1530.

Windows reports AltGr, and user-defined hotkeys like the reporter's Ctrl+Alt+A for `ä`, as Ctrl+Alt plus a `Text` event. `keymap::dispatch` already treats such a key as text (the AltGr guard added for `~` on a German layout), but when it returned `false` the grid fell through to the plain Ctrl+letter fallback, `ribbon::shortcut`, which only checks `command`. So Ctrl+Alt+A ran Select All, Ctrl+Alt+U Underline, Ctrl+Alt+O Open, and so on.

- `keymap.rs`: the AltGr check moves into `altgr_text(ctx, m, mac)`; `dispatch` calls it as before (no behaviour change there).
- `grid.rs`: the Ctrl+letter fallback is skipped when `altgr_text` holds, so the `Text` event starts the cell edit with the typed character. Like the existing guard it applies only off macOS, where Option never arrives as Ctrl+Alt; plain Ctrl+letter (no Alt, or no text typed) still runs its shortcut.
- `docs/ui-parity.md`: the AltGr note now covers Ctrl+Alt+letter hotkeys and Ctrl+letter shortcuts; revision row added.

Test: `ctrl_alt_letter_that_typed_text_is_not_select_all` in `crates/ui-egui/tests/keyboard_shortcuts.rs` presses Ctrl+Alt+A with `Text("ä")` on B2 and checks that the selection stays on B2 and the cell editor holds `ä`. Without the fix the whole sheet is selected.

title: File open: HTML pages open as workbooks, also when saved as .xls (like Excel)
author: scorredoira
body:
Banks and web apps often export "Excel" files that are an HTML page saved as `.xls` (my bank's account statement is one). Excel opens them as a spreadsheet. GridCraft sniffed them as text and read them as CSV, so the sheet showed raw markup.

Now an HTML page opens as a one-sheet workbook, whatever its extension. `gridcraft_xlsx::is_html` checks the content: the first markup, past a BOM, whitespace, an XML declaration and comments, is a doctype, `<html>`, `<head>`, `<body>` or `<table>`. `gridcraft_xlsx::read_html` then reads:

- every table, one after the other from A1, with `colspan`/`rowspan` placed correctly and turned into merges
- `x:num` / `sdval` as the cell's number, and `x:str` as text
- bold from `<b>`, `<strong>`, `<th>` and `font-weight`
- column widths and row heights from `width`/`height` attributes, inline `style`, and simple `#id` / `.class` / `td.class` rules in `<style>` (this is how the bank file sizes its columns)
- text decoded like CSV (UTF-8, else Windows-1252), plus the Latin-1 named entities and `€`

The sheet is named after the file, as for CSV. The open dialogs (desktop and web) also list `.htm`/`.html`.

**Numbers and dates.** Excel reads the cell text in the system locale, so on a Spanish Mac `-17,35` is a number and `05/10/2026` is 5 October. GridCraft's input parsing is en-US only. Here the reader looks at the document's own cells: if they write comma decimals (`1.234,56`, `-17,35`) and/or day-first dates (`16/10/2026`), the whole page is read that way. Dates get `dd/mm/yyyy`, and grouped numbers keep `#,##0.00` through the normal en-US parse of the swapped text. Text that doesn't read as a value in that convention stays text (`15.768,89 EUR`). A page with no such evidence is read exactly as before. This differs from Excel, which follows the machine rather than the file. I think it's the more useful behaviour for a file format, but I'm happy to change it if you'd prefer it tied to the UI language.

title: editor: dismiss AutoComplete proposal on Delete as well as Backspace
author: dknalp
body:
## Problem

Fixes #1521 — the inline column AutoComplete suggestion (the ghost text appended while typing in a cell) was not dismissed when the user pressed **Delete**. Only **Backspace** was handled. This made the suggestion feel stuck and forced users to press Escape to get rid of it.

Excel's behaviour: either Backspace *or* Delete cancels the suggestion (because both are "undo typed text" actions from the user's perspective).

## Change

In `crates/ui-egui/src/formula_bar.rs`, the single-line guard:

```rust
if ed.completion.is_some() && i.consume_key(egui::Modifiers::NONE, Key::Backspace) {
```

was extended to also consume `Key::Delete`:

```rust
if ed.completion.is_some()
    && (i.consume_key(egui::Modifiers::NONE, Key::Backspace)
        || i.consume_key(egui::Modifiers::NONE, Key::Delete))
{
```

No other logic is changed. The fix is minimal and localised to the completion-dismiss block.

## Testing

- All existing `gridcraft-ui-egui` unit tests pass (`cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui --lib editor`).
- Manually verified: pressing Delete while an AutoComplete suggestion is visible now clears it, and pressing Backspace still works as before.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Pressing Backspace or Delete without modifiers now clears an active completion proposal.

title: Add Parquet table import and export
author: derechopiano
body:
Adds flat Parquet table import and export for #1703. Open puts field names in the first row and typed values below them; Save As, Export and CLI conversion write the active sheet, using the first used row as unique text headers. Imported files have no workbook save target, so normal Save cannot overwrite their source.

Uses Apache parquet-rs without Arrow. Normal file opens transfer their owned input allocation directly to the decoder, avoiding a second full-file copy; borrowed APIs remain available. Export uses Snappy and bounded row groups. Import preflights metadata/page allocation sizes and rejects unsupported nested/binary data, worksheet overflow and excessive decoded expansion with explicit errors. Exact decimals/large integers become text; date/time input gets spreadsheet formats. Data-only export limitations and native/web codec differences are documented in `docs/parquet.md`.

Validation: full local `cargo xtask ci` passed all eight stages on the committed tree (fmt, Clippy with warnings denied, workspace tests, assets, layers, WASM, parity and keytips). Synthetic tests cover typed values, nulls, compression, row groups, invalid input and command/UI integration. Paired three-run local measurements reduced peak import-process memory from 137.5 to 98.1 MiB for a 39.4 MiB synthetic file (about 29%). A private 1,000-row × 19-column sample imported in about 81 ms with 87.5 MiB peak process working set; no private data or binary fixtures are included. The export UI test passed in both themes; light/dark renders were also inspected.

Closes #1703.

title: Reject unknown value-field func in insert.pivotTable
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/pivot.rs:678 (func_param at :248)` (no existing issue): insert.pivotTable silently ignores an unknown value-field `func` and falls back to the default aggregation.

## Cause
insert.pivotTable parsed a values entry's `func` with `func_param(str_param(f, "func"))`. For an unknown name such as `stdev` or a typo, `func_param` returns `None`, and `add_to_area` read that as 'no function given'. The pivot was created with the default aggregation and the command reported success.

## Fix
When `func` is present but `func_param` doesn't recognise it, insert.pivotTable now returns `unknown function `…`` and creates no pivot. This matches how pivot.addField handles the same input.

## Verified
- Regression test `insert_pivot_table_rejects_unknown_func`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p gridcraft-engine --test pivot_unknown_func`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
func_param, its accepted names (no `stdev` alias is added), and the other func_param callers (pivot.addField and the other call sites).

title: xlsx: set appName="gridcraft" in fileVersion for new workbooks (fixes #1699)
author: dknalp
body:
## Problem

Fixes #1699 — new workbooks (and workbooks that weren't opened from an existing .xlsx) emitted no `fileVersion` element at all. OOXML parsers fall back to the default `appName="xl"`, making the file appear to have been created by Excel.

## Root cause

In `crates/xlsx/src/write.rs`, the `fileVersion` element is only written when a passthrough slot exists (i.e. the workbook was previously opened from an .xlsx that had one). For brand-new workbooks there is no passthrough, so nothing was written.

## Fix

A single change in `write.rs`: if `workbook_elements(wb, "fileVersion")` returns empty, emit a default `<fileVersion appName="gridcraft"/>`. Existing workbooks opened from .xlsx continue to preserve the `fileVersion` element as-is (including `lastEdited`, `rupBuild`, etc.), which is the correct behaviour for round-tripping.

## Test

Added `new_workbook_has_gridcraft_app_name` in `crates/xlsx/src/tests/roundtrip.rs`: writes a fresh `Workbook`, reads back the zip, and asserts `appName="gridcraft"` is present in `xl/workbook.xml`.

```
test tests::roundtrip::new_workbook_has_gridcraft_app_name ... ok
```

title: ribbon: truncate long workbook title with ellipsis (fixes #1558)
author: dknalp
body:
## Problem

Fixes #1558 — a workbook with a very long file name, or a narrow window, caused the centered title in the title bar to overflow and render on top of the AutoSave toggle, toolbar icons, and Share button.

## Root cause

The title was painted with a raw `painter.text(rect.center(), …)` call that has no maximum width constraint — the text grows unbounded and overlaps the side controls.

## Fix

Replace the unconstrained `painter.text()` call with a `LayoutJob` that sets:
- `wrap.max_width = (rect.width() - 600.0).max(80.0)` — leaves ~300 px on each side for controls (80 px floor so *some* title is always visible)
- `wrap.overflow_character = Some('…')` — truncates with an ellipsis rather than clipping hard

The galley is then painted centred using its measured size, so short titles look identical to before.

## Testing

- `cargo check -p gridcraft-ui-egui` — clean
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui --lib` — 92 tests, all pass

title: Sheet protection: obey the Sort and Use AutoFilter boxes
author: Hamza0101
body:
Two of Protect Sheet's tick boxes were stored in the file and written back, but never consulted. A protected sheet could still be sorted and filtered.

## What I measured

Protecting a sheet with nothing ticked — which is what Excel's dialog opens with — and then trying each action, on `main` @ f1894c6:

| action | before | should be |
|---|---|---|
| `cell.set` on a locked cell | refused | refused |
| insert rows / columns | refused | refused |
| delete rows / columns | refused | refused |
| **sort (A‑Z, Z‑A, Sort…)** | **allowed** | refused |
| **filter (AutoFilter, Filter Column)** | **allowed** | refused |

`SheetProtection` carries eleven permissions. `format_cells` is checked in `apply_style`, and locked-cell edits are caught by `check_protection` after any command. `sort` and `autofilter` had no reader at all outside `sheet_read.rs` / `sheet_write.rs` and a round-trip test, so they only ever travelled through the file.

An AutoFilter changes no cell's contents, so the locked-cell guard could never have caught it: on a protected sheet, Ctrl+Shift+L worked regardless.

## The change

`refuse_unless_allowed` beside `locked_cell_error` in `cmd/mod.rs`, and three call sites: `do_sort` (which both the Sort… dialog and the A‑Z / Z‑A buttons come through), `toggle_filter`, and `filter_by`.

## Where the tick box actually decides, which is the interesting part

Sorting **locked** cells was already refused — not by the permission but by `check_protection`, because a sort moves values between locked cells. That matches Excel, whose dialog help says users cannot sort ranges containing locked cells on a protected worksheet *regardless of this setting*. So:

- for a range left **locked**, sorting is refused either way, before and after this change;
- for a range that has been **unlocked** (Home ▸ Format ▸ Lock Cell off, the usual way to leave some cells editable on a protected sheet), the Sort box is what decides — and that is the case this fixes;
- for an **AutoFilter**, …

title: Fonts: probe ChromeOS's /usr/share/fonts/chromeos for script fallbacks (fixes #1762)
author: dantebertuzzi
body:
Fixes #1762.

On ChromeOS's Linux container (Crostini), `cros-host-fonts` mounts the host's fonts under `/usr/share/fonts/chromeos/` (`noto/`, `notocjk/`, `crosextra/`). None of the fixed Linux path lists in `crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs` reached that folder, so Thai, Hebrew, CJK and Noto Sans Symbols 2 fell back to egui's Latin-only faces and drew tofu even with the fonts installed. The UI and cell roles missed Noto Sans and Carlito for the same reason.

## Change
- `thai()`, `hebrew()`, `symbols_more()`: probe `/usr/share/fonts/chromeos/noto`.
- `LINUX_CJK_DIRS`: add `/usr/share/fonts/chromeos/notocjk`.
- `candidates()` (UI, cell, serif, mono roles): add `/usr/share/fonts/chromeos` to `lin`, which covers `noto/NotoSans-*.ttf` and `crosextra/Carlito-*.ttf`.
- New test `chromeos_font_layout_is_probed`: a structural check that every list probes the Crostini layout. `fallback_covers_its_script` skips a script whose candidates are absent, so it can't catch a missing path on CI.

The `noto/` path comes from the report. `notocjk/` and `crosextra/` assume Crostini keeps the ChromeOS host's own font folder names. I haven't tested this on a ChromeOS machine.

## Checks
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui --lib theme::` (13 passed)

author: dantebertuzzi

title: Import classic dBASE III/IV tables safely
author: derechopiano
body:
Opening a `.dbf` currently falls through to the delimited-text reader. Import classic dBASE III/IV tables through File > Open and `file.open` instead, with field names in the first row and typed data beneath them.

The reader handles character, numeric/float, logical and date fields, declared OEM/Windows encodings, blanks and deleted records. High-precision numbers and unrepresentable dates are preserved as text with warnings. Header/record bounds and decoded-work limits reject malformed or oversized inputs. Memo fields and unsupported dialects fail explicitly; companion files are never accessed.

Imports have no DBF save target, and DBF export is refused, so ordinary Save cannot overwrite the source. Save As XLSX/CSV uses the existing export paths. One dependency, MIT-licensed `yore`, provides legacy encoding tables with no transitive dependencies.

Validation:
- Seven parser tests with original byte-level synthetic fixtures.
- Four engine tests: import, XLSX round-trip, source-preserving Save, failed-import atomicity and content detection.
- Full required `cargo xtask ci`: passed all eight stages (fmt, clippy, workspace tests, assets, layers, wasm, parity and keytips).

No real-world DBF corpus or external Excel comparison was performed. dBASE II/7, Visual FoxPro-specific layouts and memo companions are outside this change; details are in `docs/dbf.md`.

Fixes #1322.

title: Draw: Ink to Shape mode, ported from WordCraft's recogniser
author: alosslessdev
body:
Fixes #1775.

Ink to Shape is a before-drawing mode, and the recognition is now a **port of WordCraft's geometric recogniser** (`storytold/wordcraft`, `crates/engine/src/cmd/ink_shape.rs`, from PRs #408 and #1520; same MIT/Apache-2.0 licences) instead of a bespoke classifier.

## What changed

- **Ported recogniser** (`crates/engine/src/cmd/ink_shape.rs`): WordCraft's `recognise()` is unchanged — line kept to the chord between its ends, arrow from a shaft plus two barbs drawn in one stroke, ellipse by the normalised-radius RMS of the inscribed ellipse, polygon from Ramer–Douglas–Peucker corners (3–8), upright quads as rectangles, and square/circle snapping. Only the `MAX_POINTS` import and the module doc were adapted; WordCraft's own test suite came with it (9 tests).
- **Mode** (`Session::ink_to_shape`, `draw.inkToShape {on}`): while on, `draw.stroke` converts each completed stroke. `{id}` and `{}` still convert one stroke for the control channel, CLI and MCP; one undo step per conversion. The UI highlights the button while the mode is on.
- **GridCraft mapping** (`cmd/draw.rs`): the recogniser's `InkShape` is mapped onto GridCraft's shape model — line, arrow, rectangle/square, ellipse/circle, triangle/right triangle, and 4-corner polygons via the corner tests (diamond/parallelogram/trapezoid/rectangle); 5- and 6-corner polygons as the pentagon/hexagon presets. 7–8-corner polygons stay ink because GridCraft has no freeform preset (WordCraft stores them as freeform shapes).
- **Preset kinds / XLSX / renderers**: carried over from the previous revision of this PR — Diamond, Parallelogram, Trapezoid, Pentagon, Hexagon, RightTriangle, BlockArrow, ArrowDouble, with DrawingML presets (`diamond`, `parallelogram`, `trapezoid`, `pentagon`, `hexagon`, `rtTriangle`, `rightArrow`, `leftRightArrow`), screen/PDF rendering, and round-trip tests.

title: Draw: Action Pen handwriting recognition
author: alosslessdev
body:
Fixes #1777.

Draw ▸ **Action Pen**: handwriting written in the grid is recognized and entered as typed cell data, as Excel's Action Pen documents it ("Start writing in the cells; your handwriting is automatically converted into text").

## What changed

- **Command surface** (`crates/engine/src/cmd/draw.rs`):
  - `draw.actionPen {on?: bool}` toggles the tool, exactly like `draw.pen`.
  - `draw.inkToText {points, cell?, language?}` sends the stroke to the registered recognizer and enters the result through `cell.set`, so numbers and dates become typed values as if keyed. No recognizer, empty recognition and malformed points are clear errors, never panics; one undo step per entry.
- **Recognizer seam** (`crates/engine/src/handwriting.rs`): a `HandwritingRecognizer` trait stored on `Session`. The engine never links a platform service, so wasm, macOS, Linux and headless builds compile unchanged and answer "handwriting recognition is not available on this platform".
- **Windows implementation** (`apps/gridcraft/src/handwriting.rs`): Windows Ink (`Windows.UI.Input.Inking`) — the same OS handwriting service Excel documents as its offline fallback. Strokes are scaled to pen size, turned into timestamped `InkPoint`s, recognized by `InkRecognizerContainer`, and the first candidate is returned. The recognizer runs on a worker thread: blocking the UI thread on the async operation deadlocks because it is an STA (winit initializes OLE); the wait is bounded to 10 s. The recognizer for the requested language (English, Spanish) is selected when the service has one.
- **UI** (`crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs`, `ribbon.rs`): **Action Pen** on the Draw tab. With the tool on, a stroke is captured like the pen and, on release, recognized into the cell where the stroke starts; nothing is stored as ink.

No Office component, cloud service or bundled model is involved: the recognizer comes from the platform, and the text enters through the normal cell input path.

## Not in this PR (follow-ups)…

title: Export active-sheet values as dBASE III tables
author: derechopiano
body:
Adds Save As DBF for exchanging active-sheet data with dBASE-compatible software. The first used row supplies field names; remaining rows become typed character, numeric, logical or date records. Formula results are exported as values.

Depends on #1771 for DBF import. The export-only comparison is https://github.com/derechopiano/gridcraft/compare/feat/dbf-1322...feat/dbf-export. This is a separate follow-up, not schema-preserving editing of an existing database.

The writer checks names, homogeneous types, Windows-1252 encoding, field/record widths, numeric precision and calendar dates. Unsupported values fail before writing a file. Work, decoded text and output size are bounded; the export remains within the reader's limits. Save As preserves the workbook's original path and unsaved state. Native picker and browser download paths are covered.

Validation:
- Nine writer tests plus the existing reader tests: typed round-trips, exact byte layout, blank fields, both date systems, encoding, precision and bounds.
- Engine tests for cached formula results, preserving the source workbook, refusing invalid export without creating/replacing a file, and classifying calendar, literal, time-only and conditional number formats.
- Save As UI test: desktop light/dark themes and browser download, with inspected offscreen renders.
- A synthetic file generated by the actual desktop Save As flow was opened in Excel 16.0.20326.20232 x64; expected fields and values loaded with no repair/format warning.
- Full required `cargo xtask ci`: all eight stages passed (fmt, Clippy, workspace tests, assets, layers, WASM, parity and keytips). The networking test requires local loopback access, so the successful full run was outside the agent sandbox.

Limits and data-only semantics are documented in `docs/dbf.md`. No real-world DBF corpus was tested. No Excel-authored files or Office screenshots are included.

Related to #1322.

title: CSV/TSV: Shift-JIS (CP932) and UTF-8 with BOM import and export
author: midasdf
body:
## What this adds

Japanese users exchange CSV with Excel, and Excel on Windows writes (and expects) **Shift-JIS (CP932)**, usually without a BOM. GridCraft decoded anything that wasn't UTF-8/UTF-16 as **Windows-1252** — so a Shift-JIS CSV opened as mojibake — and always wrote UTF-8 **without** a BOM, which Japanese Excel opens as mojibake. There was no way to choose an encoding on open or save.

- **`CsvEncoding`** (`Auto`, `Utf8`, `Utf8Bom`, `ShiftJis`, `Windows1252`) in `crates/model`, used by `CsvOptions` and carried on the workbook (`Workbook::csv_encoding`, mirroring `csv_delimiter`: a plain save writes back the encoding the file was opened with). Spellings: `auto|utf-8|utf-8-bom|shift_jis|windows-1252`, with `cp932` as an alias; JSON names lowercase; `Default = Auto`; `None` on the workbook means UTF-8, so existing workbooks and JSON are unchanged.
- **Import**: `Auto` keeps today's contract — UTF-8/UTF-16 BOMs, then UTF-8, then **Shift-JIS only when it is convincing**: a clean CP932 decode that holds hiragana or full-width katakana, or (no kana) one whose non-ASCII bytes are at least 80% double-byte pairs and whose pairs outnumber Windows-1252 "character + letter" readings — so a kanji-only Japanese address column detects while accented or smart-quoted Western text does not — and no private-use characters, else the existing Windows-1252 fallback. Explicit values force a code page; `Utf8` on Shift-JIS bytes is deliberately lossy (`U+FFFD`, no silent fallback). The pre-existing assertions (`decode_text(&[0x80,b'a',0xE9]) == "€aé"`) are unchanged.
- **Export**: `Utf8` (the default, byte-identical to before), `Utf8Bom` (Excel detects UTF-8), `ShiftJis` and `Windows1252`. `write_csv`/`write_csv_limited` stay UTF-8 wrappers; `write_csv_encoded` is the new entry point.
- **Unmappable characters become `?`**, as Word and Excel write them when saving to a legacy code page — never encoding_rs' default HTML numeric reference (`😀`), which would corrupt a CSV fie…

title: Sheet protection: a line is locked only by a format it has
author: Hamza0101
body:
Closes #1766, though not for the reason that issue gives — see below.

## The bug

On a protected sheet, ticking **Delete rows** or **Delete columns** in Review ▸ Protect Sheet had no effect: the deletion was still refused. `check_lines_protection` grants the permission and then checks whether the lines being deleted are locked:

```rust
if (at..=end).any(|i| locked(infos.get(&i).and_then(|x| x.style).unwrap_or_default())) {
    return Err(refuse());
}
```

A row or column that carries no format of its own has `style == None`, so `unwrap_or_default()` handed the check `StyleId::default()` — and that style is locked, as cells are by default. Measured:

```
locked(StyleId::default())        = true
row 0 has an explicit style      = false
```

So every line without its own format counted as locked and the delete was refused however the permission was set. Since most rows carry no format, the permission could essentially never be used.

It also left the next check unreachable:

```rust
if sh.cells.iter_range(block).any(|(_, cell)| locked(cell.style)) {
```

That is the check that should decide — it looks at the cells actually in the block — and it never ran, because the line-level check had already refused.

The fix is that a line is only locked by a format it actually has; one with none is judged by its cells.

## Measured, before and after

With three values in A1:A3 and the sheet protected:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Delete rows granted, cells unlocked | refused | **the row goes, rows below move up** |
| Delete rows not granted | refused | refused |
| granted, but the cells are locked | refused | refused (the cell scan now decides) |
| granted, and the row has a locked format | refused | refused (the line check, doing its job) |
| unprotected sheet | works | works |

## Correcting my own issue

#1766 says the cause is `check_protection`, the post-hoc guard in `cmd/mod.rs` that refuses an edit of a locked cell's contents, firing before `delete_rows` is cons…

title: Refuse a multi-area target instead of silently acting on one area
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
A multi-area target given to a single-block command was silently reduced to one area: `target_range()` took `target_ranges().first()`, and `block()`'s no-`range` fallback took the selection's last area. `range.setValues` with `"A1:B1,C2:D2"` reported `{"cells": 4}` while writing into `A1:B2` and dropping the second area; the same shape silently truncated the fills, `autoFill`/`fillSeries`/`flashFill`, the sort/filter/removeDuplicates/subtotal family and `textToColumns` on their explicit-`range` paths, `insert.table`/`home.formatAsTable`, `sheet.read`, `pageLayout.printArea`, `insertCells`/`deleteCells`, `autoSum`, `createFromSelection`, `spelling` and `fromTableRange`.

They now refuse the target with the message `edit.copy` already shows for unlined-up areas ("This action won't work on multiple selections."), so a multi-area call fails loudly instead of acting on a fragment. Single-area calls — and calls with no target at all — behave exactly as before. Commands that already walk every area (`range.fill`, the style/border/clear/merge family, conditional formats, `data.validation`) are untouched, and chart code is left to #1653.

Four new tests (multi-area refused by `range.setValues`, `printArea` and `textToColumns`, and by `insert.table` through a Ctrl multi-area selection) fail on `main` and pass here; each also pins that the refused call left no partial effect behind and that the single-area path still works.

One corner left as-is, noted for the record: the no-`range` fallbacks of `data.sort`/`filter`/`removeDuplicates`/`subtotal` and `autoSum` resolve through their own `selection.current()` paths rather than `target_range()`, so a Ctrl multi-area selection still acts on its last area there — same class, happy to follow up if the maintainers want it.

title: Windows: 100% zoom matches Excel, cell text no longer bold in dark mode
author: ARMultimediait
body:
On Windows, GridCraft's 100% zoom looks like Excel's 80%, and in dark mode the cell text looks bold. Two small fixes in `ui-egui`.

## 1. Draw sheets 1:1 on Windows and Linux (`grid.rs`)

`DISPLAY_SCALE` draws one 96-dpi sheet pixel at 0.8 points on every platform. That matches Excel for Mac, but Excel for Windows draws sheet pixels 1:1 at 100% zoom: a default row is 20 px, a default column 64 px, and 11 pt Calibri is 14.7 px. On a Windows display at 100% scaling, GridCraft at 100% therefore showed 16 px rows, 51 px columns and 11.7 px cell text, the same as Excel at 80%.

`DISPLAY_SCALE` is now 1.0 on Windows and Linux. macOS and the web build keep 0.8, so nothing changes there. Every consumer already goes through the constant (headers and outline fonts divide by it), so this is the only change.

## 2. Keep cell text from looking bold in dark mode (`theme.rs`)

egui's dark visuals use the `2c − c²` coverage-to-alpha curve, which thickens glyph edges for light-on-dark text. The glyph atlas has one curve for all text, and the cells stay white in both themes, so in dark mode the black cell text looked bold. Both themes now use the light-mode curve. The ribbon's light text gets slightly thinner but stays legible.

## Testing

- `cargo xtask ci` passes on Windows 11. On a Windows checkout with `core.autocrlf=true`,
  `parity` and `keytips` report their generated files as out of date only because Git checked
  them out with CRLF; regenerating them changes no content, and the gate then passes.
- Checked side by side in the running app, on a 2560×1440 display at 100% Windows scaling: with the `sales` sample at 100%, rows are 20 px and columns 64 px, and the dark-mode cell text no longer looks bold.

title: Calc: a LAMBDA that calls itself without end answers #NUM! instead of overflowing the stack
author: dotCooCoo
body:
Fixes #1662.

As the issue shows on Windows, `=LET(f,LAMBDA(g,x,g(g,x)),f(f,1))` overflowed the stack and closed GridCraft, both in a cell and when a workbook holding it was opened, and a defined name `LOOP` = `=LAMBDA(n,LOOP(n))` used as `=LOOP(1)` overflowed the stack too. iluebbe found the cause and measured it.

The evaluator stopped at `MAX_DEPTH` (400) nested `eval` calls. A LAMBDA call takes one of those levels but several stack frames (`eval`, `eval_inner`, `call`, `builtin`, `apply_lambda`, `call_lambda_values`), and on the 1 MiB Windows main thread 400 such levels need more stack than the thread has. The `catch_unwind` in `Session::execute` catches panics only, so the stack overflow ended the process.

The evaluator now counts the LAMBDA calls a formula has in progress, in `call_lambda_values`, which direct calls, defined names and the MAP, REDUCE, SCAN, BYROW, BYCOL and MAKEARRAY helpers all go through, and the 141st call answers `#NUM!`. The count does not depend on frame sizes, so a formula stops at the same call in debug and release builds on macOS and Windows. 140 is 8 calls above the 132 calls that the countdown `F(F,131)` from #917 has in progress. Forms that use fewer than three levels per call now stop at 140 calls instead of at the 400-level limit: `IF(n=0,0,me(me,n-1))` reaches 139 instead of 197, and the MAP form 69 instead of 79. `eval` keeps a stack check as a guard only: it records the stack position at a formula's outermost `eval` (the address of a local variable, in safe code) and answers `#NUM!` once the formula has used 896 KiB below it. A cell that another formula computes on demand gets its own evaluator and its own call count, and shares the stack budget of the outermost formula. When a nested formula runs out of that budget, it is calculated again from the top, as a formula needed at the 64-level nesting limit is, so its value does not depend on the order cells are calculated in. The three-cell chains that overflowed in iluebbe's Win…

title: #1447: TRUE/FALSE or error values in a pivot source no longer make the file unopenable
author: Higgs32584
body:
Refs storytold/GridCraft#1447 (item 1 only; items 2–7 are in #1680–#1685).

## Problem
A pivot whose source range has a TRUE/FALSE or error column (used in the pivot or not) is written with `containsString="0"` on that cache field. Excel counts booleans and errors as strings in `<sharedItems>`, so it can't open the file. Booleans and errors were also counted as separate kinds for `containsMixedTypes`.

## Fix
`crates/xlsx/src/pivot.rs`: new `Stats::strings()` = text or boolean or error; `kinds()` = strings + numbers. `containsString="0"` is written only without strings, `containsSemiMixedTypes="0"` only without strings and blanks. This matches the "Excel writes" column of the table in the issue (same approach as the fix in the closed #1538). Date-grouped fields are untouched (item 4 is #1681).

## Test
`pivot_tests::boolean_and_error_cache_flags_match_excel`: six columns (BoolOnly, NumBool, ErrOnly, NumErr, TextBool, BoolBlank); each `<sharedItems>` start tag equals the issue's "Excel writes" column, and the file reads back with its pivot and no pivot warnings. Fails on `main`, passes with the fix. `cargo test -p gridcraft-xlsx --lib -- pivot` (12 tests) and `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-xlsx --all-targets -D warnings` pass. Not re-checked in Excel itself.

title: Charts: add Pareto charts
author: alosslessdev
body:
## Summary

Adds Excel's **Pareto** chart as a first-class chart kind: descending columns plus a cumulative-percentage line on a secondary 0–100% axis. Closes #1819.

Behaviour follows Microsoft's [Create a Pareto chart](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/excel/create-a-pareto-chart) page and an Excel 365 observation of a Pareto chart saved to `.xlsx`:

- Equal categories are grouped and their values summed before sorting.
- Bars are sorted largest first (stable for ties).
- Numeric-only data is binned like a histogram (`cx:binning intervalClosed="r"`), while category data uses `cx:aggregation`.
- The cumulative line is drawn on a secondary percentage axis (`min="0" max="1"`, `units unit="percentage"`).
- No legend by default; data labels and gridlines are honoured.
- XLSX uses a chartex part with `clusteredColumn` + `paretoLine` series, matching Excel's structure. Extra Pareto series are written hidden, as Excel does.

- `ChartKind::Pareto` in the model.

- Pareto and `Cumulative %` legend labels translated in es, ja, zh, ko, ru, pt, de, cs, fr and sr; the renderer takes the legend label from the UI layer.
- chartex read/write: `paretoLine` is read back as Pareto instead of being dropped; numeric data writes binning.

title: Charts: draw every doughnut series as a ring
author: alosslessdev
body:
## Summary

Implements the doughnut primitives needed for Excel parity, and for radial-bar charts built from doughnuts. Closes #1823.

Excel has no native radial-bar chart; users build one from a doughnut/multilayer doughnut (one ring per helper series, hidden gap slices). GridCraft already had the Doughnut kind, but its renderer only drew the first series, so those templates lost every ring after the first.

Observed in Excel 365 and checked against Microsoft's [pie/doughnut](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/excel/add-a-pie-chart) page:

- Every data series is one concentric ring; the **first series is outermost**.
- The hole size is 10–90% of the plot radius, default **75%** for new charts and Excel files.
- The first slice angle is 0–359°, default **0°**.
- Excel's default `c:varyColors=1` colours a doughnut by category: every ring repeats the same category colours and the legend names categories. With `c:varyColors=0` the legend names series instead (right-hand image below); GridCraft does not model that setting, so it follows Excel's default and keeps the category legend.
- `c:holeSize` and `c:firstSliceAng` round-trip through XLSX.

![Excel 365 doughnut legend: default vary-by-category colours names categories; vary-by-categories off names series](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f4b094db-3683-472b-a42f-a6913060a408)

## Implementation

- `Chart` gains `hole_size` (serde default **50** for documents saved before the field existed) and `first_slice_angle` (serde default 0). New charts and XLSX imports set 75 explicitly, so existing workbooks keep their old look.
- Renderer: all series as rings (first outermost), per-point colours, hole size, first slice angle, data labels. Pie also honours the first slice angle. A wedge normalizes its start into [0, TAU) before splitting at 12 o'clock, so slices rotated past 360° cover their own sweep without drawing over their neighbours.
- XLSX read/write: `c:holeSize` and `c:firstSliceAng`; new/imported charts u…

title: Expand a single-column sort to the adjacent data so rows stay together (#1825)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1825.

When the selection is one column wide (part of a column, or the whole column) and that column sits inside a wider block of data, Sort A to Z, Sort Z to A and Custom Sort sorted that column alone. The neighbouring columns stayed where they were, so the rows got mixed up. A single selected cell was already fine, because it sorts the current region.

Now a one-column selection with no explicit `range` grows to its current region before the sort, the same as choosing Excel's "Expand the selection". The sort key is still the selected column. It stays as it was when:
- an explicit `range` is passed (programmatic calls sort exactly what they ask for),
- the selection is inside a table (the table path already sorts the table's data),
- the region does not hold the whole selection, or has no other columns,
- Custom Sort runs by columns (left to right).

The issue asks for Excel's Sort Warning dialog. This PR does not add that dialog. It takes Excel's default answer, "Expand the selection", so the data can no longer be scrambled by accident. If you want the dialog too (with "Continue with the current selection"), it can go on top of this as a follow-up.

Test: `sorting_a_selected_column_expands_to_the_adjacent_data` runs Sort Z to A and Custom Sort on `B2:B4` and on `B:B` next to a name column, and checks that each name stays with its score. It fails on main.

title: PivotTable: support in-cell header renaming and protect report cells (fixes #1729)
author: sam-f-gh
body:
### Summary

Implements Excel parity for PivotTable in-cell header renaming, task pane synchronization, and report data cell protection:

1. **Value Field Headers** (e.g. `"Sum of Sales"`):
   - Typing directly into a value header cell updates the custom name of that value field (`pt.values[i].name`), re-renders the report, and synchronizes the new name directly to the PivotTable Fields task pane.
   - Preserves user input whitespace so users can use Excel's common convention of adding a trailing space (e.g. `"Sales "`) to name a value header identically to an underlying source column.
   - Validations:
     - Exact match with an underlying source column name or duplicate name of another value field is rejected with:
       `"PivotTable field name already exists."`
     - Empty string is rejected with:
       `"The name isn't valid."`
     - A single space (`" "`) is accepted to make the header appear blank.

2. **Axis Header Captions** (`"Row Labels"` / `"Column Labels"`):
   - Typing directly into `"Row Labels"` or `"Column Labels"` updates `pt.row_header_caption` / `pt.col_header_caption`.
   - Supports empty string `""` or `" "` to clear or blank out the axis label.
   - Persists and round-trips through `.xlsx` OpenXML attributes (`rowHeaderCaption` and `colHeaderCaption`).

3. **Data Cell Protection**:
   - Direct edits to calculated body cells, subtotal cells, grand total cells, or bulk mutations (range fill, range set values, paste, autofill, fill series) intersecting PivotTable report cells are blocked with Excel's error message:
     `"Cannot change part of a PivotTable report."`

4. **Undo/Redo**:
   - Full undo and redo support for in-cell renames and axis caption edits.

Fixes #1729

title: #1603: column width conversions take the Normal font's digit width
author: HyakoV3
body:
Part of #1603: step 1 of 3, with no change in behaviour. The next steps (deriving the digit width from the workbook's Normal font, then using it for picture anchors) build on this and are separate PRs, so this one does not close the issue.

A stored column width counts characters of the Normal font's widest digit, so its width in pixels depends on that digit's width (MDW). `col_width_to_px` and `px_to_col_width` had a fixed 7 px (Calibri 11). They now take `mdw`, and the readers (`sheet_read`, `.xls`) and the writer pass `DEFAULT_MDW = 7`. Checked: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p gridcraft-xlsx`. I did not run `cargo xtask ci`.

Not settled here: the digit width of other fonts (the Malgun Gothic 12 = 9 px figure comes from the issue, not from a public source), and the second column of the issue's measurements (9.08 → 84.7 px), which an integer digit width of 9 does not reproduce (82 px).

title: audit: add gridcraft-cli audit for hidden-information reporting
author: ejbarraza
body:
Implements #1829 (audit only — sanitize is a follow-up).

`gridcraft-cli audit <file>` scans the raw OPC package bytes and reports hidden information as machine-readable JSON with stable finding IDs, exiting nonzero when findings exist (CI-gate usable).

v1 finding classes: hidden rows/columns (reported as A1 ranges), hidden and veryHidden sheets, hidden defined names, external workbook links, comment authors (including threaded comments resolved through the persons part), creator/last-modified-by in core/app properties, pivot caches carrying source data, active content visibility (VBA project, embedded OLE — reported, never blocked), and orphan package parts.

- New `gridcraft-audit` crate (Layer 2): scans raw package bytes, never the document model (the model drops unmodeled parts on round-trip, so model-based auditing would miss things); fail-closed on malformed input, hostile-input caps, deterministic output order, never-crash lints.
- 16 golden tests on synthetic fixtures built from ECMA-376 (no Excel-produced files committed, per the clean-room rule).
- Exit codes: 0 = clean, 1 = findings present, 2 = audit could not run.
- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy, tests, assets, layers, wasm green.

Also includes my contributor entry in `contributors/people.toml` (`sync_github_name = true`).

title: Hide blank and text rows for numeric ordering custom filters
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/data.rs:550 (custom_ok, used from apply_filter at :623)` (no existing issue): Custom AutoFilter 'is less than' / 'less than or equal' keeps blank rows visible.

## Cause
`custom_ok` only compared numerically when both the cell and the criterion were numbers. Otherwise it fell back to `compare_text`. An empty cell displays as "", which sorts before "5", so `<` and `<=` with a numeric criterion kept blank rows visible. Text cells were matched the same way.

## Fix
When the criterion is numeric and the cell is not a number, `custom_ok` now never matches the ordering operators `<`, `<=`, `>` and `>=`. Only numeric cells can pass those filters, as in Excel. The regression test covers `<` and `<=` on a column with a blank cell and a text cell.

## Verified
- Regression test `less_than_numeric_criterion_hides_blank_and_text_rows`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p gridcraft-engine --test custom_filter_blanks`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`=` and `<>` and the text operators (`contains`, `beginsWith`, wildcards) behave as before. Non-numeric criteria still use text comparison.
