title: fix(xlsx): read and write PivotTable grand totals in Excel's direction
author: neilcawse
body:
A PivotTable saved by Excel with only one grand total opened with the other one. `rowGrandTotals` was read into `grand_totals_rows`, which the model defines as the Grand Total *column* ("On for Rows"), and `colGrandTotals` into the Grand Total row. The writer used the same swapped mapping, so a GridCraft round trip hid the bug.

Split out of #722, as requested in review.

## What changed

- `crates/xlsx/src/pivot.rs`: `rowGrandTotals` now maps to `grand_totals_cols` (the Grand Total row under the report) and `colGrandTotals` to `grand_totals_rows` (the Grand Total column at its right), when reading and when writing. The model, the engine and the `pivot.*` commands are unchanged; they already used the meanings documented in `crates/model/src/features.rs`.
- `docs/file-format-parity.md`: header and revision-history row.

## Evidence

Two files from public test suites, both last saved by Excel (`docProps/app.xml`: "Microsoft Excel Online" 16.0300 and "Microsoft Excel" 15.0300):

| File | Attribute | Excel's saved report | Refresh on main | Refresh with this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| LibreOffice `sc/qa/unit/data/xlsx/pivot/Pivot2_Row_Subtotals.xlsx` (row fields only) | `rowGrandTotals="0"` | no Grand Total row | adds a "Grand Total" row (600) | no Grand Total row |
| ClosedXML `TemplateWithTableSourcePivotTables.xlsx`, pivotTable5 on StressedAssetsPivot (row and column fields) | `colGrandTotals="0"` | Grand Total row, no Grand Total column | "Total Sum of …" columns, no Grand Total row | Grand Total row, no Grand Total column |

A scan of 3,075 corpus files saved by Excel found 20 PivotTables with exactly one of the two attributes off. In 14 of them the saved cells show the expected grand total: 12 have a Grand Total row and 2 a Grand Total column. All 14 match this mapping and none matches the old one. The other 6 show no grand total at all, because the axis that would carry it has no field, so they don't tell the two mappings apart.

title: Conditional formatting: colour-scale formula stops keep their kind, and out-of-order thresholds draw as Excel (fixes #1848)
author: zyzabruh
body:
Fixes #1848 (both cases measured in the issue).

## What

**A colour-scale stop whose value is a formula keeps its kind.** A non-numeric `cfvo` `val` used to fall back to `CfValueKind::Formula`, so a percent, percentile or number stop holding a formula (e.g. `=$Z$1*10`) was read as a plain formula stop, its raw result taken as the threshold instead of a percent/percentile, and written back as `type="formula"` — after a GridCraft save Excel then showed a changed rule.

- `CfValueKind` gains `FormulaNumber`, `FormulaPercent` and `FormulaPercentile`.
- The reader keeps the stop's `type` for a non-numeric `val`; the writer writes `num`, `percent` or `percentile` back (2006 and x14 `cfvo`).
- `threshold` evaluates the formula and reads the result as that stop's kind (a percent of the span, a percentile of the values).
- A **Percentile** stop's formula counts as a percentile only when it is a single cell reference (`=$Z$10`, `Sheet1!$A$1`); any computed formula (`=$Z$1*10`, `=($Z$10)`, `=MAX($Z$10)`) gives the threshold 0, the number, as Excel reads it.
- `home.conditionalFormat` accepts a formula in a typed stop without losing the type. That covers the data bar's `min`/`max` on `main`; colour-scale `stops` arrive with #1822.
- A typed stop's formula now goes through the same validation as a formula stop (#1999): `{"type": "num", "value": "1+"}` is refused instead of being written as `<cfvo type="num" val="1+"/>`, which Excel cannot open, not even with repair.

**Out-of-order thresholds draw as Excel does.** A colour scale stored with its thresholds not ascending now draws them sorted, with the colours kept in stop order (the first stop's colour at the lowest threshold). Equal thresholds follow the measured rule: a value at or above the highest takes the last colour, otherwise one at or below the lowest takes the first. So `2 / 2 / 8` gives the first colour at 2, and `2 / 8 / 8` and `8 / 8` give the later one.

title: Use the shared Region parser for DATEVALUE/TIMEVALUE and recalculation
author: addibbi
body:
DMY text such as `13/01/2026` produces `#VALUE!` in `DATEVALUE` under MDY interpretation; a dependent month grouping can then lose January on PivotTable refresh. Ambiguous `02/01/2026` also needs the selected Region to distinguish January 2 from February 1.

title: Allow Change Data Source to repair an invalid PivotTable source
author: addibbi
body:
When a PivotTable's existing source becomes invalid under GridCraft's current validation (an unused header is cleared or its defined name is deleted), `pivot.changeSource` rejects that old source before it can apply a valid replacement. Validate and render against the explicitly supplied replacement so the existing report can be repaired.

Missing, empty or whitespace-only `source` / `range` replacements are rejected instead of using the active selection. The change remains one undoable edit, retains selected fields found in the replacement, and preserves invalid-header, sheet-protection and occupied-cell checks with rollback on failure. Sources are not automatically trimmed.

Aligned with upstream `main` at `45f5ab18e4e57bf50ee88d2526deb4b87c5b24cb`, adapting the repair helpers to the upstream `fields.rs` / `layout.rs` command modules, while retaining shared-workbook window handling and the PivotTable Enable show details option. The desktop-theme compatibility fix is already upstream and contributes no diff here.

### Compatibility scope

The cleared-unused-header example describes GridCraft's existing validation, not a claim about every Excel entry point. [The reviewer's Excel desktop COM report](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/pull/1887#issuecomment-6459053459) accepted such a header as `Field5`; Excel's Change Data Source dialog was not measured. The same report rejected empty/whitespace replacements and allowed a valid replacement after deleting a source name. These are attributed observations, not Excel tests run by us. This update clarifies the guide and roadmap without weakening replacement validation, protection, occupied-cell or undo/rollback checks.

title: Zoom around the pointer on Ctrl+wheel instead of the top-left corner (#1851)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1851.

Ctrl+wheel and trackpad pinch zoom (both arrive as egui's `zoom_delta`) kept the scroll offset as it was, so the view shrank or grew towards the top-left corner of the sheet. Now the sheet point under the pointer stays under it.

How it works (`crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs`):
- When the wheel zoom sets a new percentage (each glide frame, or the whole step at once with animations off), it records a `ZoomAnchor` in the `WheelZoom` state: the pointer's logical position and the sheet point under it (`Geo::scrolled_point`).
- The frame grid uses a snapshot of the workbook, so the new zoom only shows on the next frame. That frame moves the scroll so the recorded point is back under the pointer (`Geo::scroll_keeping`) before anything is drawn. If the scroll were corrected in the frame that sets the zoom, that frame would draw the old zoom with the new scroll, and the sheet would jump on every glide frame.
- The new geometry is built from the sheet at its new zoom, so header and outline band widths and frozen-pane sizes, which all change with the zoom, are taken into account. On an axis where the pointer is over frozen panes, the scroll stays as it is. Page Layout view works the same way, because there the geometry has no frozen panes.
- The anchor is used once and then cleared, so ordinary scrolling afterwards isn't pulled back. If the zoom was changed some other way in between, the anchor doesn't match the zoom and is dropped.

Other ways of zooming (status bar slider, View › Zoom, Ctrl+Alt+= / Ctrl+Alt+-) aren't tied to a pointer position and keep their current behaviour.

`docs/decisions.md` (the Ctrl+wheel zoom section) now describes the behaviour.

Test: `zoom_keeps_the_point_under_the_pointer` builds a sheet with frozen rows and columns, takes the cell under a pointer position and the offset into that cell at 100%, then zooms to 200% and to 50%. After each zoom it checks that the same cell is under the pointer at the same offset. It also checks that nothi…

title: Charts: axis direction round-trips and renders mirrored (#1687)
author: zyzabruh
body:
Fixes #1687

An axis saved with `orientation="maxMin"` was dropped on reload: the reader ignored it, the writer always emitted `minMax`, and the renderer had no notion of a mirrored frame, so the direction never survived a save.

## What's in

- **Model** — `Chart` gains `cat_reverse` / `val_reverse` (`#[serde(default)]`).
- **Reader** — reads `scaling/orientation == "maxMin"` from the catAx/dateAx and the primary valAx; a scatter's y axis is picked by `axPos`.
- **Writer** — `axis_xml` writes the orientation on the axes each kind has: category + value for column/bar/line/area/…, value only for a scatter (its x axis stays `minMax`), secondary axis unchanged.
- **Renderer** — `frame()` mirrors category labels and value scales; the cartesian, scatter, histogram, waterfall (incl. bar connectors), box/whisker and stock passes mirror their point positions; trendlines follow. A mirrored category axis also flips the series order inside a cluster, and a combo's secondary series stay on the forward axes with their labels.
- **Command** — `chart.set` grows `catReverse` / `valReverse`. There is no Format Axis pane to host the tick boxes yet, so this is the only entry point.

## Tests

- `mirrored_axis_orientation_round_trips` (xlsx): `maxMin` in the written chart XML (both axes for a column chart, y-only for a scatter) + the reloaded flags.
- `mirrored_axes_flip_the_frame` (chart): category labels and the value axis swap ends; reversing one axis leaves the other alone.
- `mirrored_axes_survive_set_and_xlsx` (engine): set → save → reload → reset.
- Review follow-ups: `reversed_value_axis_draws_bars_from_the_zero_baseline`, `reversed_bars_put_their_labels_past_the_tip`, `reversed_area_labels_sit_outside_the_area`, `a_combo_charts_secondary_series_keep_the_forward_axes`, `reversed_categories_keep_a_combo_primary_bar_off_the_secondary_slot`, `a_zero_length_bar_keeps_its_label_on_the_axis_side`.

title: Keytips: letters typed with Alt held continue the sequence (fixes #1846)
author: Shnrqpdr
body:
Fixes #1846.

## Cause

The sequences themselves exist (`HOA` → `home.autofitRowHeight`, `HOI` → `home.autofitColumnWidth` in `keytips.json`), and tapping Alt, then H, O, A works. What doesn't work is the way most people type it: **holding Alt while pressing H**, which Excel accepts. In `KeyTips::process`, any `Event::Key` with `modifiers.alt` cancelled keytips, so Alt+H did nothing, and O and A went on to the grid.

Reproduced through the egui harness (before this change):

| | Alt tapped, then H, O, I | Alt held + H, then O, I |
|---|---|---|
| Windows | works | nothing happens |
| Linux | works | nothing happens |
| macOS | intentionally off (#1864) | off |

## Fix

- `KeyTips` tracks whether the **left** Alt key is down (`alt_held`, cleared on its release, on a `ModifiersChanged` without Alt, and by `clear()`).
- With left Alt held, a one-character key that continues a known sequence from the current prefix (`lookup` or `has_deeper`) is handled as a keytip letter. If no prefix is active it starts at the root, so Alt+H opens the Home level, and Alt can be held for the rest of the letters too (Alt+H+O+I).
- The release of a consumed letter still carries Alt and no longer cancels the level.
- Unchanged: Alt combinations that start no sequence (Alt+=, Alt+X, Alt+arrows) still cancel keytips and reach the keymap; AltGr (right Alt, or Ctrl+Alt on Windows) never starts keytips, so typed characters like `€` or `ą` are not taken; macOS Option stays a text modifier (#1864).

## Tests

In `crates/ui-egui/tests/keytips.rs`:
- `letters_typed_with_alt_held_run_autofit_sequences`: on Windows and Linux, Alt held through H, O, I autofits column A, and Alt+H then O, A (Alt released) autofits row 1; the cell's text is untouched and no editor opens. It fails without the fix.
- `alt_combinations_outside_a_sequence_still_cancel_keytips`: Alt+X, AltGr+H and macOS Option+H don't start keytips.

title: #1855: Backspace then Enter is one undo step; redo selects the redone cell
author: justinjohn0306
body:
Fixes #1855

## 1. Backspace then Enter left an empty undo step
Backspace on a cell runs `edit.clearContents` (one undo step) and opens an empty editor. Committing that editor (Enter, Tab or a click elsewhere) ran `cell.set ""` on the now-empty cell, which recorded a second, empty undo step. The first Ctrl+Z undid that empty step, so the deleted value didn't come back, and the next Ctrl+Z undid an unrelated earlier edit.

Fix: `commit_edit` skips the command when it would commit empty text into a cell that is already empty (no value, no formula). Ctrl+Enter fills and array entry are unchanged.

## 2. Redo jumped to the clicked cell (reported in [this comment](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/issues/1855#issuecomment-6259302494))
Type into A1, A2, A3, click A1, Ctrl+Z, then Ctrl+Y: "third" came back in A3, but the selection went to A1. `edit.undo` stored the selection at undo time in the redo entry. It now stores the undone step's own selection, so redo selects the cells it changes (A3), the same way undo does.

## Verification
- `undo_after_backspace_restores_the_cleared_cell` (UI) and `redo_selects_the_redone_cell` (engine). Both failed before their fix and pass after.
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui` and `cargo test -p gridcraft-engine` (this includes `command_sequence_fuzz`) pass. `cargo fmt --check` and clippy `-D warnings` on both crates are clean.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Keep the in-cell editor at the cell's height for one line

title: Reject signed or exponent parts in fraction text
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/core/src/parse.rs:150` (no existing issue): Fraction text with a signed numerator or denominator is read as a number.

## Cause
`parse_fraction` parsed the numerator and denominator with `f64::parse`, which accepts signs, exponents and a leading `.`. It also removed every leading minus from the whole part with `trim_start_matches('-')`. Text such as `1 -1/2`, `1 1/-2` and `--1 1/2` was therefore read as a number instead of staying text.

## Fix
The numerator and denominator must now be non-empty strings of ASCII digits. The whole part allows at most one leading `-` or `+`, and what remains must start with a digit or `.`. The regression test covers the rejected and the still-accepted inputs.

## Verified
- Regression test `parse::tests::fraction_rejects_signed_parts`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p gridcraft-core fraction_rejects_signed_parts`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Other number parsing paths and the handling of `.` in the whole part are unchanged.

title: Pan the grid on a one-finger touch drag instead of selecting
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #1907

## Cause
The grid only scrolled on `smooth_scroll_delta`, and egui does not fill that for a one-finger touch drag. The drag therefore reached the grid as an ordinary primary-button drag and went down the mouse selection-drag path, so the viewport stayed still and cells were selected.

## Fix
When a drag on the grid starts while touches are active, `GridState::touch_pan` is set. While one finger is down, the drag delta now scrolls the view, with the content following the finger and the horizontal direction mirrored on right-to-left sheets. The grid's selection/object interaction is skipped for the frames of that pan, including the release, so a tap still selects the tapped cell.

## Verified

- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Pinch-to-zoom is unchanged and still goes through egui's `zoom_delta`, and panning pauses while two fingers are down. While touch panning is active, a touch drag cannot select a range, use the fill handle, or move charts or other objects; mouse and pen input is unchanged.

title: Print CJK text with a CID font instead of question marks
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #1908

## Cause
The PDF writer used for printing and PDF export only had the standard Type1 fonts with WinAnsiEncoding. `pdf_string` passed every character through `win_ansi`, which returns `?` for anything outside CP1252, so Chinese and other non-Latin text became `????` before it reached the printer.

## Fix
`Page::text_rotated` now splits text into runs. Runs WinAnsi can encode keep the chosen standard font. Other runs are written as UTF-16BE hex strings in a non-embedded, predefined Adobe-GB1 CID font (`STSong-Light`, `UniGB-UTF16-H` CMap), and its Type0, CIDFont and FontDescriptor objects are emitted only when needed. Width measurement treats those characters as full-width (1000/em) to match the font, so text is still aligned and wrapped correctly.

## Verified
- Regression tests `tests::cjk_text_is_not_replaced_by_question_marks`, `cmd::print::tests::pdf_prints_cjk_text_instead_of_question_marks`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p gridcraft-pdf --lib cjk_text_is_not_replaced_by_question_marks && cargo test -p gridcraft-engine --lib pdf_prints_cjk_text_instead_of_question_marks`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
No font is embedded: fonts live outside this repo, so the viewer or printer driver supplies the CJK face. Only one Chinese (Adobe-GB1) CID font is used, so there are no separate Japanese or Korean faces. That means Hangul may still show missing glyphs. Text containing only WinAnsi characters keeps the same font and string encoding; the only change in its content stream is that `Tf` now follows `Tm` instead of preceding it.

title: Reuse one D-Bus session connection in the desktop theme watcher
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #1915

## Cause
On Linux, `read()` in `desktop_theme.rs` called `zbus::blocking::Connection::session()` on every poll. The watcher therefore opened a new connection, with a new handshake and `Hello`, every 4 seconds.

## Fix
The watcher thread now keeps its session-bus connection between polls and passes it to `read()`. It opens the connection on first use and drops it only when a call fails with an I/O error, so the next poll reconnects. The regression test runs the watcher under `dbus-run-session` and checks that it makes at most one new bus connection over three polls. The test panics with a clear message if `dbus-run-session` or the session bus is missing, so it can't pass silently without checking anything.

## Verified
- Regression test `desktop_theme::tests::the_watcher_reuses_one_bus_connection`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui --lib the_watcher_reuses_one_bus_connection`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The 4 s polling is unchanged and the watcher does not subscribe to the portal's `SettingChanged` signal. It still reads only the existing `color-scheme` schemas, so #530 is not addressed.

title: Skip control requests whose client already timed out
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #1914

## Cause
When the connection thread timed out after 60 s, it told the client the command failed, but the request stayed in the queue. The next `control::poll` ran it anyway and discarded the reply, so the change was applied after the client had been told it failed.

## Fix
`ControlRequest` now carries a shared cancelled flag. `ControlRequest::new` returns a `ControlReply` wrapper that sets the flag when `recv_timeout` fails or when the wrapper is dropped. `poll` skips cancelled requests without running them.

## Verified
- Regression test `control::tests::timed_out_request_is_not_run`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui --lib timed_out_request_is_not_run`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
I did not add a journal entry for skipped requests. I also did not change the screenshot pending queue or the 60 s timeout value.

title: Number formats: honour the B1/B2 calendar prefixes (Hijri dates for B2)
author: Mouhand-Kaddo
body:
## Summary

Arabic Excel writes a calendar prefix at the start of a date format: `B1` for Gregorian, `B2` for Hijri (for example `B2dd/mm/yyyy`). GridCraft printed the prefix as text, so a Hijri-formatted date showed as `B219/10/2026`.

```diff
 =TEXT(DATE(2026,10,19),"B2dd/mm/yyyy")
- B219/10/2026
+ 08/05/1448
 =TEXT(DATE(2026,10,19),"B1dd/mm/yyyy")
- B119/10/2026
+ 19/10/2026
```

- `B1`/`B2` (any case) at the start of a section, or after a colour or condition tag such as `[Red]`, set the section's calendar and are never printed. A repeated prefix (`B2B2`) is accepted, as in Excel.
- A `[$...]` locale or currency tag before the prefix (`[$-401]B2dd/mm/yyyy`, `[$€-407]B2dd/mm/yyyy`) hides `B2` but keeps the date Gregorian, as Excel does; `B2[$-401]dd/mm/yyyy` and `B2[Red]dd/mm/yyyy` are Hijri.
- Any other `B` and digit (`B0`–`B9` other than a prefix, `B12`, `B1B2`, `B2[Red]B2`, `dd/mm/yyyyB2`, `dd B2 mm`, even escaped `B2`), and a `B1` or `B2` prefix before a number format (`B20.00`, `B1#,##0`), make the code invalid, as in Excel: `TEXT` returns `#VALUE!` and a cell shows the value as General (the same handling as a code over 255 characters). A quoted `"B2"` is literal text. `B2General` and `B2@` show the plain value.
- Under `B2`, year, month and day use the tabular Hijri calendar; `mmm` and `mmmm` show the Arabic month name (two-word names joined by a no-break space, U+00A0, as Excel writes them), `ddd` and `dddd` the Arabic weekday name (full names in both cases). Times are unchanged.
- Serial 60 (the 1900 system's fictitious 29 February 1900) has no Hijri date: under `B2`, any date or clock part (even `hh:mm` alone) makes `TEXT` return `#VALUE!` and a cell show `####`; `[h]` and literal-only sections still show. Serial 0 shows as serial 1 (`29/08/1317`). There is no other range limit: Hijri dates continue to 31 December 9999 (`03/04/9666`), e.g. 17 November 2077 is `02/01/1501`.

title: fix(edit): Ctrl+Enter gives each cell the number format typing gives it (#1919)
author: vedran-dobos
body:
Fixes #1919.

`range.fill` (Ctrl+Enter) parsed the input once at the active cell, then put each target cell’s old
style back when it already held a cell, so `5%`, `$5`, `3/4/2026` or `=DATE(…)` lost their
automatic format there (0.05, 5, 46085). Empty targets took the active cell’s style instead of
their own. Now each target gets what `input_to_cell` gives for that cell, which is what typing the
input there gives.

## What changed
- **engine** `cmd/edit.rs` `range_fill`: the input goes through `input_to_cell` for each target
  cell, so a General cell gets the automatic format, a cell with its own format (or a formatted row
  or column) keeps it, and a Text cell gets the input as text, as with `cell.set`. The result only
  depends on the cell’s style, so it’s parsed once per distinct style, not per cell; relative
  formulas are still shifted from the active cell as before.
- The step that put the old style back is gone (`input_to_cell` already starts from the cell’s own
  style).

## Tests
`crates/engine/tests/range_fill_formats.rs`:
- `filled_cells_that_already_hold_a_value_get_the_automatic_format`: `5%`, `$5`, `3/4/2026`,
  `1:30 PM`, `1.5E+3` over A1:A2 with A2 holding 1; both cells must match what `cell.set` gives in

- `filled_formulas_still_shift_and_get_their_date_format`: `=DATE(2026,3,ROW())` gets `m/d/yyyy`
  in a cell that held a value, and `=C1*2` still shifts to `=C2*2`. Fails on `main` (General).

title: Selection: the outline lies on the gridlines at any display scale
author: arcanii
body:
Split out of #549 at review: this is its first half, the outline. The in-cell editor follows in #549, which is now stacked on this one.

## What was wrong

The selection's outline was drawn centred half a point outside the cells. Gridlines are drawn just before each cell edge, so the top and left sides sat on their gridline but the bottom and right sides a point past theirs. On a display at 125% or 150% the renderer rounded the two differently, and a grey line showed inside the outline's bottom and right sides.

## What it does now

Each side covers the gridline that bounds the selection and reaches outward from it, a whole number of device pixels wide. The inside of the outline is exactly the inside of the cells, so no gridline shows inside it, and every edge is sharp. `outline_bands` still cuts the sides to the view, so a whole selected column keeps its left and right sides.

The outline's weight is unchanged at two points: three pixels at 150%, where Excel's is two. The fill handle and the in-cell editor are unchanged.

## What is checked, and against what

- **Against Excel, at 150% only.** Measured in Windows Excel at 150% display scaling, from a capture: the gridline is one device pixel and the outline two, the gridline's own pixel and the one outside it, on each side. Excel was not measured at any other scale.
- **Against the renderer, at 100%, 125%, 150%, 175% and 200%.** `tests/selection_outline.rs` tessellates the gridlines and the sides as they were painted, and fails if a side does not cover its gridline or reaches into the cells. That is what "at any display scale" means in the title: the outline stays on the gridlines at every scale. It does not claim to match Excel's pixels at scales other than 150%.

## Where

- `crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs`:
  - `gridline_centre`: where a gridline is centred; the gridline loops in `paint_quadrant` use it.
  - `gridline_span`: which device pixels a gridline covers. It repeats epaint's rule for moving a line onto pixel…

title: Reject signed and multi-$ whole-row ranges in RangeRef::parse
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/core/src/addr.rs:217` (no existing issue): RangeRef::parse accepts signed row numbers like "+1:+3" as whole-row ranges.

## Cause
The whole-row branch of `RangeRef::parse` parsed the row numbers with `u32::parse`, which accepts a leading '+'. It also stripped any number of leading '$' characters. So `+1:+3` and `$$1:3` were accepted as whole-row ranges.

## Fix
The row parts are now parsed through a helper that strips at most one leading '$'. The helper requires a non-empty, all-ASCII-digit string before parsing as `u32`. `+1:+3`, `-1:3`, `$$1:3` and `:3` now return `None`, and `$1:$3` still parses as rows 1 to 3.

## Verified
- Regression test `addr::tests::range_parse_rejects_signed_rows`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p gridcraft-core range_parse_rejects_signed_rows`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The whole-column branch still strips any number of leading '$' characters. I did not change `CellRef::parse` or the row-number bounds check.

title: Protection: a line can be deleted only when its cells are unlocked (#1766)
author: zyzabruh
body:
Refs #1766

Review ▸ Protect Sheet's **Delete rows** and **Delete columns** boxes were ignored in one case that has nothing to do with the permission: a line with no format of its own was judged by the *default* format, which is locked, so deleting it was refused even when every one of its cells was unlocked. Insert rows / Insert columns worked because that path never asks the question.

This doesn't close the issue on its own: the example in it is refused by Excel too, so whether #1766 still tracks something the maintainers want is their call.

## What the permission actually covers

`AllowDeletingRows` and `AllowDeletingColumns` only cover lines "where every cell in the row (or column) to be deleted is unlocked" — empty cells included, and an empty cell is locked by default. The example in the issue (locked values in A1:A3, delete row 2) is refused by Excel too; that expectation was mine, not Excel's. Inserting shifts cells without changing any, so the permission alone decides there, which is why the two halves of the dialog looked inconsistent.

## Fix

`check_lines_protection` keeps the permission gate, then refuses a deletion only when a cell of the deleted line is locked. The question is answered the way `Sheet::style_id` answers it everywhere else: a stored cell by its own format, an empty one by the line's format, then the crossing line's, then the default.

That makes a line with no format of its own deletable when its cells are unlocked (after Select All → unlock, for instance), which is what was broken, and keeps the rest refused: locked values, a blank row of default cells, a row unlocked only on part of its width.

`sheet.moveColumns` keeps its own refusal — a move keeps the cells, so the delete permission doesn't cover relocating them — and asks the same question of the columns it moves.

## Tests

`protection_allows_deleting_a_line_of_an_unlocked_sheet` (new) is the case `main` gets wrong: Select All → unlock, one cell locked back, protect; the blank …

title: Accounting format: the documented currency `symbol` is honoured
author: zyzabruh
body:
`home.accounting` documents `{range?, symbol?}`, but the `symbol` was never read: the command applied the `$` code whatever it was given, so a control-channel or MCP client asking for another currency — lempiras (#1893), for instance — silently got dollars. The Accounting menu (#1068) and the format gallery go through `home.numberFormat`, so nothing in the UI could reach the parameter either, which is how it stayed dead.

## Fix

- `accounting` reads `symbol` (default `$`) and builds the accounting code with it — the same layout Excel's button writes, with the symbol in place of `$`.
- A symbol holding a `"` or a `\` would break the format string, so it is refused with an error rather than pasted in.
- The default output is unchanged, character for character: the built code equals the named `Accounting` format.

`home.accounting {"range": "A1", "symbol": "L"}` on 1234.5 now shows ` L 1,234.50 ` where it showed ` $ 1,234.50 `.

## Tests

- `accounting_format_takes_the_symbol_it_is_given` (engine): the displayed text with `L` and with the default, plus the two refused symbols.

title: AutoFit: estimate Arabic text width from measured glyph widths
author: Mouhand-Kaddo
body:
## Summary

AutoFit sized Arabic text as if every character were a full em wide, the width of a CJK ideograph. A vowelled Arabic phrase got a column about 3.5× wider than its text, and wrapped Arabic rows grew too tall.

```diff
 AutoFit Column Width, A1 = "مُحَمَّد يَدْرُسُ فِي الْمَدْرَسَةِ", B1 = "Hello there in school"
- column A 493 px, column B 144 px
+ column A about as wide as column B, as the two phrases are when drawn
```

`approx_text_width` (the engine's font-free estimate behind AutoFit Column Width, AutoFit Row Height for wrapped text and PivotTable column fit) now counts:

- Arabic vowel and Quranic marks and invisible format characters (ZWNJ, ZWJ, LRM, RLM, ALM, the bidi embeddings and isolates) as zero width, since they draw on another letter or not at all.
- Arabic-script letters at 0.48 em.
- The word ligatures and the rial sign (U+FDF0–FDFC) at 1.2 em, and the bismillah ligature ﷽ at 11 em.

CJK and other scripts keep 1 em, and ASCII is unchanged.

The widths come from HarfBuzz shaping of real text in Noto Sans Arabic, Noto Naskh Arabic and DejaVu Sans. Shaped Arabic letters measured 0.36–0.53 em (0.48 is set slightly above the average so text isn't clipped), the ligatures 1.0–1.35 em, and ﷽ 9.8–12.2 em.

## Evidence

- Before, on `main`, the new tests fail. The vowelled phrase measured 486 against 266 without its marks, and its column fitted to 493 against 144 for the Latin phrase. After the fix, all 7 `cmd::format` tests pass: `arabic_vowel_and_direction_marks_add_no_width`, `arabic_text_fits_a_column_about_as_wide_as_latin_text_of_the_same_length`, `arabic_word_ligatures_are_wider_than_letters` and `cjk_text_keeps_a_full_em_per_character`, plus the existing ones.

title: Names: count characters, not bytes, in the 255-character name limit
author: Mouhand-Kaddo
body:
## Summary

Defined names are limited to 255 characters in Excel, in any script. GridCraft checked the limit in UTF-8 bytes, and an Arabic letter is 2 bytes. So an Arabic name longer than 127 letters was refused with "The name that you entered is not valid", and Create from Selection silently skipped long Arabic headers.

```diff
 fn valid_name(n: &str) -> bool {
-    if n.len() > 255 || …
```

title: XLSX: keep right-to-left paragraph direction in text boxes and shapes
author: Mouhand-Kaddo
body:
## Summary

Arabic and Hebrew text boxes made in Excel carry a right-to-left paragraph direction (`<a:pPr algn="r" rtl="1"/>`). GridCraft read only the alignment, so opening and saving such a workbook dropped `rtl`. In Excel the box then read left to right: trailing punctuation jumped to the wrong end (`المجموع: 100.`), and wrapped lines started on the wrong side.

```diff
 <a:p>
-  <a:pPr algn="r"/>
+  <a:pPr algn="r" rtl="1"/>
```

title: Keep date text with signed parts like +3/4/2026 as text
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/core/src/parse.rs:214` (no existing issue): Date text with signed parts like "+3/4/2026" is parsed as a date.

## Cause
`parse_date` read the day, month and year parts with `str::parse::<i64>()`, which accepts a leading `+`, so `+3/4/2026` became a date serial. The time parser used f64 parsing, which also accepts `+`, so `1/1/2020 +5:00` became a date-time.

## Fix
The date-part parser now accepts only non-empty strings of ASCII digits. `parse_time` now rejects any part that starts with `+`. The new test covers `+3/4/2026`, `3/+4/2026`, `3/4/+2026` and `1/1/2020 +5:00`, and checks that `3/4/2026` still gives 46085.

## Verified
- Regression test `parse::tests::signed_date_parts_stay_text`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p gridcraft-core signed_date_parts_stay_text`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The signed-fraction and signed-range code paths are unchanged. Time parsing still accepts fractional seconds and other f64 forms apart from the leading `+`.

body:

Legacy `.xls` files keep each sheet's display options in the WINDOW2 record, which GridCraft's `.xls` reader skipped. title: Sort: order Arabic text by its letters, not its vowel marks or digit script
author: Mouhand-Kaddo
body:
## Summary

Text order compared lower-cased code points, so in Arabic the vowel marks (harakat), tatweel and invisible direction marks decided where a word sorted. Arabic-Indic digits also sorted after Arabic letters. Excel's collation gives vowel marks only a secondary weight and sorts digits as digits.

```diff
 Data › Sort ascending on A1:A4 = بيت, بَاب, تمر, ‏بحر (RLM-prefixed)
- بيت, بَاب, تمر, ‏بحر        (fatha U+064E sorts after yeh U+064A; the RLM sorts last)
+ بَاب, ‏بحر, بيت, تمر
```

`compare_text` now compares in three levels:

1. **Primary:** lower-cased characters with Arabic vowel and Quranic marks (U+064B–065F, U+0670, U+0610–061A and the U+06D8–06ED marks Excel skips), tatweel (U+0640) and invisible format characters (ZWNJ, ZWJ, LRM, RLM, ALM, bidi embeddings/overrides/isolates U+202A–202E and U+2066–2069, BOM, soft hyphen, CGJ, word joiner) skipped, and Arabic-Indic and Extended Arabic-Indic digits read as `0`–`9`.
2. **Secondary** (same letters): letter by letter, skipping the ignorable characters, the digit script (ASCII, Arabic-Indic, Extended Arabic-Indic) and then the marks on that letter: unmarked first, then marks in Excel's measured order (e.g. sukun before shadda). A mark on an earlier letter outranks a later digit script, as in Excel.
3. **Tie-break:** exactly the old comparison. Two strings compare equal only when they did before, so `=`, exact MATCH and XLOOKUP, COUNTIF `=`, UNIQUE and Remove Duplicates don't change. Only order does: Data › Sort, SORT/SORTBY, `<`/`>`, approximate MATCH/XLOOKUP (still consistent with the sort that produced their data), `"<x"` criteria, PivotTable item order and the AutoFilter value list.

ASCII-only pairs skip the first two levels. The primary pass is lazy and allocation-free; the secondary key (two small `Vec<u16>`) is built only when two non-ASCII strings have the same letters.

title: Search from the end for negative TEXTBEFORE/TEXTAFTER instances
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/functions/src/text.rs:511-552` (no existing issue): TEXTBEFORE/TEXTAFTER with negative instance don't search from the end (overlapping delimiters).

## Cause
text_before_after made one list of non-overlapping delimiter matches by scanning left to right, and for a negative instance_num it took the k-th match from the end of that list. When delimiter occurrences overlap, this misses the matches you get by searching from the end. For example, TEXTBEFORE("aaa","aa",-1) returned "" instead of "a".

## Fix
find_matches takes a new from_end flag. When it is set, the function scans right to left and takes the longest delimiter that ends at each position. The results still come back in ascending order, so the existing negative-instance indexing and the match_end (0,0) insertion keep working. text_before_after sets the flag for negative instances. The regression test `text::tests::before_after` covers the reported case plus TEXTAFTER, a two-match case, and a case-insensitive case.

## Verified
- Regression test `text::tests::before_after`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p gridcraft-functions text::tests::before_after`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Positive instances and TEXTSPLIT (split_by) still use the left-to-right scan, and the handling of all-empty delimiters is unchanged.

title: CSV import: read Windows-1256 Arabic files as Arabic
author: Mouhand-Kaddo
body:
## Summary

Excel on Arabic Windows saves "CSV (Comma delimited)" and "Text (Tab delimited)" in code page 1256. GridCraft read any file without a BOM that wasn't valid UTF-8 as Windows-1252, so Arabic opened as accented Latin gibberish.

```diff
 bytes E3 D1 CD C8 C7 20 31 32 33 A1  (Windows-1256)
- ãÑÍÈÇ 123¡
+ مرحبا 123،
```

- A 128-entry Windows-1256 table, transcribed from unicode.org's `CP1256.TXT` and checked entry by entry against Python's `cp1256` codec. No new dependency.
- `Cp1256Evidence` decides between 1256 and 1252, and only for input that has no BOM and isn't valid UTF-8. It counts the high bytes that decode differently in the two code pages, leaving out invisible marks (ZWNJ, ZWJ, LRM, RLM) and ordinals after a digit (`1º`, `2ª`). It decodes as Arabic when all of these hold:
  - at least two of those bytes are Arabic letters or `، ؛ ؟`, and they make up at least 90% of the differing bytes;
  - at most 30% of the Arabic bytes touch an ASCII letter (Western accents sit inside Latin words);
  - almost no accented Latin bytes that both code pages share sit next to another high byte (Hebrew Windows-1255 letters land there).
- UTF-8, BOM and UTF-16 handling is untouched, and everything else still decodes as Windows-1252.

## Evidence

The thresholds came from a measurement harness rather than hand-tuning. The corpus was quoted strings from 95 glibc locale files: 67 Western locales encoded as 1252, 26 Arabic, Persian, Urdu, Pashto, Kurdish, Sindhi and Uyghur locales as 1256, and Hebrew and Yiddish as 1255. These were cut into CSV-like chunks and combined with hand-written CSV samples.

| Rule | Western read as Arabic | Arabic missed | Hebrew read as Arabic |
|---|---|---|---|
| This PR | 2 / 131 | 6 / 200 | 1 / 26 |
| A first byte-run rule | 6 / 131 | 30 / 200 | 11 / 26 |

The remaining misses are contrived: a lone `ÅÄÖ`, `¿Ñ? ¡Ñ! «Ñ»`, single-letter Arabic files, Urdu and Sindhi date-format strings, and a Hebrew list of single letters with apostrophes. Re…

title: Tables: limit table names to 255 characters, counted as characters
author: Mouhand-Kaddo
body:
## Summary
`table.rename` and `insert.table` accepted table names of any length. Excel caps table names at 255 characters, so a longer name was saved into a workbook Excel refuses. The check counts characters, not bytes, so a 200-letter Arabic name (400 UTF-8 bytes) is accepted and 256 letters are refused. This follows #1934, which made the same change for defined names.

```diff

+        && name.starts_with(|c: char| c.is_alphabetic() || c == '_' || c == '\\')
```

author: Mouhand-Kaddo
body:
**Stacked on #1740.** #1740 keeps the theme's East Asian (`<a:ea>`) and complex-script (`<a:cs>`) typefaces; review only the top commit, `M12.AR14`. Once #1740 merges, this rebases down to that one commit.

## Summary
A theme's font collections also carry a per-script list after `<a:cs>`: `<a:font script="Arab" typeface="Times New Roman"/>`, plus Hebr, Jpan and the rest (ECMA-376 Part 1 §20.1.4.1.24). Arabic Excel themes use it to pick the Arabic face for shapes, charts and theme-font cells. GridCraft dropped the list on save, so after open and save those lost their Arabic theme font.

This keeps the list next to #1740's fields:

```diff
 pub struct Theme {
     …
     pub minor_font_cs: String,
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub major_font_scripts: Vec<(String, String)>,
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub minor_font_scripts: Vec<(String, String)>,
 }
-<a:cs typeface="{cs}"/></a:majorFont>
+<a:cs typeface="{cs}"/>{<a:font script typeface/>…}</a:majorFont>
```

title: XLSX: keep cell fonts' charset (Arabic 178) and family on save
author: Mouhand-Kaddo
body:
## Summary
Cell fonts in `styles.xml` can carry `<charset val="178"/>` (Arabic) and `<family val="1"/>` (roman), as in ECMA-376 Part 1 §18.8.18 (`ST_FontFamily` 0–14). When the named font is missing, Windows uses them to pick a substitute in the same script. GridCraft ignored `charset` and wrote `<family val="2"/>` for every font. After a GridCraft save, an Arabic workbook could therefore fall back to a Latin-only font on a machine without, say, Traditional Arabic.

`Font` now keeps both values, and the writer puts them back in schema order (name, family, charset). Fonts without them write exactly what they wrote before.

```diff
 pub struct Font {
     …
+    pub charset: Option<u8>,
+    pub family: Option<u8>,
 }
-<name val="{name}"/><family val="2"/>
+<name val="{name}"/><family val="{family or 2}"/>[<charset val="{charset}"/>]
```

Two details:
- `family` 2 reads as `None`, the same value a new font has. A cell opened from a file and a cell formatted in GridCraft with the same font therefore stay one style.
- **Font name** (`home.fontName`) clears both values. They describe the old font, and Excel likewise takes them from the new font.

## Evidence
- `font_charset_and_family_roundtrip`: `Traditional Arabic` with charset 178 and family 1 survives read, write and read twice. The XML has `<family val="1"/><charset val="178"/>`. On main the charset was dropped and family became 2.
- `fonts_without_charset_write_unchanged`: still `<family val="2"/>` and no `<charset>`.
- `out_of_range_family_is_ignored`: family 15 is ignored.
- `changing_the_font_name_drops_the_old_fonts_charset_and_family` (engine): fails without the `format.rs` change and passes with it.
- `full_roundtrip` passes unchanged.
- Gates: xlsx roundtrip/styles/font (36 passed), model (14 passed), engine font/style/format (16 passed), and `clippy -D warnings` and `fmt --check` on model, xlsx and engine.

## Merge Danger
- **Door:** two-way. Additive `#[serde(default)]` fields.
- **Blast Radius:** `Font` …

title: XLS: skip dialog sheets instead of importing them as worksheets
author: Mouhand-Kaddo
body:
## Summary
In a `.xls` file, a dialog sheet's BOF record carries the worksheet type (`0x0010`). Only the `fDialog` bit of its WsBool record (MS-XLS 2.4.351, first byte, `0x10`) tells the two apart. The reader never looked at WsBool, so dialog sheets were imported as extra worksheets. The skip path and its warning ("Dialog sheets and unreadable sheets were skipped.") already existed but were never reached for them. Found while reviewing the `.xls` right-to-left fix (#1939).

```diff
+const WSBOOL: u16 = 0x0081;
+const WSBOOL_DIALOG: u8 = 0x10;
 …
             _ if depth > 1 => continue,
+            WSBOOL if rec.parts.first().and_then(|p| p.first()).is_some_and(|b| b & WSBOOL_DIALOG != 0) => return Ok(None),
```

## Evidence
- New test `dialog_sheets_are_skipped_not_read_as_worksheets`: a dialog sheet followed by a worksheet. On main both were imported (`["Dialog1", "Sheet1"]`); now only `Sheet1` is, its A1 is intact, and the warning is reported.
- The xls tests pass (20 passed), and `clippy -p gridcraft-xlsx --all-targets -D warnings` and `fmt --check` are clean.
- Independent review (Codex, gpt-6-luna) found no blockers. It confirmed the bit position against MS-XLS, and that a skipped sheet keeps its BoundSheet ordinal as `None`: 3D references don't shift, and names scoped to it (Print_Area, Print_Titles) are dropped through the same guarded lookup.

## Merge Danger
- **Door:** two-way. One match arm in one function.
- **Blast Radius:** `.xls` import only. Worksheets never set `fDialog`.

title: CSV/TSV: keep UTF-16 (Excel Unicode Text) files UTF-16 on save — stacked on #1780
author: Mouhand-Kaddo
body:
**Stacked on #1780.** It adds `CsvEncoding`; review only the top commit, `M12.AR18`. Once #1780 merges, this rebases down to that one commit.

## Summary
Excel's *Unicode Text* (`.txt`, tab-delimited UTF-16) is how Arabic text is exchanged with any reader regardless of its code page. #1780 decodes such a file, but remembers no encoding for it, so saving it wrote UTF-8: the file changed format on save. This adds `utf-16le` (aliases `utf-16` and `unicode`) to the encoding choice:
- **Open:** a file starting with `FF FE` is remembered as UTF-16LE.
- **Save:** it is written back as UTF-16LE with the BOM.
- **Any save:** `encoding: "utf-16le"` writes one from any workbook.

```diff
 pub enum CsvEncoding {
     …
     Windows1252,
+    Utf16Le,
 }
-        return (decode_utf16(rest, true), None);
+        return (decode_utf16(rest, true), Some(CsvEncoding::Utf16Le));
+        CsvEncoding::Utf16Le => [0xFF, 0xFE].into_iter().chain(text.encode_utf16().flat_map(u16::to_le_bytes)).collect(),
```

Two further changes:
- UTF-16 can double ASCII text, so the 512 MiB export cap now counts the UTF-16 size (BOM included) before encoding. Previously it relied on UTF-8 being the widest encoding.
- A UTF-16 file with an odd number of bytes now ends in U+FFFD instead of silently losing its last byte. This was already the case on main.

Big-endian UTF-16 still saves as UTF-8. Microsoft documents Unicode Text only as "UTF-16"; LE with an `FF FE` BOM is the Windows convention for it.

## Evidence
- `utf16le_arabic_round_trips` (xlsx) covers:
  - An Arabic UTF-16LE CSV with a quoted comma field and Arabic-Indic digits is detected, read and written back byte for byte.
  - Forcing `utf-16le` decodes it with or without the BOM.
  - The spellings parse.
  - A dangling last byte becomes U+FFFD.
- `utf16le_export_respects_the_size_cap` (xlsx): 600 ASCII characters fit a 1,000-byte cap in UTF-8 but are refused in UTF-16.
- `unicode_text_save_keeps_utf16` (engine): an Arabic tab-delimited `.txt` o…

title: Charts: per-point formatting, Invert if Negative and vary colors by point
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
A highlighted bar, a red slice, an exploded slice or a red negative bar comes back plain after GridCraft saves a workbook, because the chart model only keeps the series colour. In a sample of 243 real-world workbooks, point formats (c:dPt) appear in 24 (355 points), Invert if Negative in 5 (78 charts) and vary colors in 16 (6 on non-pie charts).

What changes:
- Model: `Series.points` holds Format Data Point overrides keyed by point index (solid fill, line colour, marker shape/size/fill/line, pie explosion, the point's own Invert if Negative). `Series.invert_if_negative` and `invert_color` (the c14 invertSolidFillFmt fill). `Chart.vary_colors`, where None is the kind's default, so new charts write the same XML as before.
- XLSX: read from c:dPt, c:invertIfNegative, the c14 extension and c:varyColors (an absent varyColors is on). Written in CT_DPt and series schema order. The c14 fill is written only when the series has a fill of its own, as Excel does. A combo writes varyColors on its first group only.
- Drawing, matched to what Excel draws on synthetic charts: inverted negative bars are white and outlined unless the series has a fill and an inverted colour, and inversion beats a point fill unless the point turns it off. Vary colors applies to pie-like charts and to a chart's only bar, line, scatter or bubble series, and a series fill wins over it. A line point colours the segment that ends at it and outlines its marker. A single series with vary colors or point formats lists its points in the legend. title: Remove Duplicates and Sort: move legacy array ranges with their rows
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
Remove Duplicates moved each kept row up but left a Ctrl+Shift+Enter array formula's recorded range where it was, so the array no longer started at its own cell. Later edits and saves then acted on the wrong area. The command-sequence fuzzer found it (seeds 9 and 1978 at `GRIDCRAFT_FUZZ_STEPS=200`). Minimal repro on the sales sample: `cell.set {"array":true,"cell":"C21","input":"=1"}`, then `data.removeDuplicates {"header":false,"range":"C17:G23"}`.

Sort had the same problem in another form: it rebuilt every moved formula with `Formula::from_expr`, which drops the array range, so a sorted CSE array quietly became an ordinary formula.

Both commands now follow what Excel does (checked against Excel with synthetic workbooks):

- A one-cell array, or a one-row array inside the range's columns, moves whole with its row (one column for a by-columns sort), and its range moves with it. In a removed duplicate row it is removed.
- An array in the rows being moved that spans several rows, or reaches past the range, is refused with "You can't change part of an array." Excel refuses even when nothing would move, so the check runs before anything changes.
- Arrays in the header row, or in columns outside the range, are untouched.

I considered reusing the Delete Cells path for removed rows, like #1117 does for insert.table. Excel's Remove Duplicates doesn't re-point formulas outside the range (`=A3` stays `=A3`), so that would be a behaviour change. This PR only moves the array ranges.

Tests: `remove_duplicates_moves_legacy_arrays_with_their_rows`, `remove_duplicates_and_sort_refuse_to_split_a_legacy_array`, `remove_duplicates_leaves_arrays_outside_the_moving_block` and `sort_keeps_legacy_arrays_and_moves_them_with_their_line`. Three of them fail on main; the one for arrays outside the range passes on both. With this change merged onto current main they all pass. Fuzz seeds 9 and 1978 now pass at 200 steps. The insert.table seeds (323, 736, 839, 1372, 1387, 1403, 1557) are fix…

title: Recalc: an array spilling over its own input reads its old area as blank
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
What happened

A dynamic array whose spill area overlaps its own input gets different values from recalculation after an edit and from a full recalculation (Calculate Now, reopening):

- J17 =SORT(H17:L19), then H18 = 5: N18 shows #CIRC! until a full recalc, which shows 0.
- G9 =SORT(D12:H15) with numbers in D12:E15 spills over G12:H12. After D13 changes, the sorted row from D12 shows the old 4 and 40 in J and K instead of 0.
- G14:H20 =AVERAGE(...) read the array of J22 =SORT(G14:K21), which reads them: the values drift with each edit.

Why

A formula recalculated after an edit is evaluated while its previous array is still laid out, because spills are only replaced at write-back. So it reads its own old values back, a previous #CIRC! included. A full recalculation clears every spill first and reads those cells as blank.

Fix

When a pass reads a cell spilled before the pass by a formula the pass recalculates, it calculates that formula first and reads its new array. While that formula is itself being calculated (the circular reference through its own spill), its old area reads blank, as in a full recalculation. With iterative calculation on, nothing changes: the old array stays the previous value a loop reads.

Excel, observed black-box (iteration off): an array whose anchor is inside its own input is a circular reference that shows 0 and doesn't spill. An array whose spill covers part of its input spills, reads those cells as blank and is flagged circular. Excel then keeps those values through later edits and full recalcs, which GridCraft can't copy without the two recalculations disagreeing. The blank reads here match what Excel shows right after the formula is entered. Showing #CIRC! without spilling when the anchor is inside its input is left for a follow-up.

Tests

- calc: four tests for the anchor inside its input, the anchor outside it, a loop through another formula, and iterative mode. The first three fail without the fix; all four pass with it, merged o…

title: Translate and standardizes UI error feedback by locale

title: Space on a checkbox cell toggles it and nothing else
author: Hamza0101
body:
Fixes #1951.

Space on a checkbox cell did toggle it — and also started editing it, because the same key press arrives twice: once as `Event::Key { key: Space }`, which the grid handles as `cell.toggleCheckbox`, and once as `Event::Text(" ")`, which starts editing the cell as any typed character does. Enter then committed that space over the checkbox, leaving the cell blank.

### Measured

Through the real canvas (`egui_kittest`), sending the key press, the text it produces, and the release, on a `B2` with `insert.checkbox`:

| step | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| initial | `Bool(false)` | `Bool(false)` |
| Space | `Bool(true)`, **editor open** | `Bool(true)`, no editor |
| Enter | `Text(" ")` | `Bool(true)` |

### What changed

The text event for a space is ignored while the active cell is a checkbox — one arm before the general text arm, next to the `Key::Space` arm that does the toggling. A space still starts editing on an ordinary cell, and every other character still starts editing on a checkbox cell (typing `x` over a checkbox replaces it, as before).

title: Space toggles a checkbox cell instead of starting a text edit (#1951)
author: bfenty
body:
## Problem

Pressing Space on a selected checkbox cell toggled the box **and** started a text edit on the same frame: the `Key::Space` arm consumed the keypress, but the `Text(" ")` event winit types for the same keypress fell through to the edit-starting path. Pressing Enter then committed the space and wiped the checkbox (#1951).

## Fix

The keyboard handler already suppresses Text-driven edit starts for shortcut keys that also type a character (the Shift+Space case). -            if !m.alt && (m.ctrl || m.command || (m.shift && *key == egui::Key::Space)))

title: fix(grid): Space on a checkbox cell toggles without starting an edit (#1951)
author: aryamanchhikara
body:
Fixes #1951

Pressing Space on a checkbox cell now just toggles it. Before, it also opened the cell editor with a space, and Enter then replaced the checkbox with `" "`.

## Root cause
Space reaches the grid as two events in one frame: `Event::Key(Space)` and `Event::Text(" ")` (egui-winit sends the key first). In `grid::keyboard` the key arm toggled the active checkbox, then the text arm called `begin_edit(" ")`: the `shortcut_pressed` guard that drops a shortcut's typed text only covered Ctrl/Cmd and Shift+Space. Enter then committed `" "`, a text value, so the checkbox (drawn only for TRUE/FALSE/empty) disappeared. When the text arrives first, the text arm returned before the key was seen, so the box never toggled at all.

## Fix
Beside `shortcut_pressed`, note whether Space was pressed this frame and drop the frame's typed text while the active cell is a checkbox. The check runs when the text is handled, so it sees the cell Space acts on. Space on any other cell still starts an edit.

## Tests (`crates/ui-egui/tests/interaction.rs`)
A helper sends Space as a keyboard does (key press plus `" "` text, in both orders):
- `space_on_a_checkbox_toggles_it_without_starting_an_edit`: checked once, no editor; Enter keeps TRUE and the checkbox format.
- `space_toggles_the_checkboxes_of_a_selection_whose_active_cell_is_one`: A1:B2 with A1 active.

The first two fail on `main`. The existing `space_toggles_the_active_checkbox_without_clicking_the_hovered_cell` sends only the key event, so it missed this.

title: Control channel: a request its sender gave up on is not run later
author: Hamza0101
body:
Fixes #1914, along the lines the report proposes.

A request that waits more than 60 s gets `{"ok": false, "error": "timed out waiting for the UI…"}` and **stays in the queue**: `control::poll` ran it on the next UI pass and dropped the reply. The client was told its command had failed while the command was applied, so an agent that retried after the error ran it twice.

### What changed

`ControlRequest` carries the state the report suggests, as three values rather than a bool, because the race has three outcomes:

| state | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `PENDING` | queued, not yet run |
| `TAKEN` | the app has started it and will answer |
| `ABANDONED` | its sender gave up waiting; it is dropped unrun |

`poll` claims each request with `take()` and skips one it cannot claim. The connection thread calls `abandon` when the reply times out, and the message depends on which side won:

- still queued → `timed out waiting for the UI (is the window minimised?)`, and it will not run;
- already started → `timed out waiting for the UI, which had already started the request, so it may still finish; its outcome is unknown`, because claiming otherwise would be a guess.

This is the shape DeckCraft settled on for the same problem (its #719), so the two apps now behave alike; `ControlRequest::take`/`abandon` read the same there.

### Tests

`a_request_its_sender_gave_up_on_does_not_run_later` — a request still waited for is answered and applied (`A1` becomes `kept`), then one abandoned while queued is drained by `poll`: `A1` stays `kept` and nothing is replied to it. Without the guard in `poll` it fails with `A1` = `gave up`.

`taking_and_abandoning_a_request_settle_once` — a taken request cannot then be abandoned, an abandoned one cannot be taken, and repeating either gives the same answer, so the two threads cannot both think they own it.

`cargo xtask ci`: all 8 steps pass.

title: fix(ui): use fontconfig for Linux font fallback and font lists
author: soiamsoNG
body:
## Summary

This fixes Linux font discovery and fallback when GridCraft runs inside Flatpak.

Flatpak exposes only the runtime fonts under `/usr/share/fonts`; host fonts are mounted under `/run/host/fonts`, `/run/host/local-fonts`, and `/run/host/user-fonts`. GridCraft's hard-coded Linux font paths never looked there, so Chinese UI and cell text rendered as tofu and the Format Cells font list did not include installed host fonts.

## Changes

- Start the installed-font scan from the actual startup context (`setup_context_for_language`), not only from `setup_context`.
- Discover Linux fonts with `fc-list`, falling back to the existing directory walk when fontconfig is unavailable.
- Read only the SFNT/TTC table directory and `name` table while cataloguing fonts; the full file is read only when a face is bound. This removes the old 64 MiB full-file cap.
- Resolve Linux font roles with `fc-match` for UI, cell, serif, mono, CJK, Thai, Hebrew and symbol fallbacks, while keeping the old hard-coded paths as a last-resort fallback.
- Use the installed family list in the ribbon font dropdown.
- Keep the tests independent of whether the CI image has CJK fonts.

## Notes

- `fc-match` results are placed before the hard-coded candidates.
- The fontconfig face index is masked with `0xFFFF`; the upper 16 bits are the named-instance selector.
- The previous hard-coded paths remain as a fallback for systems without a usable fontconfig installation.

## Tests

- `cargo +1.95.0 fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo +1.95.0 test -p gridcraft-ui-egui --lib` — 102 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo +1.95.0 clippy -p gridcraft-ui-egui --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings`

`cargo xtask ci` still hits a pre-existing unrelated failure in `crates/xlsx/src/xls/mod.rs:273` (`clippy::collapsible_match`).

Refs #1231

title: Rows: wrapped text sizes its row by the font that draws it (#1969)
author: jcagudelo12
body:
Fixes #1969.

**Problem:** with Wrap Text on, a narrow column's row grew too little and cut off the last lines.
Two causes in `auto_row_height` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/mod.rs`):
1. It counted lines as the text's total estimated width over the column width, as if words split
   anywhere. The grid wraps whole words, so lines end early and more lines are needed.
2. The engine has no fonts and estimates widths per character, so a word drawn a little wider than
   estimated moves to its own line where the estimate thought it fit.

**What changed:**
- `wrapped_line_count` (`cmd/format.rs`) counts lines word by word, splitting words wider than the
  column, as the grid draws them. The engine uses it whenever no UI is present (CLI, MCP).
- New `gridcraft_engine::measure`: a UI can install a per-thread text measurer. `auto_row_height`
  uses it for wrapped and multi-line cells, at the width the grid wraps at (2.5 px padding a side,
  indent, filter button), and keeps the estimate otherwise.
- `gridcraft-ui-egui` installs one (`text_measure.rs`) wherever it sets the context's fonts. It owns
  its own `Fonts` built from the same definitions, so it never takes egui's context lock while a
  command runs, and falls back to the cell font for a family the definitions don't hold.

This complements #1927 (measured heights for the row-boundary double-click): here every automatic
height (typing, Wrap Text, column width, file open) is measured.

**Tests:** `wrapped_text_row_fits_every_word_wrapped_line` (fails on `main`: 77 px for 5 lines that
need 95), `a_word_wider_than_the_column_takes_several_lines`,
`wrapped_text_row_uses_the_installed_measurer`, and the UI test

three column widths). `cargo test -p gridcraft-engine -p gridcraft-ui-egui` passes; clippy, fmt,
assets, layers and wasm pass.

title: Enter bare numbers in Percentage-formatted cells as percents
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #1967

## Cause
Typing `3` into a cell already formatted as Percentage stored `3.0`, so it displayed `300%`. The input parser only divides by 100 when the text itself ends in `%`, and nothing took the cell's existing number format into account.

## Fix
In `input_to_cell` (crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs), when the cell's number format ends in `%` and the input is a plain number with no `%` and an absolute value of 1 or more, the stored value is divided by 100. So `3` becomes `0.03` and shows as `3%`. Numbers below 1, such as `0.03`, are still stored as typed, which matches Excel's automatic percent entry. Regression test: `bare_number_in_percent_cell_is_a_percent` in crates/engine/tests/percent_entry.rs. Fixes #1967

## Verified
- Regression test `bare_number_in_percent_cell_is_a_percent`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p gridcraft-engine --test percent_entry`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The input parser in `gridcraft-core` is unchanged. Cells formatted General, text cells, formulas, and input that already contains `%` behave as before.

title: Desktop theme: the watcher's link has a type off Linux, so the gate passes there
author: Hamza0101
body:
`cargo xtask ci` cannot pass on macOS (or Windows) since `cc21643`:

```
error: this let-binding has unit value
  --> crates/ui-egui/src/desktop_theme.rs:36:13
   |
36 |             let mut link = Link::default();
error: could not compile `gridcraft-ui-egui` (lib) due to 1 previous error
error: ci failed at `clippy`
```

`Link` is the session-bus connection the watcher keeps between reads, and off Linux there is no bus to keep, so it is aliased to `()`. That makes `let mut link = Link::default()` a unit binding, which `clippy::let_unit_value` reports and the gate's `-D warnings` turns into an error. CI runs Linux only, where `Link` is a real `Option<Connection>`, so nothing sees it there.

I hit this gating an unrelated rebase: the failure names `ui-egui`, which the branch did not touch, and it reproduces on a clean `origin/main` (`49fe41a`).

### What changed

Off Linux, `Link` is a unit **struct** rather than `()`, so the binding has a type and the lint does not apply. Nothing else changes: `read` still ignores it on those platforms, and `prefers_dark`/`DesktopTheme::start` are untouched.

An `#[allow(clippy::let_unit_value)]` on the binding would also silence it, but it would sit on a line that is only a problem on some platforms; a named type says what the thing is.

### Checked

- `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean (it was the one error before).
- `cargo xtask ci`: all 8 steps pass.
- The two `desktop_theme` tests pass.

Nothing here is Linux-visible, so it cannot regress the platform that CI covers; a Linux reviewer will see no change in behaviour at all.

title: Persist the AutoSave preference across restarts (#1901)
author: bfenty
body:
## Problem
AutoSave (the title-bar switch / Options ▸ Save checkbox) lived on `GridState`, which is never serialized. The desktop app persists `UiState` to `ui.json` on exit, so AutoSave silently reset to off on every restart (#1901).

## Fix
Moved the flag from `GridState.autosave` (transient) to `UiState.autosave` (persisted, `serde(default)`), with `SheetApp::toggle_autosave()` as the single flip point for both call sites (title-bar switch, Options ▸ Save). The 2-second throttle timestamp stays on `GridState` — it's per-session timing, not a preference.

Old `ui.json` files without the key load fine via `serde(default)` and read as off, matching previous behavior.

## Tests
`autosave_persist.rs`:
- toggle → serialize → restore round-trip keeps AutoSave on (fails on main: no persisted field exists)
- toggling back persists off too
- a legacy `ui.json` without the key still deserializes with the rest of the settings intact

Full `gridcraft-ui-egui` suite green; clippy and rustfmt clean.

Closes #1901

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

title: calc: LET and LAMBDA names ignore case in any script
author: webglobepl
body:
Excel matches LET and LAMBDA names case-insensitively in every script. GridCraft compared them ASCII-only, so a name with a non-ASCII letter only worked when it was always typed with the same case:

| Formula | Excel | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| `=LET(dług,100,DŁUG*2)` | 200 | `#NAME?` | 200 |
| `=LAMBDA(ćma,ĆMA+1)(1)` | 2 | `#NAME?` | 2 |
| `=LET(ŻAR,LAMBDA(x,x*3),żar(2))` | 6 | `#NAME?` | 6 |

## Changes
- `crates/calc/src/eval.rs`: a `same_name` helper (Unicode case folding) replaces `eq_ignore_ascii_case` in the three lookups of LET/LAMBDA names: evaluating a name, `ISOMITTED`, and a LET variable that shadows a function name (`MAP(…,Λ)`).
- `docs/function-parity.md`: revision row.

Defined names (`Workbook::name`) still compare ASCII-only. I left them alone to keep this change small; happy to follow up if wanted.

Found while working on Polish formula entry (#1883), where a `LET(fałsz;…)` binding is matched by `FAŁSZ`. This PR doesn't depend on #1883.

## Tests
- New `let_lambda_names_ignore_case_in_any_script` in `crates/calc/src/tests.rs`. It fails without the change.
- Locally on Windows: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-calc --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm`.

title: Formula editing: arrow pointing restarts from the edited cell after typing (#1949)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1949.

When you point at cells with the arrow keys while typing a formula, GridCraft kept the pointing cursor (`EditState::point_cell`) after you typed an operator. So in B4, `=` Up Up `+` Up gave `=B2+B1`, because the second reference started from B2 instead of from B4. In Excel, typing ends the pointing, and the next arrow starts again from the cell you edit, which gives `=B2+B3`.

The fix: when the text widget reports a change, `editor_widget` already clears `ed.point` (the reference that the next arrow replaces). Now it also clears `ed.point_cell`, so `point_move` falls back to `ed.cell`. Arrow and click pointing still keep `point_cell` between their own moves, because they edit the text directly and the widget does not report a change for that.

Test: `formula_arrow_pointing_restarts_from_the_edited_cell_after_typing` in `crates/ui-egui/tests/selection.rs` does the steps from the issue (B4, `=` Up Up `+` Up) and expects `=B2+B3`. Without the fix the result is `=B2+B1`.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Arrow-key navigation in formulas now starts from the cell being edited after formula text changes, helping selections move to the expected cell. This also keeps navigation consistent when building a formula with multiple cell references.

title: Get Data (Text/CSV): import into a new sheet of the open workbook instead of replacing it (#1956)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes the first part of #1956: **Data › Get Data (Text/CSV)** closed the open workbook and opened the CSV as a new one. This PR does not touch the other points the issue was split into.

**Cause:** the ribbon button called `open_dialog("open")`, which is File › Open. When `data.getData` / `data.fromTextCsv` ran with no file (the keytip path), they also queued the `"open"` dialog. So the picked file always went through `open_path` and replaced the workbook.

**Fix:** Excel's behaviour. The data goes into a new sheet (named after the file) as a table, and the current workbook stays open.
- `from_csv` (behind `data.getData` and `data.fromTextCsv`) now queues its own `"getData"` dialog.
- The UI handles `"getData"` like this: pick a file with the native picker, then run `data.getData {path}`. That path already imported into a new sheet.
- The ribbon button now runs `data.getData`, the same as its keytip. Both entry points go through one path.
- `Session::execute_headless` counts `"getData"` as a file dialog, the same as `"open"`/`"saveAs"`. Without a file, MCP/CLI calls still fail with "missing `path` or `text`". `file_commands_without_a_file_fail` covers this.

**Scope:** desktop only (macOS, Windows, Linux), where the bug was reported. The web build has no synchronous picker: its picker drops the file into the open-workbook inbox. So there, Get Data still falls back to Open, as before. Importing into the open workbook on the web needs a separate inbox, so it is left for a separate change.

**Test:** `get_data_imports_a_csv_into_the_open_workbook_instead_of_replacing_it` (ui-egui `tests/file_menu.rs`). It types 42 in A1, runs `data.getData` with no file and picks a CSV. Then it checks four things: there is still one workbook, it has two sheets, A1 on the first sheet still holds 42, and the CSV data is on the new active sheet. On main this test fails, because the CSV replaces the workbook.

title: French menus and section-aware percent entry (#1967)
author: meding2904
body:
Rebased onto `main` on 2026-10-22 (merge commit `e104a9e`) and re-scoped: the base rule for #1967 landed upstream in `3a2232c` ("Enter bare numbers in Percentage-formatted cells as percents"), so this PR carries the part that rule misses, plus the French coverage.

## Percent entry: the section the value lands in

Upstream's rule scales when the format code ends in `%`, which is wrong for mixed and conditional formats:

- `0;0%` shows a positive value in its plain first section, so a typed `3` must stay `3`. It was scaled to `0.03` and displayed `0`. A negative `-3` does land in the percent section and becomes `-0.03`.
- `[>=1]0%` compares its condition in the units the section displays (the x100 scale), so the scaled `0.03` still selects it: a typed `3` stays `3%` instead of falling into the plain `0` section.

`numfmt` gains `NumberFormat::is_percent_for(value)` ("is the section this value formats a percentage") and compares a percentage section's condition in its displayed units; `input_to_cell` asks it instead of `ends_with('%')`. The rest of upstream's rule is unchanged: a magnitude below 1 stays a fraction, input with its own format (`3%`, `$3`, dates) and formulas are not scaled, and the rule sits in the one place every text entry goes through, so typing, Ctrl+Enter fill, Replace and pasted text share it.

## French menus

French covers every in-window menu (cell and sheet-tab context menus, filter, ribbon galleries, chart, conditional-format and pivot menus), every dialog title and the Format Cells labels: 652 keys. Switching language repaints the whole window and reloads the font set when the script changes, so open dialogs follow without a restart.

Where upstream translated the same strings independently (`app.ui.language.tr`, `Language::code_list`, the ISO/JIS paper sizes, `color_palette_fixed`), the merge keeps upstream's code and the catalog keeps the keys it adds, deduplicated.

title: Insert/Delete Cells: ask before unmerging merged cells a shift would split, as Excel does
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
Insert Cells or Delete Cells can leave two merged areas on top of each other. From the sample budget workbook: merge `22:24`, merge `F19:F20`, then insert cells at `E8:H11` shifting down. The shift pushes `F19:F20` into `22:24` and the workbook fails its own check with "merges 22:24 and F23:F24 overlap". Delete Cells shifting left does the same. A command-sequence fuzz run found it (seeds 466, 801 and 891).

What Excel does (observed through COM on synthetic workbooks, 23 cases): when a shift would split merged cells it asks "This operation will cause some merged cells to unmerge. Do you wish to continue?". On OK it unmerges every merged area that reaches into the shifted cells but sticks out of their band sideways. Merges within the band's width shift, grow or shrink without a prompt. Merges inside deleted cells vanish.

What changes:
- `home.insertCells` and `home.deleteCells` refuse such a shift unless called with `unmerge: true`. With it, those areas are unmerged in the same undo step.
- The Insert and Delete dialogs catch the refusal, ask, and on OK run the command again with `unmerge: true`.

Tests: an engine test that insert and delete cells unmerge the merges they would split (and let the others shift, grow or shrink), and a UI test that the Insert Cells dialog asks before unmerging. Seeds 466, 801 and 891 fail on main and pass with this change.

title: AutoFill refuses a target that doesn't hold the source in a corner (whole rows into whole columns aborted the app)
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
Filling whole rows into a whole column kills the app. Run `edit.autoFill` with source `2:3` and target `A:A`. GridCraft spends minutes building about 17 billion writes, then aborts on a 24 to 51 GB allocation. The abort is not a panic, so the existing panic guard can't catch it and the window just closes. A command-sequence fuzz run hit it three times (`2:3` into `A:A`, `8:10` into `C:E`, `24:24` into `B:D`).

The size check looked at the source and the target separately (2:3 is 32,768 cells, A:A is 1,048,576, both under the 5M cap). It never looked at how much would be written.

What changes:
- `edit.autoFill` now refuses a target unless it contains the source and shares a corner with it. Targets that share a corner are accepted as before. A diagonal target (both axes, such as `A1:B2` into `A1:D4`) is still accepted and still fills one direction only; Excel tiles the source into the far block instead (`C3:D4`), which is a separate follow-up.
- `fill()` also caps source lanes times steps at the same 5M limit, as a backstop.
- The 5M literals in `auto_fill` and `fill_dir` now use one shared constant.

What Excel does: observed through COM on a synthetic workbook, Excel refuses these shapes (2:3 into A:A, 8:10 into C:E, 24:24 into B:D, H4:H9 into D:F, H4:H9 into H:H, B2:B3 into B1:B5, A1:A5 into A1:A3) and accepts any target that shares a corner with the source.

Tests: `fill::tests::autofill_refuses_targets_that_do_not_extend_the_source` checks nine refused shapes (nothing is written), that corner-sharing targets still fill, and the corner rule directly. Replaying the three fuzz traces, the crashing step is now refused in 0 ms.

title: #1997: insert local time for Ctrl+; and Ctrl+Shift+:
author: meding2904
body:
Fixes #1997.

Rebased onto `main` (`d1db71d`) on 2026-10-22. The only conflict was the `Ctrl+;` arm of `keymap::lookup`, next to the new Ctrl+[ / Ctrl+] precedent and dependent shortcuts, which are kept.

## What changed

`Ctrl+Shift+: ` inserted UTC because the shortcut reused `calc::now_serial()`, which is deliberately UTC for `NOW()`/`TODAY()`. It now reads `chrono::Local`, so the cell gets the wall-clock time the user sees, including DST and a non-UTC timezone. `Ctrl+;` takes the same path, so its date is local too: on Windows and Mac, unshifted `Ctrl+;` is the date and Mac `Command+;` is the time.

Formulas keep their UTC clock.

The old date insertion in `ribbon::shortcut` read the UTC clock and would have won on Windows, so it is gone: `keymap` is now the only place either shortcut is handled.

`chrono` (with `wasmbind`) joins the workspace dependencies so the web build keeps its clock, and `gridcraft-ui-egui` takes it as `{ workspace = true }` like every other shared dependency.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui --lib`: 154 passed, including `local_serial_is_utc_shifted_by_the_offset`, `local_serial_picks_the_local_day_when_utc_is_still_yesterday` and `date_and_time_shortcuts_are_local_on_every_platform` (Ctrl+;, Ctrl+Shift+: and Mac Command+;, on both platforms).
- `cargo check -p gridcraft-ui-egui --all-targets` and `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown` pass, so `chrono`'s wasm clock compiles.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.
- `cargo xtask ci` not run in this checkout: `/usr/bin/link` shadows the MSVC `link.exe`, so the checks above used the `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` toolchain. The shortcut was verified manually in the app on the original revision.
