title: AutoSave writes on a worker thread, and saves an idle window
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
Responds to: a new PR, no issue. Open AutoSave PRs that touch the same code: #972 (save errors and temp files), #1995 and #1549 (remember the AutoSave switch). Open issues #1901 and #1496 are about the switch not staying on, not this.

AutoSave freezes the window. With AutoSave on, the app serialised and wrote the whole workbook inside the UI frame every 2 seconds while the workbook had changes. The window couldn't paint or take input until the save finished. Measured on a release build: 0.3 to 1 s per save at 50k formula cells, about 2 s at 200k, and 8 s or more at 1M.

Second problem: if you edit within 2 seconds of the last AutoSave and then leave the window alone, that edit is never saved. Nothing asks for a frame when the 2 second gate opens. In 4 of 4 runs the second edit was still unsaved after 15 s, so a crash loses it.

What changes:
- The frame takes an Arc snapshot of the workbook (a new engine `SaveJob`) and a worker thread writes it. The document is marked clean only if it still holds that snapshot, so edits made during the write stay unsaved. The browser build has no threads and saves on the same thread as before.
- `file.*` commands and quitting wait for a running save.
- The frame asks for a repaint when the gate opens, so an idle window still saves.
- For agents: `options.autoSave` toggles AutoSave, and `ui.inspect` reports perf.autosaveMs, autosaveWriteMs and autosaves.

Tests: engine (clean documents have no job; the job saves the snapshot and cleans the document; edits during a save stay unsaved; a finished job for a closed or moved document changes nothing) and UI (the command toggles AutoSave; a change inside the gate schedules the save for an idle window; edits during the write stay unsaved; manual save waits for a running AutoSave; no wakeups when nothing is pending).

title: Paste of a whole-column or whole-row copy no longer aborts the app
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
Responds to: a new PR, no issue. Related open PR: #1108 (refuses a cut-paste whose destination doesn't fit; same function, edit.rs). The two overlap in `paste_special`; whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

Copying whole columns or rows and pasting can kill the app. Copy `C:D` (or any whole-sheet selection) and paste at `B8`: GridCraft tried to visit every cell of the copied block, up to the whole sheet. For each cell it re-cut every validation rule and added a one-cell rule, which is quadratic. A command-sequence fuzz run found two cases (seeds 757 and 1688) that aborted on a 34 to 68 GB allocation. The abort is not a panic, so the app just closes.

What changes:
- Paste visits only cells that hold something in the source or the destination. Blank onto blank changes nothing (and with an operation it stays blank, as in Excel, instead of becoming 0).
- Validation is pasted as ranges: the pasted rectangle is cut once out of the destination's rules, and each source rule comes along as one rule over its translated parts.
- Whole columns and rows paste whole, so content further down the destination columns is replaced.
- A paste that doesn't fit on the sheet is refused (whole columns below row 1, whole rows right of column A, a transposed whole column, a block at XFD).
- Paste Link, the one paste that writes every cell, is capped at 1,048,576 cells. Tiled validation is capped at 100,000 ranges.

What Excel does: an Excel 16.0 check showed Paste Special > Validation with Skip Blanks on pastes the rule of a blank source cell that has one and keeps the destination rule under a blank source cell with no rule; with Skip Blanks off the destination rule is cleared. The "doesn't fit" cases (B8, AN17, a transposed C:D, XFD1) are refused.

Tests (crates/engine/src/tests.rs): whole-column paste with validation works on ranges; a paste that doesn't fit is refused; blank cells clear the destination and blank onto blank stays blank; validation covers the pasted area as ranges.…

title: Formulas: Excel's longest legal operator chain (4,096 operands) no longer crashes entry or save
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
Responds to: #916 (flat chain of more than 400 operands is #CALC!) and #1307 item 1 (deep flat chains overflow the stack in Expr::walk). #916's #CALC! was already fixed by merged #484, so this PR does not close it. It fixes what still failed further along. Also see open #1610 and #1340.

Entering Excel's longest legal formula crashes GridCraft. Type `=1+1+...` with 4,096 operands (8,192 characters, exactly Excel's limit, which Excel accepts and calculates) and the app overflows its stack. Saving a chain that long hits the same crash in the XLSX writer. Separately, a plain sum of more than about 64 cells was saved as a dynamic-array formula.

The cause: Expr clone, equality, walk and map recursed once per operand down the left side of the chain.

What changes:
- Expr clone, equality, walk and map follow the left spine in a loop and recurse only into right operands and real nesting.
- XLSX `_xlpm.` prefixing and the implicit-intersection scan follow the spine too. The scan's depth limit of 64 is what wrote long sums as dynamic arrays. They are plain formulas again (ranges in the chain still get array evaluation).
- Evaluate Formula borrows sub-expressions instead of cloning each operator's subtree.
- Spanish formula entry and display no longer refuse chains of more than 256 operands. The leftmost operand of a chain counts at the same depth as the chain, not one deeper.

Tests run on a 1 MiB stack (the Windows main thread) and each fails without the fix: formula (clone, eq, walk, map, adjust at 4,096), calc (401 and 4,096 operands across operators, 1,500 refs), xlsx (long chains written as scalar formulas), engine (set, fill, copy and paste, insert rows and columns, undo and redo, Evaluate Formula, save and reopen), Spanish entry.

title: ui-egui: desktop_theme compiles under clippy off Linux
author: RedBearAK
body:
I'm on macOS with stable Rust 1.99, and `cargo xtask ci` has been failing for me at the clippy step on current main:

```
error: this let-binding has unit value
  --> crates/ui-egui/src/desktop_theme.rs:36:13
   |
36 |             let mut link = Link::default();
```

Off Linux, `Link` is defined as `()`, so the watcher thread ends up binding a unit value and `let_unit_value` fires under `-D warnings`. Linux CI never sees this because there `Link` is the D-Bus connection type.

I first tried a unit struct, but that just moves the problem: clippy then complains about `default_constructed_unit_structs` at the same two call sites. Making `Link` an `Option<()>` on non-Linux targets satisfies both lints, and nothing else needs to change (`read` still ignores its argument, the watcher body is untouched).

With this, all eight `cargo xtask ci` steps pass for me on macOS.

title: Reject unparseable conditional-format formulas (#1999)
author: bfenty
body:
## Problem (#1999)
A conditional-format rule with an unparseable formula was stored as typed — through the API (`home.conditionalFormat`) and the New Rule dialog alike — and Excel then refuses to open the saved file, even in repair mode. Measured repros: expression `=A1>`, cellIs value `=1+`, dataBar threshold `1+`.

title: Percent-cell entry divides bare numbers by 100, like Excel (#1967)
author: bfenty
body:
## Problem (#1967)
Entering `3` into a cell already formatted as Percentage displayed `300%`. Excel divides a bare number by 100 on entry into a percent-formatted cell, so `3` becomes `3%` (stored 0.03).

## Fix
One branch in `input_to_cell` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs`), the single entry path shared by `cell.set` (API) and the in-cell editor. When the cell's **existing** format is a percent format (`NumberFormat::is_percent`) and the input is a bare number (parses via `parse_number_text`, contains no `%`), the stored value is divided by 100.

- A typed `3%` carries its own scale — untouched (and typing `5%` into a General cell isn't double-divided, since the percent format arrives in the same commit via `parsed.format`, which takes the other branch).
- Formulas, text, dates, booleans: not bare numbers, untouched. A formula result is never rescaled.

title: Linux: time out the desktop theme's portal read
author: bmh129
body:
On Linux, "Use system setting" for the theme is driven by `DesktopTheme` (`crates/ui-egui/src/desktop_theme.rs`), which reads the desktop's light/dark choice from the XDG Desktop Portal on a background thread every 4 s. That read is a blocking D-Bus call with **no timeout**, and zbus waits forever by default. So a portal that accepts the call but never answers stalls the watcher's thread on its first read. From then on the theme no longer follows the desktop for the rest of the session, even if the portal recovers.

The UI thread isn't affected, because the read runs on the watcher's own thread, so this is a "theme silently stops following the desktop" bug rather than a freeze. The public one-shot `prefers_dark()` has the same unbounded wait for any caller that uses it.

**The fix**: the session connection is built with a 2 s `method_timeout` (`REPLY`, shorter than the 4 s `POLL`). A timed-out call returns `zbus::Error::InputOutput`, which `read()` already handles by dropping the connection, so the next poll asks again on a fresh one. Nothing else changes; when the portal answers normally, behaviour is identical. `ROADMAP.md`'s progress log has a row for it.

## How it was verified

There's no unit test in this PR: reproducing the hang needs a D-Bus bus with a fake portal on it, which `cargo test` and CI don't have. Instead it was reproduced by hand outside the repo, against the real `gridcraft_ui_egui::desktop_theme` code:

- a private bus ([`busd`](https://github.com/dbus2/busd)) with a stub `org.freedesktop.portal.Desktop` whose `Settings.ReadOne` never replies to its first N calls and answers `prefer-dark` after that
- a probe binary calling `prefers_dark()` and `DesktopTheme::start()` / `take_change()` with `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` pointed at that bus

| Scenario | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `prefers_dark()`, portal never answers | still blocked when killed at 30 s | returns `None` after 2.00 s |
| Watcher, portal hangs only its **first** call | nothi…

title: xtask: `parity --check` accepts a CRLF checkout of the checklist
author: CRBBeesy
body:
## Problem

On Windows with Git's default `core.autocrlf=true` (Git for Windows, and GitHub's
`windows-latest` image), `cargo xtask ci` stops at `parity`:

```text
=== ci: parity ===
  FAIL  parity: D:\a\...\docs/parity-checklist.md is out of date; run `cargo xtask parity`
error: ci failed at `parity`
```

The file is current. `parity --check` reads `docs/parity-checklist.md` and compares it byte for
byte with the generated text, which uses `\n`; the Windows checkout has `\r\n`. The repository has
no `.gitattributes`, so every default Windows checkout gets CRLF. Every other `cargo xtask ci` step
(fmt, clippy, tests, assets, layers, wasm) passed on `windows-latest` at `84acf629`; only `parity`
failed. Working around it needs `git config --global core.autocrlf false` before the checkout.

## Change

- `xtask/src/parity.rs`: a pure `up_to_date(current, generated)` treats CRLF line ends as
  equal to LF. Any other difference is still "out of date". `--check` uses it.
- Unit test `a_crlf_checkout_of_the_current_checklist_is_up_to_date`: the current checklist with
  LF or CRLF is up to date; a stale one is out of date with either line ending.

No change to the generated file or to `cargo xtask parity` (it still writes LF). A
`.gitattributes` rule (`docs/parity-checklist.md text eol=lf`) would also work, but it changes
every contributor's checkout; this keeps the fix inside the check.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p xtask` on Linux: 25 passed (including the new
  `a_crlf_checkout_of_the_current_checklist_is_up_to_date`); `cargo fmt --check` clean.

Prepared with the help of an AI coding agent; the change and its tests were reviewed before
submission.

author: kezmdor

Fixes #2023.

Typing `+5+4` now enters the formula `=+5+4` (result 9), as in Excel. Before, a leading `+` or `-` started a formula only when a letter or `(` came next, so `+A1` worked but `+5+4`, `-5+4` and `--5` stayed text. As in Excel, a `+` or `-` entry that doesn't read as a formula stays text; only `=` entries are refused.

| Typed | Before | After | Excel for the web |
|---|---|---|---|
| `+5+4` | text | `=+5+4`, 9 | `=5+4`, 9 |
| `-5+4` | text | `=-5+4`, -1 | `=-5+4`, -1 |
| `--5` | text | `=--5`, 5 | `=--5`, 5 |
| `- item` | text | `=-item`, #NAME? | #NAME? |
| `+5` | number 5 | unchanged | number 5 |
| `-`, `+` | text | unchanged | text |
| `--`, `-----`, `+5+`, `+49 170 1234567` | text | unchanged | text |
| `'+5+4` | text `+5+4` | unchanged | text `+5+4` |

- `gridcraft_core::parse::starts_formula` says whether an entry is meant as a formula: `=`, or `+`/`-` when the entry isn't a number on its own (`parse_number_text`). It replaces the two hand-synced copies in `input_to_cell` (engine) and `formula_locale::canonical` (UI, Spanish formula language).

title: Row auto-fit: count line breaks only in cells that wrap
author: RedBearAK
body:
I opened a workbook written by a generating library. One column holds notes with line breaks in them, and Wrap Text is off. Excel shows each of those cells on one line, at the default row height. GridCraft opened the same file with every one of those rows several lines tall, showing only the first line of text at the bottom of a tall row.

The cause is in `auto_row_height` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/mod.rs`). It counted the lines in every cell's text, whether the cell wraps or not. In Excel, line breaks only affect row height when the cell wraps. You can check this in Excel: type `a`, a line break, then `b`. With Wrap Text off, Home ▸ Format ▸ AutoFit Row Height gives a one-line row. Turn Wrap Text on and you get two lines.

The fix is about a dozen lines. The quick check for rows that keep the default height no longer treats a line break as a reason to measure, and the measuring code splits text into lines only when the cell wraps. Typing a line break into a cell still turns Wrap Text on, as before, so text typed over several lines still grows its row.

Test added: `line_breaks_grow_a_row_only_when_the_cell_wraps`. It opens a file with an unwrapped multi-line cell and checks that the row keeps the default height. Then it turns wrap on (the row grows), turns it off (back to one line), and types a line break into another cell (the cell wraps and its row grows). The open-time fit tests from #833 pass unchanged, and `cargo xtask ci` is green on my Mac.

Not in this PR: how an unwrapped multi-line cell is drawn. GridCraft shows only the first line, while Excel shows all of the text on one line. That's a separate rendering change in `ui-egui`.

Docs: one line each in the ROADMAP progress log and the `docs/target-app-parity.md` revision history.

title: Text comparison: NFC equals NFD, and accented Latin letters sort next to their base letter
author: nhdai111983
body:
Opened from the `nhdai111983` account. A follow-up PR adds a Vietnamese collation and a Sorting Language setting on top of this one.

### What this changes

GridCraft compared text by lowercasing code points. That has two effects on any text with diacritics, and Vietnamese (where nearly every word has them) hits both all the time:

- **The same text typed two ways is different text.** `ế` (U+1EBF) and `e` + U+0302 + U+0301 look identical, but `=A1=A2` is FALSE, `COUNTIF` and `MATCH` miss one of them, `UNIQUE` and Remove Duplicates keep both, a PivotTable shows two items.
- **Accented letters sort after `z`.** `Ánh` sorts after `Zebra` in Data › Sort, `SORT`, `<`, the AutoFilter list and PivotTable items.

With this change:

- **NFC and NFD are the same text** wherever text is compared for equality: `=`/`<>`, `COUNTIF`/`SUMIF`/`COUNTIFS`/`AVERAGEIF`/`MAXIFS`… (plain-text criteria), `MATCH`/`XMATCH`/`XLOOKUP`/`VLOOKUP` (exact match and binary search), `UNIQUE`, `SWITCH`, D-function field labels, Remove Duplicates, AutoFilter (value list and selection, custom `begins with` / `ends with` / `contains`), Slicers, data validation lists, conditional formatting (duplicate/unique values and the text rules), PivotTables (items, collapsed items), Consolidate labels, Advanced Filter labels and operands, custom sort lists, fill-series lists, and the XLSX PivotTable writer, so what is merged on screen is also merged in the saved file. Case is still ignored, and accents are kept: `Hoà` is not `Hòa`, `a` is not `á`.
- **`EXACT` stays case-sensitive**, but sees NFC and NFD as the same text.
- **Accented letters sort next to their base letter**: `Anh < Ánh < Ảnh < Bình < Zebra`, with the accent as the tie-break (ordered by the combining mark's code point) and `đ` sharing `d`'s primary weight and following it only as a tie-break (`Đào` sorts before `Dũng`). title: Vietnamese collation and a Sorting Language setting (`data.sortLanguage`)
author: nhdai111983
body:
Opened from the `nhdai111983` account. **This builds on the layer-1 PR, #2036** ("Text comparison: NFC equals NFD, and accented Latin letters sort next to their base letter", branch `fix/text-compare-canonical`) and should be sent after, or together with, it. This branch is stacked on that one: its first 9 commits are layer 1's and the last 7 are this PR's, so until layer 1 merges this PR's diff shows both layers, and the Vietnamese order extends the `collate` module that layer 1 adds. Please review and merge layer 1 first; this PR then shrinks to the 7 Vietnamese-collation commits on top of it.

### What this changes

After layer 1, accented Latin letters sort next to their base letter in every language (`Anh < Ánh < Ảnh`). That is the right neutral order, but it is not the Vietnamese alphabet: in Vietnamese `ă`, `â`, `đ`, `ê`, `ô`, `ơ` and `ư` are letters of their own and the tone marks only break ties. This PR adds that order and a setting to choose it.

- **New command `data.sortLanguage {lang?}`** (Data › Sort & Filter › Sorting Language; command search, CLI, control channel and MCP; there is no ribbon control yet). Without `lang` it reports the current language; with `lang` it sets it and returns `{lang}`. `vi`, `vi-VN`, `VI_vn`… select Vietnamese; any other tag (and the default) is the language-neutral Root order from layer 1, reported as an empty tag. **The default is unchanged: nothing behaves differently until someone sets `vi`.**
- **Vietnamese order** (the CLDR `vi` standard): `a ă â b c d đ e ê g h i k l m n o ô ơ p q r s t u ư v x y`. Tones are a second-level difference in the order none, huyền, hỏi, ngã, sắc, nặng: `ma < mà < mả < mã < má < mạ`. So `Hoà` (tone on `a`) sorts before `Hòa` (tone on `o`), `Đào` sorts after every `D…`, and `Hoà` is never equal to `Hòa`. Equality does not depend on the language: only the order of unequal text changes.

title: Fix WebGL startup on devices with lower GPU limits
author: mbaksa
body:
## Summary

Fix WebGL startup failures on devices with lower GPU limits by adapting the requested `wgpu` device limits to the capabilities reported by the GPU adapter.

## Problem

On an Android 10 tablet with a PowerVR Rogue GE8322 GPU, GridCraft fails to initialize even though WebGL2 is supported by the browser.

The startup error is:

```text
GridCraft failed to start:
JsValue("Limit 'max_inter_stage_shader_variables' value 15 is better than allowed 14")
```

Forcing the WebGL backend using `?webgl` does not resolve the issue.

## Solution

Wrap the existing `wgpu` device descriptor callback and adjust its required limits using `or_worse_values_from(&adapter.limits())`.

This prevents `wgpu` from requesting GPU limits that exceed the adapter's reported capabilities, while preserving the existing configuration where supported.

The change is limited to the web runner initialization and does not require modifying `eframe` or `wgpu`.

## Related issues

This fix is based on the solution proposed in [VectorCraft #2105](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/issues/2105), where the same approach was used to address GPU limit compatibility issues on a Raspberry Pi 5.

The issue also reports that the solution successfully allowed ArtCraft Launcher to run on the same hardware.

Similar GPU limit errors have been reported in [ArtCraft Launcher #109](https://github.com/storytold/craft-launcher/issues/109) and [LightCraft #862](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/issues/862).

Credit to the author of VectorCraft #2105 for the original solution.

## Testing

**Test device:**
- Android 10
- Unisoc SC9863A
- PowerVR Rogue GE8322
- Browser reports WebGL2 support

**Before:** GridCraft fails to initialize with the 15/14 shader variable limit error.

**After:** GridCraft successfully initializes and displays its interface.

The fix was tested with a locally served WASM build.

Further testing of individual rendering features and additional GPU configurations may be useful.

title: IME: the first keystroke of a composition no longer lands in the cell
author: alphazw
body:
## Problem

With a CJK input method active (reproduced with Wubi), typing into a cell that is **not** in edit mode sends the first keystroke straight into the cell instead of the IME. Entering 张 (Wubi `xta`) writes `x` into the cell and the input method only ever receives `ta`, so the character cannot be composed; the user has to delete `x` and retype.

- Plain ASCII typing works, because it needs no composition.
- Double-clicking into a cell works, because `begin_edit(None, …)` opens the editor without seeding it.
- The bug only shows on the **first** keystroke that starts a new edit.

## Root cause

`keyboard()` in `crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs` handled `egui::Event::Text` by calling `app.begin_edit(Some(text), false)`, i.e. it seeded the in-cell editor with the raw keystroke.

In egui 0.36 the IME is only enabled for whichever widget publishes `PlatformOutput::ime` during that frame, and only a focused `TextEdit` did that. The in-cell `TextEdit` opens *after* this handler has already consumed the keystroke, so at the moment the first key arrives the IME is disabled: the OS delivers it as `Event::Text`, it is written into the cell, and the first character of the composition is lost. Subsequent keys reach the IME, which is why the observable symptom is "the first character leaked".

## Fix

`crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs`, `keyboard()`:

- Every frame the grid owns input on an **editable** cell (not a picture cell), publish `PlatformOutput::ime` anchored to that cell (a merged range uses the whole range's rect), so the first keystroke is routed through composition instead of arriving as raw text.
- No publishing happens when the active cell isn't editable, which leaves `ime = None` (IME off) — no IME state leaks into dialogs or menus.
- Handle `egui::Event::Ime(ImeEvent::Commit(text))` by opening the editor with the committed text and placing the caret at its end. `Preedit` and the other IME notifications are ignored so nothing is seeded mid-composition.

title: fix: use GNOME title bar on Wayland
author: Monieswaran
body:
## Problem
On Ubuntu GNOME (Wayland), GridCraft's window gets a bare dark strip with square minimize/maximize/close glyphs and no title, above GridCraft's own title row. WordCraft on the same desktop gets GNOME's normal title bar. Related: #54, #655, #244. Overlaps #1288 (same approach); see notes below.

## Root cause
GNOME's compositor (Mutter) draws no server-side decorations for Wayland clients, so winit must draw them client-side. eframe depends on winit with `default-features = false`, which drops `wayland-csd-adwaita`, so winit uses smithay-client-toolkit's `FallbackFrame`: a plain strip with square buttons and no title. WordCraft avoids this by running through XWayland by default, where Mutter draws its themed title bar.

## Fix
`apps/gridcraft/src/main.rs`: `prefer_x11()` picks X11 (XWayland) through eframe's `event_loop_builder` hook (`EventLoopBuilderExtX11::with_x11`) only when all of these hold:
- `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP` contains `GNOME` (e.g. `ubuntu:GNOME`)
- `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is set (X11 sessions are unchanged)

title: Localization: Hebrew interface and bidirectional text
author: ARIKBAR
body:
## Summary

Hebrew support for GridCraft: a Hebrew interface and **bidirectional text** everywhere text is drawn.

Before this, Hebrew rendered wrongly. epaint's shaper guessed right-to-left for each Hebrew *font run* and reversed it, but nothing reordered the runs, so:

- words came out in the wrong order (the formula bar showed `עולם שלום` for `שלום עולם`)
- numbers and Latin words inside Hebrew were reversed (`120` → `021`, `ABC 123` → `321 CBA`)
- glyph order no longer matched character order, which breaks the caret

### Bidirectional layout (vendored epaint)
`vendor/epaint` is epaint 0.36.2 patched in via `[patch.crates-io]`, and excluded from the workspace. `VENDORED.md` lists exactly what changed:
- Shaping always runs in logical order. A new pass runs the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm (UAX #9, via `unicode-bidi`) on each laid-out row that holds right-to-left text.
- Glyphs keep their logical order in `Row::glyphs`, so cursor indices, selection and copying are unchanged. Only their x positions move to visual places.
- Clusters (a letter and its niqqud) move as one unit. Brackets mirror inside RTL runs.
- New field `Glyph::rtl`. `Row::x_offset` puts the caret on the leading edge of RTL characters, and `Row::char_at` hit-tests rows whose glyph x order isn't monotonic.
- Horizontal alignment measures bidi rows by their visual extent.
- Rows without RTL text take exactly the old code path. All 47 epaint tests still pass.

This fixes cells, the formula bar, the in-cell editor, the ribbon and dialogs at once. When egui gets bidi support upstream, the vendored crate can be dropped.

### Right-to-left grids (vendored egui)
`vendor/egui` is egui 0.36.2, patched in the same way as epaint, for one addition: `Grid::right_to_left(bool)`, off by default. When it is on, the columns run from the right edge with the first column rightmost, each cell aligns right, and the cells get a right-to-left parent, so rows and check boxes inside a cell follow. The column cursor still …

title: Word-wrap-aware automatic row height (#1969)
author: bfenty
body:
## Problem (#1969)
`auto_row_height` counted a wrapped cell's lines as total-text-width ÷ column-width, as if words could split anywhere. The grid word-wraps whole words (egui `LayoutJob`), so every drawn line ends early at the last word that fits — a narrow column needs more lines than the estimate, and the row cut off the tail of the text.

## Fix
`wrapped_line_count` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/mod.rs`: a greedy word-wrap simulation over the same `approx_text_width` character estimates — words that don't fit move to the next line whole, a word wider than the column fills the current line then breaks mid-word across lines (what egui does), and inter-word spaces are counted. Multi-line (Alt+Enter) text runs the simulation per line, as before.

## Tests
`crates/engine/tests/wrap_row_height.rs`:
- `wrapped_row_fits_word_wrapped_lines` — six-char words in a 10-char column: word wrap needs 4 lines, the old estimate said 3. Fails on main.
- `issue_repro_nasa_sentence` — the issue's exact NASA sentence in a 12-char column. Fails on main.

Full `gridcraft-engine` suite green, clippy 0 warnings, fmt clean.

title: In-cell editor honors Wrap Text (#1970)
author: bfenty
body:

title: XIRR counts a blank cash flow as 0 instead of returning #VALUE!
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
Responds to: a new PR, no issue.

A cash-flow column with unused rows made XIRR return `#VALUE!` where Excel returns the rate. I hit it opening a workbook whose returns schedule has unused blank rows at the end: GridCraft showed `#VALUE!` in four XIRR cells (and two cells that subtract them), and Excel shows the rates.

What changes (`dated_flows` in `crates/functions/src/financial.rs`):
- XIRR: a blank value counts as 0, and a blank date is ignored when its value is blank or 0. A nonzero value with no date is `#NUM!`.
- XNPV: it was already `#VALUE!` for blanks. It now returns what Excel does: `#NUM!` for a blank value, and `#NUM!` for a blank date next to a blank or 0 value (`#VALUE!` next to a nonzero one).

What Excel does: observed on a synthetic workbook, five rows with -10000, 2750, 4250, 3250 and a varying last row.

| Last row | XIRR | XNPV |
|---|---|---|
| blank value, date present | 0.033791 (same as a 0) | `#NUM!` |
| 0 value, date present | 0.033791 | -382.66 |
| blank value, blank date | 0.033791 | `#NUM!` |
| 0 value, blank date | 0.033791 | `#NUM!` |
| nonzero value, blank date | `#NUM!` | `#VALUE!` |
| text value, date present | `#VALUE!` | not observed |

Test: `blank_cash_flows_follow_excel_for_xirr_and_xnpv` covers each row above.

title: Skip filter-hidden rows when deleting, clearing and copying a selection
author: CBurgessTSU
body:
## Problem

With a filter applied, a selection that spans the hidden rows acted on them too. Deleting rows, clearing cells, or copying and pasting changed or duplicated data the user could not see. Excel only touches the rows that are still showing.

## What changed

All changes are in the engine crate (`crates/engine/src/cmd/`).

- **Delete Rows** (`sheet.rs`): removes only the visible rows of the selection. Two small helpers split a row range into the runs a filter has not hidden.
- **Clear Contents / Clear All** (`edit.rs`): leave filtered-out rows alone. An explicit `range` or `cell` parameter still acts on exactly what it names, so scripted calls keep working as before.
- **Copy then paste** (`edit.rs`): filtered-out rows are left out of the pasted block, so the pasted block is shorter than the copied range. Merged areas are not copied when rows were skipped, because their positions no longer line up. Cut is unchanged.
- Rows hidden by hand or collapsed in a group are **not** treated as filtered: they are still copied and deleted like any other row, as in Excel.

## Tests

Four new tests in `data.rs`, one per behaviour above:

- deleting the selected rows of a filtered range leaves the hidden rows
- pasting a copy of a filtered range leaves out the hidden rows
- clearing the selection (both Clear Contents and Clear All) leaves the hidden rows
- rows hidden by hand are copied and deleted normally (control case)

title: Clear the edited marker after a web save is written (#2050)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #2050.

On the web, Save (Ctrl+S on an untitled workbook), Save As and the Backstage Download all end in `open_dialog("saveAs")`, which hands the XLSX bytes to the browser's `download` service. Nothing told the app when the browser had written the file, so the document kept its "– Edited" title after a successful `showSaveFilePicker` write.

What changed:

- `Services` gets an optional `delivered` queue (`Delivered`, the same shared-queue shape as `Inbox`). The web shell pushes the file name onto it once the file is really written: after the picker's writable closes, or after the anchor-download fallback (browsers without the picker, or a picker failure that falls back) starts the download. A cancelled picker pushes nothing, so the workbook stays unsaved.
- `SheetApp` remembers each workbook it handed to `download` (name, document uid, workbook snapshot). When the name comes back, the new `Session::mark_saved` sets that document's saved state to the snapshot. Edits made while the file was being written are not in the snapshot, so the document stays "Edited" in that case. A newer save of the same name replaces an older pending one, so a cancelled save can't be matched to a later written one.
- Desktop is unchanged: it saves through `pick_save` and `file.save`, which already clear the marker.

Test: `web_save_clears_the_edited_marker_once_the_download_is_written` in `crates/ui-egui/tests/file_menu.rs` checks four things: the document stays dirty until the write is confirmed, an edit made during the write stays unsaved, a confirmed save leaves it clean, and a cancelled save followed by a written one still ends clean.

title: Use scientific notation when number_to_text rounds up to 1e15
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/core/src/value.rs:354-367` (no existing issue): number_to_text prints 16 digits for numbers just below 1e15 that round up to 1e15.

## Cause
number_to_text checked for scientific notation on the unrounded magnitude. A value just below 1e15, such as 999999999999999.9, took the fixed-point path. Rounding to 15 significant digits there produced the 16-digit text "1000000000000000".

## Fix
After the existing scientific check, number_to_text now rounds the magnitude to 15 significant digits. If the rounded value reaches 1e15, it returns the scientific text. 999999999999999.9 now gives "1E+15", matching 1e15 itself.

## Verified
- Regression test `value::tests::number_text_rounds_up_to_scientific_boundary`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p gridcraft-core number_text_rounds_up_to_scientific_boundary`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The fixed-point formatting for other values and the small-magnitude (below 1e-9) scientific handling are unchanged. I did not test values that round up across other power-of-ten boundaries.

title: Packaging: pin the signing client and appimagetool, and check their hashes
author: aiongg
body:
Both release tools were downloaded at whatever version was current, with no check. They are now pinned the same way as in designcraft:

- `packaging/windows/sign.ps1` downloads Microsoft.Trusted.Signing.Client 1.0.95 from NuGet and stops unless its SHA-256 is `3bfcf1e0a3cb42af1692f0a8ed45c15de070c2de86f28a59b2795d904d8a920f`. The working folder gets a random name and must not exist yet.
- `packaging/linux/package.sh` downloads appimagetool 1.9.1 instead of the `continuous` build and checks its SHA-256 for x86_64 or aarch64, both after the download and when it reuses a cached copy. The cached file name includes the version. Setting `APPIMAGETOOL` or having `appimagetool` on `PATH` still skips the download. An architecture with no pinned tool (riscv64) stops with exit 2 and says to set `APPIMAGETOOL`.
- `package.sh` also pins the AppImage runtime (type2-runtime `20251108`, SHA-256 checked the same way) and passes it with `--runtime-file`, so appimagetool no longer embeds the unchecked `continuous` runtime. `APPIMAGE_RUNTIME` overrides it; without a pinned runtime the script stops with exit 2.

## Checks

- `bash -n` and `shellcheck` on `packaging/linux/package.sh`: pass.
- `package.sh --skip-build --formats appimage` with stub binaries on x86_64: fresh download, cached reuse, a corrupted cached runtime (fails the check), riscv64 without overrides (exit 2 for the tool, then for the runtime), and relative `APPIMAGE_RUNTIME`. Both runtime hashes match the `20251108` release files.
- `sign.ps1`: reviewed against designcraft's script (no PowerShell available to run it). The package hash was checked against the 1.0.95 download from NuGet.

title: Home with frozen columns goes to the first unfrozen column (fixes #2044)
author: dantebertuzzi
body:
Fixes #2044.

## Cause
`Key::Home` in `crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs` always selected column A. With frozen columns, A lives in the frozen pane and is always visible, so `ensure_visible` had nothing to scroll: the scrolling pane stayed at the far-away column (e.g. BB) and Home looked like it did nothing.

## Fix
Like Excel, Home now goes to the first unfrozen column (`freeze.1`), the same rule Ctrl+Home already follows, and the pane scrolls back to it. Without frozen panes it still goes to column A.

## Tests

title: Right-click on a chart opens the chart's menu, not the cell's (fixes #2067)
author: dantebertuzzi
body:
Fixes #2067.

## Cause
In `interact` (`crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs`):
- The right-click handler never hit-tested objects, so right-clicking a chart opened the context menu of the cell under it (the "menu for L11" case).
- The object block grabbed an object on `resp.drag_started()`, which fires for **any** button. A right press that moved a little started dragging the chart and returned before the right-click handler, so no menu opened (the "does nothing" case).

## Fix
- Right-clicking (or right-pressing and wobbling) a chart, picture, shape or slicer selects it and opens a new object menu instead of the cell menu: **Delete**, plus **Select Data…** and **Format Chart Area…** for charts. They reuse `object.delete`, the `selectData` dialog and the `formatChart` pane, the same actions the Chart Design ribbon uses.

- The object menu blocks ribbon keytips like the other grid menus. The two new labels have pt and de translations.

- A right-click on a chart, still or with a 20 px wobble, selects the chart and opens its menu. The cell menu stays closed and the chart doesn't move.
- Delete in the menu removes the chart.
- A right-click outside the chart still opens the cell menu.

On `main` the same right-click opens the cell menu and leaves the chart unselected. `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui` pass.

title: Ribbon: group names under each group, no card around the commands
author: dantebertuzzi
body:
## What
- **Group names** under each ribbon group, as in Excel. The Home tab shows Clipboard · Font · Alignment · Number · Styles · Cells · Editing, and Insert, Draw, Page Layout, Formulas, Data, Review, View and Table Design are named too. Automate and Chart Design have a single group and stay unnamed.

- `sep(ui)` records the x of each separator for the frame. - Names are looked up as `Ribbon group|<name>`, so they don't collide with button labels such as "Outline" or "Show". pt-BR names are added; the other languages fall back to English.

title: fix(ui): Esc and Enter close a data validation alert, not the edit behind it, and the keyboard goes back to the entry (#2089)
author: vedran-dobos
body:
Fixes #2089.

A data validation alert (the general message box) is drawn over the cell editor, which stays open so the entry can be fixed. The editor read Enter and Esc first, so the first Esc cancelled the edit behind the alert and only the second closed it; Enter re-tried the entry and the alert came back. After the alert closed, the keyboard wasn't back in the entry, so it couldn't be fixed without clicking the cell. Now the editor leaves its keys alone while a message is open over it, so Esc and Enter close the alert (like its OK button), and closing it puts the keyboard back in the entry. The message, the button and everything else are unchanged.

## What changed
- **ui-egui** `formula_bar.rs` `editor_widget`: the editor's own key handling (Enter, Tab, Esc and the rest) is skipped while `app.message` is set. - **ui-egui** `widgets.rs` `message_box`: closing it asks the open editor for focus again (`EditState::request_focus`).

Both also apply to any other message shown over the editor (for example a formula the interface language can't read); that case wasn't tested separately.

## Tests
`crates/ui-egui/tests/validation_alert.rs`, with real key events (A1 = 5, whole number 1–10):
- `esc_closes_a_validation_alert_and_leaves_the_entry`: one Esc closes the alert, `50` is still being edited and typing `9` gives `509`; the next Esc cancels the edit and A1 keeps 5. Fails on `main` (the alert is still shown after the first Esc), and without the focus change (typing goes nowhere).
- `enter_closes_a_validation_alert_and_leaves_the_entry`: Enter closes the alert, the entry stays, and Backspace, Backspace, `8`, Enter puts 8 in A1. Fails on `main` (the alert comes back), and without the focus change.

Locally on Windows 11: `cargo xtask ci` (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm, parity, keytips) passes on `main` a2cc4b4 + this commit, 1658 tests, 0 failed. Clippy ran with #2020's fix applied locally, since `main` fails `clippy -D warnings` off Linux (`desktop_theme.rs`)…

title: Dialogs: OK and Cancel in a row, so form dialogs fit their content
author: dantebertuzzi
body:
## What happens
Every dialog built with `Dialog::form` is as tall as the screen, with OK and Cancel floating halfway down and a large empty area under them. Examples: Home › Conditional Formatting › Highlight Cells Rules › Greater Than…, Define Name, Remove Duplicates and Text to Columns. On a 1000 px window, OK sat 356 points under the last option of Greater Than….

## Cause
`ok_cancel` (`crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs`) placed the buttons with `ui.with_layout(Layout::right_to_left(Align::Center), …)` directly in the window. A layout added that way takes all the remaining height the window offers, the window auto-sizes to it, and `Align::Center` centres the buttons in it.

## Fix
The right-to-left layout now sits inside `ui.horizontal(…)`, so the row is only as tall as the buttons. The dialogs shrink to their content, and the buttons stay right-aligned under the last field. This is the only change: the dialogs' fields, labels and behaviour are untouched, so it doesn't collide with #870 (custom conditional-format styles) or #669 (dialog translation), which edit those dialogs' contents.

`docs/ui-parity.md` revision history is updated.

## Tests
`crates/ui-egui/tests/dialog_button_row.rs` opens Greater Than… and checks that OK sits less than 40 points under the last style option. It fails on `main` (356 points) and passes with the fix.

Offscreen snapshots of Greater Than…, New Name, Text to Columns and Remove Duplicates in pt-BR dark: all fit their content. `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui` pass. Checked in the desktop app on Linux.

title: Number Stored as Text: green indicator, warning button and Convert to Number (#1994)
author: dantebertuzzi
body:
Part of #1994: the first of the three problems the triage comment split it into, the indicator and Convert to Number. The background error-checking options and the XLSX `ignoredErrors` round trip, with Ignore Error, are left for their own tickets.

## What happens
A number stored as text, such as a bank export or a value typed after an apostrophe, looks like any other text and is skipped by SUM and AVERAGE, so totals come out wrong with no hint. Excel flags it with a green corner triangle and offers Convert to Number.

## Change
- **core:** `parse::number_stored_as_text(&str) -> Option<f64>` flags text that would be a number if typed: signs, thousands separators, currency, percent, exponent, and one parenthesised negative. Dates, times and fractions kept as text are **not** flagged, as in Excel (they belong to other rules), and neither are words, blanks, booleans or error text.
- **engine:**
  - `cmd::formulas::number_stored_as_text(&Cell)` covers constants only, not formula results.
  - **`formulas.convertToNumber {range?}`** converts every flagged cell in the range or selection and keeps each cell's format. It is one undo step and returns `{converted}`.
- **ui:**
  - A green triangle in the top-left corner of flagged cells, painted beside the comment indicator. It is hidden in Show Formulas view.
  - With a flagged cell active, a warning button sits beside it: left of the cell, or right of it when that would cover the row headings. Its menu shows "Number Stored as Text" and **Convert to Number**, which runs on the selection.

title: Fonts: a cell font named in another language matches its installed font (fixes #1898)
author: chessive
body:
Fixes #1898.

## What was wrong
Korean Excel saves a cell's font under its Korean name (`<name val="맑은 고딕"/>` for Malgun Gothic). The font scan kept one family name per face (`english_or_first()`), so 맑은 고딕, 굴림, 바탕 and the rest were never found and those cells were drawn in the default face. Matching alone would not have fixed it: `installed_among` returned the catalog's name, so the family was bound as `fnt:Malgun Gothic:nn` while `cell_family` looks up `fnt:맑은 고딕:nn`.

## What changed
All in `crates/ui-egui/src/fonts.rs`:
- `Face` gets `names`: the English family name first, then the typographic (ID 16) and legacy (ID 1) family names in every language, deduped and capped at 16. `family` stays the English name, so the font list doesn't change.
- `faces_of` and `installed_among` match any of those names. `installed_among` now returns the name as the workbook spells it, so the binding uses the key `cell_family` looks up.
- Names dedupe exactly rather than case-folded, since role keys are built from the cell's exact string. A workbook that uses both `Malgun Gothic` and `맑은 고딕` binds both.
- Font data is keyed by file path and face index instead of by family, so a family bound under two names loads its file once.
- If two families claim one name, the family whose English name it is wins, else the first face by path. The scan's directory order no longer decides it.

Thanks to @Hamza0101 for checking the approach against main. The second and third of their points are covered by the tests below.

## Testing
- New unit tests in `fonts.rs`. A small helper builds a font with only a `name` table, so these run without Korean fonts installed:
  - `a_face_keeps_its_family_names_in_every_language`: English and Korean names, and ID 16 plus ID 1 (`Noto Sans KR` / `Noto Sans KR Medium`).
  - `a_name_table_full_of_names_is_capped`
  - `a_family_is_found_by_any_of_its_names`
  - `a_name_two_families_claim_has_a_fixed_owner`
  - `a_legacy_name_picks_its_own_face_out_of_the_family`

title: data: Get Data (Text/CSV) opens an import dialog like Excel's
author: webglobepl
body:
Data ▸ Get Data (Text/CSV) used to open the picked file as a separate workbook. It now opens an **Import Text/CSV** dialog shaped like Excel's From Text/CSV and loads the data into the current workbook.

**Dialog**
- **Delimiter**: detected (comma, semicolon or tab, with the detected one shown) or chosen.
- **Decimal separator**: detected (a `;` file is read with decimal commas, the European convention) or chosen: dot or comma.
- **Data Type Detection**: based on the first 200 rows (Excel's default), the entire dataset, or not at all.
- **My data has headers**: off, the first row is data and the columns are `Column1`, `Column2`…
- **Preview** with a format per column: General (shows what was detected), Text, Number, Date, or Do not import column.
- **Load** puts the data on a new sheet named after the file, as a table.

A workbook (`.xlsx`, `.xls`, `.xlsb`, `.ods`) picked here opens as File ▸ Open would. The web shell has no path picker and keeps the old behaviour. File ▸ Open of a `.csv` is unchanged (it opens the file as a workbook, as in Excel).

**Engine** (`crates/engine/src/cmd/text_import.rs`)

title: Use chrono instead of hand-rolled UTC conversion
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary

GridCraft carried hand-rolled copies of Howard Hinnant's `civil_from_days` /
`days_from_civil` and hand-written `is_leap` / `days_in_month` (the `146_097`
/ `719_468` magic numbers and the leap-year rule). This routes the underlying
proleptic-Gregorian conversion and the leap-year/month-length helpers through
the `chrono` crate instead, added once as a workspace dependency
(`default-features = false`, `std` only — wasm-safe, and the existing
`js_sys`-based browser-clock paths are untouched). All output is byte-for-byte
unchanged.

Follow-up to storytold/cadcraft#1785 (reference PR storytold/cadcraft#1789).

Functions replaced and their formats:

- `apps/gridcraft/src/logging.rs` — `timestamp`
  (`2026-10-08T07:59:17.728Z`, UTC, ms; pre-1970 clamped to the epoch). Deleted
  the private `civil_from_days`.
- `crates/core/src/date.rs` — `days_from_civil` (date → days since 1970) and
  `civil_from_days` (days since 1970 → (y, m, d)) now use
  `chrono::NaiveDate` (`from_ymd_opt` / `num_days_from_ce` /
  `from_num_days_from_ce_opt`); `is_leap` and `days_in_month` are derived from
  `NaiveDate` (`days_in_month` still returns `0` for an out-of-range month).
- `crates/functions/src/financial.rs` — dropped the duplicate local `is_leap`
  in favour of `gridcraft_core::date::is_leap`.

**Spreadsheet serial-date semantics are kept exactly.** The Excel 1900
fictitious leap day (serial 60 = 1900-02-29), the 1899-12-30 / 1904-01-01
serial offsets, Excel's own weekday numbering and the 1900/1904 date systems
all keep their explicit special cases in `serial_from_ymd`,
`datetime_from_serial` and `days_in_month_in` — chrono only backs the plain
Gregorian day-number ↔ date conversion those build on. Each converted helper
keeps a small proleptic-Gregorian fallback for dates outside
`chrono::NaiveDate`'s range (year ≤ 0 or > 262143), so nothing the old code
accepted changes or panics.

title: Basis 0 securities functions: end of February to a 31st is 31 days
author: Bortlesboat
body:
## What was broken

Under basis 0 (US 30/360), the securities functions counted the end of February to a 31st as 30 days. Excel counts it as 31, the same way YEARFRAC's basis 0 does (and `date.rs` already does for YEARFRAC). For example `COUPDAYBS(DATE(2008,3,31), DATE(2011,2,28), 1, 0)` gave 30, Excel gives 31; `ACCRINTM(DATE(2007,2,28), DATE(2007,3,31), 0.1, 1000, 0)` gave 8.33, Excel gives 8.61.

## Root cause

`days360` in `financial.rs` moved an end-of-February start to the 30th *before* checking whether a 31st end date should drop to the 30th, so the end date got moved too. The fix runs that check against the original start day.

Through the shared day count this affects COUPDAYBS and COUPDAYSNC (and so PRICE, YIELD, DURATION, MDURATION), DISC, PRICEDISC, YIELDDISC, INTRATE, RECEIVED, ACCRINTM, PRICEMAT, YIELDMAT, AMORLINC and AMORDEGRC.

ACCRINT and the odd-period functions keep their old count for their coupon periods. They already disagree with Excel in other ways, and switching them to the new rule fixed some cases and broke others, so I left them for a separate fix rather than mixing that in here.

## How I tested it

- I compared about 15,700 generated formulas against Excel (Microsoft 365 on Windows, evaluated black-box). Before this change, about 400 basis-0 results differed from Excel. After it, none of those differ, and nothing that matched Excel before stopped matching (ACCRINT and ODDFPRICE/ODDLPRICE come out exactly the same as before).
- New test `financial::tests::basis_0_after_end_of_february` uses Excel's values. It fails on main (`got 30, expected 31`) and passes with the fix.
- `cargo test --locked -p gridcraft-functions`: 126 passed.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --locked -p gridcraft-functions --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

I also added a row to the revision history in `docs/function-parity.md`.

title: Find and Replace: replace the text a wildcard pattern matches (#2108)
author: luigiPinna
body:
Fixes #2108.

## Cause
`edit.replace` decides whether a cell matches with the wildcard matcher (`matches`, which reads `*`, `?` and `~` when the pattern holds `*` or `?`), then rewrote the cell with `str::replace` / `replace_ci`, which look for the pattern text literally. A cell like `10.0.0.1, fe80::1` matched `,*`, was counted in `replaced`, and kept its text.

## Fix
`crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs`: when the pattern holds `*` or `?` (the same test `matches` uses), Replace now rewrites each match, left to right and without overlaps. A `*` takes as few characters as it can, except a trailing `*`, which takes the rest of the text: the rules @iluebbe measured in Excel 365 in #1455. `~` escapes work as in Find (`wildcard` and the new code share the tokenizer). Case-insensitive matching folds one char to one char, as `criteria.rs` does since f8983e2, so match positions stay those of the cell text. A cell is counted only when a match was replaced.

When a start fails after reaching a `*`, the scan stops: what follows the star can't be placed from any later start either. Without that, a 32,767-character cell with no match took ~0.4 s (`a*b` over `aaa…`); with it, under 1 ms (release build, M1 Pro).

## Verified
- `replace_with_wildcards_replaces_the_matched_text` takes the Replace rows of #1455's Excel table that use `*` or `?` (`h*o`, `l*`, `a?b`, `~*`, `?` on `İstanbul`) plus the #2108 shape (`,*` → nothing). `wildcard_replace_follows_match_case` covers `matchCase`. Both fail on `main` (cell unchanged) and pass with the fix.
- `wildcard_replace_scans_past_a_start_that_fails_before_its_star` pins the early stop.
- `gridcraft-cli run` with the #2108 shape: `10.0.0.1, fe80::1` → `10.0.0.1`.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo xtask assets`, `layers` and `wasm` pass. `cargo xtask ci` stops at clippy on `crates/ui-egui/src/desktop_theme.rs:36` (`let_unit_value`, new in Rust 1.99; file not touched here). Clippy `-D warnings` is clean on `gridcraft-engine`…

title: Desktop theme: let clippy pass off Linux, where Link is ()
author: Aimarmndz
body:
## Summary

`cargo xtask ci` fails at the clippy step on macOS (and any non-Linux host) on current `main`:

error: this let-binding has unit value

title: PivotTable Fields pane: scan the source once per change, not every frame
author: Aimarmndz
body:
Part of #2113 (the freeze). The empty report after opening a `refreshOnLoad="1"` file, the second problem described there, is not addressed here.

## Problem

`pivot_pane::show` runs on every frame and called `pivot.fields` each time the active cell was inside a PivotTable report. `pivot.fields` reads the whole source list and collects distinct labels for every field, so with a large source every frame paid a full scan and the window looked frozen.

## Change

Cache the `pivot.fields` answer in `GridState`, keyed by `(doc uid, revision, pivot name)`, following the existing Page Break Preview cache (`GridState::pages`). Any undoable edit, undo or redo bumps `DocState::revision`, so the pane refreshes after edits to the source or the pivot layout and stays cached otherwise.

Known limit: `formulas.calculateNow` / `formulas.calculateSheet` are not undoable and don't bump the revision, so volatile formulas in the source can leave the tooltip samples stale until the next edit. The field list and areas only change through undoable commands.

## Verified

- New test `pivot_fields_pane_reuses_its_field_list_until_the_workbook_changes` (`crates/ui-egui/tests/interaction.rs`): replaces the cached list with a sentinel and checks repaints show it, then that an edit and an undo bring the real list back. It fails on `main` and passes here.
- Release build on macOS, synthetic 250,000 x 20 CSV source, PivotTable inserted over it with the pane open, `frameMs` from `ui.inspect` every 2 s:

| | first frame | following frames |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | 2,411 ms | 2,374 – 2,445 ms |
| this branch | 2,528 ms | 0.41 – 0.92 ms |

- `cargo xtask ci` passes all 8 steps (1661 tests). Note: on macOS, `main` fails clippy in `desktop_theme.rs` regardless of this change; I ran the gate with that separate fix (#2141) applied locally and did not include it here.

## Not in this change

- `pivot.fields` itself is unchanged, so the first frame (and the first after each edit) still pays one full scan.…

title: View: ふりがな表示 (phonetic guide display)
author: midasdf
body:
## What this adds

**Stacked on #1692 (branch `jp/phonetic-runs`).** This branch is based on that branch, so the PR shows #1692's two commits as well as this one; the ふりがな表示 feature is the last commit (`View: ふりがな表示 (phonetic guide display)`). Merge #1692 first and this branch rebases onto `main` unchanged — only the last commit is new here.

#1692 made XLSX keep Japanese phonetic runs (`<rPh>` offsets/readings and `<phoneticPr>`) through open + save, but nothing displayed them. This adds Excel's **表示 › ふりがな表示**:

- `display::phonetic_text(wb, sheet, cell)` finds the runs the workbook keeps for the cell's string (`Workbook::phonetics`, keyed by the shared string's text) and joins their readings in document order. Formula cells and cells without readings show nothing.
- **Toggle:** `view.furigana` — `{on?: bool}`, toggles when omitted, returns `{"on": bool}`; **off by default**. It is an application option saved with the other preferences (`prefs.json`), like View › Formula Bar, and never edits the document. The View tab's Show group gets a **Furigana** checkbox; the label is translated in every interface catalog (日本語: ふりがな表示).
- **Screen (normal and Page Layout views)** and **PDF export** draw the reading above the cell text through the shared cell painter/print text path:
  - about **half the cell text's size** (`min(size / 2, 45% of the cell height)`),
  - **shrunk to the cell width** when the reading is longer (so it never spills into a neighbouring cell) and **clipped to the cell**,
  - aligned like the cell's text (left/centre/right),
  - **the row height never changes** — the reading lives inside the cell, Excel's ふりがな表示 rule.

## Constraints (also in the PR/docs)

- **Rotated and vertical cells are out of scope**: the reading would have to follow the rotation; horizontal cells are covered.

title: Macro engine: macro.run with input checks, a file-access policy and a check of each step

title: Tables: add the Filter Button and make Header Row toggle the header (#1655)
author: alosslessdev
body:
## Summary

Adds the missing **Filter Button** checkbox to Table Design › Table Style Options and fixes **Header Row**, which previously toggled the filter dropdown instead of the header row (part of #1655).

Behaviour measured against Excel 16.0 build 20430:

- **Header Row off**: the table ref moves down one row (A1:C5 → A2:C5), the old header cells are cleared, the filter is turned off, and the column names stay in the table definition. **On** restores the row and writes those names back.
- **Filter Button off**: clears the table's criteria and reveals exactly the rows those criteria hid. Criteria stored on the table itself (`Table::filter`, as XLSX tables carry them) and on a sheet AutoFilter covering the table are both handled; rows hidden by hand stay hidden.
- **Filter Button is disabled while the table has no header row**, as in Excel.
- The **filter range excludes the totals row** (`Table::filter_range`), so a table with a total row loses its AutoFilter correctly and the total row is never hidden by a filter.
- Unchecking Header Row while the active cell is in that row moves the selection to the new first row, so the Table Design contextual tab does not disappear.
- A header-less table is saved as `headerRowCount="0"` with its column names; the filter is off after reopening, matching the file.

Engine: new `table.filterButton`; `table.headerRow` now toggles `header_row` (the old branch toggled `filter_button`). Data › Filter uses the same helper, so the ribbon checkbox and the command agree.

## Review fixes

An independent review of the first revision found two blocking state bugs, both fixed and covered:

1. Table criteria loaded from XLSX live on `Table::filter`, not on `Sheet::autofilter`; clearing now evaluates both and reveals only rows that fail the criteria.
2. The UI installed the table AutoFilter over the whole range including the totals row while the writer excluded it; both now use `Table::filter_range()`.

title: XLSX: preserve whole-column and whole-row PivotTable sources on save
author: addibbi
body:
Saving a PivotTable sourced from whole columns or rows must preserve its declared source so later refreshes include newly added data. Write the full source extent in worksheet-source XML while keeping cache generation bounded. Preserve declared header and field coordinates when used cells begin inside the source, addressing [the cache-origin finding](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/pull/2155#discussion_r4368083656).

A resolved source exceeding the existing **10-million-cell source-work budget** fails XLSX serialization with an explicit error instead of silently dropping the PivotTable. The budget counts padded fields and the header before allocation. Save, Save As and Save Bytes propagate the error before writing a destination or marking the document saved. Over the separate **two-million-cell records limit**, the PivotTable/cache definitions remain without a records snapshot.

Fixed rectangles, tables and local/global names retain their source contracts. Unresolved-source handling and both limits remain unchanged. The documentation also removes three misplaced revision-history rows from data tables, retaining the correct history entry.

Aligned with upstream `main` at `45f5ab18e4e57bf50ee88d2526deb4b87c5b24cb`, adapting cache generation to the upstream `pivot/write.rs` module while retaining shared-window active-sheet handling, original sheet IDs and Enable show details serialization. The desktop-theme workaround remains absent from the PR diff.

### Regression coverage

Generated tests cover whole-axis source XML, sparse cache origins, repeated save/reopen, append/refresh and fixed-source controls. Over-budget regressions verify explicit serialization failure and preservation of existing destination bytes, workbook/saved snapshots, path, dirty state and undo/redo history. A separate control verifies that exceeding only the records limit preserves the PivotTable on reopening. Upstream sheet-ID, Show Details and shared-window save controls remain covered.

title: calc: avoid false IFERROR cycles during suspended range reads (follow-up to #1340)
author: addibbi
body:
An unused IFERROR fallback can become a false dependency when bounded-stack recalculation suspends a deep calculation. The temporary `#CALC!` evaluates the fallback while unwinding; batching that read can report `#CIRC!` even though the primary expression succeeds after resumption.

Batch extra dependencies only for range reads begun before suspension at the nesting limit, in both `visit_range` and `range_values`. Preserve waiting guards, dependency deduplication and wide-range batching.

Parent #1340 has merged. This follow-up is aligned with main `45f5ab18e4e57bf50ee88d2526deb4b87c5b24cb` and remains ready for review. Upstream physical-stack handling and circular diagnostics after undo/redo or rollback are retained. The guard follows the upstream `recalc/pass_host.rs` module split; the PR contains the guard, its regressions and related documentation.

The [documentation finding](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/pull/2156#discussion_r4376463432) is addressed by removing two misplaced revision-history rows from the Coverage and Scope tables, while retaining the actual history entry.

### Regression coverage

Seven generated integration tests cover unused direct, streamed and materialized fallbacks, genuinely used fallbacks, true ancestor/sibling cycles and recovery, plus a primary materialized range. The primary case addresses [CodeRabbit's review suggestion](https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/pull/2156#pullrequestreview-5642528722): `SUMPRODUCT(Data!B1:B128)` terminates a 64-cell chain and must yield `191` and `192` with no circular diagnostics.

The parent's 3,000-cell suspension-count control exercises both `SUM` and `SUMPRODUCT`: each must return the expected result without cycles and with at most three suspensions. No elapsed-time speedup is claimed. Rustdoc documents the suspension/batching contracts and regression expectations; coverage thresholds remain unchanged.

title: XLSX: keep the cached values of dynamic-array spills on import (#2137)
author: alexanderalber
body:
Closes #2137

## What

When an XLSX workbook is read, the cells a dynamic-array formula spilled into (all but the anchor) lost their cached `<v>`, so an embedder that shows a workbook as saved, without recalculating, saw them empty.

The reader now keeps those values as the sheet's spill values: `Sheet::spill` gets the cached values and `Sheet::spill_ranges` the anchor's `ref`. That is where `Sheet::value` already looks, and where `sheet_write` takes the spilled `<v>` values and the `ref` from, so:

- `F4 = SEQUENCE(3)` with `ref="F4:F6"`: `value(F5)`/`value(F6)` return the saved 2 and 3 straight after `read_xlsx`;
- saving again without a recalculation writes the spill (`cm="1"`, `ref`) and its values back.

The cells themselves still hold no value, so the formula can spill over them as before. `Calc::recalc_all` (which `DocState::new` runs after every open) clears both maps before laying spills out again, so the app's behaviour after opening a file is unchanged.

Legacy CSE arrays are left as they are (their values are still dropped); that is #2048.

## Tests

- `fixtures::shared_formulas_and_value_types`: spill range and cached value of the `SEQUENCE(3)` spill are read; a legacy array's cached value does not become a spill value.
- `array_export::dynamic_spills_and_legacy_cse_keep_distinct_ranges`: after reading, the spill values are readable, and a second save without recalculation keeps `ref` and values.
- `docs/file-format-parity.md`: revision history entry.

`cargo test --workspace` passes, `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-xlsx --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo fmt` are clean. Note: `cargo xtask ci` currently stops at clippy on Windows in `ui-egui/src/desktop_theme.rs` (`let_unit_value`, pre-existing on main, fixed by #2141), so the later CI steps did not run locally.

title: security: enforce HTTPS on curl downloads (SonarCloud S6506)
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary
Enforces HTTPS on `curl` downloads flagged by SonarCloud rule **S6506** (`shell:S6506`, `docker:S6506`, `githubactions:S6506`, Security).

These `curl` calls use `-L`/`-fsSL` (follow redirects). A redirect could transparently downgrade to plaintext HTTP, exposing the download to MITM tampering. Adding `--proto '=https'` forces curl to refuse any non-HTTPS protocol, including across redirects, without changing behavior for the legitimate HTTPS endpoints already in use.

## Change
`curl <args>` → `curl --proto '=https' <args>` on each flagged line.

🤖 Generated to address SonarCloud findings.

title: XLS: formulas that call a VBA function keep their saved results (#2139)
author: alexanderalber
body:
A legacy `.xls` workbook whose cells call a VBA user-defined function (`=DIAGONALWERT(I11)`) opened with those cells as `#NAME?`, and every formula depending on them followed (462 of 555 formulas in the reporter's file). The reader decoded the call into a formula, the recalculation on open couldn't resolve the function, and the result Excel saved in the file was thrown away.

## What changed

- **Reader** (`crates/xlsx/src/xls/formula.rs`, `mod.rs`). BIFF8 stores a call to a VBA function as a `PtgName` to a defined name flagged as a function or macro (Lbl `fFunc`/`fProc`, [MS-XLS] 2.4.150), followed by `PtgFuncVar` with the user-defined index 255. Such a formula is now treated like the other formulas the `.xls` reader can't represent (references to other workbooks, skipped names, data tables): the cell keeps its saved result (number, text, boolean or error) as a value, and the import warns "Some formulas use user-defined functions (VBA macros); their saved results were kept as values."
- A defined name whose formula calls a VBA function is skipped with a warning, so the cells that use it keep their saved results through the existing skipped-name rule (#803).
- Formulas that depend on those cells stay formulas and calculate from the kept values, so `SUM`s and lookups over them come out as Excel saved them.

## Why in the reader, not in calc

- The `.xls` reader doesn't read the VBA project, so the function can never run here, nor in an `.xlsx` saved from the import. Keeping the formula would only preserve a call that is `#NAME?` everywhere it goes next.
- It reuses the reader's established rule for formulas it can't carry over, warning included, and needs no new state in the model or the recalculation.
- A calc-side fallback ("keep the saved value while the function is unknown, recalculate to `#NAME?` once a precedent changes") is what `.xlsx`/`.xlsm` would need, since there the VBA project is kept and the formula must survive the round trip. That overlaps with the s…

title: calc: bound SUBTOTAL/AGGREGATE input work (#2175)
author: Higgs32584
body:

SUBTOTAL and AGGREGATE walked every cell of a whole-column/whole-row reference, so `=SUBTOTAL(9,A:XFD)` on a sheet with a value in XFD1048576 aborted the process on open.

title: calc: linear dependency extraction for range-operator chains (#2183)
author: Higgs32584
body:
Fixes #2183.

Finding a formula's precedents went through `Expr::walk`, which re-walked shared subtrees under range-operator (`:`) nodes. A chain like `INDEX(A1,1):INDEX(A2,1):…` took exponential time, so the app hung on open.

- `precedents()` in `crates/calc/src/eval.rs` now uses its own collector. It visits each node once and builds the per-sheet bounding box for each `A:B` range node on the way.
- If it goes deeper than 4,096 levels or visits more than 1,000,000 nodes, the formula is marked dynamic (always recalculated) instead of carrying on, so the result stays correct.

- `tests::precedents_depth_is_bounded`: 10,000 nested parentheses come back as dynamic.
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-calc`: 62 passed, 1 ignored.

title: xlsx/csv: cap secondary reader allocations (#2159)
author: Higgs32584
body:
Fixes #2159.

The issue lists eight places where the XLSX, ODS and CSV readers allocated or did quadratic work driven by counts in the file. Each is now capped or made linear, and each has a hostile input built in code:

- **XML tree:** at most 1M children per element and 16,384 per row (`xml.rs`).
- **Cells:** a 16M-cell budget per workbook, and rows wider than the grid are refused.
- **Sheets:** at most 4,096. Duplicate names are deduped through a `HashSet` instead of a quadratic scan.
- **Shared strings:** at most 4M. Overlapping `<col>` entries get a 4M column-write budget.
- **Array-formula / spill ranges:** looked up by row instead of scanning every range for every cell.
- **Pivot field lists:** capped and deduped, with labels borrowed instead of cloned.
- **CSV:** stops collecting fields past `MAX_COLS`.
- **Relationships:** looked up through a `HashMap`; the first duplicate id still wins, as before.

Over-cap input is refused with `IoError::TooLarge` or dropped with a warning.

**Behaviour change:** a row with more than 16,384 children, or a workbook over one of the caps, now fails to open instead of being read leniently.

**Merge note:** #2197 (for #2173) also touches `read_hyperlinks` in `sheet_read.rs`, so whichever lands second will need a small conflict fix.

## Tests
- New: `xml::tests::too_many_children_is_refused`, `sheet_read::tests::{cells_past_the_workbook_cap_are_refused, spill_index_finds_ranges_by_row}`, `tests::malformed::{a_row_wider_than_the_grid_is_refused, overlapping_column_entries_have_a_budget, sheet_count_is_capped_and_duplicate_names_are_renamed, too_many_shared_strings_are_refused, hyperlinks_resolve_relationships_by_id}`, `tests::csv_tests::fields_past_the_last_column_are_not_collected`, `tests::pivot_tests::repeated_pivot_fields_are_used_once`. title: core: iterative number coercion for nested parentheses (#2180)
author: Higgs32584
body:
Fixes #2180.

`parse_numeric` in `crates/core/src/parse.rs` called itself once per pair of parentheses, so text like `((((…1…))))`, for example from `=VALUE(REPT("(",N)&1&REPT(")",N))` or stored in a file, overflowed the stack on open.

title: Keep a gliding selection outline moving when the selection changes every frame
author: kernexshadow
body:
When the selection changes in consecutive frames (a held arrow key, Shift+arrow extending), the gliding outline stands still instead of following it, and only catches up once the key is released.

## Cause
`SelectionGlide::frame` restarts the glide clock (`started = f.now`) whenever the destination changes, so in that frame `progress` is 0 and the outline is drawn exactly where it already was. A selection that keeps changing keeps restarting the glide, and the outline only moves in frames where the destination stays put.

## Fix
- `selection_glide.rs`: a new destination's glide is timed from the previous frame, at most one 60 Hz frame back (egui paints nothing while idle, so the previous frame can be seconds old). The outline already moves in the frame that shows the change.
- `docs/ui-parity.md`: glide row and revision history.

Pointer drags no longer glide since the mouse-button check now on `main`; this covers the keyboard side of the same freeze.

## Verified
- New tests `a_selection_changing_every_frame_keeps_up` and `a_change_after_sitting_idle_still_glides`: both fail with the old `started = f.now` and pass with the fix. Two existing tests now take the set-off position with `step(0.0)`, the frame the change lands in.
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui --no-fail-fast` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passed on Windows before rebasing onto the current `main`. After the rebase only `cargo fmt` could run locally (Windows Smart App Control blocks the new build scripts); `selection_glide.rs` differs from the tested version only in comments, and `main` changed neither that file nor its dependencies (egui 0.36.2, `engine::core`).

title: links: spawn the Windows opener by absolute path (#2176)
author: Higgs32584
body:
Fixes #2176.

On Windows the system opener was spawned as a bare `explorer`, and Windows looks for that next to the app (and in the current directory) before searching PATH. A planted `explorer.exe` would run instead of the real one. The other platforms had related bare-name and argument-injection problems.

- New `apps/gridcraft/src/opener.rs`. `open_with_system` in `main.rs` now spawns through `opener::opener_command`.
- **Windows:** the opener is `%SystemRoot%\explorer.exe`, falling back to `%windir%` and then `C:\Windows`. Local paths are accepted only as `X:\…` with no `..` and no quotes. Space, `"`, `,` and `^` are percent-encoded so Explorer can't read them as its own switches.
- **macOS:** `/usr/bin/open` by absolute path.
- **Linux/BSD:** `xdg-open` from PATH, as before.
- **All platforms:** a target that is empty or starts with `-` or `/` is refused, so it can't become an option.

Review note: refusing targets that start with `/` means bare absolute POSIX paths no longer go to the opener. Links to local files need to arrive as `file://` URLs. If some current caller passes bare paths, I can loosen this to block only a leading `-`.

`crates/engine/src/links.rs` (link policy) is untouched. That's #2203.

## Tests
- `cargo test -p gridcraft --bin gridcraft opener`: 5/5 pass, all plain functions that run on any OS: `windows_opener_is_explorer_in_the_windows_directory`, `windows_dir_prefers_system_root_then_windir_then_default`, `explorer_switch_characters_are_percent_encoded`, `mac_and_freedesktop_openers`, `a_target_never_becomes_an_option`.

title: control: require auth token and cap connections (#2174)
author: Higgs32584
body:
Fixes #2174.

The `--control` server accepted unauthenticated JSON-line commands from any local process. It also started a thread for every connection with no limit, and allowed 64 MiB request lines.

**Authentication**
- Every connection must start with `{"auth":"<token>"}`. The token comes from `GRIDCRAFT_CONTROL_TOKEN`. If that isn't set, the app generates 256 random bits and writes them to a 0600 file at `<settings>/control/<port>.token`, in a 0700 directory on Unix.
- A wrong or missing token, junk input, or 10 s of silence gets one generic refusal, and then the connection closes. Nothing is dispatched before the handshake succeeds.
- `Remote` in gridcraft-mcp does the handshake itself, so `gridcraft-cli send` and `mcp --connect` keep working. New `Remote::connect_with_token`.

**Resource caps**
- At most 8 concurrent connections, 16 MiB request lines (down from 64 MiB), and a 4 KiB handshake line.

**Docs:** `docs/control-protocol.md` has a new Authentication section; `docs/mcp.md`, `docs/cli.md` and `ROADMAP.md` are updated.

**Files:** new `crates/mcp/src/control_auth.rs`. Changed `apps/gridcraft/src/{control_server.rs, main.rs}`, `apps/gridcraft/Cargo.toml` (adds gridcraft-mcp and getrandom 0.4, already in the lockfile), `crates/mcp/src/{backend.rs, lib.rs, tests.rs}`, and `crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs` (doc comment only).

Related: #783 adds a token too. This PR was written independently against current `main`, and it also covers the connection cap and the handshake timeout.

**Follow-ups, not in this PR:**
- The "Drive it" example in CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md needs the handshake line added.
- An optional Unix-socket transport.
- Deleting the token file on exit (it's replaced on the next start).
- On Windows the token file relies on the inherited `%APPDATA%` ACL; no explicit ACL is set.

title: Grid: hold a trackpad swipe to the axis it starts along
author: RedBearAK
body:
**Summary**

- A trackpad gesture that starts out mostly vertical or mostly horizontal is held to that axis until the trackpad ends it, or egui gives the gesture up after a pause; a clearly diagonal gesture moves freely.
- Only gestures the trackpad reports with a start and an end are steered (macOS; Wayland, except for the first gesture after a wheel), and only the gesture's own movement: a mouse wheel's notch in the same frame passes beside it. Scrolling without gesture phases, the web included, mouse wheels, Shift+scroll, pinch zoom, touch panning and the scrollbars are unchanged.
- A gesture starting mid-frame decides its axis from its own movement, and the rail reads a gesture's modifiers where egui reads them, on the wheel events and from the gesture's start.
- UI tests in `crates/ui-egui/tests/it/trackpad_scroll.rs`: thirty-five, each reachable rule of the rail failing a test when removed.

Scrolling down a long column with a Mac trackpad, the sheet slowly drifts sideways, because no swipe is perfectly vertical. Scrolling along a row drifts up and down the same way. Excel does this too, but macOS's own scroll views don't, and it makes reading down a column harder than it needs to be. Shift+scroll already scrolls horizontally with no vertical drift, and this gives ordinary trackpad gestures the same stability when they're clearly meant to go along one axis.

**How it works**

The grid used to apply both axes of every scroll event (`crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs`). Now, while a gesture is in progress, it looks at the first 8 points the gesture's events report. If the gesture has gone at least twice as far along one axis as across it, which is within about 27° of that axis, it's held to that axis until the trackpad reports the gesture's end or the start of another, or until egui gives the gesture up: since egui 0.37 a scroll action that gets no event for 150 ms is over for egui (some gestures never get their end, as from mouse wheels on Wayland), or for a second wh…

title: scripts: require workbook trust before running embedded scripts (#2178)
author: Higgs32584
body:
Fixes #2178.

Scripts embedded in a workbook ran any command as soon as something invoked them, with no trust step. Opening a hostile file was enough to give it the full command surface.

- **Trust gate:** a new `DocState.scripts_trusted` flag is false whenever a workbook arrives from a file with scripts in it. `automate.runScript` refuses that workbook's scripts until it is trusted.
- **Trusting:** the new `automate.trustScripts` command, reached from a new **Trust Scripts** button in the Macros dialog, trusts the workbook for the session. - Each `automate.allScripts` entry has a new `trusted` field. New Window keeps the trust. Scripts written in this session run without a trust step.

Files: `crates/engine/src/{lib.rs, cmd/extra.rs, tests.rs}`, `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs`.
