title: dax: add parser core and complete operator support
author: alosslessdev
body:
## What

Adds `gridcraft-dax`, a clean-room DAX parser crate, plus the complete operator grammar from [dax.guide/operators](https://dax.guide/operators/).

This is the first of four stacked PRs for issue #431. Later PRs add the aggregation catalog, the DAX type system and the statement/query grammar on top of this branch; they will be retargeted/reviewed once this lands.

## Coverage

- Lexer: comments (`//`, `--`, `/* */`), case-insensitive keywords, bare/single-quoted/bracketed identifiers with doubled escapes, strings with doubled quotes, integers/decimals/exponents, TRUE/FALSE, `=>`, byte spans.
- Pratt parser: parentheses, function calls, table/row constructors, and every operator with DAX Guide precedence:
  `IN`, `^`, unary `+`/`-`, `*`/`/`, binary `+`/`-`, `&`, `= == <> < > <= >=`, `NOT`, `&&`, `||`.
- Associativity: `^` is right-associative; everything else left-associative. This was verified against Excel's engine (`2^3^2` = 512, `-2^2` = -4).
- Canonical printer with a parse→print→parse invariant; parentheses only where precedence/associativity requires them.
- Structured `ParseError` with spans; input-length and nesting-depth limits; no panics/unsafe.
- CLI surface: `gridcraft-cli dax format` and `gridcraft-cli dax parse` (text, `--file`, or stdin), so Excel-generated DAX can be opened in GridCraft.

## Excel round-trip

All 35 operator expressions were executed in Excel's DAX engine through `ModelConnection.ADOConnection` (`EVALUATE ROW("x", <expr>)`), then formatted with `gridcraft-cli dax format`, then executed again in Excel. Every case matched, including precedence/associativity, comments, quoted identifiers, `IN` over a table, BLANK comparison and unary/power interactions. `==` is parsed per DAX Guide but Excel's embedded engine rejects it; noted as an engine-version limitation, not a parser gap.

author: alosslessdev
body:
## What

Adds Excel's **Review > Check Performance** feature: the Workbook Performance pane, per-sheet used/optimizable cell counts, and Optimize all / Optimize sheet. Closes #2217.

Excel's documented feature ([Cleanup cells in your workbook](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/excel/cleanup-cells-in-your-workbook)) reports cells used and cells that can be optimized, then removes unused formatted/blank cells. This PR implements exactly that default surface.

title: Linux: drop files from the file manager on native Wayland
author: bmh129
body:
On a Linux Wayland session, a workbook dragged from the file manager onto GridCraft shows a "no" cursor and nothing opens. winit 0.30.13, the version eframe 0.36 uses, reports dropped files only on X11.

#165 fixes this by defaulting Linux Wayland sessions to XWayland. This PR keeps GridCraft on **native Wayland** and adds file drops there instead:

- **winit**: `[patch.crates-io]` pins winit to `crmne/winit@7a962fd`, which is rust-windowing/winit#4729, the 0.30 backport of Wayland file drops. It also moves the clipboard onto winit's own Wayland data device.
- **egui-winit**: `patches/egui-winit` is the published egui-winit 0.36.2 with emilk/egui#8657 ported by hand (that PR was written against egui `main`). With it, egui reads and writes text through winit's clipboard when the display belongs to a winit event loop, instead of starting smithay-clipboard on a second data device. Without it, paste breaks on Hyprland, which serves the selection only to a client's first data device. The egui 0.36.2 licence files (MIT, Apache-2.0) are included.
- Both patches are temporary: remove them once winit and egui release these changes (winit 0.31 already has Wayland drops, through rust-windowing/winit#4571). The `Cargo.toml` comment says so.

## Why native Wayland rather than XWayland (#165)

This PR and #165 fix the same bug, so only one of them should land. The case for this one:

- Under XWayland, GridCraft loses what native Wayland gives it: fractional scaling without blur, per-monitor scale, and the compositor's input handling. Upcoming work assumes Wayland, such as the GNOME title bar in #832.
- The cost of this PR is two pinned dependencies with a clear way out. #165 changes the default for every Wayland user.
- Other craft apps faced the same choice: FilmCraft #1115 vendors a patched winit for the same reason, while WordCraft #220 went with XWayland.

If the maintainers prefer #165's approach, I'm happy to close this one.

title: Charts: hovering a chart type no longer moves the list below it
author: RohanBhattacharyya
body:
## Problem
In the Insert Chart dialog's chart type list (Insert › Recommended Charts › All Charts), hovering or picking a type pushed every row below it down by 2 px, so the list jumped as the pointer moved over it.

## Cause
egui's `button_style` takes the inactive border width off a button's padding. GridCraft's theme gives inactive widgets a 1 px border, but egui draws no frame on an unselected selectable item. So an idle item came out 2 px shorter than a hovered or selected one, which draws the frame with its stroke.

## Fix
The list items are `Button::selectable(..).stroke(Stroke::NONE)`, so every state is the same height. Hover and selection still show as background fills.

## Tests
`hovering_a_chart_type_does_not_move_the_list` (`crates/ui-egui/tests/interaction.rs`): hovering a type and then clicking it leave every row's position unchanged. It fails on `main` without the fix, showing the 2 px shift.

`cargo xtask ci`: all 8 steps pass.

title: Keep '!' in structured-reference columns intact on XLSX save
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/xlsx/src/fmla.rs:101 (with crates/formula/src/printer.rs:181)` (no existing issue): XLSX save corrupts structured references to table columns whose name contains '!'.

## Cause
When saving, `expr_to_file` turns a structured reference into an `Expr::Name` holding its file spelling. The printer's `Expr::Name` arm then splits every name at its last `!` and quotes the left part as a sheet name. So a column like `Done!` or `#REF!` came out as `'Table1[Done'!]`, which no longer reads back as a table reference.

## Fix
The printer now looks for the sheet separator only outside brackets, and skips characters escaped with `'` inside brackets. It does this through a small `sheet_split` helper in `crates/formula/src/printer.rs`. Names qualified by a sheet or an external workbook are still quoted as before.

## Verified
- Regression test `fmla::tests::struct_ref_column_with_bang`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p gridcraft-xlsx --lib fmla::tests::struct_ref_column_with_bang`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
I left `expr_to_file`'s choice to carry structured references as `Expr::Name` unchanged. Escaping `#` as `'#` inside column names in files is also unchanged (for example `Table1['#REF!]`), because that is the correct file spelling and it reads back to the same formula.

title: Treat empty instance_num in TEXTBEFORE/TEXTAFTER as 1
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/functions/src/text.rs:553` (no existing issue): TEXTBEFORE/TEXTAFTER return #VALUE! when instance_num is left out with an empty argument (,,).

## Cause
text_before_after read instance_num with opt_int, which uses the default only when the argument is missing entirely. When the argument is skipped with commas (`,,`), it arrives as Empty and becomes 0, and the `inst == 0` check then returns #VALUE!.

## Fix
instance_num now uses the existing `has()` check, as TEXTSPLIT does: if the argument is missing or empty it defaults to 1. Otherwise it is converted with int(), so an explicit 0 still returns #VALUE!.

title: Dependencies: zip 3 → 9.0.5 for RUSTSEC-2026-0367, -0368 and -0369
author: Aimarmndz
body:
Closes #2135.

## Why

`cargo audit` / `cargo deny` flag `zip` 3 for RUSTSEC-2026-0367, -0368 and -0369, all fixed in 9.0.0. The three advisories are about `ZipArchive::extract` / `ZipStreamReader::extract` (SUID bits and symlink targets). GridCraft never calls `extract`: every reader keeps entries in memory, so the practical exposure is nil. The upgrade still clears the advisories for anyone embedding the crates, and 9.x hardens the path every opened file takes (reads past the declared uncompressed size fail; overflow and panic fixes for malformed archives).

Dependabot's grouped bump (#1881) also moves `zip`, but fails CI on other crates in the group (`crates/xlsx/src/ods.rs`). This PR is `zip` alone.

## API changes handled

- **Entry names are `Result`s now.** `Package::open` refuses an archive whose entry name is neither UTF-8 nor CP437 (the only way zip 9 fails to decode one) with the archive error, instead of opening it with that entry missing. `oversized_part` uses the raw name, lossily decoded, so such an entry is still sized and reported rather than skipped. `gridcraft-cli check` lists decoded names (the raw name lossily only when it doesn't decode) and opens entries by index, because zip 9 looks names up by their raw bytes, which a CP437 name's decoded form doesn't match (regression test `package_validation_reads_parts_with_cp437_names`).
- **ODS entity match.** zip 9 pulls in `typed-path`, whose `impl AsRef<Path<T>> for [u8]` made `r.as_ref()` ambiguous in `ods.rs`; it now derefs (`&*r`).
- Tests unwrap the new `Result`s (`crates/xlsx/src/tests/*`, `crates/engine/tests/chart_workbook_names.rs`, the `check.rs` test helper). `apps/gridcraft-cli/src/check.rs` had a production call site that the issue's list didn't mention.

New transitive crates: `typed-path` 0.12.4 (MIT OR Apache-2.0) and `nix` 0.31.3 (MIT, Unix targets only). `arbitrary` and `derive_arbitrary` drop out.

title: xlsx: column widths count in the Normal font's maximum digit width
author: pick2510
body:
## Summary
XLSX stores column widths in characters of the **maximum digit width (MDW) of the workbook's Normal font**. GridCraft always counted in Calibri 11's 7 px digits, so workbooks with a larger Normal font opened too narrow. In a Calibri 12 workbook, a 13-character column was 91 px instead of 104 px, and values that Excel shows rendered as `#####`.

- **model:** adds `max_digit_width(font, size)`. Digit advances come from installed fonts or their metric-compatible open counterparts: Calibri/Carlito, Arial/Helvetica/Liberation Sans/Arimo, Helvetica Neue, Times New Roman/Liberation Serif/Tinos, Courier New/Liberation Mono/Cousine, Georgia, Verdana, Tahoma. Unknown fonts count like Calibri. Also adds `base_col_width` and `Workbook::digit_width()`, and `points_to_chars` now takes the digit width.
- **xlsx:** `<col width>`, `defaultColWidth` and `baseColWidth` are read and written in the Normal font's digits, and the implied default column follows the font (72 px for Calibri 12). `.xls` keeps 7 px because its fonts aren't imported.
- **engine/calc/ui:** the Column Width dialog, `CELL("width")` and the column-resize toast use the workbook's digit width.

Calibri 11 and Arial 10 workbooks have 7 px digits and are unchanged.

## Evidence
I rendered a private corpus of 45 real-world workbooks (not committed) side by side with Excel. In a Calibri 12 workbook, all 13 money cells that showed `#####` now show their values.

One caveat: on macOS, Excel for Mac lays out columns at 72 dpi, about 6 px per character for both Calibri 11 and Calibri 12. Because of that, Calibri 12 sheets now render about 7% wider than Excel for Mac, while matching the Windows/format definition. Matching Excel for Mac's density (text and rows at 1 px per pt, 72-dpi digit width) would be a separate display change.

## Tests (built in code)
- `model::sheet::tests::digit_widths`: the spec example (Calibri 11 = 7 px), Arial 10/16, Calibri 12, and hostile sizes (NaN, negative, huge).
- `xlsx::tests::co…

title: ui: draw the grid at Excel for Mac's density on macOS
author: pick2510
body:
**Builds on #2257** (it uses the `max_digit_width` helper from there) and includes its commit until that merges; this PR's change is the last commit. Merge #2257 first.

## Summary
Excel for Mac draws a point as a pixel, and it counts column widths in the Normal font's digit width at **72 dpi** (6 px for Calibri 11 and 12). The grid drew every sheet unit at 0.8 pt. On a Mac that made text and rows 7% larger, and Calibri 11 columns 7% narrower, than in Excel. As a result, values that Excel shows were drawn as `#####`.

- **`Geo`** gets a column scale `zx` next to `z`, plus `zoom`. **`Density`** holds the scale and the column factor:
  - `Density::DESKTOP` is the old 0.8.
  - `Density::mac(wb)` is 0.75, with columns scaled by `digit72 / (digit96 × 0.75)`.
- **These use `zx`:** column positions and widths, hit testing, horizontal scrolling, column resizing and outline brackets.
- **These keep `z`:** rows, text and objects. Moving an object re-anchors it on screen.
- **`GridState::mac_density`** is the switch. The app and the `snapshot` example turn it on on macOS (`--density mac|desktop`). Tests, other platforms and the web, and Page Layout view keep the desktop density.

## Evidence (private 45-workbook corpus, not committed)
Gridline positions measured against Excel for Mac at 100%:

| | Excel for Mac | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| Calibri 11, set widths (B–I) | 89 110 61 93 86 69 81 87 | 84 102 57 86 81 64 75 82 | 89 110 60 93 87 68 81 87 |
| Calibri 12, set widths | 88 144 41 85 84 80 81 78 | (#2257: about 7% wider) | 88 144 41 85 84 80 81 78 |
| 15 pt row | 15 | 16 | 15 |
| default-width column (Calibri 11 / 12) | 53 / 65 | 51 / 64 | 55 / 66 |

Default-width columns stay up to 2 px wide. Excel for Mac builds them as base × digit + 5, while the model keeps Windows' rounded default. Charts at 40% zoom and sheets at 200% line up with Excel's cells.

`grid::tests::mac_density_matches_excel_for_mac` covers:
- Calibri 11 and 12 column widths against the…

title: ui: a General number fits as many digits as its column has characters
author: pick2510
body:
**Builds on #2258 and #2257** and includes their commits until they merge; this PR's change is the last commit. Merge #2257, then #2258, first.

## Problem
At the desktop density (`Density::DESKTOP`; Windows, Linux, web), an 8-digit General integer such as 24959397 showed `2.5E+07` in a default 8.43-character (64 px) column. Excel shows it in full. `display_text` counted digits by the drawn glyph advance (Carlito: 7.43 px at 11 pt), but Excel's column unit is the hinted maximum digit width (7 px for Calibri 11). So 8 digits plus padding came out about 0.4 px too wide.

## Change
- `grid.rs` `display_text`: the General fit uses `max_chars = (column px − 5) / digit width`, in sheet px. The digit width comes from `max_digit_width_at(cell font, size, 96)`. An n-character column now fits n digits. `numfmt::format_general_fit` is unchanged.
- Cell painter: the "numbers never overflow → ####" check measures the text in hinted digits (`w × digit_w / glyph_w`, with one pixel of tolerance). A number that fits only by that measure uses the cell padding, so it stays inside the cell.
- `print.rs` (print/PDF): the same rule applies. Helvetica's 6.1 pt digit fit only 7 digits in a default column before.
- `docs/ui-parity.md`: added a revision row.

## Tests
- `crates/ui-egui/tests/general_fit.rs` inspects the painted `Shape::Text` at desktop and Mac density:
  - 24959397 is drawn whole in a default column.
  - 100105891 is drawn whole in a 9.0-character column.
  - 1234567890 narrows to `1.23E+09`.
  - No `####` appears.
- `print::tests::general_numbers_print_as_many_digits_as_the_column_has_characters` checks the same three numbers in the PDF.
- `cargo xtask ci` results: fmt, clippy, assets, layers, wasm, parity and keytips pass. `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` passes except `header_autofit::table_filter_autofit_works_through_command_and_header_double_click`, which already fails on main when Carlito is installed.

title: calc: circular references keep the value they show, as in Excel
author: pick2510
body:
## Summary
With iterative calculation off, a circular reference gave `#CIRC!` (a GridCraft-only error) to the formula the loop closes on and to every formula reading it. Excel instead **keeps the value the formula shows**: its cached value from the file, or 0 for a newly entered formula. It reports the loop and calculates the dependent cells from that value.

This was data loss, not just a difference in display. The writer saves `#CIRC!` as 0, so opening a workbook with a loop and saving it replaced the loop cell and everything reading it with 0. In a real grade sheet from a private corpus (not committed), one self-referencing header formula turned a whole 7×39 block of 0/1 flags into `#CIRC!`.

**Change:** when a loop is met with iteration off, the read returns the formula's previous value (`previous(k)`, already used by iterative calculation), and the formula keeps that value. `calc.circular` still lists the loop, and recalculating doesn't advance it. Iterative calculation is unchanged. `CellError::Circ` stays, since older files and the CLI compare still know it.

## Tests (built in code)
- **calc:** `loop_keeps_cached_values_from_the_file` (new) checks that a self-referencing formula with cached value 1 keeps it, that formulas reading it calculate from it, and that the loop is reported and stable.
- **calc, updated to Excel's semantics:**
  - `errors_and_cycles`: a two-cell loop shows 0.
  - `circular_references_without_iterative_calculation`: 0, stable; iterating gives 100; switching iteration off keeps 100.
  - `long_circular_chain_is_circular`: 5,000-cell loop gives numbers, stable, no hang.
  - `deep_loop_is_found_where_it_closes`: A30 keeps 0, A1 = 29.
- **engine:** `circular_formula_from_a_file_keeps_its_values` (new) writes an xlsx built in code, opens it, saves and reopens it, and the cached values survive. **Fails on `main`** (`#CIRC!`). `calculation_options_enable_iterative_calculation` was updated.

title: xlsx: read conditional formats kept only in the x14 extension list

body:
## Summary
Excel 2010+ writes a conditional format into the extension list alone when the rule's formula refers to another sheet: `x14:conditionalFormatting`, with formulas in `xm:f` and the format inline in `x14:dxf`. title: xlsx/ui: open sheets at Excel's saved view: active cell, scroll, first tab
author: pick2510
body:
## Summary
Comparing renders of a private corpus of real workbooks (not committed) with Excel found four kinds of saved view state opening differently:

| In the file | Excel | GridCraft before |
|---|---|---|
| Frozen panes, `activePane="bottomRight"`, only a top-left selection `A1` | active **E2** (the pane's first cell) | A1 |
| `topLeftCell="A71"`, active D10 | top row **10** | row 71, active cell off screen |
| Rows frozen only: `sheetView topLeftCell="D1"`, pane `topLeftCell="A56"` | columns from **D**, rows from 56 | columns from A |
| `workbookView firstSheet="2"` | tab strip starts at the **3rd** tab | all tabs |

**Fixes:**
- **Reader:** the active cell is the active pane's selection (a selection without `pane` is the top-left pane's). An active pane without a selection starts at its first cell, and the old fallback to the last selection stays. With only rows or only columns frozen, the scrolling pane's first cell keeps the sheet view's column or row.
- **Writer:** in that case the sheet view gets `topLeftCell` for the unsplit axis, as Excel writes it.
- **UI:** a sheet shown for the first time scrolls just far enough to show its active cell, using the existing `ensure_visible` path.
- **First tab:** `Workbook::first_tab` reads and writes `firstSheet` and is never written past the active tab. The tab strip starts there, or at the active sheet if that comes earlier. Inserting, deleting or moving sheets resets it to 0.

**Difference left:** when the active cell is below or right of the screen, Excel scrolls for the window size saved in the file, and GridCraft for its own window. Both show the active cell, but not necessarily at the same position.

title: range.setValues: parse: false stores a string as the text it is (#2255)
author: Hamza0101
body:
Addresses #2255, taking the ticket's second option so that no existing call changes.

Every string in `values` went through typed input, which reads it with en-US rules, and nothing said so:

```
"05.04.2026"  (dd.mm.yyyy)  → the date 4 May 2026
"02/11/2026"  (dd/mm/yyyy)  → the date 11 February 2026
"2.500"       (thousands)   → the number 2.5
"4.25 %"      (text)        → 0.0425, formatted 0.00%
```

A workbook built from Turkish-format exports held different values than the script put in it, and the only way to notice was to read the saved file back cell by cell.

### `parse: false`

```
range.setValues {"range":"A1","parse":false,
                 "values":[["05.04.2026","02/11/2026","2.500","4.25 %","=1+1","'keep"]]}

A1..F1 →  05.04.2026   02/11/2026   2.500   4.25 %   2   'keep
                                                     ↑ =1+1, still a formula
```

- **A formula is still a formula.** `=` means a formula in a cell, and the ticket asks for that ("numbers, booleans and `=` formulas as today").
- **A leading apostrophe is part of the text**, not the marker that makes text text — nothing is being marked any more.
- Numbers, booleans and `null` are unaffected either way.

### The default is unchanged

`parse` is absent from every existing call, and those behave exactly as before. I did **not** flip the default, although the ticket's first preference is for strings to be text always: that would change what every current caller stores, including the app's own paths, and it is your call rather than mine. If you want it flipped, it is one line and I will send it — with `parse: true` then available for callers who want the typed-input reading.

A `parse` that is neither `true` nor `false` is a usage error (`parse "no": true or false`) rather than a quiet default, which is the habit this ticket is about.

title: model/xlsx/ui: rich-text cells (formatted runs) read, drawn and saved
author: pick2510
body:
## Summary
Text cells with formatted runs showed in the cell's own font, and the runs were lost on save. Examples are a red bold "closed book" after plain text, or a header whose second line is a smaller font. These are `<r><rPr>…</rPr><t>…</t></r>` in shared or inline strings. A render comparison of a private corpus of real workbooks (not committed) against Excel showed this in schedules and grade sheets.

**Model**
- `Cell::rich: Option<Arc<RichText>>` holds the runs. Each run is a length in characters plus an `Option<Font>`, where `None` means the cell's font.
- Because the runs are on the cell, they move with it through sorting, inserting and deleting rows, and moving cells. Replacing the content drops them.
- `RichText::spans(text)` cuts the text into runs and returns nothing when the runs no longer describe the text, so stale runs are never drawn or written.
- Hostile lengths are checked, and the number of runs per cell is capped.
- Serialised only when present.
- Cost: 8 bytes per cell for the `Option<Arc>`.

**XLSX**
- Shared and inline rich strings are read onto the cell. `rPr` goes through `read_font`, which already accepts `rFont`.
- Runs are written back as rich shared strings in `CT_RPrElt` order. The same text plain, or with other runs, is a separate item.
- Formula results get no runs.

**UI**
- The grid lays rich cells out with one egui `LayoutJob` section per run: font face, size, bold and italic, colour, underline, strikeout, and superscript or subscript. This works on one line (line breaks dropped, as Excel does) and wrapped.

**Not yet**
- Rotated or shrink-to-fit rich text, and cells whose number format changes the text, show in the cell's font.
- The cell editor edits plain text, so editing a cell drops its runs.
- Phonetic runs of a rich string aren't kept.
- Copy/fill paths that build new cells don't carry runs.

- **`model::cell::tests::rich_text_spans`:** multi-byte characters, runs that don't fit, runs without font…

title: AutoFit: a table's header is measured in the table style's bold font
author: vedran-dobos
body:
Fixes #2286.

CodeRabbit's review found that AutoFit measured a table's cells in their own style, while the grid draws them in the table style (a bold header row), so a bold heading could be fitted too narrow. AutoFit now measures a table cell in the font the table gives it, with an engine test that fails on `main`.

The 2026-10-22 integration batch also brought #1316's fix, so AutoFit now measures text in the font the grid draws it with (`theme::cell_text_width`). Where that font is installed it's narrower than the estimate, so the column is fitted to the real text and the estimate-based check fails. On Linux CI the font isn't there, both fall back to the estimate, and the test passes. Each change passed on its own; they only disagree together, off Linux.

The test now measures the heading the way AutoFit and the grid do, in the table style's (bold) font.

title: CSV: an Excel `sep=` first line names the delimiter (#1446)
author: vedran-dobos
body:
Part of #1446 (the `sep=` line; the ticket bot asked for its parts to be handled separately).

File › Open read a `sep=|` first line as data and split the file by the detected delimiter, so a `|` file stayed one column. Now, when the delimiter is detected, a first line `sep=` plus one character names the delimiter and isn't read as data, as Excel does.

I observed Excel 16.0 (build 17932, Windows, `Workbooks.Open` with and without `Local`) on 36 synthetic files:
- **Accepted:**
  - spaces anywhere in the line (`sep= |`, `sep =|`, ` sep=|  `)
  - any case (`SEP=|`, `Sep=|`)
  - the line quoted as a whole field (`"sep=;"`)
  - a BOM before the line
  - CRLF or LF line ends
  - tab, a letter, or `"` as the delimiter (`sep="` splits at the quotes)
- **Dropped, nothing split:** `sep=` with nothing after it (or only a space). A non-ASCII character after `=` is dropped too, without splitting at it.
- **Data:** two characters after `=` (`sep=ab`, `sep=||`, `sep=;,`, and `sep=|<tab>`, since a tab is not ignored), and a `sep=` line anywhere but first. An unclosed quote (`"sep=;`) swallows the rest of the file, as any quoted field does.
- **Saving:** Excel writes its list separator (`;` on this machine) and no `sep=` line, whichever delimiter the file named.

One difference from the ticket: #1446 lists `sep=` with nothing after it as data. This Excel build drops the line, and this PR follows that.

## What changed
- **xlsx** `csv.rs`: a new `sep_line` reads the first line by the rules above. `read_csv` uses it only when the delimiter is detected (`delimiter: 0`), so a given delimiter wins and the line stays data. A `.tsv`/`.txt` (read with tabs) keeps it as data.
- `parse_records` takes an optional delimiter and quote character, for `sep=` (split nothing) and `sep="` (quote nothing).
- `csv_delimiter` keeps the named delimiter only when it's `,` `;` or tab, which GridCraft detects again when the file is reopened. Any other (`|`) is saved as commas, because without the line the…

title: Format: number formats widen columns that weren't sized by hand (#1077)
author: vedran-dobos
body:
Fixes #1077.

Increase Decimal (and the ribbon's other number formats, and Format Cells) changed the format but never the column, so after a few presses the number turned into `####`. Microsoft's support article "Stop showing rounded numbers" says "the column width adjusts automatically", but not when. So I observed Excel 16.0 (build 17932, Windows) with synthetic workbooks and followed what it does. A column nobody sized by hand now widens to fit the widest formatted number in the target. A column whose width was set with Column Width (or by dragging its border) keeps its width and shows `####`, as in Excel.

What Excel did, and what this PR does:
- **Widens:** a column at the default width, one that was AutoFitted, and one widened this way before, also with Wrap Text on and with a 20 pt bold font. It fits the widest number in the formatted range.
- **Keeps its width:** a column set with Column Width, even when that width equals the default. AutoFit makes such a column automatic again.
- **Doesn't widen:** hidden columns, text, General numbers (they round to fit instead), merged cells and shrink-to-fit cells.
- **Never narrows.** Decrease Decimal leaves the width alone.
- **Format Cells too:** a number format applied to a number widens the column whichever way it's set (observed through the `NumberFormat` property). A value entered into a cell that already has the format doesn't (observed through `Value`: the cell shows `####`), and neither does GridCraft.
- **In XLSX**, Excel writes `customWidth="1"` for every width it stores and adds `bestFit="1"` for widths that AutoFit or a number format set. After hand-editing the attributes and reopening, only `customWidth` without `bestFit` kept its width; a width with no flags, `bestFit` alone, or both, kept widening.

## What changed
- **model** `LineInfo::custom` ("set by the user"), already used for rows, now marks columns too. Its doc comment says so.
- **engine** `format.rs`: `set_fmt` (Number Format list, Accounting, …

title: Charts: automatic value axis leaves 0 out like Excel's
author: bldred
body:
Fixes #1688.

Column, bar, area and combo charts always put 0 on the value axis (`force_zero`), and the range they scaled on counted the 0 that every bar and stack starts from. A stacked bar chart of start dates (about 45,200) plus durations of a few days, the usual Gantt layout, drew the durations as slivers at the far end of a 0–50,000 axis.

**Measured in Excel** (Windows, Microsoft 365), black-box, with nine synthetic workbooks written by GridCraft, each with one chart on an automatic axis. These are Excel's automatic bounds from Format Axis ▸ Bounds/Units:

| Chart | Data | Excel min / max / major | This branch |
|---|---|---|---|
| column | 95…100 | 92 / 101 / 1 | 92 / 102 / 2 |
| column | 50…100 | 0 / 120 / 20 | 0 / 120 / 20 |
| column | 84…100 | 75 / 105 / 5 | 75 / 105 / 5 |
| column | 83…100 | 0 / 120 / 20 | 0 / 120 / 20 |
| bar | 95…100 | 92 / 101 / 1 | 92 / 102 / 2 |
| stacked bar | Start 45200…45221 + Days 5, 10, 3, 8 | 45180 / 45240 / 10 | 45180 / 45240 / 10 |
| column | −100…−95 | −101 / −92 / 1 | −102 / −92 / 2 |
| area | 95…100 | 92 / 101 / 1 | 92 / 102 / 2 |
| line | 95…100 | 92 / 101 / 1 | 92 / 102 / 2 (`main`: 95 / 101 / 1) |

What the measurements show:
- Column, bar, area and line charts share one rule; bars aren't forced to 0.
- 0 is left out when every value is at least ⅚ of the largest. The cutoff is exact: 84…100 leaves it out, 83…100 keeps it.
- When 0 is left out, the axis starts half the data range below the smallest value, rounded down to a step: 95 − 2.5 → 92, 84 − 8 → 75, 45200 − 14.5 → 45180. All-negative data mirrors this at the top. `main`'s line-chart rule skipped this padding, so lines change too (95 → 92 on that row).
- Stacked charts use the stacked positions. The smallest single value in the stacked case is 3, which would have kept 0; Excel uses 45200.
- Bars start at the axis minimum (columns rise from 92) or hang from the maximum (negative columns from −92).

title: macOS: show file pickers as sheets, not a modal loop inside winit
author: Aimarmndz
body:
Fixes #1911. Fixes #2042.

## Why

On macOS GridCraft aborts while File › Open or a save picker is up. The blocking `rfd::FileDialog` runs `NSSavePanel`'s modal loop inside winit's event handler; an event delivered in that nested loop (a Finder drag over the panel is enough) re-enters winit, whose guard panics in a callback that can't unwind, and the process aborts:

```
panicked at winit-0.30.13/src/platform_impl/macos/event_handler.rs:135:17:
tried to handle event while another event is currently being handled
panic in a function that cannot unwind
thread caused non-unwinding panic. aborting.
```

The upstream issue (rust-windowing/winit#3992) is still open and 0.30.13 is the latest 0.30 release, so the fix has to be on our side: don't run a modal loop inside the event handler.

## What changes

On macOS the pickers are begun as sheets with rfd's `AsyncFileDialog`. AppKit builds the panel during the frame, as it requires; a worker thread waits for the completion handler and sends the answer back over a channel. The frame loop keeps running, so nothing re-enters.

- **ui-egui:** `Services::pick_async` (with `PathPick`) and `SheetApp::pick_path`, which runs the same follow-up (Open, Save As, Export PDF/CSV/HTML, Save a Copy) at once with a blocking picker, or on the frame the answer arrives with an asynchronous one. One sheet at a time; a cancelled or dropped request frees the picker. The answer goes to the workbook that asked, even if another one became active meanwhile (if it was closed, nothing is written and a message says so). Hosts that only set `pick_open`/`pick_save` (Windows, Linux) behave as before.
- **Insert Picture** uses the existing `pick_picture_async` inbox on macOS, and the dialog now repaints while it waits for it.
- **apps/gridcraft:** the open/save/picture file types live in one place for both pickers. No new dependencies and no `unsafe`; the worker blocks on the future with a small `Wake` that unparks it.

title: Hardening: overlong digits, NaN lookup indexes, bounded REGEXREPLACE (#2163, #2162)
author: tyrel
body:
Fixes #2163. Fixes #2162. See #2165 below: no change was needed.

## What changed

**#2163: text coercion and NaN indexes**
- `plain_number` (time and fraction parts) already refused `nan`/`inf` spellings. But a run of a few hundred digits still parsed to infinity, so `"1 <400 digits>/<400 digits>"` coerced to ∞/∞ = NaN. Such digits no longer count as a number, and a fraction must come out finite. Test: `overlong_digits_stay_text` (core).
- VLOOKUP/HLOOKUP (`vh_lookup`) and the D-functions' field index (`database::field_index`) refuse a NaN index. Before, NaN passed their `< 1` checks, became index 0 and underflowed on `- 1`: a panic in debug, a wrapped `usize::MAX` in release. Test: `nan_index_is_a_value_error`.
- `hostile_inputs_never_panic` now also passes NaN and infinity to every registered function. No other function panicked on them.

**#2162: REGEXREPLACE output**
- The result is built match by match. Each replacement is appended piece by piece within a bound of 4 × 32,767 bytes; past that the text can only be over 32,767 characters, so the call is `#VALUE!` before anything larger is built.
- The replacement is split once into pieces with the grammar `regex::Captures::expand` uses: `$$`, `$name`/`$n`, `${name}`, and a `$` that starts no reference. `template_expands_like_regex` checks they agree on 17 templates, including the edge cases `$1a`, `${}`, `${y` and a trailing `$`.
- Test `regexreplace_bounds_its_result`. Peak memory of that test, measured with `/usr/bin/time` on the test binary:

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Every char of 32,767 `a` replaced by 32,767 `b` | 1.05 GB, 0.64 s | 6.9 MB, 0.01 s |
| One 32,767-char match, replacement `$0` × 10,000 | 327 MB, 0.34 s | 7.1 MB, 0.01 s |

The occurrence form (`REGEXREPLACE(…, n)`) uses the same bounded expansion.

**#2165: MAP**
- No change needed. `main` already checks MAP's size with `broadcast_len` (`checked_mul` against `MAX_CELLS`), from 836b2698 (#2182). Its test `array_broadcast_result_is…

title: Print numbers near f64::MAX in a form that parses back
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/formula/src/printer.rs:134` (no existing issue): Printing a formula number near f64::MAX produces text that no longer parses.

## Cause
The printer writes number literals with `number_to_text`, which keeps 15 significant digits. For values at the top of the f64 range this rounds past `f64::MAX` (e.g. `1.79769313486232E+308`), and the lexer rejects the printed text as 'number too large'.

## Fix
The formula printer's `number()` now checks that the 15-digit text parses to a finite f64. If it doesn't, it falls back to Rust's shortest round-trip `{:E}` form with an explicit exponent sign (e.g. `1.7976931348623157E+308`). A regression test round-trips `±1.7976931348623157E308`.

## Verified
- Regression test `number_near_f64_max_round_trips`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p gridcraft-formula --test printer_roundtrip`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`number_to_text` in gridcraft-core is unchanged, so Excel-style text conversion (`&`, General) still yields 15 significant digits.

author: Ybrah
body:
## Why

A same-origin page hosting the web build (`?host=parent`) can open a workbook and receive saves, but it can't act on the open sheet or know where the user is. We embed GridCraft in an audit app and want the "select a cell, capture a value from a document shown beside the sheet, write it into the cell; select a linked cell to see its source" workflow, plus an agent that works on the open workbook rather than a reloaded copy.

## What

Two messages in `apps/gridcraft-web/src/host.rs`, reusing the desktop control protocol rather than adding a new API:

- `gridcraft:command {id, method, params}`: any control-protocol method (`engine.execute`, `cell.get`, `sheet.read`, `ui.cell.click`…). - `gridcraft:selection {sheet, active, ranges}` (A1 text): posted when a workbook opens and whenever the selection or the active sheet changes.

`Bridge::sync` now takes the `egui::Context` (one-line change in `web.rs`). The existing messages are unchanged.

title: Wayland: wheel without Ctrl scrolls again after a Ctrl+wheel zoom (#2213)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #2213.

On Wayland, winit starts a scroll "touch" (`TouchPhase::Start`) for a high-resolution wheel and never ends it. While a touch is open, egui's `WheelState` ORs in every modifier it sees and only clears them on `End`/`Cancel`, so after one Ctrl+wheel turn every later turn kept zooming.

The fix is in `SheetApp::raw_input_hook`, before egui reads the events: `grid::end_stuck_ctrl_wheel` remembers whether the open wheel touch has seen Ctrl/Cmd. When a wheel `Move` without Ctrl/Cmd comes after that, it puts a zero-delta `MouseWheel { phase: End }` in front of it. egui then drops the stale Ctrl and scrolls that turn normally. Ctrl+wheel still zooms, and touches that end by themselves are left as they are.

Because this runs on the raw input, every scrollable place gets the fix: the sheet, both scrollbars, the sheet tabs, and the egui `ScrollArea`s in dialogs, panes and the ribbon. It doesn't reverse-engineer a scroll out of `zoom_delta()`.

Scope: the bug comes from winit's Wayland backend, so the hook runs only on non-Apple Unix (`cfg!(all(unix, not(target_vendor = "apple")))`). On X11 the extra `End` changes nothing, because egui is not in a touch there. macOS keeps egui's intended behaviour, where a trackpad's kinetic scroll keeps the modifier it started with. Windows and the web are unchanged.

Test: `grid::tests::a_wheel_turn_without_ctrl_ends_a_ctrl_wheel_touch` walks through the issue's sequence (plain turn starting a touch that never ends, then Ctrl+wheel, then Ctrl released). It checks that the `End` is inserted only at the release, and that later plain turns and self-ending touches pass through untouched.

title: XLSX: write spilled text as cached strings, not shared strings (#2285)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #2285.

Cells covered by a dynamic-array spill (or a legacy array range) were written by the plain-value branch of `write_cell`, so text in them went into the shared strings table (`t="s"`). Only the anchor got `t="str"`. When GridCraft keeps Excel's `<fileVersion>` and calcFeatures extension, Excel trusts the saved values and showed #VALUE! in those cells until a full recalculation.

Spilled text (the values collected as `extra`) is now written as `t="str"` with the text in `<v>`, the same way the anchor's cached text is written and the way Excel saves it. Numbers, booleans and errors in a spill were already fine and are unchanged; text in ordinary cells still uses the shared strings table. The reader already handles `t="str"` cells without a formula.

Test: `spilled_text_is_written_as_a_cached_string_not_a_shared_string` in `crates/xlsx/src/tests/array_export.rs` saves `=SORT({"b";"a";"c"})` spilling into K4:K6 and checks that all three cells are `t="str"` with a, b, c in `<v>`. Without the fix, K5 and K6 are `t="s"` and the test fails.

author: alexanderalber
body:
Closes #2301 (found by @iluebbe while testing #2187, https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/issues/2137#issuecomment-6334492459).

**Problem.** The cells after the anchor of a dynamic-array spill, and the cells inside a legacy array range, have no formula of their own. `write_cell` in `crates/xlsx/src/sheet_write.rs` therefore took them through the plain-value branch, which writes text as a shared-string constant (`t="s"`). title: XLS: a defined name that uses a skipped name is skipped too, through any chain (follow-up to #2192)
author: alexanderalber
body:
Follow-up to the review of #2192 (https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/pull/2192#discussion_r4342404288): a defined name that uses a skipped name was not itself skipped. #825 (fixes #803) left that open on purpose ("a name that uses a skipped name is still imported as before; happy to drop those too if you'd rather"), and the review of #2192 showed why it matters: with `Alias = Doubled*2` and `Doubled` skipped, `Alias` was imported as a formula over a missing name, and a cell using `Alias` stayed a live formula that calculates to `#NAME?` instead of keeping its saved result.

**Change** (`crates/xlsx/src/xls/mod.rs`, `formula.rs`):
- The globals pass still decodes every name formula once. It now also records which names each formula refers to, and propagates the skipped status along those edges with a worklist. Chains of any length and names defined before the name they use (forward references) are covered, and the cost stays linear in names plus references (names are matched by text through a map; a name shared by several scopes counts for all of them, which errs towards keeping saved results).

title: Calc: calculate missing results without replacing saved formula caches
author: mrzv
body:
## Problem

Read-only embedders can use saved formula results, or call `recalc_all` and replace them. They cannot fill only missing results while preserving cached unsupported functions, volatile results, errors and formula metadata.

## Change

Add `Calc::recalc_missing(&mut Workbook)`:

- Evaluate only formula cells whose result is `Value::Empty`; all other saved results remain fixed inputs.
- Keep formula metadata visible to `ISFORMULA` and `FORMULATEXT`, and retain cached anchors' existing spill values/ranges.
- Restrict spill/dynamic follow-up rounds to the initially missing formulas.
- Restore the full dependency graph before returning, so later `cells_changed` calls retain normal editing behavior.
- Document that this does not validate cache freshness or reconstruct cached spill data absent from the workbook.

The API is additive; importers, UI open policy and `recalc_all` are unchanged. This is distinct from an all-or-none open recalculation option.

## Coverage

Regressions cover cached UDFs, stale/volatile results, error and empty-text caches, missing chains, formula metadata, cached spill references, new spills, repeated calls and subsequent incremental editing. An external public-API consumer exercises the read-only and editing lifecycle.

## Verification

- Native workspace formatting, all-target Clippy (`-D warnings`), tests, assets and layering gates passed.
- The four focused `recalc_missing` regressions and an external public-API smoke passed after the final stale-spill fix.
- Wasm workspace check, parity check and generated keytip check passed.
- Final formatting and calculator all-target Clippy passed.

The default Homebrew compiler did not have the Wasm standard library installed; the Wasm check passed with the installed rustup stable compiler via a command-local `RUSTC` override. No global toolchain settings were changed.

title: Hyperlinks: Ctrl+click on a link follows it instead of extending the selection (#1198)
author: xc4pr
body:
## Summary
Ctrl+click (Cmd+click on macOS) on a cell hyperlink now follows the link, as a plain click already does: web and e-mail addresses ask for confirmation before opening, and references jump to their target.

## Root cause
In the grid's press handler (`interact` in `crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs`), a click with the command modifier always went to the add-to-selection branch. `follow_link` was only called from the unmodified-click branch, so a Ctrl+click on a link only added the cell to the selection.

## Fix
In the command-modifier branch, a primary click on the link's text calls `follow_link`. The hit area is the same one a plain click uses (the left 80% of the cell). A Ctrl+click anywhere else, or a Ctrl+drag, still adds to the selection. `follow_link`, the confirmation dialog and `link.open` are unchanged.

## Tests
- New `crates/ui-egui/tests/hyperlink_ctrl_click.rs` (egui_kittest). Ctrl+click on a web link opens the confirmation dialog, Ctrl+click on an internal link moves to its target, and a plain click still follows the link.

## Root cause
Only a right-drag of the handle offered a choice (#1652). A left-drag ran `edit.autoFill` at once and left no way to change the result afterwards, so a dragged lone number became a series only with Ctrl+drag or the right-drag menu.

## Fix
- `crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs`: after a left-drag fill succeeds, `GridState::fill_tag` keeps the source, the filled range and the workbook state (document, sheet, revision, undo depth). `fill_options_tag` draws the button the way the error-checking button is drawn and opens a menu with the four modes. A choice undoes the drag's fill and runs `edit.autoFill` again in that mode, so the result stays one undo step, and the button stays for another choice. If the undo fails, the button goes away and the error is shown instead of filling over the old fill.
- The button goes away once anything else changes the workbook, another workbook or sheet becomes active, or the selection moves off the filled cells. While a cell is being edited, a dialog is open or a drag is under way it is not drawn.
- The right-drag menu and the button share one list of modes. No engine change: every choice is `edit.autoFill` with an existing mode, so scripts and the control channel already reach them.
- `docs/ui-parity.md`: fill handle row and revision history.

Left out, as in the right-drag menu: Fill Days/Weekdays/Months/Years and Flash Fill; the button after a double-click of the handle. Not confirmed from public docs: whether Excel keeps the button after the selection moves. Here it goes away, so the menu always acts on …

title: View: zooming is not an undo step
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #2313.

`view.zoom`, `view.zoom100` and `view.zoomToSelection` were registered with the undoable `cmd!`, so every Ctrl+wheel notch (and every slider drag, Zoom dialog OK, 100% or Zoom to Selection) pushed its own history entry and Ctrl+Z walked back through the zoom levels before reaching the last real edit. They now use the existing `cmd!(noundo …)` variant, like the selection commands: still journaled, still saved with the file, but outside Undo/Redo, and zooming between an Undo and a Redo no longer clears the Redo stack.

In Excel zoom belongs to the window, not to the workbook's edits: it's a property of the `Window` object, applied to the sheet active in that window ([Window.Zoom](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office/vba/api/excel.window.zoom)), and Ctrl+Z after zooming undoes the previous edit, not the zoom ("Excel doesn't consider a zoom change an 'undoable' action—it's a view property rather than a data change", [How-To Geek on Zoom to Selection](https://www.howtogeek.com/microsoft-excel-zoom-to-selection/)). Microsoft's own [Undo article](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/undo-redo-or-repeat-an-action-84bdb9bc-4e23-4f06-ba78-f7b893eb2d28) doesn't list zoom either way, so all five entry points (wheel, slider, dialog, 100%, Zoom to Selection) go the same way here.

The command-sequence fuzzer compares the workbook after undoing everything with the starting one, view state aside; zoom joins that view state (`canonical()`), since it's no longer undone.

Undo and Redo also keep the zoom you're at. They swap in a whole workbook snapshot, so undoing an edit made at another zoom level used to bring that zoom back (type in A1 at 100%, wheel to 200%, Ctrl+Z: A1 empties and the view jumps to 100%). `keep_zoom` now carries each sheet's current zoom into the restored snapshot, the same way `keep_watch_list` keeps the Watch Window, and when that lands back on the saved state the zoom alone doesn't make the workbook dirty (as `view.zoom` already does).

title: Recalc: plan dependency levels and calculate wide levels on worker threads
author: RedBearAK
body:
**Summary**

- Recalculation runs on every core: the dirty formulas are planned into dependency levels (on one thread too, so the order no longer depends on the machine), and levels of 512 or more formulas run on worker threads, each reading the main pass's results and handing back any formula that reads one not done yet.
- This is the simpler form of threading, the one that could be verified correct: workers read only state that can't change under them, the level is walked in one thread's order with their results merged at their turn, and when a formula lays an array out differently from what the workbook stores, or loses one, the workers run again over the formulas after it with the array in sight (the rest on the main thread after eight such passes), so the result is one thread's own at any thread count. Excel's calculation tracks what INDIRECT and OFFSET read and reorders its chain to keep more threads busy on such sheets; that is a much larger piece of work for later. A dynamic formula is run again after a round only when another formula's array changed after it began, or a value changed in a later round; and the pass reads a cell freed by a shrunk array as empty.
- The settings (`multiThreaded`, `threads`) live in the workbook, round-trip through `calcPr`, and are set by `formulas.calculationOptions`; hostile values warn or are refused.
- A 1M-cell workbook with 51K LAMBDA-name calls opens in 2.2 s on eight threads instead of 7.2 s; tests compare two and eight threads against one on every case, each rule removed in turn, plus random spill workbooks, and the calc and engine suites run threaded in `cargo xtask ci`.

Recalculation on every core. This started from the state of #208 (by @arhammusheer): its threading design seeded this, but after the #1340 rewrite of the calculation host nothing of it applied any more, so what is here is a rework for current main, with #208's other optimisations deliberately left out. It then went through several rounds of adversari…

title: Window menu: switch between the open workbooks
author: RedBearAK
body:
This does one small thing: with several workbooks open, the Window menu lists them and lets you switch between them. Nothing more. It is not multi-window support (#162, #171), and it deliberately avoids anything that work would have to undo.

Today several workbooks can be open in GridCraft's one window, but nothing in the interface moved between them: the Mac's Window menu had New Window and the sheet keys only, the ribbon's View › Window group had no Switch Windows, and the one route was `window.activate {index}` over the control channel. On the Mac the Window menu also showed the app's single window as an entry titled after the active document, always checked, which looked like a second document list.

The part I'd like a second opinion on is the shape, since the point was to be plug-and-play for whoever does the real multi-window work: the engine identifies a window by its document, not by its position, and `window.list`, `window.activate {id}`, `window.next` and `window.previous` are meant to stay the one API. A build that gives each workbook its own native window maps those windows to the same ids, and the Mac menu's document list then simply becomes macOS's own window list. If that shape is wrong for where you want to take windows, I'd rather hear it now than have this be a headache later.

Summary

- The engine identifies a window by its document rather than by its position in the list, so an id stays valid when another document closes. `window.list` (and `view.switchWindows`) report id, index, title, path, dirty, active, hidden; `window.activate` takes an id or an index and unhides; `window.next` / `window.previous` cycle the visible windows and wrap; hidden windows are kept by document, hiding the last visible one is refused, and closing a document never leaves a hidden window active.
- View › Window › Switch Windows, as in Excel: the open workbooks numbered, the active one checked, a dirty one marked; Alt, W, W opens it.
- Ctrl+F6 / Ctrl+Shift+F6 and Ctrl…

title: MCP: the stdio server keeps at most 16 MB of a message (#2164)
author: nihilist-narwhal
body:
Fixes #2164.

`Server::serve` read a whole line with `read_until` and only then compared it with `MAX_LINE`, so a client sending a payload with no newline grew the buffer without limit.

**Change** (`crates/mcp/src/server.rs`)
- The line is read through `take(MAX_LINE + 1)`, as the control server's `read_bounded_line` already does.
- When a line is longer than 16 MB, the rest of it is read and dropped (`skip_line`, which keeps nothing), the client gets the existing "message too large (16 MB max)" error, and the next message is served normally. stdio has a single client, so the stream stays open instead of closing the way the control server closes a TCP connection.
- The reading is in its own function, `read_message`, so its bound can be tested directly.

**Tests** (`crates/mcp/src/tests.rs`)
- `a_line_without_newline_keeps_at_most_the_limit_in_memory` streams a 4 GiB line from one reused 1 MiB buffer and asserts the server's buffer stays within the limit. It then reads the next message whole and reaches end of input.
- `serve_loop_bounds_a_line_without_newline` runs the same input through `serve` and checks for the error reply followed by a normal `ping` reply.

`cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm, parity, keytips).

title: PivotTables: the aggregation budget counts every value field (#2169)
author: nihilist-narwhal
body:
Fixes #2169.

The aggregation loop in `crates/engine/src/pivot.rs` refused a report once it held more than five million groups. Each group holds one accumulator per value field, though (`k + extra`, up to 256), and each accumulator is 72 bytes. A wide report could therefore allocate tens of GB before the check fired: the issue's example is one million groups × 256 fields, about 20 GB.

**Change**
- `aggregation_too_large(entries, per_entry)` replaces `aggs.len() > 5_000_000`. It keeps the five-million-group limit and adds a budget of ten million accumulators, about 720 MB.
- A report with one value field keeps exactly its old limit. Wider reports are refused in proportion: three fields allow up to about 3.3 million groups.
- The check still runs after each record, so it can overshoot by at most one record's new groups.

**Test**
- `fit_tests::aggregation_budget_counts_every_value_field` covers the issue's case (1M × 257, refused), the unchanged one-field limit (5,000,000 accepted, 5,000,001 refused), a three-field report under budget, and saturation at `usize::MAX`.
- It's a unit test of the budget, like the existing `column_budget_counts_value_fields_and_grand_total` beside it. An end-to-end test would need about 10 million source cells.

`cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm, parity, keytips).

title: JSON workbooks: loaded ranges are ordered and on the sheet, arrays hold rows × cols values (#2160)
author: nihilist-narwhal
body:
Fixes #2160.

A JSON workbook was deserialized with `RangeRef` and `Array` taken exactly as written:
- A range with its corners swapped wrapped `height()`/`width()`. That is about 4.29e9 in release, which then drove loops, or a panic in debug, outside `Session::execute` once it reached render or recalc.
- An array holding fewer than `rows × cols` values was indexed past its end.

**Change** (`gridcraft-core`)
- `RangeRef` deserializes through a raw `{start, end}` form and `RangeRef::new`, with both corners clamped to the grid. This fixes every range in a file in one place (merges, tables, conditional-format and validation ranges, print areas, charts…) and matches `RangeRef`'s documented invariant (`start <= end`). Files that were already valid load unchanged. Clamping rather than refusing keeps loading lenient, consistent with how off-grid cells are already dropped (#1008).
- `Array` deserializes through `Array::new` (`try_from`). A size mismatch or a zero dimension makes the file an error: "not a GridCraft JSON workbook: an array of 1000 × 1000 holds 0 values".

Serialization is unchanged.

**Tests**
- `core::addr::tests::a_loaded_range_is_ordered_and_on_the_sheet`: swapped, off-grid and valid ranges; a saved range round-trips unchanged.
- `core::value::tests::a_loaded_array_holds_rows_times_cols_values`: short data, a zero dimension, `usize::MAX` rows; a valid array round-trips.
- `engine::tests::json_import_orders_ranges_and_checks_arrays`: opens a saved workbook whose merge is forged with swapped, off-grid corners (it loads as `B3:F1048576`, and `height()` is 1,048,574), and one whose cell holds a forged 1000 × 1000 array with no data (an error that says why).

`cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm, parity, keytips).

title: Tables never hold merged cells, which Excel removes the table for on open
author: nihilist-narwhal
body:
A workbook with a merged cell inside a table opens in Excel with the repair prompt, and Excel then removes the table and its AutoFilter. From Excel's repair log:

> Removed Feature: AutoFilter from /xl/tables/table1.xml part (Table)
> Removed Feature: Table from /xl/tables/table1.xml part (Table)

The smallest case: a table on `A1:C3`, then `home.mergeCells {"range": "A2:B2"}`, then save. I found this by opening command-sequence fuzz output in Excel for Mac 16.113, where two of 116 random workbooks lost their tables this way.

GridCraft let merged cells into a table four ways. Each now matches Excel, observed with synthetic workbooks:

| Path | Before | Now (as Excel) |
|---|---|---|
| Merge Cells / Merge & Center / Merge Across on a range touching a table | merged | refused: "You can't merge cells in a table." Unmerging is still allowed, so a file that has one can be fixed |
| Insert Table / Format as Table over merged cells | table kept the merges | the merged cells the table covers are unmerged (in Excel, `A2:B2` is no longer merged after `make new list object` on `A1:C3`) |
| Resize Table over merged cells | same | same as Insert Table |
| Paste of a copy with merged areas into a table | merges pasted | cells pasted unmerged; outside a table, merges still travel with the copy |

**Tests**
- `tables_never_hold_merged_cells` covers each path above, plus undo bringing back the unmerged cells and an XLSX round trip.
- The command-sequence fuzzer's structure check now includes "no merged cell inside a table". That's how the paste case turned up (seed 230 at 80 steps).

title: Fuzzer: undo checks follow the bounded undo history
author: nihilist-narwhal
body:
The undo history drops its oldest steps past 100 entries or 128 MB of snapshots (#1263). The command-sequence fuzzer still compared "undo everything" with the episode's starting workbook. So any episode whose snapshots went past the budget failed with *undoing all N steps doesn't give back the starting workbook*, even though undo worked as designed.

Seeds 104, 110 and 163 at `GRIDCRAFT_FUZZ_STEPS=80` fail this way on `main`. Their undo depth shows the history being trimmed:

```
home.borders {"preset":"all","range":"E:E"}      undo depth 1, retained 6 KB
home.insertColumns {"cols":"D:D"}                 undo depth 2, retained 101 MB
home.deleteRows {"rows":"23:24"}                  undo depth 1  ← oldest step dropped
```

(The 101 MB step is a separate problem: borders on a whole column are written into every cell. I'll send a PR for that.)

**Change** (`crates/engine/tests/command_sequence_fuzz.rs` only)
- The harness records when an undoable command changed the workbook but the history didn't grow, which means the history dropped a step.
- In that case, the end-of-episode check compares "undo everything" with the state before the **oldest step still in the history** (`undo[0].wb`) instead of the episode's start.
- Everything else is unchanged: redo, the Watch Window list, the round trip.

With this, those three seeds pass. `cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm, parity, keytips).

title: CI: shared gate workflow; FreeBSD nightly and on release
author: aiongg
body:
Switches GridCraft's CI to the suite's shared gate workflow and takes the slow platform builds off the pull-request path. **Depends on storytold/craft-common-actions#69**; merge after it. Until then this PR's CI fails, because `gate.yml` doesn't exist yet.

- `ci.yml` calls `storytold/craft-common-actions/.github/workflows/gate.yml@main`. That workflow brings the cached apt install, nextest, rust-cache saved only from main (keyed on the root `Cargo.toml`, so profile changes start a fresh cache), and a check that `Cargo.lock` is unchanged. Every push to main now runs to the end, and pushes to a PR branch cancel their older run. The apt package list is the old file's.
- The old file ran without craft-fonts. The gate checks out craft-fonts at the suite's default pin and sets `CRAFT_FONTS_REQUIRED=1`, so the tests now see the fonts a release embeds. `release.yml` and `freebsd.yml` pin `abb83316d96aa59c1cf64784289e378fe9fa5695` for this app; `craft-fonts-ref` is left out, so the gate uses the suite default.
- `freebsd.yml` gains a nightly run, so a drifted dependency shows up within a day. Pushes to `release` and PRs that change the workflow or the FreeBSD packaging still run it.
- `windows-arm64.yml` is unchanged: it builds only from `release`, with no schedule.

A CI-speed PR for the `cargo xtask ci` speed changes follows. Every craft app gets the same pair of PRs. Background: storytold/craft-common-actions#60.

title: Page Up into frozen rows scrolls the rows below back to the top
author: RedBearAK
body:
Fixes #2356

With row 1 frozen, Page Up could land on A1 while the rows under the frozen row stayed scrolled
down, so the rows in between never came back into view (row 10, Page Down, Page Up, Page Up ends
on row 1 with rows 2 to 9 hidden).

- The scroll-into-view step only scrolls when the target cell is below the frozen rows. A1 is
  frozen and always on screen, so that last Page Up moved the cell without scrolling anything.
- Arrow and paging keys now record the cell they moved from. When such a move goes from the
  scrolled rows into the frozen ones, the scrolled rows go back to the top. Columns work the same
  way. This covers Page Up, Ctrl+Up, Ctrl+Left and Alt+Page Up, with or without Shift.
- Selecting a frozen cell by other means keeps today's behaviour and leaves the view where the
  user scrolled it: a click, Find, Go To, the Name Box, Undo, the control channel, and pointing at
  a header cell while editing a formula.

Other keys that can move into frozen panes aren't changed here: Home into a frozen column A,
Ctrl+Shift+Home, and Shift+Enter / Shift+Tab from a scrolled-off cell next to the freeze line.
Home is the one most likely to show the same gap, but I don't know whether Excel's Home goes to
column A or to the first unfrozen column there, so I've left it for a separate change.

GridCraft's Page Up still moves the cell a page and then reveals it, where Excel scrolls a screen
and keeps the cell's place on screen. This PR only closes the gap at the frozen rows. Two related
things I've left alone: the page step counts the frozen rows as part of the screen and assumes

title: gridcraft-web: host bridge runs engine commands (gridcraft:cmd / gridcraft:response)
author: chief-nerd
body:
GridCraft's host bridge (`?host=parent`) can open a workbook, hand over saved files and report dirty state, but a host page cannot drive the open workbook. WordCraft's bridge (#2919) and DeckCraft's (#983) have `cmd` and `response` messages for that. This adds the same to GridCraft, so a host can, for example, write an answer into a cell of the workbook the user has open.

**What it does**
- `gridcraft:cmd` (from the parent): `{ id, params?, requestId? }` runs the engine command `id` (`cell.set`, `home.bold`, ...) like a ribbon button. `params` is a JSON string (absent or `null` means `{}`), as in WordCraft's bridge; `requestId` is an optional string.
- `gridcraft:response` (to the parent): `{ id, requestId?, ok, value? }` or `{ id, requestId?, ok: false, error }`, once per `gridcraft:cmd`. The `requestId` comes back, so a host can match replies to commands.
- Malformed `params`, `params` that is not a string, params over 1 MiB and a missing `id` are refused with an error response; nothing runs.
- Only the parent window on the page's own origin is heard, as before.
- The commands waiting for the next frame are bounded: at most 256, and at most 8 MiB of `params` text together. A command beyond that is answered at once with `ok:false`.

The parsing and the response shape are a pure module (`host_cmd.rs`) with native unit tests, like `prefs.rs`; the wasm-only part just posts and drains a queue once per frame.

**Testing**
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-web` passes (10 tests); `cargo fmt --all -- --check` is clean; `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-web --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- `trunk build` succeeds. In headless Chrome with a same-origin harness page I checked that after `ready`, `cell.set` with `=1+1` on B2 answers `ok:true` with `{cell:"B2", value:"2"}` and the same `requestId`, the dirty state turns true, and an unknown command, missing parameters, invalid JSON in `params`, a non-string `params` and a missing `id` each answer `ok:false` with an error.

title: Introduces direct manipulation support for existing formula
author: Lord-Taw
body:
## Description

This Pull Request introduces direct manipulation support for existing formula reference outlines. Fixes #2224.

Previously, while GridCraft rendered colored outlines for formula references during editing, dragging those outlines did not update the underlying reference text. With this update, users can click and drag an existing formula reference outline (such as `=SUM(A1:A3)`) to a new range, dynamically rewriting the reference while preserving sheet qualifications and absolute/relative anchor semantics (e.g., `$A$1`).

## Changes

- **`crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs`**:
  - Integrated `hit_ref_outline` detection with `resp.drag_started()` to initiate a new `Drag::RefOutline` state when interacting with existing reference outlines.
  - Enabled live re-pointing and rewriting of formula reference spans during drag operations.


- **`crates/ui-egui/src/editor.rs`**:
  - Added handling for `Drag::RefOutline` interactions during formula editing.
  - Implemented in-place rewriting of formula reference spans as reference outlines are dragged to new cells or ranges.
  - Kept formula text, reference metadata, and selection state synchronized throughout the drag operation.

## How to Test

1. Open a workbook in GridCraft and enter a formula containing a range reference (e.g., `=SUM(A1:A3)`).
2. Click into the cell to enter formula edit mode and view the colored reference outline.
3. Click and drag the reference outline to a new cell or range.
4. Verify that the formula text updates automatically to reflect the new range while maintaining proper relative/absolute formatting.

- Resolves #2224

title: Drag a formula's coloured references to move or resize them
author: irhop
body:
## What

While editing a formula (typed, or an existing one opened with F2), each reference is outlined on the grid in its colour. These outlines can now be dragged, as in Excel:

- **Drag from inside the cell or by its border:** moves the reference. For example, `=A1*B5` becomes `=A1*B4` after dragging B5's outline to B4.
- **Drag a corner:** resizes the reference around the opposite corner. For example, `=SUM($A$1)` becomes `=SUM($A$1:$B$4)`.

The formula text follows the drag and keeps `$` markers and any sheet prefix (`'My Sheet'!`). The edit stays open, and the pointer shows move or resize over an outline.

Existing behaviour is kept:
- A plain click inside a reference cell still commits the edit.
- In point mode (`=SUM(`, click A1, then drag to A5), a drag inside a cell still points a new range.

Not covered yet: whole-row and whole-column references (`C:C`, `4:6`) can't be dragged.

## How

- `editor.rs`: `EditState::replace_ref` rewrites one reference span in place, keeping its sheet prefix and `$` markers.
- `grid.rs`: a new `Drag::Ref` variant and a `ref_hit` hit test on the coloured outlines, used for the press, the drag, the drag cursor and the hover cursor. The outlines are already drawn from `formula_refs`, so they follow the edited text with no extra drawing code.
- `docs/ui-parity.md`: updated.

## Tests

- `crates/ui-egui/tests/drag_formula_refs.rs` (egui_kittest, real pointer events) covers moving by the border, moving from inside the cell (B5 to B4), resizing by a corner with `$` markers, a plain click still committing the edit, and a point-mode drag still pointing a range. title: Print text that overflows out of the last used column in PDF export (#2333)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #2333.

When a sheet has no print area, PDF export and print preview print the used range. Text that runs past the last used column into empty cells was drawn, but cut off at the right edge of that range. In the issue, seven `A`s in A1 are wider than column A in the PDF font, so the last character was clipped.

`layout_sheet` now widens the used range to the right until it covers that overflow. It uses the same rules as `draw_text`: only text that is not wrapped, not shrunk, not rotated and not merged; not right-aligned or Center Across Selection; centred text counts half its overflow; and the overflow stops at the first non-empty neighbour. Text from any column counts, not only the last one. Numbers never overflow, so they are skipped.

A print area set by the user, or a `range` passed to the command, is kept as it is.

Test: `print_range_covers_text_overflowing_the_last_column` checks the print preview range for a long text in A1 (`A1:D1`), the same text with B2 filled (`A1:D2`), and with a print area set (`A1:B2`, unchanged).

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Automatically determined print ranges now extend to include text that overflows the last used column, helping prevent content from being cut off in printouts.
  * Explicitly set print areas remain unchanged. Automatic expansion is skipped when formulas are displayed or the range already reaches the final column.

title: Keep the in-cell editor wide enough for the next character at high zoom (#2336)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #2336.

When you type past the cell width, the in-cell editor gets wider to fit its text. Its width is set before the text field takes the frame's keystroke: it is the width of the text so far plus a fixed 14 px. The field sits 2 px inside the editor on each side, so only about 10 px of free space was left for the next character. At zoom levels above roughly 170%, one glyph of an 11 pt font is wider than that. So each new character overflowed the field, the field scrolled its text left, and on the next frame the editor got wider and the text snapped back. That is the horizontal jitter, and it gets worse as the zoom goes up.

The change, in `crates/ui-egui/src/grid.rs` (`in_cell_editor`, the path for cells that do not wrap):
- The extra space now comes from the new `editor_slack(size)`, which returns 14 px plus one em of the editor's font size in px. One em is enough for any glyph, so the next character always fits at any zoom. The existing cap at the grid's right edge is unchanged.
- Wrapped cells keep the column's width and grow downwards, as before. The formula bar is not affected.

At 100% zoom the editor is now about one character wider than before while you type. It still covers no more than the text plus a small margin.

Test: `editor_slack_fits_one_more_glyph_at_high_zoom` checks that the free space inside the field, after the 4 px inset, is at least one em at 100% (14.7 px), at about 170% (25 px) and at 400% (60 px). With the old fixed 14 px, every case fails.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * In-cell editors now stay within the cell width while text fits, then expand with additional room for the font size, up to the available grid width.

title: AutoFilter: grow the range when a value is entered in the row below it (#2342)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #2342.

The AutoFilter range was set only by `data.filter` and moved by row/column inserts and deletes, so rows typed right below it stayed outside the filter, Reapply, the drop-down value list, sorting and the saved `<autoFilter ref>`. In Excel the range grows as soon as a value is entered in the row below.

- New `grow_autofilter` in `cmd/data.rs`: when a non-empty cell lands in the row directly below the stored range, within its columns, the range's last row moves down to that row. Criteria are untouched, so the next Reapply hides the new row if it fails them (as in Excel).
- It is called from every typed-entry path: `cell.set`, `range.setValues` and `range.fill` (Ctrl+Enter).
- A formula counts even before it is calculated (the check runs inside the edit, ahead of the recalc).
- Not grown: a row typed after a blank row (matches the issue's Excel check), a cell outside the filter's columns, clearing a cell, and a table's own filter (the table manages its range).
- Undo restores the old range, since the edit snapshots the workbook.

Test: `autofilter_range_grows_when_a_value_is_entered_in_the_row_below` covers `cell.set`, `range.setValues`, a formula, `range.fill`, the blank-row gap and a cell outside the columns. It fails on `main` (the range stays A1:B3).


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **Bug Fixes**
  - AutoFilters now extend when nonempty values or formulas are entered directly below the filtered range, within its columns. They do not extend across blank rows, outside the filter’s columns, or when the range exactly matches a table.

title: Ribbon: fall back to Home when the active contextual tab is gone
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #2329.

The ribbon kept a contextual tab (Table Design, Chart Design, Header & Footer) as the active tab even when its object was no longer selected. The tab row already hides such a tab, but the ribbon body still matched on it, so `table_design` / `chart_design` returned early and the panel stayed blank. Two changes, following wordcraft#1700 (the fix for the same report in wordcraft#1699, "Open on the Home tab every launch, as in Word"):

- The saved ribbon tab is no longer restored at startup (`UiState::at_startup`, used by the desktop and web restore): Excel opens on Home every launch, so a contextual tab cannot come back with nothing selected.
- In a session, `ribbon::show` falls back to Home when the active tab is one of the contextual tabs (Header & Footer included, which keeps its own `prev_tab` restore while editing) and is not among this frame's contextual tabs, e.g. when the active cell leaves the table. #1189 and #1207 do the same Home fallback for their Pivot tabs, so the rules agree.

On the Excel behaviour: Microsoft's page only says that the Table Design tab appears when you click inside a table ([Where are the Table Tools?](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/where-are-the-table-tools-2afc4727-7bba-4d4e-b9bf-43ab5f995745)). I found no Microsoft page saying which tab Excel shows once the cell leaves the table, so Home for that in-session case is my choice, happy to switch.

Validation:

title: Print: Print Selection in File > Print > Settings, several selected areas print one after the other
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #2351.

File > Print > Settings now offers Print Selection next to Print Active Sheets and Print Entire Workbook. The preview and the PDF sent to the printer cover the selected cells, and the preview follows the selection if it changes while the page is open.

In Excel the first Settings menu offers Print Active Sheets, Print Entire Workbook and Print Selection ([Microsoft's "Print a sheet or workbook"](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/excel/print-a-sheet-or-workbook) describes the menu and choosing Selection after selecting the range). That page does not say what happens with a selection of several areas, or how Selection interacts with a defined print area; for those two points I only found third-party descriptions (e.g. office-watch.com/2024/excel-print-choices), so please correct me if Excel behaves differently. As implemented: the selection replaces the sheet's print area, and each selected area is laid out on its own pages, in selection order. A single selected cell prints that cell. The engine already had a `range` parameter on `file.print`, `file.exportPdf` and `file.printPreview`; it now also accepts several areas (`"A1:B5,D1:E5"`), and the UI passes the selection through it. Print titles, headers and footers and Page Setup apply to each area as usual.

Left out: "Ignore Print Area" (a separate option), and the direct Ctrl+P path without the settings page (web), which still prints the active sheet as before, since it has nowhere to choose. `print_all: bool` became a three-value `PrintScope`; the label is added to every interface catalog (translations are my own and still want a native-speaker look). title: Make HYPERLINK formula cells behave as clickable links
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #2230

## Cause
HYPERLINK() only returned its argument as a value. Cell links were read only from the sheet's stored hyperlink map, which HYPERLINK() never writes to. A cell like `=HYPERLINK(A1)` therefore never had a link. A scheme-less address such as `google.com` would have been treated as an in-workbook reference, not a web address.

## Fix
Added `links::cell_link`. It returns the stored link, or for a cell whose formula is `HYPERLINK(target, ...)`, the link that the target currently evaluates to. A scheme-less web address like `google.com` or `www.x.org` gets `https://` added, as Excel does. `link.open`, the cell inspector and the grid (click, Ctrl+click, hover tooltip) now use it. `gridcraft_calc::evaluate_expr` is now exported for this.

## Verified
- Regression test `tests::hyperlink_function_makes_a_cell_link`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p gridcraft-engine --lib hyperlink_function_makes_a_cell_link`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
I did not change HYPERLINK's value or the stored hyperlink map, so nothing is written to the file for these links. A formula that is not a top-level HYPERLINK call, such as `=IF(x, HYPERLINK(..))`, still gets no link. The link text is not styled as a link.
