title: Calc: a one-value dynamic-array result in a table is not #SPILL!
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
## What was wrong
A dynamic-array formula in a table column (FILTER, UNIQUE, SORT...) that returns one value showed #SPILL!. Excel shows a one-value result in a table; only two or more values is #SPILL!.

## Cause
Since #1510 (the #1491 fix) a one-value result is recorded as a 1x1 spill range. Three checks in `crates/calc/src/recalc.rs` treated any spill anchored in a table as blocked: `spill_blocked`, `spills_as_before`, and the layout step that writes spill ranges after a pass.

## Fix
The table condition now applies only to results of more than one value, at all three sites. #1491 behaviour (1x1 spill range, `ROWS(C1#)` = 1) is unchanged.

## Verification
New test `one_value_array_in_a_table_is_not_a_spill` covers: one value in a table, two values in a table still #SPILL!, the same formula outside a table, and a repeat full recalculation. Not built or run locally; `cargo fmt --check` is clean and the fork's CI runs the suite.

Regression report: upstream issue 2335.

author: Harrison-Booth
body:
## What this changes

On save, GridCraft dropped the self-contained extension entries (`<extLst><ext>`) of a workbook and of its sheets, so some Excel settings were lost on a round trip. This keeps the ones that hold only attributes:

- workbook: calcFeatures, x15 and x14 `workbookPr`, the workbook compatibility version (`xlwcv:version`), and the Excel for Mac `mx:ArchID`, kept in source order;
- sheet: the Excel for Mac `mx:PLV` page layout settings.

title: View: dashed page breaks in Normal view, turned on by Page Break Preview and in Options (#2474)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Normal view can now show where each printed page ends, as dashed lines, like Excel's page breaks.

In Excel, after you use Page Break Preview and go back to Normal view, the page breaks stay visible as dashed lines, and File › Options › Advanced › "Show page breaks" (a per-worksheet display option, `Worksheet.DisplayPageBreaks`) turns them on or off. This PR follows that: Page Break Preview turns the option on for its sheet, Normal view then draws a dashed line after the last column and the last row of every page, under objects and the selection, and a new `view.showPageBreaks {sheet?, on?}` command, also a "Show page breaks" checkbox in File › Options, switches it. The lines come from the same pagination printing uses (`layout_sheet`: paper size, orientation, margins, scaling, print area, manual breaks), so changing the paper or portrait/landscape moves them. The pagination runs only while the lines are on and is cached per revision; no PDF is built, and each line is cut to the visible cells, so a long list doesn't turn into thousands of dashes per frame. Like `view.normal`, switching is not an edit: no undo step, the workbook doesn't become dirty, undo and redo leave it as it is (like the Watch Window list; a sheet name brought back by undoing a rename or delete keeps its own setting), and it isn't saved to the file (XLSX has no attribute for it as far as I can tell). Excel's support page also says the lines survive a save and reopen; I didn't reproduce that part. I haven't turned the lines on after File › Print preview, which some guides describe, because I couldn't find it on a Microsoft page; happy to add it. Page Layout view is unchanged (it already shows real pages).

The issue also asks for A2 and A1, so Page Setup and the Size menu now take A2, A1 and A0. A2 is saved as `paperSize` 66; ECMA-376 has no id for A1 or A0, so like ISO B5/B6 today they don't survive an XLSX save.

title: Read cell formatting from .xls files
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
## What this adds

`.xls` (Excel 97-2003) import used to read only each cell's number format. It now also reads the cell formatting records (Font, XF, Palette and Style) from the BIFF8 workbook stream, so an opened sheet keeps:

- fonts (name, size, bold, italic, strikethrough, underline, super/subscript, colour)
- solid and pattern fills
- borders, including diagonals
- alignment (horizontal and vertical, rotation, indent, wrap, shrink to fit)
- locked and hidden protection
- the workbook's custom colour palette
- its Normal font as the default font
- its user-defined cell styles

Before this change those formats were lost on open.

## Why

Opened `.xls` workbooks looked unformatted. The decoding follows the public [MS-XLS] specification (Font 2.4.122, XF 2.4.353 with CellXF 2.5.91, Palette 2.4.188, Style 2.4.269). Nothing is copied from Excel or from another implementation.

## How it is built

- The decoding lives in a new `crates/xlsx/src/xls/styles.rs`. `xls/mod.rs` gains the four record arms and one build call; the existing number-format fallback to built-in formats is kept.
- Short or malformed formatting records keep the fields that are present and add one warning. They do not refuse the workbook.
- Counts are capped (fonts, XFs, styles, style-name length), and the duplicate-style-name check is linear, so a hostile file cannot make opening it slow.

## How it was verified

- `cargo fmt --all --check` passes locally.
- Tests build the BIFF8 records in code (`crates/xlsx/src/tests/xls_style_tests.rs`), including truncated and byte-mutated records. They run on the CI workflow for this PR. The author did not build or run them on the machine that prepared this branch.
- CodeRabbit (`cr review --gate major`) reported two major findings on the duplicate-style-name scan. Both are fixed (a set of lowercased names replaces the nested scan). The re-run then reported one minor finding, an hour estimate in `docs/gaps.md` that did not match `docs/file-format-parity.md`; t…

title: XLS: import notes, hyperlinks and frozen panes
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
## What this adds

Importing a `.xls` (Excel 97-2003) workbook now reads three things it used to skip with a warning:

- **Cell notes**: the author, the note text (including line breaks), and whether the note is shown or hidden.
- **Hyperlinks**: web and mailto links, absolute and relative file links, links to places in the workbook, tooltips, and links on a range of cells. Links are capped at 10,000 cells per sheet, as for `.xlsx`.
- **Frozen panes**, with the scrolling pane's top-left cell. Split (unfrozen) panes are still removed, with a warning.

The sheet display options (gridlines, headings, formulas, zero values, right-to-left and page break preview) are read from the sheet window record as well. A truncated window record is ignored.

## Why

Workbooks saved by Excel 97-2003 lost these features on open, and the reader only warned that they were not imported. Reading them brings `.xls` import closer to Excel's behaviour without changing anything for `.xlsx`.

## How it is built

- The new reader is in `crates/xlsx/src/xls/objects.rs`. It gathers the records of a sheet while it is read and applies them when the sheet ends, so record order in the file does not matter. A malformed note or link is skipped with a warning; it never fails the whole file.
- Every read is bounded: text and declared lengths are capped by the bytes that are actually there, `..\` steps are capped at 64, and notes and links are capped per sheet.
- The sheet display options were previously read in two places. They are now read only in `objects.rs`, with the truncated-record rule from `main`.
- Docs updated: `ROADMAP.md` and `docs/file-format-parity.md`.

## How it was verified

- Tests build the BIFF8 records in code, in `crates/xlsx/src/tests/xls_tests.rs`. They include a mutation and truncation sweep over the hostile-input cases, and a check of the 10,000-cell cap.
- The branch was merged with the current `main`. The conflicts were in the `.xls` reader, its tests and the two docs. Both si…

title: Shift+Arrow on a whole column or row keeps the view on the rows or columns it showed
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #2451.

Ctrl+Space selects the whole column (the selection the report describes as a row), and a whole column's moving end, the corner opposite the anchor, sits on the sheet's last row. Shift+Right moves that corner one column across, and the scroll-into-view added in #763 for keyboard extensions then brings the corner into view, which jumps the grid to the bottom of the sheet. Shift+Space followed by Shift+Down does the same horizontally, out to the last column. The fix is in `grid::show`: when the extended area is a whole column and the extension did not move the corner's row, the vertical scroll stays where it was, and for a whole row the horizontal scroll does the same. An extension that reaches the edge itself still follows the corner: Ctrl+Shift+Down past the data to the last row (#762) scrolls down as before, and Ctrl+Shift+Right on a whole column scrolls across while the rows stay put. I took "the view stays where it is" from the report and couldn't find Microsoft documentation on how Excel scrolls here, happy to adjust if it behaves differently.

Validation:
- `selection_scroll::shift_arrows_on_a_whole_column_leave_the_rows_where_they_are`: fails on main (the view starts at row 100 and its scroll jumps from 1351 to 20970720 after one Shift+Right), passes here
- `selection_scroll::shift_arrows_on_a_whole_row_leave_the_columns_where_they_are`: the same for Shift+Space then Shift+Down from column CA, fails on main, passes here
- `selection_scroll::ctrl_shift_down_past_the_data_to_the_whole_column_still_follows_the_moving_end` and `ctrl_shift_right_on_a_whole_column_follows_across_and_keeps_the_rows` guard the cases where the extension itself reaches the last row or column
- `cargo test --workspace --test it -- selection_scroll` (18 passed), `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

title: XLSX: keep chart style, colour and user-shape parts on save
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
## What this changes

Worksheet charts in an XLSX file keep three of their own parts when GridCraft saves the file:

- the chart style part (the Chart Styles gallery choice),
- the colour part (the Change Colors set),
- the user-shape part (text boxes, shapes and pictures drawn inside the chart).

Before this change those parts were dropped on save, so a chart came back in Excel with its default style and without its text boxes. The parts are now written back with their original bytes. The style and colour parts are left out once GridCraft changes the chart's type or style number, because they no longer describe the chart. Chartex charts (waterfall, histogram and similar) keep their style and colour parts too.

## Why

Users who open a workbook with styled charts and save it lose that formatting without any warning. The chart parts are read from the file and kept on the chart, the same way other unmodelled XLSX parts already are.

## How it was verified

- `cargo fmt --check` passes locally.
- The full test suite and `cargo xtask ci` have not been run on this machine, which has too little memory. The fork's CI workflow runs the full gate on this PR. See the checks on the PR.
- Round-trip tests in `crates/xlsx/src/tests/passthrough_tests.rs` cover the style, colour and user-shape parts for column and chartex charts, and the rules for when they are left out.
- An automated review (CodeRabbit, gated on major findings) reported two major findings. One was a test fixture missing the `Series.quartiles` field added on main; it is fixed in `7cae80ca`. The other is described under known limitations below.

## Known limitations

- A worksheet chart with user shapes that is changed to a chartex type (waterfall, histogram) drops those shapes on save. title: XLSX: keep PivotTables on a data connection, the Data Model or another workbook on save
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
## What

XLSX PivotTables that read from a data connection, from the workbook's Data Model, or from a range or name in another workbook are now kept on save instead of being dropped.

Before this change, such a PivotTable was read as unsupported. On save it was lost together with its cache, and the Data Model part (`xl/model/item.data`) was never written back. Excel then opened the file without the PivotTable.

Now the pass-through layer keeps them:

- the PivotTable parts, with their sheet, unchanged apart from renumbered style references;
- the cache definition and records parts, with the workbook and its `pivotCache` entry, keeping the original `cacheId`;
- the Data Model part byte for byte whenever the workbook's connections are kept.

A cache on a data connection is kept only with its connections, and a cache on the Data Model only when the model is kept. If that is not possible, the PivotTable is left as plain cells with one warning.

## Why

A file that Excel saved with a PivotTable on a data connection or the Data Model should still have that PivotTable after GridCraft saves it. Dropping it loses the user's report and its refresh source.

## How it was verified

- The branch adds tests to `crates/xlsx/src/tests/passthrough_tests.rs` for the kept parts and the cache and connection rules.
- The commit history records a check in Excel with synthetic workbooks (Excel opens the saved file without repair and refreshes the PivotTables). That check was not repeated for this merge.
- `cargo fmt --check` passes locally. The full `cargo xtask ci` gate runs on this PR through the fork's CI; this build was not compiled locally.

title: Journal and undo: a command that runs other commands is one step
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
## What this changes

A command that runs other commands is now one undo step and one journal entry.

- **Undo:** Subtotal, From Text/CSV and Remove Duplicates used to record each inner step as its own undo entry, so Ctrl+Z stopped halfway through the operation. The whole operation now undoes in one step, as it does in Excel.
- **Journal:** the same commands used to journal their inner steps as well, so a replayed or recorded script ran each inner step and then the command again. Only the outermost command is journaled now.
- **Run Script** is not journaled itself; the steps it runs are, once each.
- **Inserting copied cells** no longer pops undo entries by counting revisions; it relies on the same outermost-command rule.
- **Bounded history:** while a command runs, its nested undo steps are trimmed to the existing budget, but never below the history the command started with, so the steps it takes back are kept. A long script can't hold a snapshot per step until it finishes.

This branch also merges the current `main`. Conflicts were in the journal and undo code (which now combines `main`'s journal byte cap and undo memory budget with the nested-command rules), in the Run Script command (which keeps `main`'s new parameters and Trust Scripts), and in two docs.

## How it was verified

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes locally. The full build, test, clippy and wasm gate was not run on the machine that prepared this branch (low memory); it runs in this PR's CI.
- New regression test `trimming_stops_at_the_floor` covers the bounded trim. The existing `subtotal_is_one_undo_step`, `subtotal_near_the_history_limit_keeps_the_oldest_steps` and `a_recorded_subtotal_replays_once` tests cover the undo and journal behaviour.
- CodeRabbit's CLI review (`--gate major`) found two major issues in an earlier revision (unbounded history during long commands). Both are fixed in this branch, and the re-run reported zero findings.

## Summary

In Excel, the arrow next to Formulas › Error Checking opens a menu, and its Circular References submenu lists the cells on circular references. A partial recalculation now keeps the loops among the formulas it does not evaluate. In automatic calculation a loop leaves the list once an edit breaks it. title: RATE follows Excel's iteration
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
## What this changes

`RATE` now follows the iteration Excel uses, so its answers match Excel's in the cases where the old solver differed:

- Slowly converging cases return the same last iterate Excel does. For example, `RATE(5,0,-100,0)` is about -0.999999409 (it was `#NUM!`).
- Very large rates that Excel's iteration cannot reach are `#NUM!`, as in Excel (for example `RATE(4,0,-0.0001,100)`; it used to return 30.62).
- A guess at or below -100% is `#VALUE!`, as in Excel.
- Subnormal steps are flushed to zero, as Excel does.

The solver was reconstructed from observed Excel results on synthetic inputs, not from Excel's code. The comment above `rate_solve` records the rules. `solve_rate` (used by IRR, XIRR and YIELD) is unchanged.

The branch also carries new `PMT` tests (within a few ULPs of Excel's values, plus edge cases), which were on the fork branch already.

## How it was verified

- New tests in `crates/functions/src/financial.rs`: `rate_follows_excel_iteration`, `pmt_matches_excel_within_a_few_ulps`, `pmt_edge_cases_follow_excel`.

- Merged with the current `main`. Conflicts were in `ROADMAP.md`, `docs/function-parity.md` and the test module of `financial.rs`; both sides were kept.

title: SORT, SORTBY and Data > Sort order numbers exactly, like Excel
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
## What this changes

SORT, SORTBY, Data > Sort (including the AutoFilter and table sorts) now compare numbers exactly, the way Excel 365 does.

Before, `sort_compare` fell through to the 15-significant-digit comparison used by `=`. So `0.3` and `=0.1+0.2` (which is `0.30000000000000004`) tied, and the sort kept whatever order the rows were already in. Excel puts `0.3` first when sorting ascending and last when descending, in either input order.

## Why

A sort should not depend on the order the rows started in when two values differ only past the 15th digit. The fix is one arm in `sort_compare`: `(Value::Number(x), Value::Number(y)) => x.partial_cmp(y)`.

Only the sorting paths change. `=`, COUNTIF and the other criteria functions keep their 15-digit comparison, as observed in Excel. UNIQUE, RANK, LARGE, SMALL and MODE already behaved exactly and are checked in the new tests so they stay that way.

## Changes

- `crates/core/src/value.rs`: exact number arm in `sort_compare`, with a unit test. Zero and negative zero still tie.
- `crates/functions/src/dynamic.rs`: SORT and SORTBY test over several noisy/exact pairs, both input orders, ascending and descending.
- `crates/engine/src/tests.rs`: Data > Sort, ascending and descending, and the quick sort command, in both input orders.
- `crates/calc/src/tests.rs`: formula-level check of SORT, SORTBY, RANK, LARGE, SMALL and MODE alongside `=` and COUNTIF.
- `ROADMAP.md`, `docs/function-parity.md`: progress rows for the change.

title: Resize Table: refuse merged cells, PivotTables and arrays; name new columns like Excel
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
## What

`table.resize` now refuses a new range that covers merged cells, a PivotTable report, or a multi-cell array formula. A spilled formula is still allowed, as in Excel. Columns a resize adds are named the way Excel names them, and generated names are written into the header row, so the header row and the column names agree after save and reopen.

## Why

- A resize could grow a table over merged cells, a PivotTable or an array. The result is a file Excel repairs by removing the table.
- A generated column name could repeat a header already in the row. The header row and the column names then drifted apart, and the reader renamed the column on reopen.

Main already refuses a resize that lands on another table (36e45a5c). This branch keeps that check, so it is not duplicated.

## Open question for the maintainers

Upstream PR https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/pull/2331 (open) handles merged cells the other way: it unmerges them on `table.resize` instead of refusing. The two touch the same merged-cell behaviour in `table_resize`, so one choice has to win before both go upstream.

## How it was verified

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes locally.
- Build and tests were not run on the author's machine (memory limits there). The full `cargo xtask ci` gate runs in this PR's CI.
- New tests are in `crates/engine/tests/it/table_resize_overlap.rs`. They cover refusal over another table, merged cells, a PivotTable and an array, the spill case, Excel-style column names, the header row staying in step with names across save and reopen, and tables without a header row.

title: Filter: SUBTOTAL over filtered table rows keeps its value after save and reopen
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
## What this fixes

A SUBTOTAL over filtered table rows lost its value after save and reopen. The sheet AutoFilter that filtered the table could not be written to the file, because a file only holds a table's own filter in that place. The writer dropped it, so the filter criteria were lost and the rows it hid reopened as rows hidden by hand. SUBTOTAL 1-11 counts those rows, so its result changed.

## What changed

- A sheet AutoFilter that starts on a table's header row is saved as that table's own filter, merged with the table's existing criteria.

title: XLSX: keep a table's query table on save
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
## What

A table that is the result range of a data-connection query (`tableType="queryTable"`) is now saved with its query table. Before, the reader treated it as a plain table and the writer dropped `xl/queryTables/queryTableN.xml`, so Excel no longer knew where the table's data came from.

- If the part is missing, damaged, over 1 MB or has relationships of its own, the table is kept as a plain table and the read reports a warning. The writer never emits `tableType="queryTable"` without a part.
- Copy Sheet already clears tables, so a query table is never duplicated.

title: XLSX: password to modify is kept on save and asked for on open
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
Fixes #921.

## What
An XLSX with a "password to modify" (`<fileSharing>` write reservation) used to open with no prompt, and saving dropped the password.

- Model: `Workbook.write_reservation` (user name, read-only-recommended flag, password hash; never the password).
- XLSX: `fileSharing` is read (legacy `reservationPassword` and iterated SHA hashes) and written back in schema order after `fileVersion`.
- Engine: `file.open` on such a file needs `modifyPassword`, or `readOnly: true`. Without either it returns an error carrying `io::MODIFY_PASSWORD_REQUIRED` (no dialog for programmatic calls). A wrong password returns the existing "password is incorrect" error. A read-only open gets no save path, so Save asks for a new file instead of overwriting the original.
- UI: File > Open (desktop and web) shows the existing password dialog with a "Read Only" checkbox.

## Verification
Not built or run locally; relies on this PR's CI. Tests added: XLSX full round trip includes the reservation (`roundtrip.rs`), and an engine test covers required, wrong, correct and read-only opens plus the reservation surviving a save (`engine/src/tests.rs`). Docs updated (file-format-parity, ROADMAP).

## Unverified / limits
- **Not checked against real Excel**: its prompt wording, read-only behaviour and whether it accepts the files we write are unobserved.
- `readOnlyRecommended` alone does not prompt; it is only preserved.
- A file that is both encrypted and has a password to modify is not handled in the UI flow (the modify prompt does not carry the open password).

free one.

title: XLSX: the XML element cap counts only elements kept in the tree
author: RedBearAK
body:
**Summary**

- Bug fix: workbooks with a worksheet of about a million cells open whole again; since #2413 they were cut off at a few thousand rows and reported damaged.
- The XML element cap now counts only elements kept in the parsed tree, not the cells of streamed rows or shared strings.
- Tests: a streamed part just over the cap is read whole; the same part kept in a tree is still refused.

Since #2413 a workbook with a worksheet of about a million cells is reported damaged on open and cut off after a few thousand rows. This makes the new element cap count only what the parser actually keeps.

- `parse_streaming` counted every element it attached to a parent, including the cells of a `row` that is then streamed to the callback and dropped, so the count grew with the whole sheet although the tree never held more than one row. Shared strings, streamed by `si`, had the same exposure.
- The count now returns to its value at the start of a split element when that element is handed out. A streamed part of any size passes; a part that keeps a million elements in its tree is still refused, as #2413 intended.
- Regression test: 5,001 streamed rows of 100 cells, just over the cap, are read whole; the same bytes parsed into a tree are refused. The test fails on current main.

How I ran into it: a workbook from a generating library with one sheet of 12,274 rows by 103 columns (about 1.0 million populated cells) opened whole before #2413 and, since, stops at row 6,310 with "the part holds more than 1000000 elements". With this change the CLI reads it whole again, and its output is identical to a build from just before #2413.

title: Return None from datetime_from_serial when rounding carries past 9999
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/core/src/date.rs:168-177` (no existing issue): datetime_from_serial returns year 10000 for the last fraction of 9999-12-31.

## Cause
datetime_from_serial accepts any serial below max_serial+1. For serials in the last half millisecond of 9999-12-31, the fraction rounds up to 86,400,000 ms and the day carries to max_serial+1. The result is year 10000, which Excel cannot show.

## Fix
After the millisecond carry, the function now returns None if the day exceeds max_serial for the date system. This matches the documented behaviour for too-large serials. A regression test covers both the 1900 and 1904 systems.

## Verified
- Regression test `date::tests::serial_rounding_into_next_day_past_max_is_none`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p gridcraft-core serial_rounding`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `io::tests::save_keeps_the_destination_access_restrictions`, which also fails on `main` without this change.

## Not changed
Serials that don't carry, such as 9999-12-31 23:59:59.999, are unchanged. I did not clamp to 9999-12-31 23:59:59.999, because the function is documented to return None for too-large serials.

title: XLSX: a streamed row or shared string holds no more than the schema allows
author: RedBearAK
body:
**Summary**

- Depends on #2527 and is built on its commit; review the one commit on top. Once #2527 merges, that commit drops out of this diff on its own.
- Hardening: a streamed worksheet row keeps what the schema allows it, 16,384 cells and one extension list, and a shared string its one text, one phonetic properties and its runs; anything else is dropped as parsed with an import warning that says what and why, and a cell past the width can no longer overwrite a cell already read.
- Nothing representable is lost: cell text and runs past Excel's 32,767 characters are kept whole with a warning that Excel may refuse or repair the saved file, instead of being cut.
- Elements the schema does not know are tolerated a few times and then dropped, so a crafted part cannot slow the parser or crowd out legitimate children.
- Excel's limits live in `gridcraft_core::addr`, with their source and a note on raising them; tests sit on the exact edges.

Follow-up to #2527. That fix made the element cap count only what the parser keeps, which is right, but it left one streamed element free to grow to the cap itself: a crafted part could put half a million cells into one `row` and the reader would build all of them before throwing away everything past column XFD. No legitimate file comes near that, since Excel cannot write more than 16,384 cells in a row, so the parser now keeps no more than the schema allows.

- `xml::parse_streaming` takes a `Streaming` description: the split element names, and for each streamed element every child the schema allows it, by name, with its own allowance. For a row that is `("c", MAX_COLS)` and `("extLst", 1)`; for a shared string `("t", 1)`, `("phoneticPr", 1)` and the `r` and `rPh` runs without a count of their own. A child past its allowance is kept out of the tree once parsed, with its subtree (a streamed element nested inside it has already been handed out by then), and counted in the result; one such child is itself still bounded by the element…

title: fix(web): mark PDF exports in gridcraft:save (#2452)
author: Zaxaerith
body:
## Problem

In Web Host mode (`?host=parent`), saving an XLSX workbook and exporting a PDF both emit `gridcraft:save` with only a name and bytes. A parent that replaces its workbook on every save message can overwrite that workbook with the PDF.

## Changes

- Add a JavaScript boolean `export` to the outgoing save message using `JsValue::from_bool`.
- Reuse the existing case-insensitive `is_workbook` rule: XLSX saves have `export: false`; non-workbook outputs, including PDF, have `export: true`. Unknown output types are exports, not implicitly classified as PDFs.
- Put the borrowed save payload and existing save-receipt application block in a small `host_save` module, enabled for WASM and native tests using the existing `prefs` module pattern.
- Keep the saved-snapshot/title update logic unchanged: PDF receipts do not mark a workbook clean; XLSX receipts do.
- Update the protocol description at the top of `host.rs`.

## Protocol compatibility

`type: "gridcraft:save"`, `name` and `bytes` retain their existing meanings. The ArrayBuffer is still passed in the same transfer list, with no additional payload copy introduced by the borrowed metadata. Same-origin/parent validation, the download callback, other message types and dirty-state reporting remain unchanged.

Hosts should update the workbook for `export: false` and store a separate exported file for `export: true`. Older hosts can ignore the additive field and continue parsing the original fields, but need to adopt it to avoid the issue. Save versus Save As remains outside this change (#2442); no `saveAs` field is added.

## Regression coverage

Four native unit tests are written against the helpers used by the bridge:

- `finance.xlsx` / `finance.XLSX` -> false; `finance.pdf` / `finance.PDF` -> true, with the original name and byte slice retained.
- Other extensions and extensionless output remain exports; the final extension determines the existing workbook classification.
- PDF receipts preserve the dirty state…

title: Windows: the quality gate passes (clippy, test build, generated-file check, font-independent AutoFit check)
author: GabLavareda
body:
On Windows, `cargo xtask ci` cannot pass on `main` today, which blocks the gate the repository asks for before every commit. Five small fixes, none of which change behaviour:

- **`xtask` `parity` and `keytips`** — both compare the generated file with the one on disk byte for byte, so they fail on any checkout whose files carry CRLF. Git for Windows writes them that way by default (`core.autocrlf=true`), while the renderers produce LF, so a fresh clone reports `docs/parity-checklist.md is out of date` while `git diff` shows nothing — which makes the failure hard to place. Compared ignoring line endings. (A repo-wide `.gitattributes` with `eol=lf` would also fix this, if you prefer that; it changes everyone's working tree, so I went with the contained change.)
- **`crates/ui-egui/src/desktop_theme.rs`** — off Linux `Link` is `()`, so `let mut link = Link::default()` is a unit binding and `clippy::let_unit_value` fails the build under `-D warnings`. Allowed on that binding, with a comment: the loop still carries the link between reads on Linux.
- **`apps/gridcraft-cli/src/check.rs`** — `seen` is read only inside the `cfg(unix)` block, so off unix `clippy::only_used_in_recursion` fails the build. `cfg_attr(not(unix), allow(...))`, since the depth cap alone is the intended behaviour there.
- **`crates/engine/src/io.rs`** — `save_fails_upfront_when_the_temp_name_is_taken` calls `std::os::unix::fs::symlink` but is gated only on `not(target_arch = "wasm32")`, so the engine's test build does not compile. Gated on `cfg(unix)`, like the test below it.

title: Migrate GridCraft to egui 0.37
author: skylartaylor
body:
GridCraft uses the pinned egui 0.37 fork and updated shared UI/printing dependencies. The port covers IME, screenshot completion, accessibility, ribbon scrolling and embedded-font notices. This branch now includes main through `3b65b9af`, including the 0.12.1 workspace version and new iteration settings.

Review fixes preserve RTL frozen-pane editor clipping, enforce screenshot budgets during issuance and minimized-window retries, and require the exact font-mode value `1`. Shared test-harness setup preserves each test's dimensions, timing, OS and fonts. Documentation now covers the migration-touched helpers and test invariants.

The combined-main run exposed unnamed Maximum Iterations and Maximum Change inputs. Both now reference their visible labels, including while disabled. The interaction test queries those accessible names while retaining its value, validation, enable/disable and undo assertions. title: Remove sparklines when their row or column is deleted
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/sheet.rs:~199 (shift_sheet_features, sparklines loop)` (no existing issue): Deleting a row or column leaves its sparklines behind, so they land on the next row or column.

## Cause
When rows or columns are deleted, the sparkline loop in `shift_sheet_features` only updated `sp.cell` if `map_cell` returned a new position. A sparkline whose own cell was deleted kept its old address, so it stayed on whatever row or column slid into that place.

## Fix
The sparkline loop now uses `retain_mut`. It moves sparklines whose cell maps to a new position and drops those whose cell maps to None. This matches how comments and hyperlinks are handled.

## Verified
- Regression test `tests::deleting_a_row_removes_its_sparklines`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p gridcraft-engine deleting_a_row_removes_its_sparklines`).

## Not changed
The other two `sparklines.iter_mut()` loops in sheet.rs are unchanged. I added a regression test only for row deletion, not for column deletion.

title: Print huge and tiny CLI numbers in exponent form
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `apps/gridcraft-cli/src/main.rs:196-199 (number_text, used by value_text and check.rs:627)` (no existing issue): CLI eval/cat print huge or tiny numbers as hundreds of digits instead of exponent form.

## Cause
`number_text` only special-cased whole numbers below 1e15 and sent everything else through `format!("{n}")`. Rust's `Display` for f64 never uses exponent notation, so `1E300` printed 301 digits and `1E-20` printed `0.00000000000000000001`.

## Fix
`number_text` now switches to exponent form for finite values with magnitude of at least 1e15 or below 1e-5. It writes them like `1e+300` and `1e-20`, adding the `+` that Rust's `{:e}` leaves out for positive exponents. The `value_texts` test now covers huge, tiny and boundary values.

## Verified
- Regression test `value_texts`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p gridcraft-cli value_texts`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `io::tests::save_keeps_the_destination_access_restrictions`, which also fails on `main` without this change.

## Not changed
Whole numbers below 1e15 and ordinary decimals print as before. NaN and infinity are not touched. The thresholds are not tuned to Excel's own switch-over points.

author: ArkSentinel
body:
# PivotTables: Excel-parity epic — field list, value settings, filters, grouping, show-values-as, XLSX round trip

## Why

PivotTables were tracked at ~65% feature / ~45% quality against Excel. The report engine could
produce a pivot, but a working analyst could not actually *use* one:

- The field list's only gesture was a checkbox. Excel's four areas, drag & drop, right-click menus
  and reordering did not exist.
- `Value Field Settings` did not exist as a dialog, so 2 of 12 show-values-as modes, 5 of 11 summary
  functions and any number format were unreachable.
- Grouping stopped at days; there were no numeric bins, no manual text groups, no value-based
  filters, no sort-by-field, no blank lines or empty/error display.
- Most of those settings, once added, would have been lost on save.

This PR closes that epic. It is the accumulated result of several sessions; the sections below cover
the whole change, not one sitting.

## 1. Field list: drag & drop, 1:1 with Excel (`crates/ui-egui/src/pivot_pane.rs`)

`dnd_drag_source` / `dnd_drop_zone` for the unassigned field list and all four areas.

| Gesture | Result |
|---|---|
| Drag within an area | reorder |
| Drag between areas | move |
| Drag outside every area | remove |
| Drop `Σ Values` outside Rows/Columns | no-op |
| Left click | nothing |
| Right click | `Value Field Settings` |

`Σ Values` is a display slot, not a field, so the landing index subtracts the `Σ Values` slots above

title: Set ő, ű and other Latin Extended-A letters in the Latin PDF font
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #2547

## Cause
Every character without a WinAnsiEncoding (CP1252) byte, including Latin letters such as ő (U+0151) and ű (U+0171), was moved out of the text run into the non-embedded Chinese CID font STSong-Light with a fixed full-em advance. title: Keep <scheme val="minor"/> on every body-font font on save
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #2517

## Cause
The model `Font` had no record of the theme scheme link, so `write_styles` guessed it from the font's index and wrote `<scheme val="minor"/>` only on font 0. Any other font in the theme's body face lost the link on save. That covers fonts a command derives from the default one (bold, a size, a colour) and fonts that had the scheme in the loaded file.

## Fix
`Font` now has a `minor` flag. It is true for new fonts, for fonts read with `<scheme val="minor"/>`, and for fonts outside the theme's minor face (where the flag does not change the output). It is copied to every font derived from it. The writer adds the scheme to any font that has the flag and is in the theme's minor face. The reader now loads the theme before the styles, so the body-face check uses the right font name. Output for a font outside the body face is unchanged. Differential fonts keep their scheme in `dxf_stated` as before.

## Verified
- Regression tests `tests::roundtrip::minor_scheme_survives_on_every_font`, `font_scheme_minor::derived_body_font_keeps_minor_scheme`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p gridcraft-xlsx minor_scheme_survives_on_every_font && cargo test -p gridcraft-engine --test it font_scheme_minor`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Font 0 still gets the scheme whenever it is in the theme's body face, as before (#805). The dxf font writer is unchanged. For self-describing serde formats, a missing `minor` field defaults to true. No binary (postcard/bincode) format serializes `Font` in this repository, so no format version changed.

title: Format Cells: apply only the changed style properties to a range
author: Silvertree2010
body:

## Cause
The Format Cells dialog starts from the active cell's full style. On OK it sent that whole style as the `home.formatCells` patch, so the active cell's borders, fill and font were copied onto every selected cell, even when only the number format had changed. title: Text files: Text Import with delimiter and decimal detection, .prn open and save (#2553)
author: iluebbe
body:
Closes #2553.

## Problem

Excel starts its Text Import Wizard when a `.txt` file is opened. GridCraft split a `.txt` at tabs only and offered no choice, so a file separated by `;`, `,`, `|` or anything else landed in one column. A `.prn` (Formatted Text) was read like a `.csv`, so commas inside its text split the lines, and saving as `.prn` was refused.

Numbers are the other half of the problem. Excel with German region settings reads English values wrong, in the same way whether they are typed, imported with the wizard or opened as `.csv`:

| English value | Excel, German region |
|---|---|
| `1.5`, `3.12` | dates: 1 May, 3 December |
| `1.234` | 1234 |
| `1,234` | 1.234 |
| `0.125`, `1,234.5` | text |

GridCraft did the opposite and read every file with English rules, so `1,5` in a German `;` file stayed text.

## Change

**Reading text files** (`crates/xlsx/src/text_layout.rs`, `csv.rs`):
- **Splitting:** the tokenizer splits at one or more delimiters, each one or more characters (`||`), optionally treating consecutive delimiters as one. It also splits at fixed widths or not at all (whole lines).
- **Detecting the split:** each candidate is scored by complete rows × clean cells × (k − 1)/k, where k is the most common field count.
  - Candidates: `,` `;` tab `|`, any other punctuation or 2–3-character string of it found on almost every line, runs of spaces, fixed width, and none.
  - Characters that belong to values are never guessed: `.`, `-`, currency signs, `:` in times, `/` in dates.
  - Any character other than `,` `;` tab `|` or space needs clean cells, so punctuation inside text (`https://`, `Re:`, `Order #1`) never splits a line.
  - A title before the table is detected and can be skipped. A row holding a delimiter that splits every row is that table's header, never a title.
  - File › Open of a `.csv` without settings chooses only among `,`, `;` and tab, as Excel does, because it shows no preview.
  - `,` inside one column of numbers (`Betrag` above `1.…

title: AutoSum: a selected row gets its total to the right, as in Excel
author: arcanii
body:
## What it does

AutoSum over any selection of more than one cell wrote a total under each column. Select a row of numbers, say B2:E2, and press AutoSum (Home › AutoSum, Formulas › AutoSum, Alt+=): GridCraft wrote four one-cell totals in row 3, `=SUM(B2:B2)` to `=SUM(E2:E2)`. Excel writes one total, `=SUM(B2:E2)`, in F2.

Now, as in Excel, totals go in the selection's empty last row or column, and otherwise past it:

| Selection | Totals |
|---|---|
| One row | In its last cell when that is empty (the sum of the cells before it), else in the cell just to its right |
| A block whose last column is empty | Each row's total in that column |
| A block whose last row is empty | Each column's total in that row (as before) |
| Both empty | Both, and the block's total in the corner |
| Neither empty | Each column's total in the row below (as before) |

The function menu (Average, Count Numbers, Max, Min) follows the same rules.

## How

All in `auto_sum` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/formulas.rs`), in its branch for selections of more than one cell:
- A selection of one row puts its total to the right. A whole-row selection (`2:2`) stops at the data's last column, as the column totals already do, so it never writes out at column XFD.
- Otherwise the selection's last column is empty when every one of its cells in the data's rows is. It then takes each row's total. Column totals are written when the last row is empty, or when the last column isn't.
- All totals are still one edit, so one undo step, and the single-cell guess is unchanged.

## Checks

On macOS 27.0.1 with Rust 1.98.1: fmt, clippy, nextest (2,407 tests), doctests, assets, layers, wasm, parity and keytips all pass. Not run on Windows or Linux.

title: Create new saved files without group/other write permission
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #2519

## Cause
`write_file` creates the temporary file for a brand-new destination with no explicit mode, so the file gets `0o666 & !umask`. Under umask 0002 that is `0o664`, which is group-writable. This contradicts the intended restrictive default and fails `save_keeps_the_destination_access_restrictions`.

## Fix
When the destination doesn't exist, `write_file` now opens the temporary file with mode `0o644` on Unix. The umask can still remove more bits, but it can no longer leave group or other write set. The new regression test re-runs itself in a child shell with umask 0002.

## Verified

- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Saving over an existing file still copies that file's permissions. Non-Unix behaviour is unchanged. Group/other read on new files is left to the umask, so I did not make new files `0o600`.

title: XLSX: rows with a duplicate, out-of-order or wrong-row cell address are repaired on import (fixes #2531)
author: zyzabruh
body:
Fixes #2531.

## Problem

The worksheet reader placed every cell where its `r` attribute said. Nothing checked that the address belonged to the enclosing `<row>`, followed the previous cell's column, or had not been used already, so a damaged or badly generated file changed values with a clean open and no import warning:

| Row 1 holds, in order | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `A1`=1, `C1`=3, `B1`=2, `A1`=999 | `A1` is 999 (the later duplicate replaced the first) | `A1` is 1, `B1` dropped, 1 warning |
| `A1`=1, `D7`=7 (inside the row element for row 1) | `D7` is 7, moved into row 7 | `D7` dropped, 1 warning |
| `A1`=1, `D7`=7, then a cell with no `r` holding 8 | 8 lands at `E1`, after the stray address | 8 lands at `B1`, after the last cell that was kept |
| `A1`, `C1`, `E1` (a row that skips columns) | fine | fine, no warning |

Excel never writes cells out of column order, repeated or in another row than their `<row>`, and treats such a file as damaged. Placing them as written let one cell shadow another and moved values the user never sees move.

## Root cause

`read_row` (`crates/xlsx/src/sheet_read.rs`) took `pos` from the cell's `r` attribute as given, and `read_cell` writes it with `sheet.cells.set(pos, …)`, which replaces an earlier cell at the same address. `next_col`, which positions an unaddressed `<c>`, only advanced for cells that were kept, so a stray address also shifted where the next unaddressed cell landed.

## Solution

`read_row` keeps the shape Excel writes, as #2531 proposes:

- A cell whose address names another row than the enclosing `<row>` (explicit or implied), or whose column is not after the previous kept cell's column, is dropped and counted. That covers a repeated address, a cell out of order and a wrong-row cell in one check.
- Within one row element the first value read for an address is kept: a repeat there is dropped rather than overwriting what was already read. A second `<row>` element carrying the same row number is merged …

title: PDF: map multiple workbook font families through CLI and MCP
author: uwe-schwarz
body:
PDF export can now preserve several font families from one workbook by mapping their stored names to local TrueType faces. The existing global font options remain available as a fallback for unmapped families.

```sh
gridcraft-cli convert book.xlsx report.pdf \
  --pdf-font-family 'Body Sans=/path/to/Body-Regular.ttf' \
  --pdf-font-family-bold 'Body Sans=/path/to/Body-Bold.ttf' \
  --pdf-font-family 'Heading Sans=/path/to/Heading-Regular.ttf' \
  --pdf-font-family-italic 'Heading Sans=/path/to/Heading-Italic.ttf'
```

MCP, CLI scripts and the control channel use the same `file.exportPdf` / `file.print` parameters:

```json
{"command":"file.exportPdf","params":{"path":"report.pdf","fontFamilies":{"Body Sans":{"regular":"/path/to/Body-Regular.ttf","bold":"/path/to/Body-Bold.ttf"},"Heading Sans":{"regular":"/path/to/Heading-Regular.ttf","italic":"/path/to/Heading-Italic.ttf"}}}}
```

- Match workbook family names case-insensitively after trimming. Each family requires `regular` and can supply `bold`, `italic` and `boldItalic`. Omitted styles use that family's regular face. Distinct families have independent PDF resources and advance widths, including two families that would otherwise both map to Helvetica. Named mappings win over an optional global `fonts` override.

title: Clear Formats removes conditional formatting (#2536)
author: kulveersingh
body:
Fixes #2536.

**Problem:** Clear Formats (and Clear All) reset cell styles but never touched the sheet's conditional formats, so the rule's colours stayed on the cleared cells.

**Change** (`crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs`, `crates/engine/src/cmd/data.rs`):
- Clear Formats and Clear All cut the cleared cells out of every conditional format's ranges, as Excel does. The rest of each rule keeps it, and a rule left with no cells is removed. Clear Contents is unchanged.
- The cut uses the whole selection, not the used-range part `clear()` iterates, so rules on empty cells (the usual colour-scale case) go too.
- Rule formulas are relative to the first range's top-left cell. The piece that keeps that cell stays first; when the cell itself is cleared, `Expression` and `CellIs` formulas are rebased with the existing `move_rule_formula`, so the remaining cells still test themselves.
- Cuts apply largest first. A cut that would grow one rule past 16,384 ranges (and past its own size) is refused and nothing changes, so a hostile `range` with many parts can't grow a rule without bound. Go To Special's largest selection (2,000 areas) stays well under it.

**Tests** (`crates/engine/src/tests.rs`): partial clears, rules on empty cells, Clear All vs Clear Contents, undo/redo, formula rebasing for a column and a 2-D cut through the corner, an XLSX round trip of the split rules, 500 Go To Special areas, and the cap (refused unchanged; a large area in the same selection removes the rule). The rebasing tests fail without it. `cargo xtask ci` passes locally (all 10 steps, with `CRAFT_FONTS_REQUIRED=1`).

**Left alone, possibly worth separate issues:**
- `home.clearRules` ("Clear Rules from Selected Cells") still drops every range the selection touches; the HLCE/HLCT keytips call it without parameters and rely on that, so changing it belongs with a keytip change.
- Data validation has the same anchor issue: cutting a validation's first cell (paste, `data.validation` clear) doesn't rebase i…

title: Web: page host mode, so a page can host GridCraft in its own document (#2592)
author: helenkwok
body:
Closes #2592.

A page that loads the GridCraft module into its own document can now opt into the host bridge with `data-host="page"` on `<canvas id="gridcraft_canvas">`. The messages are the `?host=parent` ones, carried as non-bubbling DOM `CustomEvent`s on the canvas: GridCraft dispatches `gridcraft:ready`, `gridcraft:save`, `gridcraft:dirty` and `gridcraft:failed` with the message fields as `detail`, and the page dispatches `gridcraft:open`.

**Design.** `Bridge` now holds a `Transport` (`Parent` or `Page`), and the two differ only in how an event goes out and how `open` comes in; the save, dirty and ready logic is shared. `?host=parent` is checked first and behaves as before, including `None` when the page isn't framed, so opening that URL directly still gives the normal app with downloads. Only the exact attribute value `page` opts in (`hostmode.rs`, unit-tested). `packaging/web/README.md` documents both host modes, with a host-page example that adds its listeners before `init`.

**Checks.** `cargo xtask ci` on Linux: i18n-report, fmt, clippy, doctest, assets, layers, wasm, parity and keytips pass; tests 2402 passed, 1 failed (`header_autofit::table_filter_autofit_works_through_command_and_header_double_click`, which fails the same way on unchanged `main` in my container). In a browser, with a release build of this branch: a page with `data-host="page"` received `gridcraft:ready`, opened a workbook it dispatched, got `dirty: true` after an edit, and on Ctrl+S received `gridcraft:save` with the workbook, whose sheet XML held the edited value; `dirty` then went back to false. The events didn't reach a `document` listener. A page without the attribute got no events, and the iframe bridge (`?host=parent`) still answered `ready` and opened a workbook.

title: fix: save through a symlink updates the target instead of replacing the link
author: SofiaAFigueredo
body:
Closes #2583

`io::write_file` wrote a temporary file and renamed it over the path it was given. When that path was a symlink (e.g. a desktop shortcut to the real workbook), the link was replaced by a regular file and the original was left unchanged, so users could silently end up editing a copy.

The path is now resolved first, so the temporary file is created beside the link's target and renamed onto it; the symlink stays in place. Paths that don't resolve (new files) are written as given.

## Tests
- New `save_through_a_symlink_updates_the_target_and_keeps_the_link`.
- Engine tests, fmt, clippy, assets and layers pass.
- Not related to this change: two `ui-egui` font-glyph tests fail locally (no `craft-fonts`), `save_keeps_the_destination_access_restrictions` is umask-dependent (fails with umask 0002 on main too), and `cargo xtask wasm` couldn't run (target not installed here; the change is non-wasm only).

title: Undo and redo keep each sheet's view (Normal, Page Layout, Page Break Preview)
author: prxnvt
body:
## What happened

Undoing an edit changed the sheet's view. Set A1, switch the sheet to Page Break Preview, then undo: A1 is cleared, and the sheet is back in Normal. Redo switches it to Page Break Preview again.

The command-sequence fuzz reports the same thing as a failed undo check after one step, `view.pageBreakPreview {"sheet": 0}` on the `sales` sample (seed 177 with `GRIDCRAFT_FUZZ_SEEDS=300`):

```
invariant [undo]: undoing all 0 steps doesn't give back the starting workbook: Sales: other sheet properties differ
```

## Why

Switching between Normal, Page Layout and Page Break Preview is not an undo step, in Excel and here (`view.normal`, `view.pageLayout` and `view.pageBreakPreview` are `noundo`). But undo and redo swap in a whole snapshot of the workbook, so they put back the view each sheet had when the snapshot was taken. The fuzz's undo check, which resets the other view state before comparing (active sheet, scroll position, active cell), compared the view mode as content.

## Changes

- **Undo and redo keep each sheet's current view** (`extra::keep_view_modes`), carried through each step of a multi-step undo or redo. Sheets are matched by name, and while a rename is undone or redone, by position under the name the restored snapshot doesn't have. A view kept this way doesn't make a saved workbook dirty, as `set_view` doesn't.
- **The fuzz's `canonical()`** resets each sheet's view mode along with the other view state, because a view switch is still not itself undone.

## Tests

- `undo_and_redo_keep_each_sheets_view`: undo and redo with each view, undoing a rename, and undoing a new sheet. Fails without the change (the view reverts to Normal).
- `a_multi_step_undo_keeps_views_through_each_step`: a rename and a new sheet undone and redone with `steps: 2`. Fails without the change.

v0.42.0 - String Ergonomics

What's Changed

0.42.0 -- 2026-08-22

This is a large release. The primary change is an ergonomic improvement across the entire API - quick_xml now makes use of &str and String types where possible instead of &[u8] and Vec<u8>. title: Local file and folder links open; =HYPERLINK() cells follow their link (#2596)
author: SofiaAFigueredo
body:
Fixes #2596.

## Problem
- A hyperlink to a local file or folder (Insert ▸ Link, or a path / `file:` address) did nothing but select the cell: the link policy from #777 refused every non-web target, `file:` and plain paths included.
- A cell with `=HYPERLINK("path", "text")` never followed its link at all (web links too), because only stored hyperlinks were looked at on click.

## Change
- `links::classify` gains `LinkKind::Local` for `file:` addresses (no host or `localhost`, percent-decoded) and paths (absolute, `~/`, relative, drive letter). `classify_link` uses the workbook's `external` mark so a bare file name is a file, not a defined name.
- `links::resolve_local` takes relative paths from the workbook's folder and refuses: missing targets; programs and scripts by extension (`.exe`, `.sh`, `.app`, `.lnk`, …), also after resolving symlinks; files with the Unix executable bit. Network shares / UNC paths and other schemes stay refused.
- `links::link_at` returns a cell's link: its stored hyperlink, or the first argument of a top-level `=HYPERLINK()`. The grid click, the tooltip and `link.open` use it.
- A click on a local link still asks first (the Open Hyperlink dialog now says it is a file or folder). The host opener (`open_with_system`) re-validates before calling `xdg-open`/`open`/`explorer`. Scripts still can't open links; the web build still opens only http(s)/mailto.

## Security note
#777 deliberately limited links to http/https/mailto. This relaxes that for existing documents and folders on the same machine only, behind the confirmation, with programs/scripts and network locations kept out. Please review that trade-off.

## Tests
- `links` unit tests: recognition, refusals (network, programs, bad escapes), `resolve_local` incl. symlink/exec-bit cases.
- Engine: `link_open_opens_existing_local_files_and_folders_but_not_programs` (hyperlink, `=HYPERLINK()`, `file:` URL, relative to saved workbook); the old refusal test now uses a remote `file://host/…`.

body:
## Summary
The Chart Type section of the Format Chart Area pane listed nine types, with stacked column as the only stacked one. GridCraft draws stacked bar, 100% stacked column and bar, stacked line, and stacked and 100% stacked area, but a chart could not be switched to them from the pane. The entries were plain buttons, so the pane did not show which type the chart had.

Microsoft's "Available chart types in Office" page lists each of these subtypes (for example "100% stacked column and 3-D 100% stacked column", "Stacked bar and 3-D stacked bar", "Stacked area and 3-D stacked area"): https://web.archive.org/web/20260417051336/https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/available-chart-types-in-office-a6187218-807e-4103-9e0a-27cdb19afb90. "Change the chart type of an existing chart" describes choosing a type for an existing chart: https://web.archive.org/web/20220601045046/https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/change-the-chart-type-of-an-existing-chart-c686d8c2-b294-43c0-b744-f54000f51454

## Changes
- Chart Type lists "100% Stacked Column", "Stacked Bar", "100% Stacked Bar", "Stacked Line", "Stacked Area" and "100% Stacked Area" after their family's entries. Each runs `chart.set` with the type and subtype the Insert menus use.
- "Stacked" is renamed "Stacked Column".
- The entry for the chart's current type is drawn selected, as the Legend entries are. The pane compares the chart's kind with `chart_kind(type, subtype)`, the mapping `chart.set` applies.

Open #2602 adds 100% stacked line kinds; this list does not include them. Open #2380 moves this section into a new Chart Settings group, so the two change the same lines.

title: Paste Special: a transposed paste turns formula references as Excel does (fixes #2450)
author: zyzabruh
body:
## Problem

Paste Special ▸ Transpose moves the copied cells but leaves each formula pointing where it pointed in the source, so the pasted cell reads the wrong neighbour.

From #2450: A3 holds 10/31/2025 and A4 holds `=A3+1` (11/1/2025). Copy A3:A4, Paste Special ▸ Transpose, and the second cell shows 1/1/1900 instead of 11/1/2025 — it still reads the cell *above* itself instead of the cell to its left.

## Root cause

`paste_special` adjusted every formula with `adjust::shift_relative(dest − sc)`, the adjustment of an **ordinary copy**: each reference moves by the same `(dr, dc)` as the cell that carries it. A transposed paste moves cells on a different mapping — the block's rows become its columns — so a shifted reference points somewhere else entirely.

## Solution

Excel **turns** the references instead of shifting them, so `paste_special` now calls a new `adjust::transpose_relative(e, src, dest)` when `transpose` is set. The paste-link and cut-paste paths are untouched.

The rule is not a guess: it is what Excel 16 produces on this machine, read out of nine synthetic workbooks over COM (relative, `$B$1`, `B$1`, `$B1`, ranges, another sheet, whole rows and columns, a reference off the grid, a source block not starting at A1, a 2×2 block, and the issue's own scenario):

- a reference's **row offset becomes its column offset** and the other way round, around the pair of positions of the cell carrying the formula: `(r, c)` → `dest + (c − src.col, r − src.row)`. `=B1+1` in A1, pasted at F6, comes out as `=F7+1`.
- a reference **pinned with `$` is left exactly as written** (`=$B1`, `=B$1`, `=$B$1`, `=SUM($B$1:$C$3)`, `=SUM($B:$C)` are byte-for-byte what Excel leaves).
- a **whole row or column comes back as a cell range** open to the sheet's edge: `=SUM(1:2)` → `=SUM(F$6:G$1048576)`, `=SUM(B:D)` → `=SUM($F7:$XFD9)` (rows/cols pinned, the open side running to the last row/column).
- a result that lands **off the grid is `#REF!`**, as for a copy that runs past the edg…

title: Fix dark mode worksheet cell colors
author: JonathanLee2020
body:
Dark mode currently changes the window chrome while leaving the worksheet white with black text. This change gives default worksheet cells black backgrounds and white text, including merged cells, overflowing text, and the in-cell editor.

Gridlines, formula reference highlights, automatic borders, sheet controls, and sheet icons follow the active theme. Explicit workbook fills and font colors remain intact; automatic cell text chooses whichever of black or white has the higher WCAG contrast against the resolved fill. The in-cell editor shares the grid's resolved style and active conditional-format cache, preserving table, conditional, color-scale and patterned fills. Its text preserves the resolved explicit font color, using automatic contrast when the font color is automatic. The caret independently chooses contrasting black or white so it stays visible even when explicit text matches the fill. Text overflow and Center Across Selection stop at empty neighbours with resolved fills, including table, conditional and patterned fills and offscreen blockers. Light-mode defaults remain white with black text. Workbook calculation, storage, and file formats are unchanged.

Adds regression coverage for light/dark/light repainting, merged-cell backgrounds, explicit colors, bright green fills in both themes, editor text/caret contrast, table and conditional styling during editing, color-scale and patterned fills, matching text/fill caret visibility, filled-neighbour overflow boundaries in both directions and themes, center-across handling, offscreen blockers, and token contrast. Documents the affected rendering helpers and regression-test guarantees. Updates the UI and architecture documentation.

title: Window per workbook (1/4): a cell draft stays in its workbook; Switch Windows
author: aiongg
body:
With several workbooks open, a cell being edited belongs to the workbook it was started in, and View › Window › Switch Windows lists the open workbooks.

This is the first of four stacked PRs that give each workbook its own window: #2616, #2617, #2618, #2619. It has no craft-libs change and can merge on its own.

## What changes

- **A cell draft stays in its workbook.** Every `file.*` and window command settles an open cell draft first, as Enter would: it commits into the workbook the draft was started in, even when another workbook is showing. If the draft can't commit (a validation Stop, a bad formula, a protected cell), the command stops, the draft stays open and its reason shows. An F2 draft nobody changed closes without writing the cell, so it doesn't mark the workbook unsaved.
- **Switch Windows.** `view.switchWindows` (no undo) lists the open workbooks as `{index, doc, title, dirty, active, hidden}` and with `{doc}` activates one. View › Window has a Switch Windows dropdown after Freeze Panes: the active workbook is checked and an unsaved one is marked. On macOS the Window menu lists the workbooks too.
- **Scripts.** A stored script already can't run `window.*` steps. It now also refuses `view.switchWindows`, `view.newWindow`, `view.hideWindow` and `view.unhideWindow`, which switch the active workbook too.
- **Quit on macOS** goes through the app's own Quit item (Cmd+Q), so the save prompt runs for each unsaved workbook.

## Overlap

#2325 also adds Switch Windows and window commands, identifying a window by its document. #2617 gives each window an id of its own, separate from its document, because New Window puts two windows on one workbook.

## Checks

Tests: a draft started in Book1 stays in Book1 after a switch; a refused draft stops the switch and stays open; an untouched F2 draft leaves the workbook clean; the quit prompt asks once per unsaved workbook. The stack was tested by hand on macOS at its top (#2619).

title: Window per workbook (2/4): windows in the engine; New Window shares the workbook
author: aiongg
body:
The engine keeps a list of windows, each showing one workbook, and View › New Window opens a second window on the same workbook.

Stacked on #2616; review the commits after it. No craft-libs change.

## What changes

- **Windows in the engine** (`crates/engine/src/windows.rs`). A session holds windows, each `{id, doc, hidden, view}`. The active window's view (selection, active sheet, scroll) lives in its document, as before, and the others keep theirs until they are activated. Opening or creating a workbook adds a window, and closing a workbook removes its windows. Window ids are never reused.
- **New Window.** `view.newWindow` opens a second window on the active workbook; it shares the workbook, and an edit in one shows in the other. Titles are `Name:1`, `Name:2`, renumbered when one closes. `file.close` closes the active window, with no prompt while the workbook has another window, and `{document: true}` closes the workbook.
- **Commands.** These take a window id, a document id or an index:
  - `window.list` (query) and `window.close {window?, doc?, force?}`;
  - `window.activate {window | doc | index}`;
  - `view.switchWindows`, `view.hideWindow` and `view.unhideWindow`.

  Rows are `{window, doc, index, title, dirty, active, hidden}`.
- **Control channel and MCP.** `engine.execute` takes `window` or `doc` and runs the command there. The previously active window comes back afterwards, unless the command switched windows. `ui.inspect` reports the windows, and every MCP workbook tool takes `window`/`doc`; `list_windows` is new.
- A cell draft settles on every window switch, including between two windows of one workbook.

## Checks

Engine tests cover window ids, New Window titles and renumbering, closing a window or a document, hide and unhide, and routing by window or doc. `window.close` is left out of the empty-params and command-sequence fuzz, as `file.close` is.

title: Window per workbook (3/4): a native window per workbook window
author: aiongg
body:
Each window gets its own native window: opening or creating a workbook opens a window, and New Window opens a second native window on the same workbook.

Stacked on #2617; review the commits after it.

The native windows come from `craft-window` (storytold/craft-libs#340). Every craft-libs crate is pinned to one storytold/craft-libs main revision, b926b5c0.

Fixes #162.

## What changes

- **Per-window UI state** (`crates/ui-egui/src/window_ui.rs`). Each window keeps its own cell and text-box drafts, dialog, Backstage, messages, grid state, Name Box, key tips, chart selection and mode. The window shown in a viewport is swapped in before the viewport draws.
- **Native windows** (`crates/ui-egui/src/doc_windows.rs`, native builds only). The engine's visible windows are mirrored into `craft_window::Viewports`. A title gets " — Edited" while its workbook is unsaved. When the first window closes, another window takes over the root viewport. The web build keeps one window.
- **Routing.** Shortcuts and menus act on the focused window. The ribbon acts on its own window, and control requests and scripts go to the last-focused window. Leaving a window commits its draft.
- **Close and quit.** Closing one of several windows on a workbook doesn't prompt; closing the last window of an unsaved workbook asks to save. Quit asks once for each unsaved workbook, in that workbook's window, and Cancel stops it. On Windows and Linux, closing the last window quits. On macOS the app keeps running with no window, and New or Open shows one again.

- **Control channel.** `ui.screenshot` and synthetic input run in the first (root) window's pass. With several windows open, a screenshot captures the root window, and it fails if that window shows another workbook than the one asked for.

`crates/ui-egui/tests/it/doc_windows.rs` runs each viewport as a nested pass. It covers:

title: Window per workbook (4/4): two windows on one workbook without copying it; Arrange All
author: aiongg
body:
Two windows on one workbook show their own sheets without copying the workbook, and View › Arrange All lays the windows out.

Stacked on #2618; review the commits after it.

## What changes

- **A sheet per window without copying.** Two windows on one workbook can show different sheets. Switching between them used to clone the workbook on every swap. `Workbook.active_sheet` is an `ActiveSheet` value that is set in place through the shared workbook: reads go through `active_sheet()` and writes through `set_active_sheet()`.
  - The trade-off: everything that shares the current workbook (the saved copy, a clipboard snapshot) sees the change. Nothing reads their active sheet, and undo snapshots keep their own value.
  - A save records the sheet of the most recently active window.
  - The alternative is to move the active sheet into per-window document state; that touches about 600 call sites, so it is left for a decision here.
- **Dialogs stay with their window** across a switch, whether it comes from a menu, a native click or a script.
- **Arrange All.** `view.arrangeAll {arrange?: tiled | horizontal | vertical | cascade, activeWorkbook?}` returns `{arrange, windows}`; it used to be a stub. It places the native windows over the first window's monitor, active window first. View › Window has New Window and Arrange All, and the key tip W, A opens it.

## Checks

- Engine test: swaps share the workbook (the same `Arc`), and the workbook doesn't turn unsaved. An edit in window 2 lands on window 2's sheet, and save and reopen keep the latest window's sheet.
- UI tests: two windows on one workbook show their own sheet and each other's edits; a dialog stays with its window; Arrange All picks the visible windows, active first, and lays out the native windows.

Tested by hand on macOS at 2ed3df2b, which is this stack on main 06920de8. This branch merges current main into that build.

title: Charts: read, write and draw error bars
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
## What this adds

Chart error bars, the last piece of the chart-model work on `feat/chart-error-bars`:

- **Model:** each series can hold error bars, at most one set per direction (X or Y). A set has a direction, plus, minus or both sides, an amount (fixed value, percentage, standard deviation multiple, standard error, or custom plus/minus ranges or arrays), an optional end cap, and line colour, width and dash.
- **XLSX:** `c:errBars` is read and written in schema order, after the trendlines. Column and bar series keep one Y set, as Excel writes them; area, scatter and bubble series keep one per direction.
- **Drawing:** error bars are drawn on 2-D column, bar, line, area (stacked too), scatter and bubble series, and the value axis grows to hold them. Non-finite or hostile amounts give finite lengths.
- **Engine:** `chart.addElement` with `element="errorBars"` adds, replaces or removes them; `chart.set` drops error bars the new chart kind cannot keep; `document.inspect` lists them.
- **Docs:** chart parity, gaps, roadmap and the progress log.

## Why

Charts in workbooks often carry error bars, and without them GridCraft loses them on an XLSX round trip and cannot draw them.

## Merge notes

This branch was based on the 0.7.0 release. It is merged into current `main`, with the import and docs conflicts resolved by hand. Two follow-up fixes came out of review:

- A test helper now sets the `category_levels` field that `main` added to `ChartData`.
- Gap 4 in `docs/gaps.md` lists only what is still missing, and records PRs #158 and #161 as merged.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --check` passes locally. Nothing else was built or tested on the machine that prepared this PR, because of its memory limits. The fork's CI runs the full `cargo xtask ci` gate on this PR.
- The CodeRabbit CLI review (`cr review --agent --base main --gate major`) passes with no blocking findings.

title: Fill handle: Linear Trend and Growth Trend on the right-drag menu for numbers
author: dotCooCoo
body:
## Summary
When every source cell holds a number, the right-drag fill menu now also offers Linear Trend and Growth Trend. `docs/ui-parity.md` listed them as missing from the menu.

Microsoft's "Project values in a series" page (https://web.archive.org/web/20250910221013/https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/project-values-in-a-series-5311f5cf-149e-4d06-81dd-5aaad87e5400) says:
- "Hold down the right mouse button, drag the fill handle in the direction that you want to fill with increasing values or decreasing values, release the mouse button, and then click Growth Trend on the shortcut menu."
- "In a linear series, the starting values are applied to the least-squares algorithm (y=mx+b) to generate the series."
- "In a growth series, the starting values are applied to the exponential curve algorithm (y=b*m^x) to generate the series."
- "The series that is created is equivalent to the values that are returned by the TREND function or GROWTH function."

The `XlAutoFillType` page (https://web.archive.org/web/20241128020612/https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office/vba/api/excel.xlautofilltype) says of xlLinearTrend: "Extend the numeric values from the source range into the target range, assuming that the relationships between the numbers is additive (for example, '1, 2,' is extended as '3, 4, 5', ...)". Of xlGrowthTrend it says "'1, 2,' is extended as '4, 8, 16'", and of both: "Formats are copied from the source range to the target range, repeating if necessary."

Neither page puts Linear Trend on the right-drag menu, says whether the source keeps its values, or says what happens with one starting value, zero or mixed signs. These rules are GridCraft's own: the menu lists Linear Trend next to Growth Trend, the source keeps its values, a lone number repeats, numbers that are all below zero grow away from zero (GROWTH itself returns #NUM! for them), and the menu lists each trend only when the source fits it.

title: Python cells as data: stored, edited and saved as Excel's PY formula (no code runs)
author: prxnvt
body:
## Summary

This pull request adds Python cells as data. A Python cell holds Python code and the last result a file cached for it. This pull request stores, edits, copies and saves Python cells; it runs no Python code. It is the first part of a series that follows the design described in the comment on #469 (off by default, enabled only in the user interface, sandboxed, data only through the cells, strict limits, a small core). It replaces the data and file-format parts of #469.

## Changes

**Model.** `Cell` gains an optional `py: PyCode`: the code, the return type (Excel's `PY(python_code, return_type)`, where 0 is an Excel value and 1 is a Python object), the cached result and a stale flag. The cell's value remains the cached result, so formulas, display and saving read a Python cell as any other cell. `CellError` gains `#PYTHON!`, `#BUSY!`, `#TIMEOUT!` and `#BLOCKED!`. `ERROR.TYPE` gives 11 for `#BLOCKED!`, as Excel does; Microsoft documents no number for the other three, which take 19, 20 and 21.

**Size limit.** Excel limits a formula to 8,192 characters. A Python cell's code must fit in that limit once it is encoded as the file formula, with quotes doubled and the 255-character literals joined by `&`. The limit is therefore measured on the encoded formula (`PyCode::fits`), not on a character count of the code: 8,079 characters of plain code fit exactly, and code with many quotes fits in fewer.

**Editing.** `python.set {cell?, code, output?}` makes a Python cell. New or changed code shows `#BLOCKED!`, because nothing runs it; unchanged code keeps its cached result. A table header row and a locked cell on a protected sheet refuse it. Typing `=PY(` is refused with a message that names `python.set`. An edit that begins on a Python cell (F2, a double-click or the formula bar) commits changed text through `python.set`, so the cell stays a Python cell; typing over the cell replaces it, as it replaces a formula. Copy, paste, fill, sort, cut-move, sheet copy and undo…

title: fix: start system font scan during language-aware context setup
author: Karloss1234
body:
## Problem

On Linux, GridCraft was not rendering installed system fonts such as Arial, Calibri, Courier New, and Times New Roman correctly. Bold and italic variants were also affected.

The font scanner was never started during the normal desktop startup path.

## Root cause

`fonts::start_scan()` was called by `setup_context()`, but the desktop application uses `setup_context_for_language()` instead.

Consequently, the background font scan never started, leaving system font families unavailable to the renderer.

## Fix

Call `fonts::start_scan()` from `setup_context_for_language()`.

The scanner uses `OnceLock`, so repeated calls are safe.

## Verification

Tested on Kubuntu 26.04. Before the fix, the font scan never completed because it was not started. After the fix, installed system fonts were discovered and registered, and normal, bold, and italic rendering worked correctly.
