title: PDF: set Romanian ș ț Ș Ț (comma below) in the Latin font (on #2556)
author: vioreltus
body:
Stacked on #2556 (its commit is the first one here; only the top commit, **PDF: set Romanian ș ț Ș Ț (comma below) in the Latin font too**, is new). Part of #446.

## Why

#2556 sets the Latin Extended-A letters (U+0100..U+017F) in the standard face, which covers Romanian ă/Ă. But Romanian ș ț Ș Ț are U+0218..U+021B, Latin Extended-B, so with #2556 they still go to the non-embedded STSong-Light CID font. Adobe-GB1 has no glyph for them: on Windows they print as boxes followed by a full-em gap (`Comand□  manuale`, `□tiin□e`). Every Romanian document has them.

## What this changes

- `ext_code` gives Ș ș Ț ț bytes 0x01..0x04 of the same per-face resource, and the `/Differences` array names them `uni0218 uni0219 uni021A uni021B`. The `uniXXXX` form is found both by fonts that name these glyphs so (TeX Gyre Heros, poppler's Helvetica substitute, has no `scommaaccent`) and by viewers that map a glyph name to its code point. The AGL names would not do for Ț/ț: the AGL maps `Tcommaaccent` to the cedilla letter U+0162.
- The resource now carries `/FirstChar 1 /LastChar 255 /Widths`. A viewer takes a standard font's advances from its own metrics by glyph name; those have no `uni0219`, so without widths ș advanced by nothing and overprinted the next letter (seen with poppler). Unused codes are 0.
- `fold` measures them like S and T, so wrapping and alignment use the right widths.

## How it was verified

- `cargo test -p gridcraft-pdf --lib`: 19 passed. `romanian_letters_use_the_latin_font` fails on #2556 without this commit (reverted and re-run).
- `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-pdf --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`.
- A real school order sheet (A4 landscape, Calibri, Romanian text) printed from a Windows build of main + #2556 + this to Microsoft Print to PDF: every ă â î ș ț Ș Ț prints correctly, where 0.12.1 printed boxes. Exported on Linux, poppler draws them too and `pdftotext` extracts them.

title: Type with an input method straight into a cell
author: nct88
body:
## Cause
The grid only reacted to `Event::Text`. It never turned the input method on, and it ignored `ImeEvent::Preedit` and `ImeEvent::Commit`. So when you typed Vietnamese with fcitx5-unikey (XIM, on the spot) into a selected cell, the word sat in a box drawn by the input method itself, or nothing appeared, until you pressed Space. The same applies to any input method that composes, such as Chinese, Japanese or Korean.

## Fix
- `grid/keyboard.rs`: while no editor has the focus, the grid owns an IME context, and the candidate window sits at the active cell (a merged range uses its top-left cell). The owner and generation come from an `egui::ime_context::ImeContextTracker` stored in `GridState`. The grid has no committed text of its own, so the surrounding text stays `Unavailable`. When the grid gives up the keyboard, it observes `None`, so taking the focus back starts a new context.
- The first `Preedit` opens the cell's editor empty, the same way typing a letter does. The composition is handed to the editor once the editor has the focus, two frames later through `SheetApp::synthetic`. From then on the composition shows in the cell, in the cell's font, through the editor's `TextEdit`.
- A `Commit` that arrives without a composition is typed into the cell like text.
- Opening the editor calls `request_focus`, and egui interrupts the input method on every focus move. fcitx5 then dropped the letter it was composing, so typing "không" gave "hong". A small `egui::Plugin` (`KeepComposition`) clears `should_interrupt_composition` in its output hook for that frame and the next one.

## Verified
- `tests/it/ime_typing.rs` has 3 tests. All 3 fail on `main` and pass with this change. Without the `KeepComposition` call, `opening_the_editor_keeps_the_letter_being_composed` fails (frame 0 is interrupted).
- `cargo fmt --all` makes no changes, and `cargo clippy -p gridcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- `cargo test -p gridcraft-ui-egui` passes, except `intera…

title: Keep saved formula results when opening workbooks
author: ro-legal-docx
body:
Opening an XLSX currently recalculates every formula. An unsupported function can replace its saved result with an error, propagate that error into dependents and write the errors back on save, even after an unrelated cell edit. A hand-authored synthetic file reproduced 1250.25, 2500.5 and 833.5 becoming `#NAME?` in v0.12.1.

`file.open` now keeps nonempty saved formula results and calculates only missing results. It reports that caches may be stale and that edits/recalculation can replace unsupported results with errors. Callers can opt into the previous full-recalc policy with `recalculate: true`; Calculate Now remains a full recalculation. Newly created workbooks retain their existing calculation path.

Unresolved calls no longer become implicitly volatile solely because the function is absent. Their explicit argument dependencies remain active, and workbook-defined functions and supported dynamic references continue to recalculate.

**Builds on open PR #2308 by @mrzv**, pinned at `7f2cdebcd9a32e17af5b7951b44c3e883f774272`. Its existing `Calc::recalc_missing` implementation, tests and documentation are included with the original contributor history preserved. The separate follow-up commit adds the engine open policy, cache notice, explicit opt-in, unresolved-call invalidation fix and nine engine lifecycle tests. title: grid: middle-button pan (AutoCAD-style grab)
author: soiamsoNG
body:
## What

Holding the middle mouse button on the grid now pans the sheet, AutoCAD style, instead of doing nothing (and instead of the accidental object/selection drags the unguarded `resp.drag_started()` calls in `crates/ui-egui/src/grid/interact.rs` produced on a middle drag).

- The pan starts **on the press**, not after egui's drag threshold, so the content follows the pointer from the first pixel.
- It follows the pointer **1:1** at the current zoom (`view.scroll -= pointer_delta / z`), respects right-to-left sheets, and stops dead on release — no inertia.
- Nothing selects while it is held: `show_grid_interactions` skips the paper and grid interaction passes for the duration, so a middle drag that begins over a chart pans the sheet under it and does not move or select the chart.
- The cursor is `CursorIcon::Grabbing` for as long as the pan lasts, even if the pointer leaves the grid.
- Cell/text-box/header-footer editors keep the middle click — X11 pastes PRIMARY with it.

## Control channel

`ui.drag` / `ui.cell.drag` take a `button` parameter (`"middle"`, `"right"`, default left), and `ui.click` / `ui.cell.click` share the same parser, so the pan is drivable headlessly instead of only by hand.

- `a_middle_click_without_moving_leaves_the_view_alone`
- `the_cursor_is_a_grabbing_hand_while_the_pan_lasts`
- `a_middle_drag_over_a_chart_does_not_move_it` — the chart's anchor/size and `selected_chart` are unchanged while the sheet pans.
